shabbos/accidental-shabbos-violation-tha.intro: A fisherman forgot it was Shabbos, cast his net, and pulled up a baby who had fallen into the water. Must he bring a korban chattas? Menachos 64a says no, because a chattas is brought for an accidental act that breaks Shabbos, not for an accidental thought, and this act turned out to be pikuach nefesh.
shabbos/accidental-shabbos-violation-tha.description: A fisherman forgot it was Shabbos and netted a drowning baby. Must he bring a chattas? Menachos 64a says no, since the act turned out to save a life.

shabbos/adding-wine-to-charoses-on-shabb.intro: Tosfos noticed a tension on Pesachim 116a: charoses should be thick like mortar, yet elsewhere it is treated like a liquid. He suggests making it thick and adding red wine just before dipping, to recall the blood the Egyptians shed. [Charoses: Bricks, Straws, and Blood](/daf/pesachim/116/charoses-bricks-straws-and-blood) notes that this cannot be done when the Seder falls on Shabbos, since thinning the charoses would be the melacha of kneading.
shabbos/adding-wine-to-charoses-on-shabb.description: Why not thin the charoses with wine when the Seder falls on Shabbos? Tosfos' custom of adding wine, and the melacha of kneading. Pesachim 116a.

shabbos/animals-resting-on-shabbos.intro: The Torah forbids having one's animals do melachah on Shabbos, and the Ohr Sameach suggests the Torah wanted to give animals a break too. [Horsing Around](/daf/avodah-zarah/14/horsing-around) builds riddles on it: a needle on a horse's back makes the owner liable even though the animal does not know it is carrying, and the Pri Megadim is unsure whether tosefes Shabbos applies. These ideas sit beside the mishnah on Avodah Zarah 14b.
shabbos/animals-resting-on-shabbos.description: Why a horse carrying a needle makes its owner liable on Shabbos: the mitzvah of letting animals rest, shinui, and tosefes Shabbos, from Avodah Zarah 14b.

shabbos/asking-another-jew-after-early-s.intro: After making an early Shabbos, may one ask a Jew who has not yet accepted Shabbos to turn on a light? The Shulchan Aruch quotes an opinion, accepted by the Rema, that one may ask directly and even read by that light, and the Rema extends this to motzaei Shabbos. [Split Decision](/daf/pesachim/52/split-decision) on Pesachim 52 brings the Magen Avraham's reason: the requester accepted Shabbos early by choice and need not be observing it yet.
shabbos/asking-another-jew-after-early-s.description: After an early Shabbos, may you ask a Jew who has not accepted it yet to do melacha for you? The Shulchan Aruch, Rema and Magen Avraham. Pesachim 52.

shabbos/blech-for-a-crockpot.intro: On a stove, a blech cuts down the heat and covers the knobs, so no one will adjust the fire, but how do you make one for a crockpot? Some line it with foil, while others say only heavy-duty foil or several layers help. In [More Crockpot Questions](/daf/shabbos/36/more-crockpot-questions), Rav Reuven Feinstein and Rav Moshe Heineman allow just covering the knob, in light of Shabbos 36b.
shabbos/blech-for-a-crockpot.description: Does a crockpot need a blech, like a foil lining, or is covering the knob enough? Poskim including Rav Reuven Feinstein weigh in, in light of Shabbos 36b.

shabbos/breaking-shabbos-to-prevent-conv.intro: The Beis Yosef rules that a father may even break Torah prohibitions of Shabbos to rescue a daughter taken by a priest to be raised as a gentile. But what about someone who chose to leave on his own? Based on Tosfos's two answers about the half-slave in Gittin 41a, the article shows that it depends on whether he was negligent and whether a mitzvah rabbah is at stake.
shabbos/breaking-shabbos-to-prevent-conv.description: May Shabbos be broken to stop a Jew from leaving the faith? The Beis Yosef and Tosfos's half-slave case in Gittin 41a show it depends on who is at fault.

shabbos/building-a-temporary-ohel-on-sha.intro: Chazal forbade building even a small, flimsy shelter on Shabbos, an ohel arai, and the Chasam Sofer explains that the Mishkan's cover was also just laid on top. Eruvin 101a lists examples, from logs piled for a fire to eggs stacked with a hollow space. The roof must be at least a tefach, and the Rema rules it is a problem only when the hollow space is wanted.
shabbos/building-a-temporary-ohel-on-sha.description: Why is even a small temporary ohel forbidden on Shabbos? The Chasam Sofer's reason, the Gemara's cases in Eruvin 101a and the minimum size of a tefach.

shabbos/bungalow-colony-shabbos-meals.intro: Summer Shabbos in a bungalow colony has its own rhythm, with shared ovens, family pitching in, and pots moving from one bungalow to the next. [Bungalow Cooking at Its Best](/beyond-the-daf/bungalow-cooking-at-its-best) follows one Pine Knoll Shabbos in Monticello, from grilled salmon and sous vide London broil to a cholent with a single potato. It ends with the full Friday night and Shabbos lunch menu.
shabbos/bungalow-colony-shabbos-meals.description: A lighthearted look at cooking Shabbos meals in a summer bungalow colony, with shared ovens, family helpers, a cake rescue and the full Friday night menu.

shabbos/buying-and-selling-on-shabbos.intro: Commerce on Shabbos and Yom Tov is usually seen as a rabbinic ban, lest people write down their deals. Rebbe Akiva Eiger, based on Rashi on Beitzah 36a, suggests it may even be a Torah prohibition. Small purchases without money are possible, but only with a clear change from weekday buying, such as never discussing the price.
shabbos/buying-and-selling-on-shabbos.description: Why is buying and selling forbidden on Shabbos and Yom Tov? Rebbe Akiva Eiger suggests it may even be a Torah ban, based on Rashi on Beitzah 36a.

shabbos/challah-cover-at-seudah-shlishis.intro: Of the three reasons for covering the challah, only one seems to apply at the third Shabbos meal: recalling the dew that covered the manna. As explained on Pesachim 100, there is no Kiddush to shame the bread, and no one would mistake the meal for a weekday one. The Aruch HaShulchan did not cover it, while the Kaf HaChaim says to, and at Melaveh Malkah after Havdalah, the shame reason may return.
shabbos/challah-cover-at-seudah-shlishis.description: Should the challah be covered at seudah shlishis or Melaveh Malkah? Which of the three reasons for the cover still apply, explained on Pesachim 100.

shabbos/clearing-a-clogged-gutter-on-sha.intro: A beraisa in Kesubos 60a discusses a clogged roof gutter threatening to flood a house on Shabbos. Nochum Ish Galya permits clearing it with one's foot when no one is looking, and Rav Yosef rules that way. Fixing the gutter is a Torah prohibition of repairing, but the shinui makes it rabbinic, which Chazal waived for the great loss.
shabbos/clearing-a-clogged-gutter-on-sha.description: May a clogged roof gutter be cleared on Shabbos to prevent flooding? Nochum Ish Galya allows using one's foot, a shinui, in the beraisa in Kesubos 60a.

shabbos/climbing-trees-on-shabbos.intro: The Shulchan Aruch rules that one may not climb a tree on Shabbos, whether living or not. This follows Rav's stringency in Eruvin 100a, made for a place where Torah knowledge was scarce and a simple rule was needed. [Seeking a Shady Exemption](/daf/eruvin/100/seeking-a-shady-exemption-2020) traces how the Gemara first settles the dead tree question by the season.
shabbos/climbing-trees-on-shabbos.description: Why may one not climb or use a tree on Shabbos, even a dead one? The Gemara in Eruvin 100a, Rav's strict local rule and the Shulchan Aruch's ruling.

shabbos/color-changing-spoons-and-cups-o.intro: May a child's spoon that changes color in cold milk be used on Shabbos? Rav Moshe Feinstein holds such a temporary change is not tzovaya at all, and Rav Dovid Feinstein allowed a mug that changes color with hot liquid. Rav Avigdor Nebenzahl, though, says not to chill a Coors bottle in order to change its color, in a discussion that starts from Sanhedrin 77a.
shabbos/color-changing-spoons-and-cups-o.description: May color-changing spoons, mugs or beer bottles be used on Shabbos? Rav Moshe Feinstein, Rav Dovid Feinstein and Rav Nebenzahl on intent, Sanhedrin 77a.

shabbos/crockpot-on-shabbos.intro: Rav Shlomo Zalman Auerbach reportedly ruled that a crockpot may not be used on Shabbos, since its heated walls surround the insert, and the 1995 controversy shook many homes. Many poskim permit it anyway, including Rav Moshe Feinstein. [Crockpot Controversies](/daf/bava-basra/19/crockpot-controversies) shows how Rav Pinchas Scheinberg's approach may find a source in a Tosfos on Bava Basra 19a about flintstones.
shabbos/crockpot-on-shabbos.description: May a crockpot be used for cholent on Shabbos? Rav Shlomo Zalman forbade it, while Rav Moshe and others permit it, using a Tosfos in Bava Basra 19a.

shabbos/cutting-a-cake-with-writing-on-s.intro: Bakeries often write Happy Birthday on a piece of chocolate instead of on the cake, to avoid mocheik, erasing, when it is cut on Shabbos. The Noda B'Yehuda fully permits cutting through frosting letters, the Mishnah Berurah forbids it as an inevitable result, and the Chazon Ish won't even let one chew it. [Piece Of Cake](/daf/menachos/94/piece-of-cake) traces a leniency to Menachos 94b.
shabbos/cutting-a-cake-with-writing-on-s.description: Is cutting through frosting letters on a cake erasing on Shabbos? The Noda B'Yehuda, Mishnah Berurah and Chazon Ish, with a leniency from Menachos 94b.

shabbos/dieting-on-shabbos.intro: The Ben Ish Chai writes that eating delicious food on Shabbos is a choice mitzvah, but the Kaf HaChaim says one should still not eat his fill. Rabbeinu Moshe Kohen even suggests the three Shabbos meals were meant to limit eating, since a person paces himself. The discussion grows out of the warnings against overeating in Gittin 70a.
shabbos/dieting-on-shabbos.description: Can you diet on Shabbos and still enjoy its food? The Ben Ish Chai, the Kaf HaChaim and Rabbeinu Moshe Kohen weigh in, building on Gittin 70a.

shabbos/drawing-lots-on-shabbos.intro: The Shulchan Aruch forbids casting lots on Shabbos, since it resembles commerce, but a family may use lots to divide food among its children. The Magen Avraham allows lots for a mitzvah, like an aliyah, citing the Yom Kippur lotteries in the Beis HaMikdash. The Shvus Yaakov objects from Yoma 32 that the Kohen Gadol did all the avodah, and the Kesef Mishneh answers that the daily avodos still needed a lottery.
shabbos/drawing-lots-on-shabbos.description: When may lots be drawn on Shabbos? The Shulchan Aruch's rule, the family exception, and the Magen Avraham's mitzvah lottery, tied to Yoma 32.

shabbos/eating-fish-on-shabbos.intro: Fish is a staple of the Shabbos table, but what if its price shoots up? When fishmongers raised prices, the Tzemach Tzedek called for a boycott, following Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's step to lower the price of birds for korbanos in Bava Basra 166a. He ruled that eating fish is just one way of fulfilling oneg Shabbos, which other dishes can fulfill as well.
shabbos/eating-fish-on-shabbos.description: Is fish on Shabbos required, or one way of oneg Shabbos? The Tzemach Tzedek's fish boycott, based on a Mishna in Bava Basra 166a, weighs the question.

shabbos/ebay-auctions-ending-on-shabbos.intro: May one bid on an online auction that closes on Shabbos, when no action happens on Shabbos but the sale is completed then? [Is eBay For-Bid-Den?](/daf/yoma/13/is-ebay-for-bid-den) traces the question to Yoma 13b and Rebbe Akiva Eiger, and brings poskim on both sides: one Brooklyn posek permits it based on the Terumas HaDeshen, while another contemporary posek says not to bid.
shabbos/ebay-auctions-ending-on-shabbos.description: May you bid on an eBay auction that ends on Shabbos? Rebbe Akiva Eiger, the Terumas HaDeshen, and today's poskim on both sides, from Yoma 13b.

shabbos/electric-lights-as-shabbos-candl.intro: Can an electric light serve as a Shabbos light? Rav Shlomo Zalman allowed a bracha on a flashlight, and Rav Elyashiv reportedly even on fluorescent lights, since the mitzvah is to light the home. [Illuminating The Shabbos Blessing](/daf/sanhedrin/32/illuminating-the-shabbos-blessing) also explains, from Sanhedrin 32b, why candles still get a bracha in a lit house.
shabbos/electric-lights-as-shabbos-candl.description: Can a flashlight or electric bulb be a Shabbos light with a bracha? Rav Shlomo Zalman, Rav Elyashiv and why candles still matter, with Sanhedrin 32b.

shabbos/emergency-phone-calls-on-shabbos.intro: On Shabbos, a heartbroken mother called a Jewish Air Force chaplain because her son planned to be baptized after Shabbos. Was she allowed to make that call? In [Of Baptisms and Half-Slaves](/daf/gittin/41/of-baptisms-and-half-slaves), on Gittin 41a, many poskim see phone use as only a rabbinic prohibition, and Rav Dovid Feinstein agreed the mother acted correctly.
shabbos/emergency-phone-calls-on-shabbos.description: May one make a phone call on Shabbos to stop a Jew from converting? A mother's call to a chaplain and Rav Dovid Feinstein's view, explored on Gittin 41a.

shabbos/fasting-on-shabbos.intro: Why is fasting on Shabbos avoided? The twelve loaves of lechem hapanim were replaced each Shabbos, and the kohanim had to eat the old batch, so they could not fast, except when Yom Kippur fell on Shabbos. While the Rambam holds they could eat it only on Shabbos day, Menachos 100b supports others who allow motzaei Shabbos, and the Mishnas Chayim says Shabbos day was still preferred.
shabbos/fasting-on-shabbos.description: Why is fasting generally on Shabbos avoided, except on Yom Kippur? The kohanim had to eat the showbread, with the Rambam and others on Menachos 100b.

shabbos/feeding-birds-on-shabbos-shirah.intro: Many families feed birds on Shabbos Shirah, but the Gemara in Shabbos 155 forbids any effort on Shabbos to feed animals that are not yours, and the Mishnah Berurah questions the custom. Many put the food out before Shabbos. The Aruch HaShulchan defends the practice, because we feed the birds to recall the miracles of the sea and the manna, for our own sake.
shabbos/feeding-birds-on-shabbos-shirah.description: Can you feed birds on Shabbos Shirah if you may not feed animals that aren't yours? The Mishnah Berurah and Aruch HaShulchan, based on Shabbos 155.

shabbos/gerama-on-shabbos.intro: Opening a freezer on Shabbos lets in warm air and makes the compressor turn on sooner. Rav Shlomo Zalman Auerbach ruled this is at worst a rabbinic issue, and since there is usually a delay before the compressor starts, it is only gerama, indirect causing. In [Machmir Or Make Cool?](/daf/kesubos/6/machmir-or-make-cool), filed on Kesubos 6, he permits gerama for a rabbinic prohibition.
shabbos/gerama-on-shabbos.description: When is indirectly causing a forbidden result on Shabbos allowed? Rav Shlomo Zalman permits gerama for a rabbinic issue, like a freezer, from Kesubos 6.

shabbos/getting-paid-for-work-on-shabbos.intro: Even when a job itself does not break Shabbos, being paid for it can be a problem. The article on Bava Metzia 10a raises s'char Shabbos while discussing a Jewish ballplayer: one may not earn wages for services done on Shabbos. It also notes that there are permissible ways to structure a contract to get around this.
shabbos/getting-paid-for-work-on-shabbos.description: May you be paid for Shabbos work that is itself permitted? The rule of s'char Shabbos and the contract fixes for it, in an article on Bava Metzia 10a.

shabbos/giving-gifts-on-shabbos.intro: The Mishnah Berurah writes that giving presents on Shabbos is not allowed, yet a gift for a Shabbos need or a mitzvah is permitted, such as wine for the meal or a lulav on Yom Tov. Rebbe Akiva Eiger gave gifts to a chassan to gladden him. For other gifts, [Business Or Pleasure?](/daf/beitzah/36/business-or-pleasure), filed on Beitzah 36a, offers two solutions.
shabbos/giving-gifts-on-shabbos.description: May you give presents on Shabbos? Gifts for a Shabbos or mitzvah need are allowed, and there are ways to give others, in an article on Beitzah 36a.

shabbos/giving-medicine-to-animals-on-sh.intro: One Shabbos, children in a yeshiva dormitory saw that a pet fish was sick and asked the mashgiach whether medicine could go into the tank. The Sages forbade taking medicine for minor ailments, as learned in Shabbos 109. In [Calling Doctor Dolittle](/daf/shabbos/109/calling-doctor-dolittle), the Mishnah Berurah, citing the Rif and the Rosh, says the ban does not apply to animals.
shabbos/giving-medicine-to-animals-on-sh.description: May you put medicine in a fish tank on Shabbos? The Mishnah Berurah says the rabbinic ban on medicine does not cover animals, as learned in Shabbos 109.

shabbos/hatmana-insulating-food-for-shab.intro: Chazal forbade wrapping hot food before Shabbos in anything that adds heat, for fear a person might come to stoke coals. The Rema allows partially covering a pot this way. Tosfos on Bava Basra 19a says flintstones were never included because no one used them, and Rav Moshe Feinstein concludes that Chazal's list of forbidden materials stays fixed even when customs change.
shabbos/hatmana-insulating-food-for-shab.description: What exactly did Chazal forbid with hatmana, insulating food for Shabbos? The Rema on partial covering and Tosfos in Bava Basra 19a on flintstones.

shabbos/how-many-shabbos-candles-to-ligh.intro: The mitzvah of Shabbos lights is met with just one, so why do we all light more? In [Light Up The Night](/daf/shabbos/23/light-up-the-night), the Ravyah learns from the old man with two bundles of myrtle that two lights show we honor Shabbos, for zachor and shamor. Others light seven, ten, 26 or 36, and some add one for each child, all from Shabbos 23.
shabbos/how-many-shabbos-candles-to-ligh.description: How many Shabbos candles should one light? Two for zachor and shamor, or seven, ten, 26 or 36, or one per child? The customs, from Shabbos 23.

shabbos/husbands-cooking-for-shabbos.intro: What happens when the wives head to the city and the husbands are told to make Shabbos? Two brothers-in-law split the menu, and the mistakes pile up: a teaspoon used where a tablespoon was needed for the potato kugel, a forgotten lokshen kugel, and a birthday cake that fell apart. The wife's verdict at the end is kind, with one firm rule about leaving the kitchen clean.
shabbos/husbands-cooking-for-shabbos.description: Husbands take over the Shabbos cooking: a potato kugel saved after a salt mix-up, a cake turned into mousse cups, and a wife's honest review of it all.

shabbos/idle-chatter-on-shabbos.intro: From the words v'dabeir davar, Tosefos learn that one should speak less about mundane topics like politics and sports on Shabbos, and the Shulchan Aruch rules that even idle chatter should be limited. The Rema allows people who enjoy the news to keep discussing it. [Word To The Wise](/daf/kiddushin/31/word-to-the-wise), filed on Kiddushin 31, adds the Mishnah Berurah's caution and the story of Rebbe Tarfon and his mother.
shabbos/idle-chatter-on-shabbos.description: Should talk of news, politics and sports be limited on Shabbos? Tosefos, the Rema and the Mishnah Berurah on idle chatter, from an article on Kiddushin 31.

shabbos/instant-ramen-noodles-on-shabbos.intro: Ramen noodles are precooked, so pouring hot water on them should not be cooking on Shabbos. But some brands steam rather than boil their noodles, and baked items can be cooked again, while Tosafos on Avodah Zarah 74b holds that water straight from the urn can cook a thin layer. The raw spice and vegetable packets add another problem, so the practical answer is a kli shlishi.
shabbos/instant-ramen-noodles-on-shabbos.description: May instant ramen soup be made on Shabbos? Steamed noodles, raw spice packets, and why Tosafos on Avodah Zarah 74b rules out pouring straight from the urn.

shabbos/ki-eshmerah-shabbos-zemer.intro: The zemer Ki Eshmerah Shabbos, by Rav Avrohom Ibn Ezra, has a line that is easy to sing without understanding. It says that because the kohanim set out the showbread on Shabbos, fasting is forbidden on it, except for Yom Kippur. In [Fresh Bread: The Original Baker’s Dozen](/daf/menachos/100/fresh-bread-the-original-bakers-dozen), this seems to follow the Rambam, though Menachos 100b allows eating it on motzaei Shabbos.
shabbos/ki-eshmerah-shabbos-zemer.description: What does the line about the showbread and fasting mean in the zemer Ki Eshmerah Shabbos? The Ibn Ezra and the Rambam, explained from Menachos 100b.

shabbos/kli-shlishi-on-shabbos.intro: To make instant noodle soup on Shabbos, one fills a cup from the urn, pours it into a second empty cup, and only then adds the noodles and flavoring. This kli shlishi solves the problem raised by Tosafos on Avodah Zarah 74b, that water from a kli rishon can cook a thin layer of food. It relies on Rav Moshe Feinstein's view that there is no bishul in a kli shlishi, a ruling not universally accepted.
shabbos/kli-shlishi-on-shabbos.description: How pouring hot water into a third vessel avoids cooking on Shabbos, Rav Moshe Feinstein's view of kli shlishi, and Tosafos on Avodah Zarah 74b.

shabbos/leaning-on-a-tree-on-shabbos.intro: After a long kiddush, a tree outside shul can look like the perfect place to lean. The Gemara in Eruvin 100a says plainly that leaning on a tree counts as using it, which is forbidden on Shabbos. In [Seeking A Shady Exemption](/daf/eruvin/100/seeking-a-shady-exemption), the suggestion is simple: a utility pole or a bench works just fine.
shabbos/leaning-on-a-tree-on-shabbos.description: May you lean on a tree on Shabbos? The Gemara in Eruvin 100a counts leaning as using the tree, which is forbidden, so a pole or bench is the alternative.

shabbos/lechem-mishneh-on-shabbos.intro: Rebbe Abba teaches on Shabbos 117b that Hamotzi on Shabbos is said over two loaves, recalling the double portion of mann that fell on Friday. The loaves must be whole, so the one making Hamotzi should not slice too deeply before the bracha. [Dough Adir](/daf/sanhedrin/102/dough-adir) explains why a small incision is made instead, and when it is not needed at all.
shabbos/lechem-mishneh-on-shabbos.description: Why two whole loaves at Shabbos meals? Rebbe Abba on Shabbos 117b ties lechem mishneh to the double mann. How to keep the challos whole before Hamotzi.

shabbos/lehadlik-ner-shel-shabbos-wordin.intro: A woman lighting several Shabbos lights still says l'hadlik ner shel Shabbos, in the singular, though neiros might seem more correct. The Pri Megadim says she should always say ner, because the mitzvah is fulfilled with just one light. In this article filed on Shabbos 23, the Mishnah Berurah adds that someone with very little money should light only one and spend the rest on Shabbos food.
shabbos/lehadlik-ner-shel-shabbos-wordin.description: Why does the blessing on Shabbos candles say ner, in the singular, even when many lights are lit? The Pri Megadim explains, in an article on Shabbos 23.

shabbos/lending-an-animal-to-a-non-jew.intro: An owner may not rent or lend his bull to a non-Jew who does not keep Shabbos, since the animal stays his and its work would make him violate a Torah prohibition. The mishnah on Avodah Zarah 14b goes further and forbids even selling a large work animal to such a person, lest people think renting is allowed too. The Reishis Bikkurim adds that owning such an animal may itself be a mitzvah, like buying chametz to burn.
shabbos/lending-an-animal-to-a-non-jew.description: Why may one not rent, lend or even sell a work animal to a non-Jew who works on Shabbos? The mishnah on Avodah Zarah 14b explains the rabbinic ban.

shabbos/magna-tiles-on-shabbos.intro: A Shabbos newsletter shocked families by forbidding Magna-Tiles, since building with them can form an ohel arai. In [Building Blocks of Halachah](/daf/eruvin/101/building-blocks-of-halachah), on Eruvin 101a, the problem arises with a roof of a four-inch tile. Following Tosfos and the Rema, a structure whose inside will not be used may be fine, and placing the roof first also helps.
shabbos/magna-tiles-on-shabbos.description: May children build with Magna-Tiles on Shabbos? The ban on a temporary ohel, tile sizes and the Rema's view on using the hollow space, from Eruvin 101a.

shabbos/oneg-shabbos-as-a-torah-mitzvah.intro: Rebbe Yannai feared his weekly gift of fruit would arrive too late to tithe before Shabbos, so he designated terumah and maaser for it in advance. Rebbe Chiya assured him on Yevamos 93a that the Torah allows such leniencies for oneg Shabbos. The Rashba says oneg Shabbos is a Torah mitzvah, and the Siddur Rashash suggests saying so aloud while enjoying Shabbos food.
shabbos/oneg-shabbos-as-a-torah-mitzvah.description: Is oneg Shabbos a Torah mitzvah? The Rashba's view, Rebbe Yannai's tithing leniency for Shabbos fruit, and the Siddur Rashash, from Yevamos 93a.

shabbos/personally-preparing-for-shabbos.intro: The Shulchan Aruch rarely tells stories, yet when it rules that everyone should prepare for Shabbos personally, it lists Rav Chisda cutting vegetables and Rav Zeira kindling the fire. Even a great sage may not say it is beneath him. In [Holy Cows](/daf/makkos/19/holy-cows), filed on Makkos 19, the Mishnah Berurah adds that doing it oneself is a bigger mitzvah than using an agent.
shabbos/personally-preparing-for-shabbos.description: Must even great scholars take part in Shabbos preparations themselves? The Shulchan Aruch and the Mishnah Berurah, from an article filed on Makkos 19.

shabbos/pets-and-electricity-on-shabbos.intro: May a trained dog turn on a light for its owner on Shabbos? For a Jew, switching on an incandescent bulb is a Biblical prohibition according to most poskim, but some poskim suggest a dog doing it on its own may be permitted. Telling the dog to do it is certainly forbidden, and Rav Shlomo Zalman rules that a pet playing on its own need not be stopped, in a discussion that grows from Avodah Zarah 14b.
shabbos/pets-and-electricity-on-shabbos.description: May a trained dog turn on a light on Shabbos? What poskim say about pets, v'dabeir davar, and pets playing on their own, growing from Avodah Zarah 14b.

shabbos/picking-ripe-fruit-on-shabbos.intro: In Shevuos 42b, Rebbe Meir holds that grapes ready for harvest are treated as if already picked. Does that mean he would allow picking ripe fruit on Shabbos? Tosfos says no, because the melachos follow the work of the Mishkan, and the plants for its dyes were surely picked when fully ripe, so all agree that even ripe fruit may not be picked.
shabbos/picking-ripe-fruit-on-shabbos.description: May ripe fruit be picked on Shabbos if Rebbe Meir treats it as already picked? Tosfos says no, based on the Mishkan, in the discussion on Shevuos 42b.

shabbos/playing-ball-on-shabbos.intro: Playing baseball on Shabbos is a weekday activity and a public disgrace to the day. [One, Two, Three Years You're Out At The Old Ball Game](/daf/bava-metzia/10/one-two-three-years-youre-out-at-the-old-ball-game) also weighs carrying a home run ball out of the stadium and plowing with cleats, set beside Bava Metzia 10a. The Midrash on Eichah tells of a city destroyed for playing ball on Shabbos.
shabbos/playing-ball-on-shabbos.description: What is wrong with playing baseball on Shabbos? Carrying, plowing with cleats and weekday activity are weighed in an article on Bava Metzia 10a.

shabbos/preparing-for-shabbos-personally.intro: The Shulchan Aruch urges everyone to rise early on Friday and prepare for Shabbos personally, even with household help. Rav Chisda chopped vegetables, Rabah and Rav Yosef split wood, and Rabbi Zeira kindled the fire. In [Raising the Steaks: Why the Nasi Bought the Cow](/daf/makkos/14/raising-the-steaks-why-the-nasi-bought-the-cow), tied to Makkos 14a, this follows the principle that a mitzvah done oneself is greater than through a messenger.
shabbos/preparing-for-shabbos-personally.description: Why should one prepare for Shabbos personally even with help at home? The Shulchan Aruch and the example of the Amoraim, in a piece on Makkos 14a.

shabbos/psik-reisha-on-shabbos.intro: When an action will surely cause an unintended melachah, it is a psik reisha and forbidden on Shabbos. What if the result is only possible? The Taz allows closing a cabinet that may hold mosquitoes, and the Mishnah Berurah agrees only because trapping pests is rabbinic, in the article on Kesubos 6.
shabbos/psik-reisha-on-shabbos.description: Is an action with an inevitable forbidden result allowed on Shabbos? Psik reisha, the Taz and the Mishnah Berurah on uncertain outcomes, from Kesubos 6.

shabbos/sending-messages-on-shabbos-for-.intro: One Shabbos, a rider came into Brody to ask the Belzer Rebbe to daven for a critically sick man, and Rav Shlomo Kluger was shocked. The Rebbe's son-in-law pointed to Bava Basra 156b, which allows a kinyan on Shabbos to ease a dying person's mind. The Mordechai and Shulchan Aruch allow hiring a gentile to tell the relatives, and some go further still.
shabbos/sending-messages-on-shabbos-for-.description: May one send a message on Shabbos to calm a critically ill patient? From Bava Basra 156b, the Mordechai and others on informing relatives or a rebbe.

shabbos/serving-legal-papers-on-shabbos.intro: New York law forbids serving court papers on a defendant's Sabbath. In [Rabbeinu Tam & the Lawsuit](/daf/pesachim/94/rabbeinu-tam-the-lawsuit), a frum couple was served at 5:30 p.m., after the common 50-minute end of Shabbos, and argued that they keep Rabbeinu Tam. Judge Johnny Lee Baynes agreed and dismissed the case, a modern twist on a debate rooted in Tosfos on Pesachim 94a.
shabbos/serving-legal-papers-on-shabbos.description: A frum couple served court papers after 50 minutes but before Rabbeinu Tam's time won their New York case. The Shabbos zman behind it is in Pesachim 94a.

shabbos/seudah-shlishis-halacha.intro: The Shulchan Aruch urges care with the third Shabbos meal, which can be fulfilled with an egg-sized piece of bread even when full. It also allows splitting a long second meal after midday by bentching and washing again. In [Eat but Don’t Overeat](/daf/gittin/70/eat-but-dont-overeat), on Gittin 70a, the Rema prefers eating after Mincha, and a pause to daven early may satisfy both concerns.
shabbos/seudah-shlishis-halacha.description: How much bread does seudah shlishis need, and can you split the second meal? The Shulchan Aruch and the Rema on the third meal, in a piece on Gittin 70a.

shabbos/several-women-lighting-shabbos-c.intro: When several families light Shabbos candles in one place, may each say the bracha? The Shulchan Aruch prefers that only one bless, while the Rema says the custom is for all to bless, since more candles add light. Electric lights raise a new question, and the Minchas Asher answers from Sanhedrin 32b that candles bring joy even when not needed for light.
shabbos/several-women-lighting-shabbos-c.description: May several women each say the bracha when lighting Shabbos candles in one place? The Shulchan Aruch, the Rema and the Minchas Asher on Sanhedrin 32b.

shabbos/shabbos-candles-burning-into-sha.intro: Rebbe Yochanan holds that a person's fire is like his arrow, so everything it burns is counted as lit by him. If so, asks the Nemukei Yosef, how can candles lit before Shabbos keep burning into Shabbos? [We Need To Start The Fire](/daf/bava-kamma/60/we-need-to-start-the-fire) explains his answer from Bava Kamma 60b: all the burning is counted at the moment of lighting, before Shabbos began.
shabbos/shabbos-candles-burning-into-sha.description: If every moment a fire burns counts as new lighting, how can Shabbos candles burn on Shabbos? The Nemukei Yosef answers, based on Bava Kamma 60b.

shabbos/shabbos-clothes-on-shabbos-chazo.intro: On Shabbos Chazon, the Shabbos before Tishah B'Av, should one wear Shabbos clothes? The Rema writes that weekday clothing is worn that Shabbos. [Shabbos In Disguise](/daf/bava-kamma/37/shabbos-in-disguise), written for that week and filed on Bava Kamma 37a, notes that our minhag today is to wear Shabbos clothes even on Shabbos Chazon.
shabbos/shabbos-clothes-on-shabbos-chazo.description: Do we wear Shabbos clothes on Shabbos Chazon before Tishah B'Av? The Rema says weekday clothes, but our minhag differs. A note filed on Bava Kamma 37a.

shabbos/shabbos-goy.intro: Many believe that hinting to a Shabbos goy removes every problem, but the article on Pesachim 52 explains otherwise. One may not ask a gentile directly to do melacha, and even after hinting, one may not directly benefit from the work done for him. Turning off a light so one can sleep removes an obstacle and is fine, but lighting a dark room to read is not, unless there was already enough light.
shabbos/shabbos-goy.description: Does hinting to a Shabbos goy solve everything? Why you still may not benefit directly from his melacha, with cases of lights and reading. Pesachim 52.

shabbos/shabbos-raffles-for-children.intro: Is the prize raffle at a Shabbos afternoon learning program allowed? Rav Yitzchak Berkowitz said he knew of no heter, while Rabbi Rosenberg of Kollel Zichron Chaim permits it for a mitzvah of that day, but advises that the child not acquire the prize until after Shabbos. [The Shabbos Afternoon Showdown: Raffles, Bungalows, and the Kohen Gadol](/daf/yoma/32/the-shabbos-afternoon-showdown-raffles-bungalows-and-the-kohen-gadol) on Yoma 32 adds an idea: announce that the raffle is only advisory.
shabbos/shabbos-raffles-for-children.description: May a raffle be held at a Shabbos learning program? Rav Yitzchak Berkowitz, Rabbi Rosenberg, and an advisory-raffle idea, in a look at Yoma 32.

shabbos/shehiya-and-half-cooked-food.intro: Shehiya is the rabbinic ban on leaving food on a fire when Shabbos begins, because one might stoke the coals, and Shabbos 36b gives two fixes: remove the coals or cover them with ashes. The Shulchan Aruch adds a second opinion that food already half cooked may stay on the fire. The Rema, the Kaf HaChaim and the Chazon Ish follow it, though the Mishna Berura advises caution.
shabbos/shehiya-and-half-cooked-food.description: Shehiya forbids leaving food on a fire as Shabbos begins, but half-cooked food may be different. The Shulchan Aruch and Rema, building on Shabbos 36b.

shabbos/shtreimel-and-hat-on-shabbos.intro: The Rema says a person should not go out on Shabbos the same way he does during the week, but should have something that reminds him it is Shabbos. Rav Eliyahu Fisher says a businessman who wears suits all week is not reminded by a nicer suit, so he should wear a shtreimel, or a fedora if he wears no hat all week. He finds support in the Yerushalmi that Tosfos brings on Bava Kamma 37a.
shabbos/shtreimel-and-hat-on-shabbos.description: Why wear a shtreimel or fedora on Shabbos if you dress formally all week? Rav Eliyahu Fisher reads the Rema this way, with support from Bava Kamma 37a.

shabbos/stacking-items-on-shabbos.intro: Everyone stacks challah rolls and sefarim on Shabbos, so why does Eruvin 101a forbid stacking barrels or eggs with a hollow space beneath? Tosfos explains that an ohel arai is a problem only when one wants the space created. Barrels and eggs were stacked to let air flow and keep them fresh, while no one cares about the gaps between sefarim, and the Rema codifies this.
shabbos/stacking-items-on-shabbos.description: When does stacking eggs, barrels, rolls or sefarim on Shabbos create a forbidden ohel? Tosfos and the Rema on wanting the hollow space, from Eruvin 101a.

shabbos/stitches-on-shabbos.intro: Many people assume that a cut that needs stitches allows breaking Shabbos, out of a remote fear of infection. One contemporary posek objects, noting that people often bandage a cut and delay treatment for insurance reasons. Another posek seems to permit it, and the article on Kesubos 39a suggests the two may not disagree, since it depends on how deep the cut is.
shabbos/stitches-on-shabbos.description: Does a cut that may need stitches justify going to the hospital on Shabbos? Two poskim differ, and the depth of the cut may decide it, from Kesubos 39a.

shabbos/taking-attendance-on-shabbos.intro: A yeshiva marked Shabbos attendance by covering names with bobby pins, and a bachur argued this was forbidden, since the usual way is by writing and one might come to write. The mashgiach sent the question to a renowned posek. As [Chapter And Verse](/daf/yoma/37/chapter-and-verse) on Yoma 37a recounts, the posek agreed with the logic but allowed it for a mitzvah purpose, since a record improves attendance at seder.
shabbos/taking-attendance-on-shabbos.description: May a yeshiva take attendance on Shabbos with pins instead of writing? A posek's ruling on the concern of coming to write, from a story tied to Yoma 37a.

shabbos/talking-business-on-shabbos.intro: A pasuk in Yeshayahu teaches that one should not pursue business on Shabbos, even by strolling through a house under construction to check the work. Rashi reads v'dabeir davar as a ban on business talk, and Rabbeinu Tam asks why a second source is needed. In a discussion filed on Kiddushin 31, the Bach explains that business actions and business speech are both forbidden, each from its own verse.
shabbos/talking-business-on-shabbos.description: Why is discussing business forbidden on Shabbos? Rashi, Rabbeinu Tam and the Bach on two phrases in Yeshayahu, in an article filed on Kiddushin 31.

shabbos/tasting-shabbos-food-on-friday.intro: There is a custom to taste the Shabbos food on Friday, based on the phrase toameh chayim zachu. In [Taster’s Choice](/daf/menachos/103/tasters-choice), filed on Menachos 103b, a husband caught sampling his wife's cooking is advised to quote it. Still, the real purpose is to check whether the food needs more salt or spices, not just to satisfy one's appetite.
shabbos/tasting-shabbos-food-on-friday.description: Why do people taste the Shabbos food on Friday? The phrase toameh chayim zachu and its real purpose, from a lighthearted article filed on Menachos 103b.

shabbos/tearing-letters-on-wrappers-on-s.intro: Opening a sugar packet on Shabbos may rip through printed letters. The Noda B'Yehuda says there is no concern, since tearing the letters is unintended and not true erasing. The Mishnah Berurah permits it only when ripping the letters is not certain, and he allows breaking a tea biscuit with letters baked in, as the article on Menachos 94b explains.
shabbos/tearing-letters-on-wrappers-on-s.description: May one open a sugar packet or wrapper on Shabbos if it may tear printed letters? The Noda B'Yehuda and Mishnah Berurah, in an article on Menachos 94b.

shabbos/transition-lenses-on-shabbos.intro: Rebbetzin Leah Auerbach was caught between her father, Rav Elyashiv, who advised against photochromic lenses on Shabbos, and her father-in-law, Rav Shlomo Zalman, who permitted them. Rav Shlomo Zalman reasons that the wearer does nothing, as the sun darkens the lenses, but the Orchos Shabbos compares Sanhedrin 77a, where one who ties a person in the sun is liable. [A Pair of Glasses, a Spoon, and a Bottle of Beer Walk Into a Halachic Debate](/daf/sanhedrin/77/a-pair-of-glasses-a-spoon-and-a-bottle-of-beer-walk-into-a-halachic-debate) shows most poskim permit them.
shabbos/transition-lenses-on-shabbos.description: May you wear transition lenses on Shabbos? Rav Moshe Feinstein and Rav Shlomo Zalman permit them; the Orchos Shabbos raises Sanhedrin 77a on causing harm.

shabbos/trapping-insects-on-shabbos.intro: May you close a cabinet door on Shabbos if mosquitoes might be inside? The Taz says yes, without even checking, since trapping is not certain to happen. The Mishnah Berurah objects, yet agrees in the end, since trapping creatures only because they are a nuisance is rabbinic, and a doubt in a rabbinic law is lenient, as explained on Kesubos 6.
shabbos/trapping-insects-on-shabbos.description: Is closing a cabinet that might hold mosquitoes forbidden trapping on Shabbos? The Taz and the Mishnah Berurah both allow it, in an article on Kesubos 6.

shabbos/unclogging-a-toilet-on-shabbos.intro: The Kovetz Halachos and the Be'er Moshe allow using a plunger on Shabbos, while Rav Shlomo Zalman and the Minchas Yitzchak permit it only in great need. Rav Moshe Feinstein's answer depends on how often the drain clogs. In [Draining the Swamp](/daf/kesubos/60/draining-the-swamp), on Kesubos 60a, these views are compared with the Gemara's clogged gutter.
shabbos/unclogging-a-toilet-on-shabbos.description: May you use a plunger on a clogged toilet or sink on Shabbos? The Kovetz Halachos, Rav Shlomo Zalman and Rav Moshe Feinstein, compared with Kesubos 60a.

shabbos/using-a-crockpot-on-shabbos.intro: Leaving cholent in a crockpot over Shabbos raises two rabbinic issues, hatmana and shehiya, both from the fear that one might stoke the coals. Rav Shlomo Zalman held that hatmana can happen in the crockpot itself, while others disagreed. The old fixes of Shabbos 36b don't fit a crockpot, so the poskim had to find new answers.
shabbos/using-a-crockpot-on-shabbos.description: Can cholent sit in a crockpot over Shabbos? The issues of hatmana and shehiya, Rav Shlomo Zalman's view, and how Shabbos 36b applies to a slow cooker.

shabbos/wearing-special-clothes-on-shabb.intro: The Shulchan Aruch says to make an effort to have nice clothes for Shabbos, and the Gra changed every garment, even his belt. Elsewhere the Rema says to go out on Shabbos with something that reminds you of the day. Rav Eliyahu Fisher explains these as two reasons, honoring Shabbos and remembering it, and draws on the Yerushalmi about the ox on Bava Kamma 37a.
shabbos/wearing-special-clothes-on-shabb.description: Why dress differently on Shabbos? To honor the day, and also to remind yourself it is Shabbos, as Rav Eliyahu Fisher explains, drawing on Bava Kamma 37a.

shabbos/writing-acronyms-on-shabbos.intro: Writing two letters on Shabbos is the full melacha of kesivah, but what about one letter that stands for a whole number, like a mem for forty? In Shabbos 104b, Rebbe Yehoshua ben Besaira and the chachamim argue, and the Mishnah Berurah follows the chachamim. Tosfos seems to say even a three-letter acronym is less severe, but other Rishonim disagree.
shabbos/writing-acronyms-on-shabbos.description: Is writing an acronym or one letter that stands for a word the full melacha of writing on Shabbos? The Mishnah in Shabbos 104b and Tosfos weigh in.

muktzeh/are-pets-muktzeh.intro: Tosfos on Bava Metzia 46b says a cow can serve for kinyan chalipin, since animals with set uses count as utensils. Rav Yaakov Hagiz learned from this that a singing bird is not muktzeh. In [Are Pets Muktzeh?](/daf/bava-metzia/46/are-pets-muktzeh), Rav Moshe Feinstein's Dibros Moshe explains that an animal designated as a pet is not muktzeh, though other poskim disagree.
muktzeh/are-pets-muktzeh.description: Are pets muktzeh on Shabbos? Rav Yaakov Hagiz uses Tosfos on Bava Metzia 46b to permit a singing bird, and Rav Moshe's view on pets is debated.

muktzeh/is-a-get-muktzeh-on-shabbos.intro: A dying man wanted to give his wife a get on Shabbos, but Tosfos says he could not touch it, since a get is muktzeh. Why, if it has a use? The Rosh explains it resembled written oral law, which was once forbidden to write, and the Smag argues that now that oral law may be written, a get should no longer be muktzeh, as the article on Gittin 77 explains.
muktzeh/is-a-get-muktzeh-on-shabbos.description: Why was a get muktzeh on Shabbos, and is it still? The Rosh links it to the old ban on writing oral law, and the Smag disagrees, in a piece on Gittin 77.

muktzeh/moving-a-trapped-animal-on-shabb.intro: Animals are muktzeh on Shabbos, but what if one is trapped without food and the only way to help is to lift it? Concern for an animal's pain, tza'ar ba'alei chayim, comes from the Torah. In a discussion based on Shabbos 109, the Mishnah Berurah records a machlokes, the Az Nidberu reads him as lenient, and the Chayei Adam allows relying on the lenient view.
muktzeh/moving-a-trapped-animal-on-shabb.description: May you lift a trapped, suffering animal on Shabbos though it is muktzeh? The Mishnah Berurah and Chayei Adam on tza'ar ba'alei chayim, from Shabbos 109.

muktzeh/moving-muktzeh-on-yom-tov-for-fo.intro: Ashes from wood burned on Yom Tov are muktzeh, yet in Tosfos's day people cleared them from ovens to bake. Tosfos, discussing Beitzah 8b, suggests that muktzeh may be moved on Yom Tov for food and festival enjoyment, as the Rema rules. The Magen Avraham adds a major limit: you may move the item, but you may not actually use it.
muktzeh/moving-muktzeh-on-yom-tov-for-fo.description: May muktzeh be moved on Yom Tov to reach food? Tosfos says yes, the Rema agrees, and the Magen Avraham limits it to moving, not using. Beitzah 8b.

muktzeh/rocks-and-sand-as-muktzeh.intro: A rock has no use when Shabbos begins, so it is muktzeh, unless it was set aside beforehand as a doorstop or played with as a toy. In [Why Your Pet Rock is Not Muktzeh](/daf/beitzah/8/why-your-pet-rock-is-not-muktzeh), Beitzah 8b shows Rava allowing a pile of dirt to be designated before Shabbos for covering a child's accident on an earthen floor.
muktzeh/rocks-and-sand-as-muktzeh.description: Are rocks, sand and dirt muktzeh on Shabbos? Rava allows dirt designated beforehand for use, and a pet rock counts as a toy. Learn more from Beitzah 8b.

muktzeh/saving-baby-fish-on-shabbos.intro: Baby fish hatch in an aquarium on Shabbos, and the adult fish are ready to eat them, so may you move them to another tank though they are muktzeh? HaRav Shlomo Zalman doubts it, since small fish being eaten is just nature, not pain. [Calling Doctor Dolittle](/daf/shabbos/109/calling-doctor-dolittle), filed on Shabbos 109, notes he may allow it if someone put them in the wrong tank by mistake.
muktzeh/saving-baby-fish-on-shabbos.description: May newly hatched fish be moved to another tank on Shabbos so the adults don't eat them? HaRav Shlomo Zalman's view, in a discussion based on Shabbos 109.

muktzeh/seeing-eye-dog-on-shabbos.intro: Animals are usually muktzeh because they are not set aside for a permitted use. A guide dog is different: Rav Shlomo Zalman writes that a seeing-eye dog, designated by its nature for a permitted Shabbos use, is not muktzeh. His ruling supports Rav Moshe Feinstein's view on pets, in an article built on Tosfos on Bava Metzia 46b.
muktzeh/seeing-eye-dog-on-shabbos.description: Is a seeing-eye dog muktzeh on Shabbos? Rav Shlomo Zalman says no, since it is designated for a permitted use, in an article on Bava Metzia 46b.

eruv/carrying-on-yom-tov-without-an-eruv.intro: Many think one may carry freely on yom tov, but where there is no eiruv there are real limits. One should not carry extra keys he does not need, nor even his house key if he can get in another way, and some poskim forbid carrying Tylenol or Advil. [A Drive-Thru Eiruv](/daf/moed-katan/13/a-drive-thru-eiruv), on Moed Katan 13a, notes that even the Shevet HaLevi agrees about yom tov.
eruv/carrying-on-yom-tov-without-an-eruv.description: What may one carry on yom tov where there is no eruv? Extra keys, a house key and medicine, in an article on Moed Katan 13a that clears up a misconception.

eruv/eruv-chatzeiros-beracha.intro: A radio trivia question once asked which berachah is said only on a Wednesday or Thursday, and the answer given was eruv tavshilin. But the same berachah is recited on an eruv chatzeiros, and the article on Pesachim 46 explains this is no accident. An eruv chatzeiros reminds us that only carrying between private domains is permitted, just as the eruv tavshilin reminds us that only cooking for Shabbos is allowed.
eruv/eruv-chatzeiros-beracha.description: Why is the bracha on an eruv chatzeiros the same as on an eruv tavshilin? Both remind us of what stays forbidden, as explained on Pesachim 46.

eruv/eruv-chatzeiros-in-apartment-buildi.intro: Where there is no community eruv, residents of a building can still carry into shared hallways and other apartments through an eruv chatzeiros. Rebbe Yehoshua requires each resident who contributes to give a whole loaf, so neighbors will not quarrel over who gave less. In [Something To Pick At](/daf/eruvin/81/something-to-pick-at), on Eruvin 81, Rav Chisda allows a torn loaf joined with toothpicks.
eruv/eruv-chatzeiros-in-apartment-buildi.description: How can apartment residents carry into shared hallways on Shabbos without a community eruv? The eruv chatzeiros and its whole loaf rule, from Eruvin 81.

eruv/eruv-chatzeiros-with-a-non-jewish-n.intro: An eruv chatzeiros unites the homes around a shared courtyard, with each family giving a bit of bread. What if one home belongs to a non-Jew? Rav Yehudah said in Shmuel's name that a contribution from the non-Jew's tenant is enough, and Rav Nachman praised the teaching, which sets up the debate in the article on Eruvin 64.
eruv/eruv-chatzeiros-with-a-non-jewish-n.description: How does an eruv chatzeiros work when one home in the courtyard belongs to a non-Jew? Shmuel lets his tenant contribute, in the discussion on Eruvin 64.

eruv/mavoi-entrance-rectification.intro: Long ago, several courtyards opened onto a shared alleyway called a mavoi, walled on three sides and open to the street on the fourth. Carrying there on Shabbos requires a fix at that open entrance. The Mishnah discussed on Eruvin 13 records a debate over whether Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argued about entrances under four amos wide or only wider ones.
eruv/mavoi-entrance-rectification.description: What must be done to the open side of a mavoi before carrying on Shabbos? Beis Shammai, Beis Hillel and the four amos width, from the Mishnah on Eruvin 13.

eruv/measuring-the-techum-of-a-city.intro: On Shabbos one may walk 2,000 amos past the outskirts of a city, but where does the measuring begin if the city is not a perfect square? The Mishnah in Eruvin 53 squares off the city with a straight line past its outermost part. Rav and Shmuel even argue over how to spell the Mishnah's word for this, comparing the outskirts to a fetus or to limbs.
eruv/measuring-the-techum-of-a-city.description: How is a city squared off before measuring its Shabbos techum of 2,000 amos? The Mishnah in Eruvin 53 and the spelling debate between Rav and Shmuel.

eruv/whole-loaves-for-eruv-chatzeiros.intro: For an eruv chatzeiros, each resident once gave bread, and it had to be a whole loaf, so even one half-loaf made the eruv invalid. Rav Chisda teaches in Eruvin 61a that two pieces fastened with toothpicks may count. The Panim Meiros explains this as a special leniency to prevent resentment between neighbors, since today a box of matzah is usually used instead.
eruv/whole-loaves-for-eruv-chatzeiros.description: Why did eruv chatzeiros bread have to be whole loaves? Rav Chisda's toothpick rule in Eruvin 61a and the Panim Meiros on avoiding fights between neighbors.

yom-tov/carrying-on-chol-hamoed.intro: Melachah on chol ha'moed is allowed only for five kinds of needs, and the Chazon Ish held that carrying is included, so he checked his pockets before going out. The Shevet HaLevi disagrees, proving from the Nemukei Yosef on the Mishnah in Moed Katan 13a that hotza'ah does not apply on chol ha'moed. The Meiri says so clearly, and the common custom is to be lenient.
yom-tov/carrying-on-chol-hamoed.description: Does the ban on carrying apply on Chol HaMoed? The Chazon Ish checked his pockets, while the Shevet HaLevi and Meiri say no, from Moed Katan 13a.

yom-tov/cooking-on-yom-tov-for-a-weekday.intro: Cooking is permitted on Yom Tov when it provides food for Yom Tov itself. According to Rav Chisda on Pesachim 46, cooking on Yom Tov for a weekday is a biblical violation. Rabbah disagrees, reasoning that uninvited guests might always show up and eat the extra food, as the author learned when six boys arrived for a Shabbos meal, so the cooking counts as for Yom Tov and the ban is only rabbinic.
yom-tov/cooking-on-yom-tov-for-a-weekday.description: Is cooking on Yom Tov for a later weekday a Torah or rabbinic ban? Rav Chisda and Rabbah debate it in Pesachim 46, with the uninvited guests logic.

yom-tov/cooking-on-yom-tov-for-shabbos.intro: Cooking on Yom Tov for the Shabbos that follows raises a timing question when the food will only be ready near sunset. According to Rabbah on Pesachim 46, that would be forbidden, while Rav Chisda allows it once an eruv tavshilin is made, and [What’s Cooking?](/daf/pesachim/46/whats-cooking) explains why the Mishnah Berurah urges finishing early, allowing leniency only in case of need.
yom-tov/cooking-on-yom-tov-for-shabbos.description: How late on Yom Tov may you cook for the Shabbos that follows? Rabbah and Rav Chisda in Pesachim 46, and the Mishnah Berurah's advice to finish early.

yom-tov/eruv-tavshilin.intro: Before a Yom Tov that falls on Friday, one sets aside a cooked food and a baked food, the eruv tavshilin, so the household may cook for Shabbos. Rav Chisda on Pesachim 46 explains that cooking for Shabbos is biblically allowed, since Yom Tov and Shabbos are one unit of sanctity, but the rabbis feared it would look like cooking for another day. The eruv shows that Shabbos preparations began before Yom Tov.
yom-tov/eruv-tavshilin.description: What does an eruv tavshilin do? Why setting aside two foods before Yom Tov permits cooking for Shabbos, according to Rav Chisda on Pesachim 46.

yom-tov/fasting-on-chol-hamoed.intro: Is fasting on Chol HaMoed forbidden by the Torah or only by the Rabbis? While the Beis Yosef cites an opinion that it is a Torah prohibition, Megillah 16a shows Mordechai fasting on the 16th of Nissan, Chol HaMoed by Torah law, yet the Gemara never says the fast overrode that ban. The Rosh Yosef concludes that Rashi holds fasting on Chol HaMoed is permitted by the Torah.
yom-tov/fasting-on-chol-hamoed.description: Is fasting on Chol HaMoed forbidden by the Torah or only by the Rabbis? Mordechai's fast on the 16th of Nissan and Rashi's view, from Megillah 16a.

yom-tov/haircut-before-yom-tov.intro: The Shulchan Aruch writes that there is a mitzvah to get a haircut on erev yom tov. The Pri Megadim is unsure if this means looking one's best in honor of yom tov, or only cutting hair that is overgrown. Since haircuts are forbidden on chol ha'moed, [Haircuts on Chol Hamoed](/daf/nazir/38/haircuts-on-chol-hamoed), filed on Nazir 38, shows why the day before matters.
yom-tov/haircut-before-yom-tov.description: Is there a mitzvah to get a haircut before yom tov, and what exactly does it require? The Shulchan Aruch and Pri Megadim, in an article on Nazir 38.

yom-tov/learning-yom-tov-laws-thirty-day.intro: The Shulchan Aruch says we discuss the laws of Pesach thirty days before Pesach, and the Mishna Berura says this applies to every yom tov. The Vilna Gaon says Shavuos needs study only from Rosh Chodesh Sivan, and some say the rule is only for Pesach. All agree, as Megillah 32a teaches, that one should learn each yom tov's laws on the yom tov itself.
yom-tov/learning-yom-tov-laws-thirty-day.description: Should a yom tov's laws be studied for thirty days before it, or only before Pesach? The Mishna Berura, the Vilna Gaon and Megillah 32a weigh in.

yom-tov/measuring-flour-on-yom-tov.intro: May flour be measured exactly on Yom Tov for baking? Shmuel says no, though spices may be measured, since a small mistake can ruin a dish while flour can be a bit off. Abaye explains on Beitzah 28a that it is really permitted but not taught, and Tosfos says that today all agree flour is not measured.
yom-tov/measuring-flour-on-yom-tov.description: May flour be measured exactly on Yom Tov, though spices may be? Shmuel, Abaye and Tosfos explain a rule that is permitted but not taught, Beitzah 28a.

yom-tov/melacha-on-chol-hamoed.intro: Is the ban on melacha during Chol HaMoed from the Torah or from the Rabbanan? Chagigah 18a seems to say Torah, but Rabbeinu Tam calls the pesukim mere hints and asks why work is allowed to prevent a loss. The Ramban takes a middle path, and the Biur Halacha says to rely on the lenient view only in great need.
yom-tov/melacha-on-chol-hamoed.description: Is work on Chol HaMoed forbidden by the Torah or the Rabbanan? Rabbeinu Tam, the Ramban and the Biur Halacha on festival labor. Learn it from Chagigah 18a.

yom-tov/shaping-food-on-shabbos-and-yom-.intro: Beitzah 28a forbids making a handle in a piece of meat on Yom Tov, but Rabbah bar Rav Huna cut his meat into triangles. The Mishnah Berurah says a meaningful shape or letter may not be carved, so no watermelon birds. In [Of Gefilte Fish Balls and Trees on Cakes](/daf/beitzah/28/of-gefilte-fish-balls-and-trees-on-cakes), round gefilte fish balls are fine, and cake letters may be bitten but not cut.
yom-tov/shaping-food-on-shabbos-and-yom-.description: May food be carved into shapes on Shabbos and Yom Tov? Triangles and balls are fine, but birds and letters are not, based on the Gemara in Beitzah 28a.

yom-tov/sharpening-a-knife-on-yom-tov.intro: Rava was seen rubbing a knife on a utensil on Yom Tov, and when asked, said he was only cleaning it. Beitzah 28a tells the same of Rabbah with Abaye. In [Can You Keep A Secret?](/daf/beitzah/28/can-you-keep-a-secret), Rashi explains that sharpening is allowed only in a specific case, and people might wrongly permit it everywhere and break a Torah law.
yom-tov/sharpening-a-knife-on-yom-tov.description: May a knife be sharpened on Yom Tov? Rava and Rabbah did it quietly but would not say so, as Beitzah 28a explains, to keep others from erring.

yom-tov/shehecheyanu-on-the-last-days-of.intro: The second days of Pesach are the only nights of yom tov when Kiddush is said without Shehechiyanu. The last days are a continuation and conclusion of the yom tov that already began with Shehechiyanu, while Shemini Atzeres counts as a new yom tov with its own. [Shehechiyanu and Kiddush on Yom Tov: A Deeper Look](/daf/menachos/75/shehechiyanu-and-kiddush-on-yom-tov-a-deeper-look) starts here, on Menachos 75b.
yom-tov/shehecheyanu-on-the-last-days-of.description: Why is Kiddush on the last days of Pesach said without Shehechiyanu, while Shemini Atzeres gets its own? The answer, in an article on Menachos 75b.

yom-tov/yom-tov-sheni-for-visitors-to-is.intro: An American keeps two days of Yom Tov even in Eretz Yisrael, but status can change fast. The Chazon Ish ruled that the moment a visitor decides to settle permanently, he becomes a resident and may need to make havdalah. Rav Moshe Feinstein ruled that an Israeli wife planning to move abroad still keeps one day, building on Rebbe Zaira's move in Chullin 18b.
yom-tov/yom-tov-sheni-for-visitors-to-is.description: How do visitors to Eretz Yisrael keep Yom Tov Sheni? The Chazon Ish and Rav Moshe Feinstein on residency, with Rebbe Zaira's story from Chullin 18b.

pesach/afikomen-before-chatzos.intro: Why do many rush to eat matzah and the afikomen before chatzos on Seder night? Rabbi Akiva says the Korban Pesach may be eaten all night, while Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah says only until midnight. Rava ties the matzah to the Korban Pesach, so the Mishnah Berurah and Shulchan Aruch say to finish before chatzos, in a Seder dialogue built on Zevachim 56b.
pesach/afikomen-before-chatzos.description: Why rush to eat matzah and the afikomen before chatzos on Seder night? The Korban Pesach deadline in Zevachim 56b, and the Mishnah Berurah's ruling.

pesach/afikomen-in-memory-of-korban-pesa.intro: The Bnei Yissaschar explains that the matzah before the meal fulfills the mitzvah of matzah, while the afikomen after the meal recalls the Korban Pesach, which was not eaten on an empty stomach. Yet the article on Pesachim 61a adds a surprising point: one should still be somewhat hungry when eating the afikomen. Eating it on a full stomach does not fulfill the mitzvah in the choicest way.
pesach/afikomen-in-memory-of-korban-pesa.description: Why is the afikomen eaten after the meal, and how full should you be? The Bnei Yissaschar links it to the Korban Pesach, discussed on Pesachim 61a.

pesach/are-peanuts-kitniyos.intro: Shimon is munching Cracker Jack on Erev Pesach, and Boruch is horrified. Shimon answers that Rav Moshe Feinstein wrote peanuts are not kitniyos and may be eaten where no custom forbids them. On pumpkin seeds, Rav Moshe and Rav Shlomo Zalman Auerbach disagree, in a dialogue that runs through Pesachim 35a and Zevachim 48b.
pesach/are-peanuts-kitniyos.description: Are peanuts or pumpkin seeds kitniyos on Pesach? Rav Moshe Feinstein and Rav Shlomo Zalman disagree, in a dialogue tied to Pesachim 35a and Zevachim 48b.

pesach/bedikas-chametz-in-a-large-house.intro: How long should bedikas chametz take? When the Chazon Ish heard the Steipler searched all night, he ruled that floors need checking only for a kezayis of chametz, and that places sold on the 13th need no search. Rav Chaim Kanievsky still emptied many drawers, then asked his grandson to put everything back, since the bedikah is only d'rabbanan while causing distress to his wife is a Torah violation.
pesach/bedikas-chametz-in-a-large-house.description: How the Chazon Ish shortened bedikas chametz, and why Rav Chaim Kanievsky worried about large American houses and asked that the drawers be put back.

pesach/borrowing-chametz-before-pesach.intro: Someone lends his friend bagels just before the time to stop eating chametz, when the lender would have thrown them out anyway. Must the borrower pay him back after Pesach? Based on Avodah Zarah 62, the Shulchan Aruch rules that he must, since the bread had value when it was borrowed, and he may even pay its value on Chol HaMoed.
pesach/borrowing-chametz-before-pesach.description: If you borrow bread just before Pesach, must you repay it, though it would have become worthless? The Shulchan Aruch says yes, based on Avodah Zarah 62.

pesach/burning-chametz-with-lighter-flui.intro: Many pour lighter fluid on their chametz before burning it, but if the chametz is now poison, maybe it is no longer chametz and the custom of burning it is lost. In [Dog Foodies](/daf/shabbos/155/dog-foodies), filed on Shabbos 155, the Ohr L'Tzion answers that some dogs will eat it anyway, so burning still counts. He also suggests pouring the fluid on only some of it.
pesach/burning-chametz-with-lighter-flui.description: Does lighter fluid ruin chametz before it burns, so the custom of burning is lost? The Ohr L'Tzion's answer, with a nod to the dogs of Shabbos 155.

pesach/buying-chametz-after-pesach.intro: Even someone who will not rely on mechiras chametz for a Torah prohibition may buy chametz after Pesach from a Jewish store that sold it, since chametz she'avar alav ha'Pesach is a rabbinic ban. Rav Dovid Feinstein was strict even here, yet he bought fresh challos the day after Pesach from a small bakery that had closed for nine days. [Chametz for Sale](/daf/avodah-zarah/63/chametz-for-sale), on Avodah Zarah 63b, explains why.
pesach/buying-chametz-after-pesach.description: May you buy chametz right after Pesach from a store that sold its chametz? The rabbinic ban, Rav Dovid Feinstein's chumrah, and Avodah Zarah 63b.

pesach/chametz-mixed-into-other-foods-on.intro: Kutach haBavli, a Babylonian dip of milk and stale bread, contained real chametz. Yet the Gemara on Pesachim 43 concludes that eating it in the normal way on Pesach does not violate the Torah prohibition. To be liable, one must eat a k'zayis of chametz within k'dei achilas p'ras, anywhere from two to nine minutes by the various opinions, and dipping matzah in kutach never adds up to that much bread in time.
pesach/chametz-mixed-into-other-foods-on.description: Does eating a dip with a little chametz on Pesach break the Torah law? Kutach haBavli in Pesachim 43 and the time limit for eating a k'zayis.

pesach/chametz-stuck-in-a-mixer.intro: What if challah dough is stuck deep in a mixer's cracks where no one can reach it? Bava Metzia 42a says chametz buried under rubble may stay over Pesach, so inaccessible chametz counts as destroyed and bitul is enough. Technically the mixer may be used, as long as no crumbs reach the food, though the Piskei Teshuvos notes that few would actually do so.
pesach/chametz-stuck-in-a-mixer.description: Can a mixer with dough stuck in its cracks be used on Pesach? Hidden chametz is treated like chametz under rubble, as taught in Bava Metzia 42a.

pesach/chametz-unfit-for-a-dog.intro: Chametz must be destroyed or sold unless it is no longer fit for a dog to eat, which sounds easy until you remember that a dog will eat almost anything. The dog Chazal meant is a wild dog with little food, not a spoiled pet who eats only human food. So, as this article filed on Shabbos 155 warns, one should not rush to say a food is no longer chametz.
pesach/chametz-unfit-for-a-dog.description: Chametz no longer fit for a dog need not be destroyed, but dogs eat almost anything. Why that standard is hard to meet, in an article filed on Shabbos 155.

pesach/charoses-ingredients-and-symbolis.intro: According to Rebbe Yochanon, charoses recalls the mortar the Egyptians forced us to use, and its spices recall the straw. Some even added crushed brick, but the Maharam Lonzono was aghast, tracing the custom to a missing letter in the Rashbam on Pesachim 116a that turned charoses into earthenware. The Rashbam really means the charoses should be ground well, neither liquidy nor chunky.
pesach/charoses-ingredients-and-symbolis.description: What does charoses stand for, and how thick should it be? The mortar, the straw and the strange custom of crushed brick, explained on Pesachim 116a.

pesach/cinnamon-sticks-in-charoses.intro: The merchants of Yerushalayim called out for spices for the mitzvah of charoses, and the Rashbam on Pesachim 116a says they recall the straw. The Rema recommends ginger or cinnamon because they resemble straw, and the Steipler Gaon reportedly ground his spices so they would stay long. Rav Dovid Feinstein wrote that ground cinnamon loses the symbolism entirely, and he welcomed the newer availability of cinnamon sticks for Pesach.
pesach/cinnamon-sticks-in-charoses.description: Why are cinnamon sticks better than ground cinnamon in charoses? The spices recall the straw of Egypt, explains the Rashbam on Pesachim 116a.

pesach/cleaning-under-heavy-furniture-fo.intro: Do you have to move the couch to check for chametz? Rav Vozner says no, even if you would move it to find lost jewelry, since Bava Metzia 42a does not require moving rubble. There is one big exception: furniture moved within thirty days of Pesach must be cleaned under, which raises a question about a repairman who moves the fridge.
pesach/cleaning-under-heavy-furniture-fo.description: Must you move heavy furniture to search for chametz? Rav Vozner says no, except items moved within thirty days of Pesach, based on Bava Metzia 42a.

pesach/eating-at-a-sephardi-home-on-pesa.intro: May an Ashkenazi eat at Sephardi in-laws on Pesach when their pots were used for kitniyos? Rav Yitzchok Berkowitz ruled that it is permitted by basic halacha, since the stringency about kitniyos in utensils is a recent one. That does not permit eating the kitniyos itself, notes a dialogue tied to Zevachim 48b.
pesach/eating-at-a-sephardi-home-on-pesa.description: May an Ashkenazi eat at a Sephardi home on Pesach if the dishes were used for kitniyos? Rav Yitzchok Berkowitz's ruling, in a dialogue on Zevachim 48b.

pesach/eating-matzah-on-erev-pesach.intro: Eating matzah on erev Pesach is forbidden by rabbinic decree, and some refrain for 30 days or from Rosh Chodesh Nissan. Based on Pesachim 36a, the Shulchan Aruch rules that the decree does not apply to matzah ashirah like egg matzah, which cannot be used at the Seder, and Rabbeinu Tam ate it on erev Pesach. [Yolk Tales](/daf/pesachim/36/yolk-tales) explains why Ashkenazim still stop eating egg matzah four hours into the day.
pesach/eating-matzah-on-erev-pesach.description: Why is matzah forbidden on erev Pesach but egg matzah allowed? Matzah ashirah in Pesachim 36a, and why Ashkenazim stop eating it four hours in.

pesach/egg-matzah-on-erev-pesach.intro: Eating matzah on Erev Pesach is forbidden by rabbinic decree, but the Shulchan Aruch rules that the decree does not cover matzah ashirah, and Tosafos records that Rabbeinu Tam ate it even after chametz was forbidden. The article on Menachos 57a adds two caveats: the Vilna Gaon reads the Rambam as avoiding it, and Rav Shmuel Kamenetsky says the custom is to follow the Gaon when possible.
pesach/egg-matzah-on-erev-pesach.description: May egg matzah be eaten on Erev Pesach when regular matzah is forbidden? The Shulchan Aruch, Rabbeinu Tam and the Vilna Gaon, from Menachos 57a.

pesach/egg-matzah-on-pesach.intro: Menachos 57a teaches that dough made with fruit juice cannot become chametz, and the Shulchan Aruch includes eggs. Still, egg matzah is matzah ashirah, rich man's bread, so it cannot be used at the Seder. In [The Mysterious Matzah](/daf/menachos/57/the-mysterious-matzah), the Rema's custom to avoid it on Pesach, except for the elderly or ill, gets three explanations.
pesach/egg-matzah-on-pesach.description: Is egg matzah kosher for Pesach, and why do Ashkenazim avoid it? Fruit juice dough, matzah ashirah and the Rema's custom, explained from Menachos 57a.

pesach/egg-on-the-seder-plate.intro: The egg on the Seder plate recalls the Korban Chagigah, so what about a year when erev Pesach falls on Shabbos and no Chagigah would be brought? The Tur cites an opinion to leave it off, but Rabbeinu Peretz says to keep the plate the same. [Eggs and Shank Bones](/daf/pesachim/82/eggs-and-shank-bones) on Pesachim 82 explains his reasoning: dropping the egg would suggest it is a real korban.
pesach/egg-on-the-seder-plate.description: Why is there an egg on the Seder plate, and does it belong there when erev Pesach falls on Shabbos? The Tur and Rabbeinu Peretz, on Pesachim 82.

pesach/flashlight-for-bedikas-chametz.intro: Pesachim 8a gives four reasons not to search for chametz with a torch: it blinds, it flickers, it cannot fit into tight spaces, and it makes the searcher afraid of fire. A flashlight solves all four, so most poskim permit it, and Rav Moshe Feinstein even prefers it. [Sparking Debate](/daf/pesachim/8/sparking-debate) explains why many rabbanim still advise beginning the search with a candle.
pesach/flashlight-for-bedikas-chametz.description: May you search for chametz with a flashlight? Why it solves the problems of Pesachim 8a, why Rav Moshe preferred it, and why many start with a candle.

pesach/forgot-to-do-bedikas-chametz.intro: If someone forgot bedikas chametz on the night of the fourteenth, he must search the moment he remembers, though the Ben Ish Chai lets him daven Shacharis first. [Searching Ourselves](/daf/pesachim/10/searching-ourselves) explains, on Pesachim 10, that the Shulchan Aruch requires a search even on Pesach with a berachah, and after Pesach without one. Rebbe Yehudah worries the searcher may eat what he finds, but the chachamim say the search itself reminds him.
pesach/forgot-to-do-bedikas-chametz.description: Forgot bedikas chametz on the night of the fourteenth? When to search the next day, on Pesach or after it, and with or without a berachah. Pesachim 10.

pesach/gebrochts-on-pesach.intro: Some families never let matzah touch liquid on Pesach, while others happily eat matzah balls. Questions posed to Rav Chaim Kanievsky include whether a wife must follow her husband's gebrochts custom, and he answered that this is not one of the customs she must adopt; he also said hataras nedarim works for it. [Beyond The Letter Of The Law](/daf/chullin/105/beyond-the-letter-of-the-law) on Chullin 105a asks when such a practice is only a chumrah.
pesach/gebrochts-on-pesach.description: Must a wife follow her husband's gebrochts custom? Rav Chaim Kanievsky's answers on wet matzah, with chumros and customs discussed on Chullin 105a.

pesach/grape-juice-for-the-four-cups.intro: Can the four cups at the Seder be filled with grape juice, or even grapefruit juice for someone who cannot drink wine or grape juice? Rav Chaim Kanievsky answered yes to both, and he ruled that the lenient shiurim of Rabbi Avraham Chaim Naeh should not be used for children drinking the four cups. The questions were translated from Hebrew, and Rav Chaim himself wrote that his quick answers carry no halachic responsibility.
pesach/grape-juice-for-the-four-cups.description: May grape juice or grapefruit juice be used for the four cups at the Seder? Rav Chaim Kanievsky's short answers, and the shiur that children should drink.

pesach/ha-lachma-anya-invitation.intro: At the start of the Seder we invite anyone to come and join in the Pesach, but Pesachim 61a teaches that only those registered before the slaughter could eat from a Korban Pesach. Some communities therefore had no guests on the first days and changed the text to say guests may come but not eat. [Korban Pesach Conundrums](/daf/pesachim/61/korban-pesach-conundrums) brings the Bnei Yissaschar's reading: the invitation is to the matzah, which anyone may still join.
pesach/ha-lachma-anya-invitation.description: How can Ha Lachma Anya invite anyone to join the Pesach if the korban needed advance sign-up? Pesachim 61a and the Bnei Yissaschar's answer.

pesach/horseradish-for-marror.intro: The Mishnah in Pesachim 39a lists five species for marror, and some identify the third as horseradish. The Shulchan Aruch prefers the first, chazeres, and the Tevuos Shor explains why the Mishnah's order counts here. The Chofetz Chaim warns that raw horseradish eaten without grinding does not fulfill the mitzvah and may even be an aveirah.
pesach/horseradish-for-marror.description: Can horseradish be used for marror, and must it be ground? Pesachim 39a's five species, the Shulchan Aruch's preference and the Chofetz Chaim's warning.

pesach/iceberg-lettuce-for-marror.intro: Rav Dovid Feinstein writes that all kinds of lettuce are essentially one species, and he heard that a renowned gaon permitted common lettuce for marror. [Lettuce Discuss Marror](/daf/pesachim/39/lettuce-discuss-marror) reports that Rav Aharon Kotler used iceberg lettuce at his Seder, and iceberg has far fewer insects than romaine. On Pesachim 39a, the Chazon Ish wanted romaine to taste bitter, while Rav Shlomo Zalman held that lettuce too bitter to eat does not count at all.
pesach/iceberg-lettuce-for-marror.description: May iceberg lettuce be used for marror? Rav Dovid Feinstein and Rav Aharon Kotler's Seder, plus how bitter romaine should be, on Pesachim 39a.

pesach/inaccessible-chametz-before-pesac.intro: Bava Metzia 42a says chametz under three tefachim of rubble may stay over Pesach, since a dog will not dig it up. Rav Vozner applies this to chametz under garbage, but he requires opening a coat's lining to remove crumbs, since anyone can open seams. In [Chametz and Chumros](/daf/bava-metzia/42/chametz-and-chumros), Dayan Fisher disagrees and relies on bitul.
pesach/inaccessible-chametz-before-pesac.description: Must chametz under rubble or stuck in a coat lining be removed, or is bitul enough? Rav Vozner and Dayan Fisher apply Bava Metzia 42a to new cases.

pesach/kos-shel-eliyahu.intro: Why do we pour a cup for Eliyahu HaNavi at the Seder? It declares our belief in the Ultimate Redemption that Eliyahu will herald, and the Matteh Moshe links it to opening the door to greet him. Yet the Kitzur Shulchan Aruch and the Shtei HaLechem point to a custom of setting the cup on the table from the start, as [An Open Door Policy](/daf/pesachim/86/open-door-policy-pesachim-86) explains alongside Pesachim 86a.
pesach/kos-shel-eliyahu.description: Kos Shel Eliyahu expresses faith in the Final Redemption. Is it poured at the end of the Seder or set out from the start? The custom, with Pesachim 86a.

pesach/learning-before-bedikas-chametz.intro: Once the time for bedikas chametz arrives, one should not start a meal, any other activity or even learning before searching. The Agudas Eizov allows one exception, learning the laws of the bedikah itself, since that will surely remind him to search. [A Time To Learn](/daf/pesachim/6/a-time-to-learn) on Pesachim 6a brings the Nitei Gavriel, who forbids even that, based on the Rambam's concern that he will miss the proper starting time.
pesach/learning-before-bedikas-chametz.description: May you learn Torah, even the laws of the search, once the time for bedikas chametz arrives? The Agudas Eizov and Nitei Gavriel disagree. Pesachim 6a.

pesach/lettuce-for-marror.intro: Romaine lettuce is hardly bitter, so why is it the preferred marror? The Shulchan Aruch prefers chazeres, first on the list in Pesachim 39a, and Rav Dovid Feinstein allows any kind of lettuce. The Chazon Ish wanted a detectable bitterness, but Rav Shlomo Zalman Auerbach says lettuce left to grow truly bitter is not eaten that way and does not count, as [The Bitter Truth](/daf/sanhedrin/49/the-bitter-truth) explains.
pesach/lettuce-for-marror.description: Why is romaine lettuce preferred for marror, and must it taste bitter? Pesachim 39a, Rav Dovid Feinstein, the Chazon Ish and Rav Shlomo Zalman Auerbach.

pesach/machine-matzah-and-hand-matzah.intro: Families differ on whether they eat handmade or machine matzah on Pesach, and the difference raises practical questions. Rav Chaim Kanievsky said that someone whose family ate only handmade matzah should not change his custom. When two people who eat only handmade matzah sit with one who eats only machine matzah, he said they seem not to combine for a zimun, unless avoiding the other kind is a mere chumrah.
pesach/machine-matzah-and-hand-matzah.description: Handmade or machine matzah? Rav Chaim Kanievsky on keeping a family custom, a wife's custom, and whether different matzah eaters join for a zimun.

pesach/matzah-made-from-bran.intro: Pesachim 36b teaches that the mitzvah of matzah is not limited to pas hidra'ah, and the Rif explains that term as bread made solely of bran. The Ran objects that all-bran dough is not subject to challah and would take a Shehakol, and the Shulchan Aruch rules that 100% bran matzah does not fulfill the mitzvah. [A Bran Plan For Matzah](/daf/pesachim/36/a-bran-plan-for-matzah) adds that bran mixed into refined flour does not count toward the shiur.
pesach/matzah-made-from-bran.description: Can matzah made of bran fulfill the mitzvah at the Seder? The Rif, the Ran and the Shulchan Aruch, and how bran counts toward the shiur. Pesachim 36b.

pesach/onen-bringing-the-korban-pesach.intro: Yosef HaKohen's wife died on the morning of erev Pesach, making him an onen, and he held that an onen may still bring the Korban Pesach. His friends knew the halacha was against him. As Zevachim 100a is explained, had she died after midday his Pesach duty would have come first, but since she died in the morning he would have to wait for Pesach Sheini.
pesach/onen-bringing-the-korban-pesach.description: May an onen bring the Korban Pesach? Yosef HaKohen's wife died on the morning of erev Pesach, and his friends knew he must wait, in Zevachim 100a.

pesach/opening-the-door-at-the-seder.intro: Near the end of the Seder we open the front door. The Rema says it shows our trust in Hashem on Leil Shimurim. Rav Yosef Salant offers another reason from Pesachim 86a: after eating the Korban Pesach behind a bolted door, people opened it and went up to the roof to say Hallel.
pesach/opening-the-door-at-the-seder.description: Why open the door at the Seder? The Rema's Leil Shimurim reason, and Rav Yosef Salant's link to the Korban Pesach meal and roof Hallel, Pesachim 86a.

pesach/popcorn-on-pesach.intro: Zevachim 48b says something secondary is never stricter than the main thing.
