Shimon argues that grain never touched by water cannot become chametz, so why forbid air-popped popcorn? In [Cracker Jack Kitniyos Controversy](/daf/zevachim/48/cracker-jack-kitniyos-controversy), the Maamar Mordechai warns of a slippery slope, while Rav Yehoshua Pfeffer permits roasted pumpkin seeds.
pesach/popcorn-on-pesach.description: Is air-popped popcorn kitniyos if it never touched water? A playful dialogue weighs Zevachim 48b, the Maamar Mordechai and Rav Yehoshua Pfeffer's ruling.

pesach/potatoes-for-karpas.intro: Rav Dovid Feinstein writes that the best vegetables for karpas are green ones eaten raw, like celery. Potatoes fail on both counts, yet many use them, a custom from European communities that had little choice of vegetables after the winter. [Pesach Planning In October](/daf/pesachim/115/pesach-planning-in-october) on Pesachim 115a adds that cooked potatoes eaten with a fork may not even require washing, so some dip them by hand.
pesach/potatoes-for-karpas.description: Why do so many families use potatoes for karpas when green raw vegetables are best? The custom's origin and the washing question, on Pesachim 115a.

pesach/roasting-the-zeroa-shank-bone.intro: Many Rishonim hold that a Korban Pesach roasted on a grill was invalid, so some roast the zeroa directly over a fire, and the VaYaged Moshe suggests holding it on a fork over the stovetop. But the Shelah Hakodesh says it is better to cook it in water, so it does not look too much like a real korban, and then everyone can eat a piece at the meal. The article on Pesachim 82 weighs both customs.
pesach/roasting-the-zeroa-shank-bone.description: Should the zeroa on the Seder plate be roasted over fire or cooked in water? The VaYaged Moshe and the Shelah Hakodesh, discussed on Pesachim 82.

pesach/selling-chametz.intro: Selling chametz to a gentile is widely accepted, though the Vilna Gaon famously opposed it, and Rav Shlomo Zalman urged a sale even for someone who owns no chametz. Avodah Zarah 63b adds a wrinkle: one may not want something forbidden for benefit to exist. A seller usually does not mind whether he gets back the chametz or cash, so the sale is fine, unlike renting a new pot to a gentile for chametz over Pesach.
pesach/selling-chametz.description: How mechiras chametz works and why some avoid it, from the Vilna Gaon to Rav Shlomo Zalman, and the wrinkle that Avodah Zarah 63b adds to the sale.

pesach/selling-shirayim-with-chametz.intro: Avodah Zarah 63b implies that one may not want something forbidden for benefit to continue existing. The Arugas HaBosem therefore says shirayim of bread from a Rebbe should be eaten before Pesach rather than sold, since the chassid surely wants that very bread to survive, not its few dollars. The Makor Chaim disagrees, because the chassid gains nothing from it over Pesach, and the Shevet HaLevi weighs in for bakers.
pesach/selling-shirayim-with-chametz.description: May holy shirayim from a Rebbe be sold with the chametz, or must they be eaten first? The Arugas HaBosem and the Makor Chaim debate, from Avodah Zarah 63b.

pesach/siyum-for-firstborns-on-erev-pesa.intro: Firstborns fast on Erev Pesach, but a siyum lets them eat. What learning counts? Building on Bava Basra 121a, where the Nemukei Yosef finds the source for a seudah at the end of a masechta, Rav Vozner rules that finishing a sefer of Navi on Erev Pesach also exempts the firstborns, and Rav Moshe Feinstein once had a student make a siyum on a single daf.
pesach/siyum-for-firstborns-on-erev-pesa.description: Can finishing a sefer of Navi exempt firstborns from the Erev Pesach fast? Rav Vozner and Rav Moshe on what learning counts, from Bava Basra 121a.

pesach/smelling-chametz-on-pesach.intro: May one take a deep whiff of a hot pretzel at a ball game on chol ha'moed Pesach? The Biur Halachah cites Acharonim who forbid smelling a gentile's baking bread, and Rav Hershel Schachter ruled one should not smell it on purpose. But [Something In The Air](/daf/pesachim/26/something-in-the-air) shows from Pesachim 26a that unintended smelling is fine, so there is no need to avoid walking past a bakery.
pesach/smelling-chametz-on-pesach.description: May you enjoy the smell of a bakery or hot pretzels on Pesach? Intentional versus unintended smelling, from Pesachim 26a to Rav Hershel Schachter.

pesach/washing-for-karpas.intro: Why do we wash before karpas when no bread is eaten? Pesachim 115a requires washing before food dipped in liquid, though the Chofetz Chaim allowed eating less than a kezayis without washing. He then noted that the Tur requires washing for a small karpas, and later found support in the Rashbatz, who uses karpas the size of an olive.
pesach/washing-for-karpas.description: Why wash before karpas at the Seder? The Tur, the Chofetz Chaim and the Rashbatz on wet food smaller than a kezayis. Learn it from Pesachim 115a.

pesach/when-erev-pesach-falls-on-shabbos.intro: In years when erev Pesach is Shabbos, several things change. The Mishnah in Pesachim 69b teaches that the Korban Chagigah was not brought, since it does not override Shabbos, so the Bach rules to reverse zevachim and pesachim in the Haggadah that Motzei Shabbos. [Made to Order](/daf/pesachim/69/made-to-order) shows how the Knesses Yechezkel, Shulchan Aruch HaRav and Nimukei Orach Chayim disagree, while many Haggados follow the switch.
pesach/when-erev-pesach-falls-on-shabbos.description: What changes when erev Pesach falls on Shabbos? No Korban Chagigah, and the Bach's switch of words in the Haggadah, from the Mishnah in Pesachim 69b.

pesach/whole-wheat-matzah.intro: Following the Rosh, the Gemara in Pesachim 36b teaches that one might have thought only whole-wheat matzah, the bread of the poor, is valid, so the Torah adds that refined white matzah is fine too. Which is better for the Seder? Whole-wheat better recalls the matzah fed to us as prisoners, but the Nechamas Yosef reasons that the Jews leaving Egypt had time to sift their flour, just not to let it rise.
pesach/whole-wheat-matzah.description: Is whole wheat or white matzah better for the Seder? The Rosh's reading of Pesachim 36b and the Nechamas Yosef on the matzah eaten at the Exodus.

pesach/zevachim-and-pesachim-in-the-hagg.intro: At the end of Maggid we pray to eat "hazavachim u'min hapesachim", the sacrifices and the Passover offerings. One explanation is that the Chagigah was eaten first so the Korban Pesach would be eaten on a full stomach, but the Nimukei Orach Chayim says zevachim means the offerings of Shavuos and Sukkos that come before next Pesach. The article on Pesachim 69b weighs whether the order should ever change.
pesach/zevachim-and-pesachim-in-the-hagg.description: Why does the bracha after Maggid say zevachim before pesachim, and should the order flip some years? The Bach and his critics on Pesachim 69b.

sefiras-haomer/counting-forty-nine-or-fi.intro: The Torah says to count fifty days, yet we count only forty-nine. Tosfos answers with ad v'lo ad bichlal, up until but not including, and the Rosh says the Torah sometimes rounds up by one, as with forty lashes. [Making Our Days Count](/daf/menachos/66/making-our-days-count), on Menachos 66a, brings the Aderes Eliyahu's bold idea that Kiddush on Shavuos is itself the count of day fifty.
sefiras-haomer/counting-forty-nine-or-fi.description: Why count forty-nine days of the Omer when the Torah says fifty? Tosfos, the Rosh and the Aderes Eliyahu explain, in an article on Menachos 66a.

sefiras-haomer/counting-the-omer-after-b.intro: A boy who turns thirteen during Sefirah counted the first days as a minor, so can he keep counting with a bracha? The Eretz Tzvi proves from the ben sorer u'moreh, judged al sheim sofo, on Sanhedrin 68, that a minor who will mature during the Omer is already obligated. Rav Shlomo Zalman ruled he continues with a bracha, though Rav Ovadya Yosef ruled differently.
sefiras-haomer/counting-the-omer-after-b.description: Can a boy who becomes bar mitzvah during Sefirah keep counting the Omer with a bracha? The Eretz Tzvi's proof from Sanhedrin 68 and Rav Shlomo Zalman.

sefiras-haomer/counting-the-omer-in-engl.intro: Shimon blurted out the Omer count in English and hoped that meant it did not count. The Mishnah Berurah says one fulfills the mitzvah even in English, and someone who does not understand basic Hebrew is not yotzei with the Hebrew formula and should count in English, much like Kol Chamira. [Make Your Days Count](/daf/menachos/66/make-your-days-count) tells the story on Menachos 66a.
sefiras-haomer/counting-the-omer-in-engl.description: May Sefiras HaOmer be counted in English, and what if one doesn't understand the Hebrew? The Mishnah Berurah's ruling, in a shul story on Menachos 66a.

sefiras-haomer/counting-the-omer-without.intro: Shimon mentioned that tonight is the first night of Sefiras HaOmer while talking with a friend, so can he still count with a bracha? It depends on mitzvos ein tzrichos kavana, the Radbaz and the Vilna Gaon, and the Elya Rabbah says to count again without a bracha. The Kovetz Halachos offers a way out, since he never named the day's number, in a story built on Menachos 66a.
sefiras-haomer/counting-the-omer-without.description: If someone casually mentions the Omer day, can he still count with a bracha? Mitzvos ein tzrichos kavana and the Elya Rabbah, from Menachos 66a.

sefiras-haomer/death-of-the-24-000-stude.intro: Was Rebbe Yehoshua ben Korcha, mentioned on Bava Basra 113, the son of Rebbe Akiva? The Ramas Shmuel suggests that Korcha, the bald one, hinted that Rebbe Akiva was left bereft of his 24,000 talmidim, who perished for not showing one another respect. [Hair-Raising Thoughts](/daf/bava-basra/113/hair-raising-thoughts) sees the name as a lasting reminder to honor our peers, while his five new students show that quality matters as much as quantity.
sefiras-haomer/death-of-the-24-000-stude.description: Why did Rebbe Akiva's 24,000 students die, and how might the name Korcha recall them? A lasting lesson about respecting peers, from Bava Basra 113.

sefiras-haomer/is-sefiras-haomer-biblica.intro: The Torah ties the Omer count to the Omer offering, which cannot be brought without the Beis HaMikdash. In Menachos 66a, Ameimar counted days but not weeks, since counting today is only a commemoration, while Abaye counted both. The Rambam holds the count remains a Torah mitzvah, but the Shulchan Aruch rules that nowadays it is rabbinic.
sefiras-haomer/is-sefiras-haomer-biblica.description: Is counting the Omer still a Torah mitzvah with no Omer offering? Ameimar and Abaye, the Rambam and the Shulchan Aruch weigh in, from Menachos 66a.

sefiras-haomer/missing-a-day-of-sefiras-.intro: The Torah requires seven complete weeks of counting. Tosfos in Menachos 66a quotes the Hilchos Gedolos that someone who forgot to count one day can no longer continue counting with a berachah. In his view, a count with a missing day is no longer temimos, complete, since the person cannot finish all forty-nine days.
sefiras-haomer/missing-a-day-of-sefiras-.description: Can someone who missed a day of the Omer keep counting with a berachah? The Hilchos Gedolos says no, quoted by Tosfos on temimos in Menachos 66a.

sefiras-haomer/seven-complete-weeks-of-t.intro: The pasuk says the seven weeks of the Omer must be temimos, complete. Menachos 66a explains that this is why counting starts at night, and the Ran quotes an opinion to count as early as possible on the first night. The Acharonim apply the same idea to the end of the count, which is why Shavuos is not accepted before the forty-ninth day is over.
sefiras-haomer/seven-complete-weeks-of-t.description: Why must the Omer count be seven complete weeks? Menachos 66a explains starting at night, and the Acharonim apply it to when Shavuos may begin.

shavuos/davening-after-staying-up-shavuo.intro: After learning all Shavuos night, many people struggle through davening, and some even fall asleep. The Shevet HaLevi suggests going to sleep, with a shomer if needed, and davening at a later minyan. The Mishnah Berurah allows one who stayed up all night to daven before Netz, which may help him stay alert, a point raised with Yoma 21a on how hard it is to wake early.
shavuos/davening-after-staying-up-shavuo.description: How should you daven after staying up all Shavuos night? The Shevet HaLevi's advice to sleep first and the Mishnah Berurah on davening early. Yoma 21a.

shavuos/learning-masechta-shavuos-before.intro: Masechta Shavuos is about oaths, not about the yom tov, so why learn it before Shavuos? [Preparing for Shavuos: More Than Just Cheesecake](/daf/shevuos/7/preparing-for-shavuos-more-than-just-cheesecake), filed on Shevuos 7, tells of the young Pinchas Horowitz, later the Haflaah. He said it fits because at Har Sinai we swore to keep the Torah, and the custom is noted in the name of the Chasam Sofer.
shavuos/learning-masechta-shavuos-before.description: Why learn Masechta Shavuos, a tractate on oaths, before the yom tov of Shavuos? The young Haflaah's answer about Sinai, in an article on Shevuos 7.

shavuos/shavuos-and-the-oath-at-sinai.intro: On the first Shavuos, at Har Sinai, Klal Yisrael swore to uphold the Torah, and learning about oaths reminds us how serious that moment was. On a later Pesach, young Pinchas Horowitz suggested Kesubos and Kiddushin, since Hashem married Klal Yisrael at Sinai and the Torah is the kesubah. The story is told in an article filed on Shevuos 7.
shavuos/shavuos-and-the-oath-at-sinai.description: Shavuos recalls the oath at Sinai to keep the Torah, and Sinai as a wedding between Hashem and Klal Yisrael. The young Haflaah's insight, on Shevuos 7.

shavuos/why-shavuos-starts-late.intro: Many shuls daven Kabbalas Shabbos before sunset, but Shavuos is not started early. If it began before the forty-ninth day ended, the seven weeks of the Omer would not be complete. In [Making Our Days Count](/daf/menachos/66/making-our-days-count), Menachos 66a sets up this late start and a playful case, built on the Aderes Eliyahu, for davening early, not meant to be relied upon.
shavuos/why-shavuos-starts-late.description: Why isn't Shavuos accepted early like Shabbos, shortening the night of learning? Seven complete weeks of the Omer, from Menachos 66a, explain the wait.

rosh-hashanah/apple-dipped-in-honey.intro: Abaye's list of Rosh Hashanah simanim in Horayos 12b and Kerisus 6a does not include an apple in honey, a custom the Rema mentions. Why an apple? The Vilna Gaon notes that Yaakov smelled like a field, which one Targum calls an apple orchard, and the Zohar says Yitzchak blessed him on Rosh Hashanah, so the apple is both sweet and a reminder of that blessing.
rosh-hashanah/apple-dipped-in-honey.description: Why do we dip an apple in honey on Rosh Hashanah? The Rema's custom and the Vilna Gaon's link to Yaakov's blessing, beside Abaye's simanim in Horayos 12b.

rosh-hashanah/bentching-on-rosh-hashanah.intro: Many skip the word Melech in Yaaleh VeYavo of bentching, since the third berachah speaks of the kingdom of David. Why, then, does the ArtScroll Siddur note to add it on Rosh Hashanah? In [Find The Missing Word](/daf/berachos/49/find-the-missing-word), the Mateh Ephraim explains that on Rosh Hashanah we should not miss a chance to declare Hashem as King, building on Berachos 49.
rosh-hashanah/bentching-on-rosh-hashanah.description: Should Melech be said in Yaaleh VeYavo of bentching on Rosh Hashanah? The Mateh Ephraim says yes, to proclaim Hashem as King. Building on Berachos 49.

rosh-hashanah/financial-losses-decreed-o.intro: Just as one's sustenance is decreed on Rosh Hashanah, teaches Bava Basra 10a, so are one's losses. Rebbe Yochanan ben Zakai saw in a dream that his nephews would lose 700 dinarim, pressed them to give 683 to tzedakah, and the Kaiser's officers took exactly the remaining 17. [Your Loss Is Your Gain](/daf/bava-basra/10/your-loss-is-your-gain) draws the lesson that giving charity loses nothing, since that money was destined to go anyway.
rosh-hashanah/financial-losses-decreed-o.description: Are a person's financial losses for the year set on Rosh Hashanah? Rebbe Yochanan ben Zakai's nephews and the 700 dinarim, from Bava Basra 10a.

rosh-hashanah/hataras-nedarim-on-erev-ro.intro: After davening on erev Rosh Hashanah, men gather in small groups to annul their vows. [Is a Bar Mitzvah Boy an Adult?](/daf/nedarim/23/is-a-bar-mitzvah-boy-an-adult) notes on Nedarim 23 that this custom, already cited by the Shelah, is not mentioned in the Shulchan Aruch or Mishnah Berurah, and it raises a practical problem: a boy who just turned 13 needs hataras nedarim himself, but should not sit on the beis din for others.
rosh-hashanah/hataras-nedarim-on-erev-ro.description: The erev Rosh Hashanah custom of hataras nedarim: its source in the Shelah, its limits, and why a bar mitzvah boy should not be a judge. Nedarim 23.

rosh-hashanah/hearing-shofar-without-int.intro: Must a person focus on the mitzvah during every blast of the shofar? Discussing the dozing Megillah reader of Yevamos 55, the Mishnah Berurah rules that intent formed at the start is enough for the whole mitzvah. So one who walks into shul on Rosh Hashanah intending to fulfill the shofar blowing later has done enough, though it is still better to have it in mind during the blasts themselves.
rosh-hashanah/hearing-shofar-without-int.description: Is intent on entering shul enough for the shofar blowing heard later? The Mishnah Berurah's view, built on dozing during a mitzvah in Yevamos 55.

rosh-hashanah/joy-on-rosh-hashanah.intro: Rosh Hashanah is a day of judgment, yet we eat festive meals, wear fine clothing and get haircuts. HaRav Shaya Cohen explains with a parable of a frightened prisoner who walks into court and finds that the judge is his own father. Kiddushin 36a calls the Jewish people Hashem's children, and knowing that our Judge is a merciful Father lets us face the day with some confidence.
rosh-hashanah/joy-on-rosh-hashanah.description: Why do we celebrate with meals and fine clothing on a day of judgment? Hashem judges us as a merciful father, drawing on Kiddushin 36a for Rosh Hashanah.

rosh-hashanah/judgment-of-the-departed-o.intro: In Mussaf of Rosh Hashanah we say that Hashem remembers all who ever lived. Why judge the departed again each year, when they were judged at death? The Vilna Gaon explains that a person is rewarded for every good deed he inspired, even indirectly, so each year his account grows, an idea tied to Yoma 28a and Avraham's role in the Mincha prayer.
rosh-hashanah/judgment-of-the-departed-o.description: Why are those who passed away judged again each Rosh Hashanah? The Vilna Gaon on the lasting ripple effects of inspiring others, tied to Yoma 28a.

rosh-hashanah/pomegranate-on-rosh-hashan.intro: On Rosh Hashanah night we eat a pomegranate and ask that our merits be as many as its seeds. But the Pri Chadash asks: the Gemara compares even the sinners of Israel to a pomegranate full of mitzvos, so are we asking merely to be like them? The article on Pesachim 74 brings the Asifas Z'keinim's answer: sinners are like a slice, but the people of Tveryah were like a whole pomegranate, and so we hope to be.
rosh-hashanah/pomegranate-on-rosh-hashan.description: Why ask on Rosh Hashanah for merits like a pomegranate's seeds if even sinners are compared to one? The Pri Chadash's question answered, on Pesachim 74.

rosh-hashanah/rosh-hashanah-on-rosh-chod.intro: Rosh Hashanah is the only Torah festival that falls on Rosh Chodesh, and Rosh Hashanah 8a uses this to show it is the Day of Judgment, the festival when the moon is covered. Rabbeinu Meshulam explains that in Mussaf the verses of the Rosh Chodesh korban are left out. Tosfos traces this to the son of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, who stopped before saying them as chazzan.
rosh-hashanah/rosh-hashanah-on-rosh-chod.description: Why is Rosh Hashanah the only festival on Rosh Chodesh, and why are the Rosh Chodesh verses skipped in its Mussaf? Rosh Hashanah 8a and Rabbeinu Meshulam.

rosh-hashanah/rosh-hashanah-simanim.intro: Sanhedrin 65b forbids relying on omens, yet Abaye in Horayos 12b says to look at, or eat, gourd, rubia, leek, beets and dates on Rosh Hashanah. The Meiri explains that the foods are reminders to do teshuvah, which is why a Yehi Ratzon prayer is said with them. The Maharsha distinguishes between forbidden negative omens and permitted positive ones.
rosh-hashanah/rosh-hashanah-simanim.description: Why eat simanim on Rosh Hashanah when omens are forbidden? Horayos 12b and Sanhedrin 65b, the Meiri on the Yehi Ratzon and the Maharsha's answer.

rosh-hashanah/shofar-from-a-non-kosher-a.intro: The Rema writes that the horn of a non-kosher animal is not valid for a shofar. His source is the Gemara that tefillin must come from kosher animals, from the verse about the Torah being in your mouth. The Torah Lishmah suggests in this article on Sukkah 23 that shofar may be different, since it recalls our merit on Rosh Hashanah.
rosh-hashanah/shofar-from-a-non-kosher-a.description: Why must a shofar come from a kosher animal? The Rema learns it from tefillin, and the Torah Lishmah says shofar may be unique, in an article on Sukkah 23.

rosh-hashanah/what-is-judged-on-rosh-has.intro: The Mishnah on Rosh Hashanah 16a teaches that produce is judged on Pesach, fruit on Shavuos, water on Sukkos, and people on Rosh Hashanah. Tosfos asks from the story of the chassid in the cemetery, who heard about crops on Rosh Hashanah night. The Ritva says the halacha does not follow the Mishnah, while the Turei Even explains that each person's share is decided within the earlier decrees.
rosh-hashanah/what-is-judged-on-rosh-has.description: Are crops judged on Pesach or on Rosh Hashanah? Tosfos, the Ritva and the Turei Even on how a person's judgment fits the world's, in Rosh Hashanah 16a.

yom-kippur/backup-wife-for-the-kohen-gad.intro: The Kohen Gadol had to be married for the Yom Kippur avodah, and Rebbe Yehuda required a backup wife in case his wife died. Tosfos on Yoma 13b explain that the Bavli has him marry her beforehand, while the Yerushalmi has him marry her on Yom Kippur itself, relying on the rule that rabbinic restrictions did not apply in the Mikdash. Rebbe Akiva Eiger asks why he could not marry her on erev Yom Kippur with a condition.
yom-kippur/backup-wife-for-the-kohen-gad.description: Why was a second wife prepared for the Kohen Gadol before Yom Kippur? The Bavli, the Yerushalmi and Rebbe Akiva Eiger on Rebbe Yehuda, Yoma 13b.

yom-kippur/confessing-sins-you-did-not-c.intro: Why confess on Yom Kippur to sins one surely never did, and even say, in Rabbeinu Yonah's tefillah, that one has violated all the mitzvos? The answer comes from Avodah Zarah 18, where the wife of Rabi Chanina ben Tradyon was punished because she should have protested. [Accounting For All](/daf/avodah-zarah/18/accounting-for-all) concludes that we confess for others' sins because we can be held responsible for them.
yom-kippur/confessing-sins-you-did-not-c.description: Why does Viduy include sins a person never did? Rabi Chanina ben Tradyon's wife on Avodah Zarah 18 shows how each Jew can answer for what others do.

yom-kippur/eating-on-yom-kippur-when-ill.intro: Saving a life comes before the Yom Kippur fast, but a sick person who must eat should still avoid a full shiur that would carry kareis. So the infirm eat less than a shiur every nine minutes. The article on Shevuos 28 tells how Rav Yisrael Salanter, during the 1848 cholera epidemic, had the whole community eat, and how Rav Nosson Kamenetzky explained it.
yom-kippur/eating-on-yom-kippur-when-ill.description: When may a sick person eat on Yom Kippur, and why in small amounts spaced apart? The halacha and Rav Yisrael Salanter in 1848, in an article on Shevuos 28.

yom-kippur/eating-shiurim-on-yom-kippur.intro: When someone must eat on Yom Kippur for health reasons, we advise small amounts, each less than a large date, every nine minutes. According to Reish Lakish that is only a rabbinic ban, while Rebbe Yochanan calls even a small amount a Torah ban without kareis, as [A Tzaddik Before Birth?](/daf/yoma/82/a-tzaddik-before-birth) explains through Yoma 82b.
yom-kippur/eating-shiurim-on-yom-kippur.description: Why does someone who must eat on Yom Kippur take small amounts every nine minutes? Reish Lakish and Rebbe Yochanan on chatzi shiur, from Yoma 82b.

yom-kippur/going-to-shul-sick-on-yom-kip.intro: Someone who can fast only by staying in bed all day faces a hard choice on Yom Kippur. Rav Shlomo Zalman ruled that he may not go to shul if going will force him to eat or drink more than staying home. The article on Chullin 86b adds a striking ruling: if a mother cannot fast while caring for her children, her husband must stay home to help.
yom-kippur/going-to-shul-sick-on-yom-kip.description: Should someone who can fast only in bed go to shul on Yom Kippur? Rav Shlomo Zalman's rulings, including a husband's duty to help, on Chullin 86b.

yom-kippur/kohen-gadols-prayer-on-yom-ki.intro: After his service in the Kodesh HaKedashim on Yom Kippur, the Kohen Gadol said a short prayer, as the Mishnah in Yoma 52b records. Part of it was in Aramaic, though an individual normally should not pray in that language. The Gevuras Ari answers that the Shechinah rests in the Beis HaMikdash, while a chiddush of the Steipler points to the power of the Ten Days of Repentance.
yom-kippur/kohen-gadols-prayer-on-yom-ki.description: Why was part of the Kohen Gadol's Yom Kippur prayer in Aramaic, when one alone shouldn't pray in it? The Gevuras Ari and others answer, from Yoma 52b.

yom-kippur/kohen-gadols-yom-kippur-praye.intro: Bava Basra 147a says that watching the weather on Rosh Hashanah helps predict the coming year, and that this matters for the Kohen Gadol's prayer on Yom Kippur. Why only his prayer? The Darchei Dovid explains that the whole nation waited anxiously for him to come out of the Kodesh HaKedoshim, so knowing the weather let him say a shorter tefillah.
yom-kippur/kohen-gadols-yom-kippur-praye.description: Why did the Kohen Gadol need to know the year's weather before his Yom Kippur prayer? So he could keep it short for a waiting nation. From Bava Basra 147a.

yom-kippur/kol-nidrei.intro: Is Kol Nidrei a release of past vows, or a declaration voiding future ones? [Void Where Prohibited](/daf/nedarim/77/void-where-prohibited) on Nedarim 77 explains that the Mishnah Berurah follows Rabbeinu Tam's view of a personal declaration for the coming year, so everyone should say it. Many recite both versions, and the Rema and Magen Avraham explain why it is said before Yom Kippur begins.
yom-kippur/kol-nidrei.description: Does Kol Nidrei annul past vows or void future ones? Rabbeinu Tam, the Rivash and the Rema on its text and why it is said before Yom Kippur. Nedarim 77.

yom-kippur/pregnant-woman-fasting-on-yom.intro: In Yoma 82b a pregnant woman had a strong craving on Yom Kippur, and Rebbi told them to whisper, "Today is Yom Kippur." She held back and later gave birth to Rebbe Yochanan. Rav Shlomo Zalman Auerbach says we may still use these words with a blessing, but never scare a woman into fasting, and any real danger to mother or baby overrides the fast.
yom-kippur/pregnant-woman-fasting-on-yom.description: How to help an expectant mother with cravings on Yom Kippur: Rebbi's advice in Yoma 82b and Rav Shlomo Zalman's warning never to scare her into fasting.

yom-kippur/red-wool-turning-white-on-yom.intro: On Yom Kippur a strip of red wool hung in the Beis HaMikdash, and it turned white if the nation was forgiven. Rebbe Yochanan ben Zakai, whose takanos appear on Rosh Hashanah 30a, had the strip hidden from public view. The Aruch L'ner says a white strip might lead individuals to stop repenting, while the Shem m'Shmuel says a red one left people in despair.
yom-kippur/red-wool-turning-white-on-yom.description: Why was the red wool that turned white on Yom Kippur hidden? The Aruch L'ner and Shem m'Shmuel on Rebbe Yochanan ben Zakai's takanah, Rosh Hashanah 30a.

yom-kippur/yizkor-on-yom-kippur.intro: The Shulchan Aruch records the custom to pledge tzedaka for the departed on Yom HaKippurim, and the Rema adds that we say Yizkor, since even the dead can gain atonement that day. Because Yizkor matters so much, it may be said at home without a minyan. Rav Shlomo Zalman cautions against this when one can get to shul, as [Days of Teshuva](/daf/nazir/31/days-of-teshuva) explains on Nazir 31.
yom-kippur/yizkor-on-yom-kippur.description: Why do we say Yizkor and pledge tzedaka on Yom Kippur, and may it be said without a minyan? The Rema and Rav Shlomo Zalman, in an article on Nazir 31.

yom-kippur/yom-kippur-and-purim-connecti.intro: Megillah 14a teaches that the removal of the king's ring moved the Jews to teshuva more than 48 prophets and 7 prophetesses. The Arizal first suggested that Yom HaKippurim hints at Ki-Purim, a day like Purim, and we hope our teshuva will match theirs. The article on Nazir 31 adds the Mishna Berura's reason for the plural name.
yom-kippur/yom-kippur-and-purim-connecti.description: How is Yom HaKippurim a day like Purim? The Arizal links them through teshuva prompted by Haman's decree in Megillah 14a, in an article on Nazir 31.

yom-kippur/yom-kippur-prohibitions-bibli.intro: Besides eating and work, Yom Kippur forbids bathing, anointing and wearing leather shoes, but are these from the Torah? Discussing Nedarim 80b, Tosfos calls them rabbinic, while the Rambam holds they are Torah prohibitions excluded from kares. [Biblical or Rabbinic: That is the Question](/daf/nedarim/80/biblical-or-rabbinic-that-is-the-question) shows why it matters, from a man mocked while walking barefoot to shoes that may be leather.
yom-kippur/yom-kippur-prohibitions-bibli.description: Are bathing, anointing and leather shoes on Yom Kippur Torah or rabbinic prohibitions? Tosfos and the Rambam, and why it matters. Nedarim 80b.

sukkos/adding-schach-for-warmth.intro: On a cold Sukkos, may you pile on extra schach to keep the sukkah warm? Sukkah 13b is the backdrop, and the Gemara says schach must be placed for shade. The Ritva says schach put up for privacy is invalid, and Rav Elyashiv understood that schach added for warmth is excluded too and may even ruin the whole sukkah, unless it is put back for both shade and warmth.
sukkos/adding-schach-for-warmth.description: May you add extra schach to keep a sukkah warm? Rav Elyashiv says schach must be placed for shade, so schach added for warmth is a problem, on Sukkah 13b.

sukkos/beautiful-esrog-of-questionable-v.intro: Someone has two esrogim: a plain one that is surely kosher and a beautiful one that may be from a grafted tree. Rav Chaim Brisker said to make the berachah on the beautiful one first, and then take the plain one. In [Hands-On Solutions](/daf/eruvin/49/hands-on-solutions), filed on Eruvin 49, HaRav Silber uses a Rashi to challenge this, and Rav Yitzchok Zev Soloveitchik defends his father.
sukkos/beautiful-esrog-of-questionable-v.description: Should the berachah be made on a beautiful esrog that may be invalid, or a plain one surely kosher? Rav Chaim Brisker's answer, as discussed on Eruvin 49.

sukkos/borrowing-someone-elses-lulav.intro: On the first day of Sukkos, a person cannot fulfill the mitzvah with a borrowed lulav. The way around it is a gift on condition that it be returned, and Rava says the giver should say so when handing it over. In [Shaking Shailos](/daf/sukkah/42/shaking-shailos), set on Sukkah 42a, the Magen Avraham adds that between two people who know the halacha, the gift is understood even without saying it.
sukkos/borrowing-someone-elses-lulav.description: Can you use a borrowed lulav on the first day of Sukkos? A gift on condition of return, Rava's rule, and the Magen Avraham's view, from Sukkah 42a.

sukkos/building-your-own-sukkah.intro: Is building a sukkah a mitzvah of its own, or just a preparation for sitting in it? A Yerushalmi quoted by Tosfos on Sukkah 46a gives it its own bracha, la'asos sukkah, and the Aruch L'ner on Makkos 8a says Rashi also sees it as a mitzvah. That is a reason to build one's own sukkah, and even the Chasam Sofer, who calls it a hechsher mitzvah, allows Shehechiyanu at the building.
sukkos/building-your-own-sukkah.description: Is building a sukkah a mitzvah in itself? The Yerushalmi's bracha, the Aruch L'ner on Rashi, and the Chasam Sofer, from Sukkah 46a and Makkos 8a.

sukkos/buying-a-lulav-with-shadchanus-mo.intro: On the first day of Sukkos, a lulav must belong to you, not be borrowed. The Belzer Rebbe called shadchanus money the most kosher income there is, and the Maharal of Prague used his shadchanus fees to buy his arba minim. He felt the cleanest money was the best way to own them fully, in an article filed on Bechoros 55.
sukkos/buying-a-lulav-with-shadchanus-mo.description: Why did the Maharal buy his lulav and esrog with shadchanus money? The arba minim must be fully yours, as noted in an article filed on Bechoros 55.

sukkos/children-and-the-mitzvah-of-sukka.intro: When Shammai's daughter-in-law gave birth over Sukkos, he cut a hole in the roof above her bed and covered it with s'chach. For whom? [A Sukkah for a Baby](/daf/yevamos/15/a-sukkah-for-a-baby) brings two answers on Yevamos 15a: the Maharshal points to a boy of about four, and the P'nei Yehoshua says it was for the newborn, though the halacha follows Hillel.
sukkos/children-and-the-mitzvah-of-sukka.description: At what age must a child eat in the sukkah? Shammai's sukkah for a newborn, the Maharshal and the P'nei Yehoshua, with Hillel's view, Yevamos 15a.

sukkos/choosing-between-two-esrogim.intro: One esrog is plainly kosher but ordinary, and another is beautiful but may come from a grafted tree. Rav Chaim Brisker ruled to say the bracha on the beautiful one and then switch to the kosher one. [Separate And Unequal](/daf/sukkah/46/separate-and-unequal) on Sukkah 46 weighs the challenges: a possible hefsek after the bracha, and the loss of holding all four minim at once.
sukkos/choosing-between-two-esrogim.description: Which esrog gets the bracha, a plain kosher one or a beautiful doubtful one? Rav Chaim Brisker's ruling and the questions raised on it, from Sukkah 46.

sukkos/clotheslines-over-a-sukkah.intro: Boruch wants to build his sukkah right under his neighbor's clotheslines, and Shimon refuses to take them down. Even laundry hanging straight down may not block the schach's shade. Building on Chullin 125b, Rav Shlomo Zalman applies the stringency only to permanent fixtures like security bars, the Minchas Yitzchak disagrees, and Rav Zilberstein says the lines may stay.
sukkos/clotheslines-over-a-sukkah.description: Can clotheslines above the schach make a sukkah invalid? Rav Shlomo Zalman, the Minchas Yitzchak and Rav Zilberstein differ. Building on Chullin 125b.

sukkos/display-model-sukkah.intro: Sukkah 8b teaches that a sukkah built by anyone for shade is valid, even one a shepherd built for his animals. But what about a model a sukkah dealer set up only to attract customers? [A Snow-Covered Sukkah](/daf/sukkah/13/a-snow-covered-sukkah) suggests it may be invalid, since it was made neither for shade nor for the mitzvah, unless one lifts the schach and puts it back down with the right intention.
sukkos/display-model-sukkah.description: Can you use a sukkah built only for display, like a store's model? Sukkah 8b says a sukkah must be made for shade, so the schach may need to be put back.

sukkos/dofen-akumah-sukkah.intro: Dofen akumah, a bent wall, is a halacha l'Moshe mi'Sinai: kosher s'chach within four amos of a wall counts as joined to it. That is how Shammai made a sukkah from a hole in his roof on Yevamos 15a, and how many build a removable ceiling at home. A shul in England learned the limit the hard way, when its roof opening sat more than four amos from the walls.
sukkos/dofen-akumah-sukkah.description: How can a hole in the roof make a kosher sukkah? Dofen akumah, the four amos rule, and a shul in England with a ceiling sukkah, from Yevamos 15a.

sukkos/eating-an-esrog-after-sukkos.intro: An esrog used for the mitzvah may not be eaten until Simchas Torah. Rebbe Yochanan says a minor's esrog may be eaten on Hoshanna Rabbah after it was used, and Rav Shlomo Kluger suggests it may be eaten even earlier. [A Knotty Situation](/daf/sukkah/42/a-knotty-situation), filed on Sukkah 42a, explains that mitzvah items used by a minor have less kedushah.
sukkos/eating-an-esrog-after-sukkos.description: When may an esrog used for the mitzvah be eaten, and may a child's esrog be eaten sooner? Rebbe Yochanan and Rav Shlomo Kluger, from Sukkah 42a.

sukkos/elephant-as-a-sukkah-wall.intro: The Gemara discusses using a live elephant as a sukkah wall. Walls must start within three tefachim of the ground, so a standing elephant's legs would need filling in, or the elephant could lie down. In [A Sukkah Made Out of Elephants](/daf/sukkah/23/a-sukkah-made-out-of-elephants), filed on Sukkah 23, the Gemara suggests tying the elephant or training it not to move, in case it walks away.
sukkos/elephant-as-a-sukkah-wall.description: Can a live elephant serve as a sukkah wall? The Gemara's discussion in Sukkah 23, the three-tefachim rule, and what to do if the wall walks away.

sukkos/forgot-the-aravos-in-the-lulav.intro: Someone says al netilas lulav, finishes Hallel, and only then notices the aravos still sitting in their case. Or the esrog stayed upside down the whole time. Many Acharonim rule that he now says the rare bracha of al netilas aravah or al netilas esrog, while the Chofetz Chaim leaves it unresolved in the Biur Halachah, a question raised alongside Sukkah 46.
sukkos/forgot-the-aravos-in-the-lulav.description: Forgot the aravos, or held the esrog upside down, until after Hallel? Many Acharonim call for a rare bracha; the Chofetz Chaim is unsure. Sukkah 46.

sukkos/holding-the-esrog-upside-down.intro: A bracha should come before the mitzvah, but simply lifting the four minim already fulfills it, as Sukkah 42a teaches. That is why many hold the esrog upside down until after the bracha, as Tosfos explains. Those who follow the Gra hold it normally and have in mind not to be yotzei yet, and Rav Elyashiv suggested that turning the esrog satisfies the Gra's view as well.
sukkos/holding-the-esrog-upside-down.description: Why do many turn the esrog upside down before the bracha? Tosfos, the Minhag HaGra, and Rav Elyashiv on saying a bracha first, based on Sukkah 42a.

sukkos/holding-the-four-minim-together.intro: The Shulchan Aruch rules that the mitzvah of the four minim is fulfilled even when each species is taken separately. Still, holding them together is a mitzvah, and the Chelkas Yoav suggests this outweighs having the nicest esrog. The Mishnah Berurah advises that one who took them one after another should take them all again at once, following Rabbeinu Tam, a point discussed with Sukkah 46.
sukkos/holding-the-four-minim-together.description: Must the lulav, esrog, hadasim and aravos be held at once? The Shulchan Aruch, the Chelkas Yoav and the Mishnah Berurah on this, tied to Sukkah 46.

sukkos/indoor-sukkah-with-a-retractable-.intro: Rav Mordechai Finkelman turned down a sukkah built into his house, because he wanted to schlepp the boards himself. The harder a mitzvah, the greater the reward, yet many Admorim and Rabbanim chose indoor sukkahs with roofs that open. [A More Mehudar Mitzvah](/daf/shevuos/27/a-more-mehudar-mitzvah), filed on Shevuos 27, suggests why: such a sukkah is drier, safer and warmer, and so a more mehudar mitzvah.
sukkos/indoor-sukkah-with-a-retractable-.description: Is a sukkah built into the house with a retractable roof better than an outdoor one? Effort against beauty in the mitzvah, in an article on Shevuos 27.

sukkos/intent-while-eating-in-the-sukkah.intro: Can someone eat in a perfectly kosher sukkah and still fall short of the mitzvah? Since the Shulchan Aruch requires intent for a mitzvah, Rav Shlomo Zalman Auerbach suggested that eating in a sukkah without it might count as mevateil mitzvas aseh. [Nod If You’re Awake](/daf/yevamos/55/nod-if-youre-awake), on Yevamos 55, notes that he was unsure, but still urged an extra effort to have the mitzvah in mind.
sukkos/intent-while-eating-in-the-sukkah.description: Does eating in the sukkah without intent fulfill the mitzvah? Rav Shlomo Zalman Auerbach's concern about mevateil mitzvas aseh, tied to Yevamos 55.

sukkos/lavud-making-a-sukkah-invalid.intro: Lavud treats small gaps as solid, and many sukkos rely on it to make fabric walls kosher, but can it also work against you? Boruch argues that three clotheslines spaced close together count as one wide strip of invalid schach, as the Gemara in Chullin 125b treats a lattice as solid. The Bach says lavud applies to be strict, while the Magen Avraham disagrees.
sukkos/lavud-making-a-sukkah-invalid.description: Can lavud make a sukkah invalid, as when closely spaced lines hang overhead? The Bach, the Magen Avraham and the Mishnah Berurah, building on Chullin 125b.

sukkos/lulav-all-seven-days-of-sukkos.intro: In the time of the Beis HaMikdash, the lulav was taken seven days only in the Mikdash and one day elsewhere. The Mishnah on Rosh Hashanah 30a tells how Rebbe Yochanan ben Zakai extended it to seven days everywhere as a remembrance. Rebbe Shlomo Zalman would remind his family of the reason, since one who forgets it has not properly fulfilled the zecher.
sukkos/lulav-all-seven-days-of-sukkos.description: Why do we take the lulav all seven days of Sukkos? Rosh Hashanah 30a: a remembrance of the Beis HaMikdash, and why Rav Shlomo Zalman said to recall it.

sukkos/maximum-height-of-a-sukkah.intro: A sukkah taller than twenty amos is invalid, and Rabbah explains why: the eye does not look higher than twenty amos without a conscious effort, and we want a person to be aware of the schach. In [Standing Tall](/daf/sukkah/2/standing-tall), Sukkah 2b adds that for Rabbah, walls reaching the schach guide the eye up, though the halacha does not follow him.
sukkos/maximum-height-of-a-sukkah.description: Why is a sukkah taller than twenty amos invalid? Rabbah in Sukkah 2b says the eye won't notice schach that high, unless the walls lead it up.

sukkos/minimum-sukkah-height.intro: When snow weighs down the schach and it sags in the middle, has the sukkah become too low? The Gemara in Sukkah 4a discusses leaves that hang down into the space below. Rava rules that as long as there are at least ten tefachim of living space from the floor to the schach, the sukkah is kosher.
sukkos/minimum-sukkah-height.description: How low may sagging schach go before a sukkah is invalid? Rava in Sukkah 4a requires ten tefachim of space under the schach, as a snowy sukkah shows.

sukkos/pesukim-on-sukkah-decorations.intro: The Mishnah Berurah writes that one may not write the pasuk of basukos tashvu on sukkah decorations, since the leniency to write pesukim is only for learning Torah. Rav Elyashiv held that buying decorations already printed with pesukim is fine. And if one reads them, that is learning, which we permit, a discussion that grows out of the golden tablet of Yoma 37a.
sukkos/pesukim-on-sukkah-decorations.description: May you write or buy sukkah decorations with pesukim on them? The Mishnah Berurah's limit and Rav Elyashiv's view, in a discussion tied to Yoma 37a.

sukkos/picking-arba-minim-in-eretz-yisra.intro: According to Tosfos in Bava Basra, every Jewish family owns an ancestral share somewhere in Eretz Yisrael, even if they cannot find it. That raises a surprising concern. Some advise against picking your own arba minim in Israel for the first day of Sukkos, since it may be like stealing, as the article on Chagigah 2 explains.
sukkos/picking-arba-minim-in-eretz-yisra.description: Can picking your own arba minim in Eretz Yisrael count as theft? Every family owns ancestral land there, so some advise against it. From Chagigah 2.

sukkos/sleeping-outside-the-sukkah.intro: If Shammai's sukkah on Yevamos 15a was for a newborn, what was the baby doing that needed one? Perhaps nursing counts like a bread meal, or perhaps Shammai held that a sleeping baby needs a sukkah. That raises a practical question: if someone dozes off outside the sukkah, during a shiur for example, must he be woken?
sukkos/sleeping-outside-the-sukkah.description: If someone dozes off outside the sukkah, must you wake him? A question raised by Shammai's sukkah for a newborn baby boy, discussed on Yevamos 15a.

sukkos/snow-on-the-sukkah.intro: Snow is water, and water cannot be schach, so does snow on top of the schach ruin the sukkah? The Ginas V'radim ties it to Sukkah 13b, where Rashi and the Meiri argue whether a leafy vegetable that will soon wilt can be a roof for tumah. In [Global Cooling](/daf/sukkah/13/global-cooling), the Aruch HaShulchan says not to make the bracha in a sukkah covered with snow.
sukkos/snow-on-the-sukkah.description: Does snow on the schach invalidate a sukkah, and may you eat or make a bracha there? Rashi, the Meiri and the Aruch HaShulchan, building on Sukkah 13b.

sukkos/sukkah-decorations-on-yom-tov.intro: Sukkah decorations are generally muktzeh on Yom Tov. But what if one falls onto the table just when the space is needed for the meal? Building on the Yom Tov leniency of moving muktzeh for food needs in Beitzah 8b, the decorations may be moved, though the Pri Megadim suggests moving them indirectly when possible.
sukkos/sukkah-decorations-on-yom-tov.description: A sukkah decoration fell on the table on Yom Tov. May it be moved? The muktzeh rules for food needs, and the Pri Megadim's advice, from Beitzah 8b.

sukkos/sukkah-walls-not-reaching-the-sch.intro: The halacha is that sukkah walls do not have to reach the schach, as long as they are at least ten tefachim high and stand right under it. This saved Rabbi Rothberg in an English shul whose sukkah was just an opening in the ceiling, far from the walls. In an article filed on Sukkah 2b, he stacked chairs under the opening and tied them with twine to make four walls.
sukkos/sukkah-walls-not-reaching-the-sch.description: Must sukkah walls reach the schach? The halacha needs only ten tefachim of wall under it, and a stack of chairs in England, in an article on Sukkah 2b.

sukkos/thick-schach.intro: The Shulchan Aruch says that ideally one should be able to see the stars through the schach, but the sukkah is still valid if they cannot be seen. If the schach is so thick that rain cannot get in, Rabbeinu Tam rules the sukkah invalid. The Mishna Berura allows using such a sukkah in time of need if the schach cannot be thinned, as the article on Sukkah 13b explains.
sukkos/thick-schach.description: How thick may schach be? Seeing stars through it, schach that blocks rain, and Rabbeinu Tam's view, from an article filed on Sukkah 13b on cold Sukkos.

sukkos/tying-down-schach-with-string.intro: Whatever holds schach in place should itself be valid schach, so may cotton string be used to tie it down? The cotton has been changed from its original form, though Rashi in Chullin 125b says string is not mekabel tumah. In [A Snag in the Plans](/daf/chullin/125/a-snag-in-the-plans), the answer is that the rabbis allowed it for support, since cotton is kosher by Torah law.
sukkos/tying-down-schach-with-string.description: May cotton string be used to tie down schach? Rashi on string, the Rambam on changed materials and the rule of maamid, building on Chullin 125b.

sukkos/wooden-blinds-as-schach.intro: A photo of a snow-covered sukkah shows schach made of wooden blinds. The issue of blinds and mats as schach deserves its own article, but the article on Sukkah 13b notes that Rav Moshe Feinstein ruled at least some wooden venetian blinds invalid as schach from the Torah. It also notes that the Mishna Berura prefers that only kosher schach material hold up the schach.
sukkos/wooden-blinds-as-schach.description: Are wooden venetian blinds kosher schach? Rav Moshe Feinstein ruled some are invalid from the Torah, noted in an article on a snowy sukkah, Sukkah 13b.

chanukah/chanukah-menorah-above-twenty-a.intro: A Chanukah menorah may not be placed higher than twenty amos, because it must be easy to see to publicize the miracle. But if, as Sukkah 2b says, walls lead the eye up to the schach, why can't a wall lead the eye up to a high menorah? The Turei Zahav answers that the menorah is lit at night, when the wall itself is hard to see.
chanukah/chanukah-menorah-above-twenty-a.description: Why is a Chanukah menorah above twenty amos invalid when walls can lead the eye up to schach? The Turei Zahav's answer, in light of Sukkah 2b.

chanukah/congealed-olive-oil-for-the-men.intro: Pre-filled cups of congealed olive oil avoid leaks and splatters, but do they fulfill the hiddur of lighting with olive oil? [Pesachim 16a: Fueling the Flames of Chanukah](/daf/pesachim/16/pesachim-16a-fueling-the-flames-of-chanukah) brings Rav Moshe Shternbach, who says no, since congealed oil is a food and was not fit for the Menorah. The Shevet HaLevi and Rav Elyashiv permit it, and one opinion even calls it a hiddur, since the miracle oil had congealed.
chanukah/congealed-olive-oil-for-the-men.description: Does congealed olive oil in pre-filled cups fulfill the hiddur of olive oil for the menorah? Rav Shternbach, the Shevet HaLevi and more. Pesachim 16a.

chanukah/did-the-chanukah-menorah-burn-c.intro: Did the Menorah in the Chanukah story burn for eight days straight, or was it relit each night? If it never went out, the mitzvah of lighting seems to be done only once, and Rashi on Menachos 89a suggests a fire still burning by day was put out. [A Burning Question](/daf/menachos/88/a-burning-question) weighs a Midrash Tanchuma, Rav Chaim Brisker and the Sfas Emes, who sides with eight straight days.
chanukah/did-the-chanukah-menorah-burn-c.description: Did the Chanukah Menorah burn for eight straight days or get relit each night? Rashi, Rav Chaim Brisker and the Sfas Emes weigh in, from Menachos 88.

chanukah/electric-menorah-for-chanukah.intro: Can an electric menorah fulfill the mitzvah of Chanukah lights? Since the mitzvah is done at the moment of lighting, all the fuel must be present then, which rules out plug-in lights though perhaps not battery flashlights. The article on Pesachim 8a adds that Chanukah lights recall burning oil, so most poskim reject flashlights, while Rav Shlomo Zalman allowed IDF soldiers who cannot use real fire to light them with a berachah.
chanukah/electric-menorah-for-chanukah.description: Can an electric or battery menorah fulfill the mitzvah of Chanukah lights? Most poskim say no, but Rav Shlomo Zalman allowed it for soldiers. Pesachim 8a.

chanukah/havdalah-or-chanukah-candles-fi.intro: On Motzaei Shabbos Chanukah, tadir suggests Havdalah first, and many Acharonim say so. Others light first because we do not rush to say goodbye to Shabbos, and the Mishnah Berurah says either way has support. [Tumult Over Tadir](/daf/zevachim/89/tumult-over-tadir) tells of Rav Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld, whose wife set up the menorah so he met it first, building on Zevachim 89.
chanukah/havdalah-or-chanukah-candles-fi.description: On Motzaei Shabbos Chanukah, Havdalah or candles first? Tadir, delaying Shabbos's end, and Rav Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld's clever solution, from Zevachim 89.

chanukah/latest-time-to-light-chanukah-c.intro: In the times of the Gemara, the menorah was lit outside, and one view says the mitzvah lasts only while people walk in the streets. The Mishnah Berurah allows lighting while someone at home is awake, and without a bracha if all are asleep. Tied to Menachos 101b, Rav Shmuel Kamenetsky says it is better to light right away with wax candles than to wait for oil.
chanukah/latest-time-to-light-chanukah-c.description: Until when may the menorah be lit, and is it better to light early with wax or later with oil? The Rema, Mishnah Berurah and poskim, tied to Menachos 101b.

chanukah/miracle-of-the-chanukah-oil.intro: If the jug of oil held enough for one day, why is Chanukah eight days and not seven? This is the Beis Yosef's kasha, and the sefer Nes LaShoshanim gathers 250 answers, from oil that burned for two lightings to a new Menorah that absorbed some of it. On Menachos 69b, [It’s Raining Wheat](/daf/menachos/69/its-raining-wheat) asks whether a jug that was miraculously refilled would even count as olive oil.
chanukah/miracle-of-the-chanukah-oil.description: Why is Chanukah eight days if the oil found sufficed for one? A sampling of the 250 answers to the Beis Yosef's kasha, plus miracle oil on Menachos 69b.

chanukah/mixing-wax-and-oil-in-the-menor.intro: On the sixth night, a man has set up three wax candles when olive oil arrives. If he lights three wax and three oil, the Shaar Efraim says he has fulfilled the mitzvah, but not in the mehadrin way, since onlookers may think two people used the menorah. In [Waxing About Oil](/daf/shevuos/11/waxing-about-oil), filed on Shevuos 11b, the Shevus Yaakov allows mixing different oils.
chanukah/mixing-wax-and-oil-in-the-menor.description: Can you light some wax candles and some oil on one menorah and still be mehadrin? The Shaar Efraim and Shevus Yaakov, in an article on Shevuos 11b.

chanukah/olive-oil-for-chanukah-lights.intro: There is a mitzvah to use the nicest-burning fuel for the menorah, and the Rema adds an extra mitzvah to use olive oil, since the miracle in the Beis HaMikdash happened with olive oil. As the article on Pesachim 16a stresses, any oil or wax still fulfills the mitzvah, and the debate is only about the added hiddur. The poskim then ask whether congealed olive oil qualifies for it.
chanukah/olive-oil-for-chanukah-lights.description: Why is olive oil the best fuel for the Chanukah menorah, and does every form of it count for the hiddur? The Rema and the poskim, on Pesachim 16a.

chanukah/origin-of-the-chanukah-oil-jug.intro: Yaakov Avinu went back across the river, alone and at some risk, for a few small jugs. The Daas Zekeinim finds a hint in the word levado that they held olive oil, and the Sifsei Kohen says one of those jugs was the pure jug the Chashmonaim found. [The Gist Of The Jugs](/daf/shevuos/9/the-gist-of-the-jugs), filed on Shevuos 9a, sees it waiting over 1,000 years for its purpose.
chanukah/origin-of-the-chanukah-oil-jug.description: Was the Chanukah jug of oil one of the small jugs Yaakov Avinu went back for? The Sifsei Kohen's tradition, in an article filed on Shevuos 9a.

chanukah/replacing-candles-already-in-th.intro: A man finally fills his menorah with wax candles, and then the olive oil he was waiting for arrives. The Shevus Yaakov says removing candles set aside for a mitzvah would degrade them, but the Chacham Tzvi proves from the Parah Adumah in Shevuos 11b that we always swap for something nicer. The Aruch HaShulchan sides with the Chacham Tzvi, but only until he begins the blessing.
chanukah/replacing-candles-already-in-th.description: May wax candles already in the menorah be replaced with olive oil that just arrived? The Chacham Tzvi cites Shevuos 11b, and the Aruch HaShulchan rules.

chanukah/wax-coated-chanukah-wicks.intro: Olive oil is the best choice for the menorah, since the miracle was about oil. But many wicks come coated in wax so they light easily, and the wax burns first, so does that ruin the hiddur? In [Lighting the Menorah](/daf/menachos/101/lighting-the-menorah), tied to Menachos 101b, Rav Shlomo Zalman answers that the wax burns off quickly, so one is really lighting with oil.
chanukah/wax-coated-chanukah-wicks.description: Do wax-coated wicks still let one light the menorah with olive oil as preferred? Rav Shlomo Zalman's answer, in an article tied to Menachos 101b.

chanukah/why-chanukah-is-eight-days.intro: There was enough oil for one night, so only seven nights were a miracle, and yet Chanukah is eight days. [Mitzvah Mission](/daf/chullin/7/mitzvah-mission) answers with the baalei mussar: the first night celebrates that oil burns at all. Nature is Hashem's will just like a miracle, as the river in Chullin 7a flowed to the sea because Hashem willed it.
chanukah/why-chanukah-is-eight-days.description: Why is Chanukah eight days if the oil was enough for one? The baalei mussar say the first night celebrates that oil burns at all. Building on Chullin 7a.

purim/achashveiroshs-feast.intro: The Gemara in Megillah 12a says Achashveirosh wore the bigdei kehuna at his party, and Rashi says they were the garments of the Kohen Gadol. Rav Chaim Kanievsky explained that he wanted the choicest clothing, and that his punishment for using the Beis Hamikdash vessels covered the garments as well. Mordechai working at the feast misled no one, because he had already warned the Jews not to attend.
purim/achashveiroshs-feast.description: Why did Achashveirosh wear the Kohen Gadol's garments at his feast, and why could Mordechai be there? Rav Chaim Kanievsky answers, from Megillah 12a.

purim/anonymous-mishloach-manos.intro: If Amazon delivers mishloach manos and the recipient has no idea who sent it, is the mitzvah done? It depends on why we send it. If it is so everyone has food for the seudah, it works, but the Aruch HaShulchan, who sees the goal as friendship, says an anonymous gift does not count, in an article tied to Bava Metzia 11a.
purim/anonymous-mishloach-manos.description: Does mishloach manos count if the recipient doesn't know who sent it? The Aruch HaShulchan says no, in an article on the mitzvah tied to Bava Metzia 11a.

purim/bris-milah-on-purim.intro: A bris in shul on Purim morning: does it come before or after the Megillah? Some Acharonim say the bris goes first, since it is far more frequent. Others argue that a bris is not a set mitzvah of the day, since it could have fallen on any date, so tadir does not apply and the Megillah comes first, in a discussion of Zevachim 89.
purim/bris-milah-on-purim.description: A bris in shul on Purim: before or after the Megillah reading? Why some Acharonim say tadir puts the bris first and others disagree, from Zevachim 89.

purim/dozing-during-megillah-reading.intro: Yevamos 55 concludes that a mitzvah can be done while dozing, defined as being able to answer a simple question about where one put something. One who reads the Megillah while dozing fulfills the mitzvah, but one who listens while dozing does not, since the Mishnah Berurah says he surely missed some words. The Pri Megadim asks how a sleepy reader can keep his intent, and the Mishnah Berurah answers that his intent at the start is enough.
purim/dozing-during-megillah-reading.description: Does reading or hearing the Megillah while half asleep count? Yevamos 55 on dozing, the Pri Megadim's question, and the Mishnah Berurah's answer.

purim/eating-seeds-on-purim.intro: The Kol Bo writes of a custom to eat zironim, legumes or seeds, on Purim night, recalling the food Daniel, Chananya, Mishael and Azariah ate instead of Nevuchadnezzar's royal fare. The Mishnah Berurah notes that Esther did the same in Achashveirosh's palace. The Levush adds another link: according to Megillah 15a, Hasach, who carried Mordechai's message to Esther, was none other than Daniel.
purim/eating-seeds-on-purim.description: Why eat seeds or legumes on Purim? The Kol Bo's custom recalls the diet of Daniel and Esther, and Megillah 15a reveals that Hasach was Daniel himself.

purim/esthers-three-day-fast-on-pesach.intro: Haman's letters went out on the 13th of Nissan, and the Gemara says Esther's three-day fast fell on Pesach, but which three days were they? In [When Purim Was on Pesach](/daf/megillah/16/when-purim-was-on-pesach), the Alshich says Mordechai declared it on the 12th, while Megillah 16a shows Mordechai still fasting on the 16th. The Rashash explains that Rashi counts the 14th to 16th, or that Mordechai alone kept fasting.
purim/esthers-three-day-fast-on-pesach.description: When did Esther's three-day fast take place, and how could the Jews fast on Pesach? The Alshich, Rashi and the Rashash work out the dates in Megillah 16a.

purim/getting-drunk-on-purim.intro: How drunk should one get on Purim? The Chaya Adam says someone who will not bentch or daven Maariv properly should not get drunk, the Nimukei Yosef on Megillah 7b says one need only act jovially, and Rabbeinu Efraim learns from Rabba and Rebbe Zaira that one should not get drunk at all. The Rema says to drink a bit more than usual and fall asleep.
purim/getting-drunk-on-purim.description: How much should one drink on Purim? The Chaya Adam, Nimukei Yosef, Rabbeinu Efraim and the Rema read the Gemara in Megillah 7b in very different ways.

purim/haman-and-the-kings-ring.intro: Megillah 14a says the removal of the king's ring did more to bring the Jews to teshuvah than 48 prophets and 7 prophetesses. A playful Purim Torah builds on Rabba's rule on Bava Basra 45a that a borrower may claim he returned an item. Haman says he gave back the ring, until Esther exposes him as a liar who still has it.
purim/haman-and-the-kings-ring.description: Why did the king's ring move the Jews more than 48 prophets? A Purim Torah uses Megillah 14a and Bava Basra 45a to explain Esther's party with Haman.

purim/hamans-daughter-on-the-roof.intro: The Megillah says Haman went home mourning with his head covered, but the refuse hit his head before his daughter died, so why that order? The Rogochover Gaon answers with Tosfos on Bava Kamma 17b. A falling object is considered broken from the moment it falls, while a target is struck only on impact, so his daughter counted as dead the moment she jumped.
purim/hamans-daughter-on-the-roof.description: Why does the Megillah mention Haman's mourning before the refuse on his head? The Rogochover Gaon answers with a rule of damages from Bava Kamma 17b.

purim/hamans-downfall.intro: Questions that open with the Gemara in Megillah 12a carry all the way to Haman's fall in [Rav Chaim Kanievsky, shlita, on Megillas Esther](/beyond-the-daf/rav-chaim-kanievsky-shlita-on-megillas-esther). Haman paraded Mordechai rather than end his own life because he expected the last laugh, and his daughter missed his voice because she was too far up. Once Haman was executed his estate passed to the king, so Mordechai and Esther could use what had been Amalek's wealth.
purim/hamans-downfall.description: Why did Haman parade Mordechai instead of taking his own life, and how could his estate be used? Rav Chaim Kanievsky's answers, starting from Megillah 12a.

purim/hanging-of-hamans-ten-sons.intro: Haman and his ten sons were hanged on a beam fifty amos tall, and the Targum Sheni explains how all eleven fit. Tosfos in Chagigah 11b holds that the sons were beheaded first and then hanged. The Chasam Sofer explains that people could still tell who they were because they hung beside their father.
purim/hanging-of-hamans-ten-sons.description: How did Haman and his ten sons all fit on one beam, and were the sons already dead? Tosfos, the Targum Sheni and the Chasam Sofer, from Chagigah 11b.

purim/hearing-the-megillah-with-a-large-.intro: Rebbe Yehuda HaNasi closed his yeshiva on Purim so his students could hear the Megillah in shul. The Shaar HaTziyon explains that they went to join a bigger crowd, and the Chofetz Chaim concludes that one should hear it in the largest minyan. In [Yearn To Learn](/daf/megillah/3/yearn-to-learn), filed on Megillah 3, the Chayei Adam lets a regular stay in his own shul.
purim/hearing-the-megillah-with-a-large-.description: Should one hear the Megillah in the largest minyan available? The Chofetz Chaim, the Chayei Adam and exceptions, from an article filed on Megillah 3.

purim/height-of-hamans-gallows.intro: If people do not look above twenty amos without effort, as Sukkah 2b teaches, why did Haman build his gallows fifty amos tall? The article jokes that Haman didn't learn the daf. The Imrei Emes answers that just as walls lead the eye to the schach, people would see the bottom of the gallows and follow the wood up to the top.
purim/height-of-hamans-gallows.description: Why build Haman's gallows fifty amos tall if people don't look above twenty? The Imrei Emes answers using the sukkah height rule of Sukkah 2b.

purim/interrupting-torah-study-for-the-m.intro: If kohanim interrupt their service in the Beis HaMikdash to hear the Megillah, surely yeshiva students must stop learning too. But how can the Gemara call hearing a book of Tanach bitul Torah? In a discussion tied to Megillah 3, the Shaar HaTziyon says it is the time spent walking to a shul, while the Rashash says that leaving deep study just to listen to verses is bitul Torah.
purim/interrupting-torah-study-for-the-m.description: Why do yeshiva students and kohanim stop for the Megillah, and how is it bitul Torah? The Shaar HaTziyon and the Rashash, in an article on Megillah 3.

purim/liquor-instead-of-wine-on-purim.intro: When the wine runs out at a Purim seudah, does whiskey count? Rashi explains the mitzvah to drink as being with wine, and Rebbe Shlomo Zalman Auerbach is reported to have ruled that only wine will do. [Drunk on Mitzvos](/daf/bava-metzia/23/drunk-on-mitzvos), filed on Bava Metzia 23b, notes that Rav Moshe Feinstein is reported to have allowed any alcoholic drink.
purim/liquor-instead-of-wine-on-purim.description: Can the Purim mitzvah to drink be done with liquor, or only wine? Rav Shlomo Zalman and Rav Moshe are reported to differ, in an article on Bava Metzia 23b.

purim/mishloach-manos-on-condition.intro: A child who got nothing back for his mishloach manos plans to give the next one on condition it be returned, citing Rava in Kiddushin 6b. His father explains that this does not build friendship, since the friend cannot use the food at his seudah. Rav Shlomo Zalman adds that giving only on condition of getting a package back does not fulfill the mitzvah at all.
purim/mishloach-manos-on-condition.description: Does mishloach manos count if it must be returned, or given only for a package back? Rav Shlomo Zalman and the Kaf HaChaim, from Kiddushin 6b.

purim/mishloach-manos-that-was-refused.intro: What if a person offers mishloach manos and his friend refuses it? The Rema rules he has still fulfilled the mitzvah, and the Prisha traces this to the Rashba on Nedarim 24a: why give a gift only to have it handed back, when both can treat it as given and returned? In [An Exercise in Futility](/daf/nedarim/24/an-exercise-in-futility), the Mishna Berura notes that the Pri Chadash and Chasam Sofer do not accept this ruling.
purim/mishloach-manos-that-was-refused.description: Is mishloach manos fulfilled if the recipient refuses it? The Rema says yes, based on the Rashba in Nedarim 24a, but the Chasam Sofer disagrees.

purim/mishloach-manos-to-a-rebbi.intro: Megillah 7b tells how Rabbi Yehuda Nesiah sent Rabbi Oshaya a calf's thigh and a bottle of wine, and Rabbi Oshaya replied that his teacher had fulfilled the mitzvah. The Chida explains that even a rebbi giving to a student counts. The Sefas Emes says a talmid may send to his rebbi only if the rebbi sent first, but the accepted halacha is that sending to a rebbi counts.
purim/mishloach-manos-to-a-rebbi.description: Does mishloach manos count when sent from a rebbi to his talmid, or from a talmid to his rebbi? The Chida and the Sefas Emes, from Megillah 7b.

purim/mordechai-trying-to-free-esther.intro: Mordechai sensed that Esther was taken to the palace so she could save the Jews, yet he told her to hide her lineage so the king would send her away. In [Not Above The Law](/daf/bava-metzia/106/not-above-the-law), on Bava Metzia 106, Rav Henoch Leibowitz explains that halacha required him to try to free her. A hint about the Divine plan does not change the halacha.
purim/mordechai-trying-to-free-esther.description: Why did Mordechai try to get Esther out of the palace if she was meant to save the Jews? Rav Henoch Leibowitz explains, in an article on Bava Metzia 106.

purim/names-of-achashveiroshs-advisers.intro: Achashveirosh's seven advisers had strange names, and the Gemara in Megillah reveals a hidden meaning in each, from lambs and turtledoves to the Shulchan, which the angels used to recall the Temple service and argue for Vashti's downfall. The Ben Yehoyada notes the timing, since Vashti had opposed rebuilding the Beis HaMikdash, as [What’s In A Name?](/daf/sanhedrin/10/whats-in-a-name-2017) explains alongside Sanhedrin 10b.
purim/names-of-achashveiroshs-advisers.description: Karshena, Shesar, Admasa: the hidden meanings of Achashveirosh's advisers' names and how they recalled the Temple service, discussed with Sanhedrin 10b.

purim/nevuchadnezzars-steps-and-their-re.intro: Nevuchadnezzar ran after a messenger to put Hashem's name first in a letter, and he was richly rewarded for his steps. Sanhedrin 96 counts four steps, while the Midrash counts three. In [One Small Half-Step](/daf/sanhedrin/96/one-small-half-step), the Chofetz Chaim says he took three and a half, and the half-step earned his descendant Vashti a reign that was cut short, making room for Esther.
purim/nevuchadnezzars-steps-and-their-re.description: Did Nevuchadnezzar take three steps or four to honor Hashem? The Chofetz Chaim says three and a half, linking Sanhedrin 96 to Vashti and the Purim story.

purim/no-kosher-megillah-on-purim.intro: What should someone do on Purim if no kosher Megillah is available? Megillah 14a gives two reasons Hallel is not said, and the Meiri notes that by Rav Nachman's view one who cannot read the Megillah should say Hallel. In [Hallel On Purim: The Whole Megillah](/daf/megillah/14/hallel-on-purim-the-whole-megillah), the Shaarei Teshuvah says Hallel without a bracha, even with a Chumash, while the Shivas Tzion says not to.
purim/no-kosher-megillah-on-purim.description: What should one do on Purim with no kosher Megillah? The Meiri, Shaarei Teshuvah and Shivas Tzion on saying Hallel instead, from Megillah 14a.

purim/origin-of-hamantaschen.intro: Poppy-seed hamantaschen are often traced to the Purim custom of eating seeds, but that explains only the filling, not the dough. Building on Avodah Zarah 35b and the Rashbam, who holds that Daniel's pas bag was a dish and that he ate his seeds with bread, [Top-seeded Treat](/daf/avodah-zarah/35/top-seeded-treat) offers a playful reason for the pastry. Anyone who eats pas palter cookies, it concludes, should certainly eat hamantaschen.
purim/origin-of-hamantaschen.description: Why do hamantaschen wrap poppy seeds in dough? A playful explanation built on Daniel's diet, the Rashbam, and gentile bread on Avodah Zarah 35b.

purim/purim-in-a-leap-year.intro: In a leap year, Rebbe Eliezer the son of Rebbe Yose would put Purim in Adar Rishon, since we should not pass up a mitzvah. The halacha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, who chooses Adar Sheini. [Double Trouble](/daf/yoma/58/double-trouble) explains his reason, tied to Yoma 58b: Purim and Pesach should be kept close, as one season of redemption.
purim/purim-in-a-leap-year.description: Why is Purim in Adar Sheini in a leap year? Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel wants it near Pesach, despite ein ma'avirin al ha'mitzvos, discussed with Yoma 58b.

purim/purim-katan.intro: In a leap year, should there be any celebration on the fourteenth of the first Adar? The Rema says this is not our practice, yet one should feast a little more, and he ends with a verse from Mishlei. Rebbe Akiva Eiger explains the verse through Bava Basra 145a, which reads it as a reference to learning Mishna, so the Rema is telling us to follow the Mishna's view.
purim/purim-katan.description: Do we feast on Purim Katan, the 14th of Adar Rishon? The Rema's puzzling comment, explained by Rebbe Akiva Eiger through Bava Basra 145a and the Mishna.

purim/questions-on-megillas-esther.intro: HaRav Zev Aryeh Steiglitz recorded many questions he asked Rav Chaim Kanievsky about Megillas Esther, starting with the Gemara in Megillah 12a. Why does the Megillah never mention Vashti's death? Following the advisers' counsel is the same as saying she was killed, and Esther kept seven maidens to count the days because she feared losing track of Shabbos in the palace.
purim/questions-on-megillas-esther.description: Why was Esther's being an orphan key to the Purim miracle, and why is Vashti's death not mentioned? Rav Chaim Kanievsky's answers, from Megillah 12a on.

purim/reading-hamans-sons-in-one-breath.intro: The custom is to read the names of Haman's ten sons in one breath, since they all died together. According to Tosfos, cited in [The Demise of Haman and His Sons](/daf/chagigah/11/the-demise-of-haman-and-his-sons), they were beheaded at once. The Rambam says they were hanged and killed at the same time, and the Manos Halevi explains his reading of the pasuk, building on Chagigah 11b.
purim/reading-hamans-sons-in-one-breath.description: Why do we read the names of Haman's ten sons in one breath? Tosfos and the Rambam differ on how they died together. A Purim discussion from Chagigah 11b.

purim/reading-the-megillah-out-of-order.intro: The second perek of Megillah opens with the rule that one who reads the Megillah out of order has not fulfilled his obligation. In [Our Better Halves](/daf/megillah/17/our-better-halves), filed on Megillah 17, the Kotzker Rebbe gives it a deeper meaning. Someone who reads the Megillah only as a story from the past has missed the point, since Divine Providence guides events today too.
purim/reading-the-megillah-out-of-order.description: Why does reading the Megillah out of order not count? The halacha and the Kotzker Rebbe's lesson about seeing Hashem's hand today, from Megillah 17.

purim/rechesh-in-megillas-esther.intro: What is a Rechesh, the swift creature ridden by the couriers in Megillas Esther? Rav compares a strong gift to one riding on two of them, and the Rashbam links it to the Megillah. [The Rechesh and Restlessness](/daf/bava-basra/147/the-rechesh-and-restlessness), filed on Bava Basra 147a, brings the Aruch, the Metzudas Dovid, and the Vilna Gaon on why the fastest riders went out with the second decree.
purim/rechesh-in-megillas-esther.description: What was the Rechesh ridden by the couriers in Megillas Esther? Views on the mystery animal and why the fastest riders were sent, tied to Bava Basra 147a.

purim/sending-mishloach-manos-before-pur.intro: Can you order mishloach manos before Purim to arrive on Purim day? The Torah L'Shma says it depends on the reason for the mitzvah. In [Special Delivery](/daf/bava-metzia/11/special-delivery), the Terumas HaDeshen's focus on food for the seudah allows it, while the Aruch HaShulchan, focused on goodwill, rules the sender has not fulfilled the mitzvah, alongside Bava Metzia 11a.
purim/sending-mishloach-manos-before-pur.description: Does mishloach manos sent or ordered before Purim count if it arrives on Purim? The answer turns on why we send it, in an article on Bava Metzia 11a.

purim/sending-mishloach-manos-with-a-chi.intro: A rav complained to the Satmar Rebbe that a child dressed as a monkey delivered his mishloach manos, and the Rebbe answered that even a real monkey would be acceptable. In [No Monkeying Around](/daf/gittin/22/no-monkeying-around), on Gittin 22b, the Yaaleh Yehudah allows sending with a minor. The Chasam Sofer explains that no real shaliach is needed for this mitzvah at all.
purim/sending-mishloach-manos-with-a-chi.description: May mishloach manos be delivered by a child, or even a monkey? The Yaaleh Yehudah and the Chasam Sofer say no real shaliach is needed, from Gittin 22b.

purim/themed-mishloach-manos.intro: Many families build their mishloach manos around a theme, such as black and white, breakfast, coffee, Shabbos or a kiddush of whiskey, herring and kichel. Where does the idea come from? In [Mishloach Manos From Rebbi to Talmid](/daf/megillah/7/mishloach-manos-from-rebbi-to-talmid), tied to Megillah 7b, one suggestion is the royal reward Haman proposed, which Mordechai received.
purim/themed-mishloach-manos.description: Where do themed mishloach manos come from? Examples and a suggested source in the royal reward given to Mordechai, in an article tied to Megillah 7b.

purim/using-a-messenger-for-mishloach-ma.intro: Usually it is better to do a mitzvah yourself than through an agent, but the Eishel Avraham says this does not apply to mishloach manos. The Binyan Tzion even suggests the gift must go through a shaliach, and Rav Shlomo Zalman used one at least once. The Ksav Sofer adds, in the article on Gittin 22b, that the recipient must know who sent it.
purim/using-a-messenger-for-mishloach-ma.description: Should mishloach manos go through a messenger, and must the recipient know the sender? The Binyan Tzion, the Ksav Sofer and others, as seen on Gittin 22b.

purim/why-esther-invited-haman.intro: Why did Esther invite Haman to her parties with Achashverosh? Megillah 15b offers a long list of answers: to trap him, to keep him from plotting a revolt, to make the king and the nobles jealous, or so the Jews would think she had betrayed them. In [Royal Motives](/daf/megillah/15/royal-motives), Eliyahu HaNavi tells Rabbah bar Avuha that all the reasons were true.
purim/why-esther-invited-haman.description: Why did Queen Esther invite Haman to her feasts with Achashverosh? The many answers of the Tannaim and Amoraim in Megillah 15b, all of them true.

fast-days/asarah-bteves.intro: On Asarah B'Teves, Nevuchadnezzar laid siege to Jerusalem, the start of the road to the first Churban. The Shulchan Aruch lists the 8th and 9th of Teves as fitting fast days too, and the Mishnah Berurah reminds us that a fast is only a preparation for teshuvah. The article ends with Tosfos in Shevuos 15b, that the third Beis HaMikdash will come down from heaven, so our teshuvah could bring it right after the fast.
fast-days/asarah-bteves.description: Asarah B'Teves marks the start of the siege of Jerusalem and calls us to teshuvah. Its message and the fasts around it, with a teaching from Shevuos 15b.

fast-days/breaking-a-fast-when-rain-fall.intro: If rain begins in the middle of a communal fast for rain, the Rambam rules the community may end the fast early. The Ran explains that a community should not be overburdened, so an individual fasting for rain must finish his day, while the Rosh says the community should break the fast to thank Hashem right away. [Not So Fast](/daf/taanis/16/not-so-fast) on Taanis 16 even applies the idea to a group making aliyah on the second day of Shavuos.
fast-days/breaking-a-fast-when-rain-fall.description: When rain falls during a fast for rain, may the fast end early? The Rambam, the Ran and the Rosh on community versus individual, from Taanis 16.

fast-days/fast-of-the-ninth-of-teves.intro: The Shulchan Aruch notes an ancient custom to fast on the ninth of Teves but gives no reason. The Taz links it to the passing of Ezra HaSofer and the BaHaG to Nechemyah's yahrzeit, and others name the Granada massacre and more. In [Who Knows Nine?](/daf/bava-metzia/99/who-knows-nine), set on Bava Metzia 99b, the Birchei Yosef says the Sages left the reason vague on purpose.
fast-days/fast-of-the-ninth-of-teves.description: Why is there a little-known fast on the ninth of Teves? The Taz, BaHaG and Birchei Yosef point to Ezra, Nechemyah and others, from Bava Metzia 99b.

fast-days/fasting-for-rain.intro: During a severe drought, beis din declares fasts in stages: Monday, Thursday and Monday, then the same again, and then seven more. The Mishnah sets these 13 fasts as the limit, and Rebbe Ami explains that the community should not be overly burdened, even for something as vital as rain. After that, beis din turns to other steps, like limiting weddings and some construction, as Taanis 16 describes.
