fast-days/fasting-for-rain.description: How many fasts may a community be asked to keep in a drought? Thirteen fasts for rain, Rebbe Ami's reasoning, and what comes next, from Taanis 16.

fast-days/kinnah-for-the-destroyed-frenc.intro: Kinnah 22 of Tishah B'Av mourns the massacred Jewish communities of France and asks who will now interpret the nazirite vows. But were there nezirim in France? Rav Yosef Dov Soloveitchik explained that it laments there is no one left to explain Nedarim and Nazir, where students lack Rashi's commentary, as the article on Nazir 24a explains.
fast-days/kinnah-for-the-destroyed-frenc.description: Why does a Tishah B'Av kinnah for the French Tosafists ask who will explain nazirite vows? Rav Yosef Dov Soloveitchik explains, in an article on Nazir 24a.

fast-days/minor-fasts-versus-tishah-bav.intro: Rosh Hashanah 18 explains that Beis Din sent no messengers in Tammuz and Teves, since those fasts were once optional in peaceful times. The Ritva says they are now binding because Klal Yisrael accepted them, but without Tishah B'Av's stringencies of bathing, leather shoes and starting at night. The Mishnah Berurah advises a ba'al nefesh to follow the stricter Ramban.
fast-days/minor-fasts-versus-tishah-bav.description: How do Tzom Gedaliah, Asarah B'Teves and the 17th of Tammuz differ from Tishah B'Av? The Ritva and the Ramban on the stringencies, from Rosh Hashanah 18.

fast-days/shabbos-leftovers-during-the-n.intro: Meat is permitted on Shabbos during the Nine Days, so may Sunday's leftovers be served too? Some Acharonim compare it to Chullin 17a, where Rebbe Yirmiya asks whether desert meat stayed permitted after entering Eretz Yisrael, and since the custom is rabbinic, they lean lenient. The Aruch HaShulchan rejects this, and the prevailing custom follows him.
fast-days/shabbos-leftovers-during-the-n.description: May Shabbos meat leftovers be eaten during the Nine Days? Some Acharonim lean lenient, but the Aruch HaShulchan forbids it. A question tied to Chullin 17a.

fast-days/showering-on-a-fast-day.intro: May one shower on the 17th of Tammuz, Asarah B'Teves or Tzom Gedaliah? [Think Fast](/daf/rosh-hashanah/18/think-fast) starts from Rosh Hashanah 18, where the Ritva holds these fasts were accepted without a ban on bathing. Yet the Shaar HaTziyon reports a custom not to shower, which the P'ri Megadim limits to hot water, and the Mishnah Berurah allows a hot shower for Shabbos when Asarah B'Teves falls on Friday.
fast-days/showering-on-a-fast-day.description: May you shower on the 17th of Tammuz or Tzom Gedaliah? The Ritva, the custom limited to hot water, and Asarah B'Teves on Friday, from Rosh Hashanah 18.

fast-days/tishah-bav-called-a-moed.intro: Tishah B'Av is the saddest day of the year, yet we skip Tachanun on it and at Minchah the day before. The reason comes from a verse in Eicha, He proclaimed a moed to crush my young men. In [Tachanun Technicalities](/daf/shevuos/10/tachanun-technicalities), Shevuos 10 brings Abaye's reading for Rabbi Meir, but if we follow Rabbi Yehuda, the moed in that verse is Tishah B'Av itself.
fast-days/tishah-bav-called-a-moed.description: Why do we skip Tachanun on Tishah B'Av and the Minchah before it? A verse in Eicha calls the day a moed, as the discussion in Shevuos 10 brings out.

fast-days/why-tishah-bav-is-on-the-ninth.intro: The Beis HaMikdash was set on fire on the ninth of Av, but most of it burned on the tenth, and Rebbe Yochanan said he would have set the fast on the tenth. The Kotzker Rebbe asks how this fits his own view on Bava Kamma 60b that a fire's damage counts from the moment it is lit. The Birchos Shimon answers that a fire Hashem lit is different.
fast-days/why-tishah-bav-is-on-the-ninth.description: Why is the fast on the ninth of Av if most of the Beis HaMikdash burned on the tenth? The Kotzker Rebbe's question, based on Bava Kamma 60b.

rosh-chodesh/adar-rishon-or-adar-sheini.intro: In a leap year there are two months of Adar, so which one is the real Adar? Shekalim 2 brings a dispute between Rebbe Meir and Rebbe Yehudah over what a document means when it simply says Adar. [The Great Leap Forward](/daf/shekalim/2/the-great-leap-forward) shows that they may be arguing about which month is the leap month, or only about how people speak.
rosh-chodesh/adar-rishon-or-adar-sheini.description: In a Jewish leap year, which Adar is the real Adar? Rebbe Meir and Rebbe Yehudah argue over how to date documents, in Yerushalmi Shekalim 2.

rosh-chodesh/adding-a-leap-month.intro: Chizkiyahu wanted the nation to bring the Korban Pesach, but many were tamei from idol worship. Sanhedrin 12b records that he added Adar Sheini to give them time to become tahor, and then asked Hashem for forgiveness. The Gemara also teaches that only Adar can be doubled, and a month cannot be added before Rosh Hashanah or once Nissan arrives.
rosh-chodesh/adding-a-leap-month.description: How did Beis Din add Adar Sheini? Sanhedrin 12b tells of Chizkiyahu's leap year to allow purification before Pesach, and the limits on adding a month.

rosh-chodesh/diminishing-of-the-moon.intro: The moon rightly said there should not be two great lights of equal stature, and Hashem made the moon smaller. Shevuos 9a teaches that the Rosh Chodesh korban is a kapparah for that. The Orech L'Chaim links it to Sanhedrin 110a, where Korach's followers return every Rosh Chodesh, since Korach should have learned that there cannot be two Kohanim Gedolim.
rosh-chodesh/diminishing-of-the-moon.description: Why is the Rosh Chodesh offering a kapparah for making the moon smaller? Shevuos 9a, and the lesson Korach should have learned, from Sanhedrin 110a.

rosh-chodesh/festive-meal-on-rosh-chodes.intro: The Torah puts Rosh Chodesh right beside the moadim, and the Tur learns from this that it is a mitzvah to eat a festive meal on Rosh Chodesh. The Mishna Berurah adds that careful people serve an extra dish, and he cites a Midrash that money spent in honor of Rosh Chodesh is paid back by Hashem. The article on Shevuos 10 traces this to the debate over whether Rosh Chodesh is called a moed.
rosh-chodesh/festive-meal-on-rosh-chodes.description: Is there a mitzvah to eat a festive meal on Rosh Chodesh? The Tur, the Mishna Berura's extra dish and its promised reward, in an article on Shevuos 10.

rosh-chodesh/kiddush-levanah-before-yom-.intro: Should Kiddush Levanah be said during the Aseres Yimei Teshuvah? The Rema quotes the Maharil that the awe of judgment makes the needed joy impossible, but many Acharonim say we should grab every mitzvah when our life hangs in the balance. The Gra did not wait until after Yom Kippur, while Rav Elyashiv did, as [Once in a Blue Moon](/daf/sanhedrin/41/once-in-a-blue-moon) relates alongside Sanhedrin 41b.
rosh-chodesh/kiddush-levanah-before-yom-.description: Say Kiddush Levanah in the Ten Days of Repentance or wait until after Yom Kippur? The Maharil, the Gra and Rav Elyashiv's custom, with Sanhedrin 41b.

rosh-chodesh/messengers-announcing-the-n.intro: Before the fixed calendar, Beis Din declared each new month and sent messengers to distant communities. The Mishnah on Rosh Hashanah 18 lists six months for which they went: Nissan, Av, Elul, Tishrei, Kislev and Adar. Rav Papa explains why Teves and Tammuz were left out, since their fasts were optional in times of peace.
rosh-chodesh/messengers-announcing-the-n.description: Beis Din sent messengers to announce the new month only six times a year. Rosh Hashanah 18 lists the months and explains why Teves and Tammuz were skipped.

rosh-chodesh/seven-judges-for-a-leap-yea.intro: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says on Sanhedrin 10b that the decision to add a leap year was finalized by seven judges. The Gemara gives two reasons for the number. One links it to the seven words in the third verse of Birkas Kohanim, and the other to seven royal advisers, a dispute repeated for the aliyos of Shabbos.
rosh-chodesh/seven-judges-for-a-leap-yea.description: Why did adding a leap year need seven judges? Sanhedrin 10b ties the number to the third verse of Birkas Kohanim or to seven royal advisers.

rosh-chodesh/shalom-aleichem-at-kiddush-.intro: At Kiddush Levanah, the custom is to say shalom aleichem three times, each time to a different person. Rav Alter Henoch Leibowitz, rosh yeshiva of Yeshivas Chofetz Chaim, once had two bachurim beside him and three standing farther away, so he waved to the whole group with one loud greeting. With six bachurim around him another time, he simply kept going, since adding greetings beyond three does no harm.
rosh-chodesh/shalom-aleichem-at-kiddush-.description: How Rav Alter Henoch Leibowitz said shalom aleichem at Kiddush Levanah so that no bachur felt left out, and why adding extra greetings is perfectly fine.

rosh-chodesh/testimony-about-the-new-moo.intro: When witnesses came to testify about the new moon, Rabban Gamliel would show them drawings and ask them to pick out the moon they had seen. Avodah Zarah 43 asks how he could have such pictures, since the beraisa in Rosh Hashanah 24b forbids images of the sun and moon. The Gemara answers that a non-Jew drew them, permitted for the mitzvah of kiddush ha'chodesh, and that Rabban Gamliel as nasi was above suspicion.
rosh-chodesh/testimony-about-the-new-moo.description: How did Rabban Gamliel question witnesses about the new moon with pictures of its phases? Why it was allowed, from Avodah Zarah 43 and Rosh Hashanah 24b.

rosh-chodesh/vkapparas-pesha-in-a-leap-y.intro: Many add the words V'kapparas pesha to Rosh Chodesh Mussaf in a leap year, and the Elya Rabba says it adds a request for the extra month. The Torah Temima traces the custom to Sanhedrin 12b, where Chizkiyahu asked forgiveness for adding a month. That explains why most say it only until Adar Sheini, the window when Beis Din could add a month.
rosh-chodesh/vkapparas-pesha-in-a-leap-y.description: Why add V'kapparas pesha to Rosh Chodesh Mussaf in a leap year, and only until Adar Sheini? The Torah Temima traces it to Chizkiyahu in Sanhedrin 12b.

rosh-chodesh/when-to-say-kiddush-levanah.intro: On Sanhedrin 41b, Rav Yehuda says Kiddush Levanah may be said until seven days of the new moon, and the men of Nehardai say until sixteen. The Bach infers that one need not wait seven days, against the Rema MiPano and the Shulchan Aruch, and most Acharonim permit it after three. The Gra urged saying it at the first chance rather than waiting for Motzei Shabbos, as Rav Dovid Feinstein did.
rosh-chodesh/when-to-say-kiddush-levanah.description: When may Kiddush Levanah be said: after three days or seven, and should one wait for Motzei Shabbos? Sanhedrin 41b, the Bach, the Gra and Mishnah Berurah.

rosh-chodesh/women-and-kiddush-levanah.intro: Kiddush Levanah is customarily said by men, not women. Some say it is a time-bound mitzvah, though women have taken on other such mitzvos. The most intriguing explanation, in the article on Sanhedrin 41b, is that righteous women chose not to adopt it, worried that the joyous dancing afterward might lead to mixed dancing.
rosh-chodesh/women-and-kiddush-levanah.description: Why don't women say Kiddush Levanah? The time-bound mitzvah reason, and the view that righteous women avoided the dancing after it. With Sanhedrin 41b.

rosh-chodesh/women-not-working-on-rosh-c.intro: Rashi on Megillah 21b explains that Rosh Chodesh is a holiday for women, a reward for refusing to give their jewelry for the Golden Calf. The Shulchan Aruch calls their custom of not working a good one, and the Mishnah Berurah says a similar custom for men is no custom at all. In [A Rosh Chodesh Holiday](/daf/megillah/21/a-rosh-chodesh-holiday), the Rema says each woman refrains only from the work her tradition names.
rosh-chodesh/women-not-working-on-rosh-c.description: Why do women refrain from some work on Rosh Chodesh, and which work does the custom cover? Rashi, the Shulchan Aruch and the Rema, from Megillah 21b.

tefillah/being-specific-in-prayer.intro: Should a prayer for success be general, or name the actual trade or crop? Explaining Rebbe Yochanan's advice on Arachin 16b, the Ben Yehoyada assumes a father's tefillos are specific to his profession. The sugya on Bava Metzia 105b shows the same power: a landowner who davened on Rosh Hashanah for his wheat can claim that a tenant who planted barley lost the benefit of that prayer.
tefillah/being-specific-in-prayer.description: Why a tefillah that names specifics carries special power: a father's prayers for his son's trade on Arachin 16b and the wheat field of Bava Metzia 105b.

tefillah/birkas-kohanim-during-shemoneh-.intro: What should you do if the kohanim begin to bless the congregation while you are still in your silent Shemoneh Esrei? Rav Elyashiv says to keep davening, since the view that hearing Birkas Kohanim is a mitzvah is a minority one. Rav Moshe Feinstein, building on the mitzvah the kohen has in Sotah 38, says to pause and listen, and even not to start Shemoneh Esrei if you won't finish in time.
tefillah/birkas-kohanim-during-shemoneh-.description: What if the kohanim start Birkas Kohanim while you are in Shemoneh Esrei? Rav Elyashiv and Rav Moshe Feinstein disagree, in light of Sotah 38.

tefillah/changing-a-decree-after-rosh-ha.intro: Can a harsh decree be changed once Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur have passed? Tosfos on Rosh Hashanah 16a holds that public prayer still works, and even a prayer that includes the public counts. That is why we ask for a sick person to be healed together with all the sick of Klal Yisrael.
tefillah/changing-a-decree-after-rosh-ha.description: Can prayer overturn a bad decree after Rosh Hashanah? Tosfos on Rosh Hashanah 16a says communal prayer still works, which is why we pray for all the sick.

tefillah/chazzan-who-mispronounces-words.intro: Rebbe had Rebbe Chiya and his sons lead a fast-day prayer, even though Rebbe Chiya could not pronounce some words correctly. Tosfos asks how he could be chosen, since a public chazzan should say every word properly. In [It’s a Miracle](/daf/bava-metzia/106/its-a-miracle), set beside Bava Metzia 106, the Brisker Rav is amazed that this rule could stand even in the way of Moshiach.
tefillah/chazzan-who-mispronounces-words.description: May someone who mispronounces words lead the prayers? Tosfos asks about Rebbe Chiya, and the Brisker Rav draws a lesson, in an article on Bava Metzia 106.

tefillah/conditional-prayers.intro: The Likutei Maharil records a custom not to make a Mi She'beirach for a gravely ill person unless he is known to be alive, to avoid a meaningless prayer. The Nachalas Shiva objected, then offered a compromise: pray that if the sick person is still alive, he should recover. [Of Minhagim And Manhigim](/daf/gittin/33/of-minhagim-and-manhigim), filed on Gittin 33, adds the Maharam Schick's version for someone who may already be healed.
tefillah/conditional-prayers.description: Can a prayer be made conditional, like if he is still ill, heal him? The Nachalas Shiva and the Maharam Schick avoid a meaningless prayer, from Gittin 33.

tefillah/davening-for-israeli-soldiers.intro: Rav Chaim Shmuelevitz, the mashgiach of the Mirrer Yeshiva, applied the Gemara on Bava Basra 10b to soldiers protecting Eretz Yisrael. If the Torah demands gratitude to someone who opens a door for us, surely we owe it to those who risk their lives, so he wrote during the Yom Kippur War that we must daven for them without limit. Rav Yitzhak Pinchas Goldwasser does not know how anyone today cannot cry and pour out his heart for them.
tefillah/davening-for-israeli-soldiers.description: Why Rav Chaim Shmuelevitz wrote that we must daven without limit for the soldiers protecting Eretz Yisrael, based on the Gemara on Bava Basra 10b.

tefillah/davening-for-others-with-feelin.intro: If people already daven for the poor, the blind and the childless, why does the Gemara need to teach that they are like the dead? Tosfos on Nedarim 64b says the teaching is meant to move us to daven harder. [A Powerful Tefillah](/daf/nedarim/64/a-powerful-tefillah) explains that a tefillah filled with feeling is so much stronger that, by comparison, a prayer without it is almost like not davening at all.
tefillah/davening-for-others-with-feelin.description: Why does every bit of feeling count when davening for someone who suffers? Tosfos on Nedarim 64b explains why the Gemara calls them like the dead.

tefillah/davening-for-the-sick-when-visi.intro: The Rema says anyone who visited a sick person and did not pray for him has not done the mitzvah. Rav Moshe Feinstein says the best place to daven is right beside the patient, where the Shechina rests. Rav Shlomo Zalman warns not to frighten the patient, so one may turn away or pray quietly, as discussed in an article on Bava Metzia 30b.
tefillah/davening-for-the-sick-when-visi.description: Must you pray for a sick person when you visit? The Rema says yes, and Rav Moshe and Rav Shlomo Zalman explain how, in an article on Bava Metzia 30b.

tefillah/davening-on-a-raised-platform.intro: Just as nothing could separate a kohen's feet from the floor during the avodah, the Mishnah Berurah says nothing should separate a person from the ground while davening. A platform over three tefachim shows arrogance, but less than that is fine according to most Acharonim. Rav Chaim Kanievsky resolved a seeming contradiction about leaves on Yom Kippur, in a discussion tied to Zevachim 46.
tefillah/davening-on-a-raised-platform.description: May you daven standing on a mat, platform or raised surface? The Mishnah Berurah's three-tefachim rule and Rav Chaim Kanievsky, discussed with Zevachim 46.

tefillah/davening-shemoneh-esrei-sitting.intro: Tefillah takes the place of the korbanos, and avodah done sitting is invalid in Zevachim 23b. Is sitting for Shemoneh Esrei just a flaw, or does the tefillah not count? The Shulchan Aruch lets a rider on a donkey daven without getting off, and Rav Chaim Kanievsky ruled when davening on time beats davening standing.
tefillah/davening-shemoneh-esrei-sitting.description: When may Shemoneh Esrei be said sitting? The Shulchan Aruch's rider on a donkey and Rav Chaim Kanievsky's rulings, from the avodah in Zevachim 23b.

tefillah/days-without-tachanun.intro: People joke that skipping Tachanun brings a Jew such joy, and some even feel a lift when three short verses are left out at Shabbos Minchah. This light opening leads into a real question from Shevuos 10: where does the rule to skip Tachanun on Tishah B'Av come from? The answer runs through the Korban Mussaf and the debate over which days are called a moed.
tefillah/days-without-tachanun.description: Why does skipping Tachanun feel so good, and where do the days without it come from? A light look at tefillah and the Mussaf debate in Shevuos 10.

tefillah/forgetting-hamelech-hakadosh.intro: What if someone says HaKeil HaKadosh instead of HaMelech HaKadosh on the night of Rosh Hashanah? Since Rosh Hashanah 8a ties the day to Rosh Chodesh, one might argue the night was once not yet Rosh Hashanah, so the mistake is minor. The Chofetz Chaim rejects this in the Shaar HaTziyon as a mixed-up formula, though Rav Moshe Feinstein defended the other view.
tefillah/forgetting-hamelech-hakadosh.description: Said HaKeil HaKadosh on Rosh Hashanah night? The Chofetz Chaim says repeat Shemoneh Esrei, while Rav Moshe Feinstein defends leniency. Rosh Hashanah 8a.

tefillah/forgetting-yaaleh-veyavo.intro: Forgetting Yaaleh V'Yavo on Rosh Chodesh by day means repeating Shemoneh Esrei, but not at Maariv, since Beis Din declared the new month only by day. [Obviously, Rosh Hashana Falls Out on Rosh Chodesh](/daf/rosh-hashanah/8/obviously-rosh-hashana-falls-out-on-rosh-chodesh) explains how Rabbeinu Yonah, because Rosh Hashanah 8a links the two days, applies the same logic to a weekday prayer said on Rosh Hashanah night.
tefillah/forgetting-yaaleh-veyavo.description: Why must you repeat Shemoneh Esrei for forgetting Yaaleh V'Yavo by day but not at night? Rabbeinu Yonah links it to Rosh Hashanah night, Rosh Hashanah 8a.

tefillah/four-considered-like-the-dead.intro: Hashem told Moshe that the men who sought his life had died, yet Dasan and Aviram later joined Korach. Nedarim 64b resolves this with a baraisa: a poor person, a metzora, a blind person and one with no children are considered like the dead. Dasan and Aviram had become poor, and Tosfos adds that the teaching changes no halacha but urges us to daven for these people.
tefillah/four-considered-like-the-dead.description: A poor man, a metzora, a blind man and the childless are like the dead, says Nedarim 64b. How it explains Dasan and Aviram, and what Tosfos learns.

tefillah/kavanah-in-shemoneh-esrei.intro: A man told the Chofetz Chaim that his mind wanders in Shemoneh Esrei, so his tefillah is wasted. The Chofetz Chaim told of an apple vendor whose cart tipped over: grab what you can while the animals grab too. Even one bracha said with focus is a great feat, a lesson set beside Zevachim 24 and Dovid HaMelech's part in the Beis HaMikdash.
tefillah/kavanah-in-shemoneh-esrei.description: Is your Shemoneh Esrei lost if your mind wanders? The Chofetz Chaim's apple-cart parable on saving what you can, in a discussion of Zevachim 24.

tefillah/latest-time-for-minchah.intro: The Shulchan Aruch opens the laws of Minchah with a case of barely any time left, and Rav Shlomo Zalman rules that the chazzan must finish by shekiah. The Maharit warns not to wait that long, citing the curse on those who daven at sunset and the lesson of the last shift in Pesachim 65a. [Minutes Till Minchah](/daf/pesachim/65/minutes-till-minchah-pesachim-65) also notes that the Arizal was careful to daven close to sunset.
tefillah/latest-time-for-minchah.description: How late can you daven Minchah? Rav Shlomo Zalman on shekiah, the Maharit's warning against waiting, and the Arizal's practice. Pesachim 65a.

tefillah/mi-shebeirach-for-an-unknown-st.intro: The Maharil says not to make a Mi Shebeirach for a sick person if you don't know how he is now, since the outcome may already be decided. The Nachalas Shiva strongly disagrees: recovery is slow, and the chance of saving a life outweighs a wasted tefillah. In [Past Prayer](/daf/shevuos/37/past-prayer), Rebbe Chanoch Siegel uses Shevuos 37b to say the Maharil meant only a goseis.
tefillah/mi-shebeirach-for-an-unknown-st.description: May you pray for a sick person whose condition you don't know? The Maharil and Nachalas Shiva disagree, and Shevuos 37b on a goseis helps explain.

tefillah/modim-derabbanan.intro: When the chazzan says Modim, the congregation says its own Modim, and the Gemara lists versions from Rebbe Simai, Shmuel, the Nehardeans and Rav Acha Bar Yaakov. Rav Papa says to recite them all, and that is our practice, which [Who Was Rav Papa?](/daf/yoma/67/who-was-rav-papa) fits into a pattern of his rulings, starting from Yoma 67a.
tefillah/modim-derabbanan.description: Modim DeRabbanan joins several texts because Rav Papa said to recite them all. How this prayer fits his pattern of rulings, in a discussion from Yoma 67a.

tefillah/never-too-late-to-pray.intro: Yeshayahu told the sick King Chizkiyahu that he would die, because he had chosen not to marry and have children. Chizkiyahu answered with a tradition from his ancestors: even with a sharp sword on a person's neck, it is never too late to pray. The story, told in connection with Sanhedrin 96, ends with Hashem hearing his tears and adding fifteen years to his life.
tefillah/never-too-late-to-pray.description: Even with a sword on one's neck, it is never too late to pray. Chizkiyahu's tefillah after a decree of death added fifteen years, as in Sanhedrin 96.

tefillah/prayer-on-entering-the-beis-mid.intro: Rebbe Nechunya ben Hakanah said a short prayer each time he entered the beis midrash. Berachos 28b explains that he asked not to stumble in halacha so his friends would rejoice, and that they not stumble so he would rejoice. Rashi, the Chasam Sofer and the Maharsha each read that rejoicing differently, and the prayer is codified in Shulchan Aruch.
tefillah/prayer-on-entering-the-beis-mid.description: Rebbe Nechunya ben Hakanah prayed on entering the beis midrash not to err in halacha. Rashi, Chasam Sofer and Maharsha explain it, from Berachos 28b.

tefillah/praying-about-the-past.intro: The Shulchan Aruch rules that a prayer about the past is wasted, like praying that a commotion in town is not in your house. Rav Scheinberg adds that such a prayer is not just wasted but improper. But Berachos 60a says Hillel heard a scream and was sure it was not from his home, and the Anaf Yosef explains how that fits, in an article filed on Shevuos 37b.
tefillah/praying-about-the-past.description: Why is praying to change what already happened a wasted prayer? The Shulchan Aruch, Rav Scheinberg and Hillel's story in Berachos 60a explain.

tefillah/praying-at-length.intro: Berachos 32b promises that whoever davens at length will not have his prayer returned empty-handed. Yet a few lines later, the Gemara advises someone who prayed and was not answered to daven again. Rabbi Akiva Grunblatt explains that a long tefillah is guaranteed to have an effect, though perhaps not the one the person hoped for.
tefillah/praying-at-length.description: Is a long tefillah guaranteed an answer? Rabbi Akiva Grunblatt explains that it never returns empty, though the effect may differ. From Berachos 32b.

tefillah/praying-for-others-with-the-sam.intro: Bava Kamma 92 teaches that whoever prays for a friend while needing the same thing himself is answered first. Does it still work if you know about the reward? Iyov prayed for his friends and was healed first, and the Mogen Avraham rules that after a bad dream, one should pray first for a friend and then for himself.
tefillah/praying-for-others-with-the-sam.description: One who prays for a friend with the same need is answered first. Iyov, Avrohom Avinu and the Mogen Avraham show how this works, from Bava Kamma 92.

tefillah/praying-from-desperation.intro: Rabbi Nechemiah in Megillah 15b says Esther invited Haman so the Jews would see her as a traitor and turn to Hashem. But facing a decree of destruction, would they really have relied on the queen? The Maharal explains that they would have prayed anyway, yet Esther knew that a prayer born of desperation is stronger, and every added drop of feeling matters.
tefillah/praying-from-desperation.description: Why is a prayer said in desperation more heartfelt? Esther made the Jews feel she had abandoned them so they would pray harder, in Megillah 15b.

tefillah/praying-in-aramaic-alone.intro: Pesachim 87b says Hashem sent the exile to Bavel partly because Aramaic is so close to Hebrew. Still, an individual should not pray in Aramaic, so Yekum Purkan and similar prayers are said with a minyan. [When To Say It In Aramaic](/daf/pesachim/87/when-to-say-it-in-aramaic) covers the exceptions, like praying beside a sick person, where the Shechinah is present.
tefillah/praying-in-aramaic-alone.description: Why are Aramaic prayers like Yekum Purkan said only with a minyan? The rule for an individual, and exceptions such as praying for the sick, Pesachim 87b.

tefillah/praying-in-english.intro: The Mishna in Sotah teaches that one may pray in any language, and the Gemara in Sotah 33a explains that Hashem wants tefillah from the heart. The Shulchan Aruch makes this the halacha, though praying in Hebrew is strongly encouraged for one who understands it. The Chofetz Chaim adds two conditions: the person must understand the language, and more than a few people where he lives must speak it.
tefillah/praying-in-english.description: May you say Shemoneh Esreh in English or another language? Sotah 33a, the Shulchan Aruch and the Chofetz Chaim's conditions for praying in another tongue.

tefillah/reciting-the-aseres-hadibros-da.intro: The Shulchan Aruch opens by saying the Aseres HaDibros should be recited every day, and the Mishnah Berurah explains it as a daily reminder of Ma'amad Har Sinai. Yet the Rema says to say them only privately, so no one thinks the Torah is just ten mitzvos. The question comes up alongside the Luchos in the Aron on Bava Basra 14a.
tefillah/reciting-the-aseres-hadibros-da.description: Why say the Aseres HaDibros every day, but only privately? The Shulchan Aruch, Rema and Mishnah Berurah on this daily reminder of Sinai. Bava Basra 14a.

tefillah/saying-korbanos-before-davening.intro: Each morning we say Parashas HaTamid, the Mishnayos of Eizeh Mekoman and the beraisa of Rebbe Yishmael Omer, so that we learn Torah, Mishnah and Gemara every day. Unlike the main tefillos, these may be said after davening when one is late. As Rabbi Paysach Krohn put it, korbanos are often the first thing to be sacrificed, notes a discussion of Zevachim 47a.
tefillah/saying-korbanos-before-davening.description: Why do we say korbanos each morning, and may they be said after davening when running late? The Shulchan Aruch's reason, discussed with Zevachim 47a.

tefillah/selichos-at-midnight-or-early-m.intro: Some say Selichos at midnight and others rise early to say them before davening. For someone with no family custom, Rav Zilberstein suggests rising early is better, based on Yoma 21a, which teaches that waking early is harder than staying up late. The extra effort is a merit and a sign of love for Hashem, as long as one can concentrate fully.
tefillah/selichos-at-midnight-or-early-m.description: Is it better to say Selichos at midnight or early in the morning? Rav Zilberstein prefers rising early, since Yoma 21a says waking early is harder.

tefillah/shabbos-shopping-before-davenin.intro: If oneg Shabbos is a Torah mitzvah, may one shop for Shabbos food before saying Shema? The Pri Megadim says Shema comes first, since the more frequent mitzvah takes precedence, and the Mishnah Berurah adds that if an item will sell out, one says Shema, shops, and then davens. [Oneg Shabbos](/daf/yevamos/93/oneg-shabbos) on Yevamos 93a brings the Biur Halachah that Shabbos shopping even comes before davening with a minyan.
tefillah/shabbos-shopping-before-davenin.description: May you shop for Shabbos before Shema or davening, or skip a minyan? The Pri Megadim, the Mishnah Berurah and the Biur Halachah, from Yevamos 93a.

tefillah/tefillah-in-place-of-korbanos.intro: The Shulchan Aruch writes that Shemoneh Esrei stands in place of a korban. So it should be said with focused intent, standing, in a fixed place, and ideally in special clothing, like the kohanim's garments. [The Avodah of Shemoneh Esrei](/daf/zevachim/46/the-avodah-of-shemoneh-esrei) links this to Zevachim 46, where wrong intentions can make a korban invalid.
tefillah/tefillah-in-place-of-korbanos.description: Shemoneh Esrei is modeled on the korbanos: intent, standing, a fixed place and special clothing. The Shulchan Aruch's comparison, tied to Zevachim 46.

tefillah/three-steps-back-after-shemoneh.intro: At the end of Shemoneh Esrei we take three steps back and then pray for the Beis HaMikdash to be rebuilt. The Mishna Berura ties this to Nevuchadnezzar, whose steps to honor Hashem gave him the power to destroy it. The trouble is that Sanhedrin 96 says he took four steps, while the Midrash says three, and the Chofetz Chaim offers a way to settle it.
tefillah/three-steps-back-after-shemoneh.description: Why do we step back three times after Shemoneh Esrei and pray for the Beis HaMikdash? The Mishna Berura links it to Nevuchadnezzar in Sanhedrin 96.

tefillah/unanswered-prayers.intro: What happens to sincere prayers that seem to go unanswered? Berachos 32b teaches that a person who prayed and was not answered should daven again, and the Iyun Yaakov says the first time may not have been auspicious. [Prayer And Unity](/daf/berachos/32/prayer-and-unity) adds Rav Aryeh Levin's words to a widow: not one of her tears was wasted.
tefillah/unanswered-prayers.description: Were prayers that seemed unanswered wasted? The Gemara says to daven again, and Rav Aryeh Levin consoles a widow about her tears. From Berachos 32b.

tefillah/unsure-if-you-said-vesein-tal-u.intro: If you are unsure whether you said Vesein Tal Umatar in the first 30 days, you must assume you said the old words out of habit. The Maharam M'Rottenburg suggests saying the phrase 90 times to build the habit at once. [Roaring Lions and Goring Oxen](/daf/bava-kamma/15/roaring-lions-and-goring-oxen) shows his source: Rebbe Meir's reasoning about a goring ox, discussed on Bava Kamma 15b.
tefillah/unsure-if-you-said-vesein-tal-u.description: Unsure if you said Vesein Tal Umatar? Saying it 90 times may build the habit at once, an idea based on Rebbe Meir's goring ox logic, near Bava Kamma 15b.

tefillah/why-do-we-pray.intro: How can prayer change the will of Hashem? Chullin 60b teaches that rain did not fall until Adam was created to pray for it, because Hashem desires the prayers of the righteous. In [Keep In Touch](/daf/chullin/60/keep-in-touch), the Pri Ha'aretz answers with the parable of a king who always meant to support his son and was only waiting for the son to ask.
tefillah/why-do-we-pray.description: Why pray if we cannot change Hashem's will? The Pri Ha'aretz says Hashem wants to give and waits for us to ask. Rain waited for Adam in Chullin 60b.

krias-shema/birchos-krias-shema-out-of-o.intro: Kohanim busy with the avodah had only a few moments to daven, so the sages set a minimum for them, including one of the berachos before Shema. The Rashba learns from Berachos 11 that birchos Krias Shema may be said out of order. He then asks why Ahavah Rabbah needs no opening of Baruch atah when said alone, and answers that a berachah keeps its original text.
krias-shema/birchos-krias-shema-out-of-o.description: May the berachos before Shema be said out of order, as the kohanim did? The Rashba's proof and his answer about Ahavah Rabbah, from Berachos 11.

krias-shema/chassan-saying-shema-on-wedd.intro: A chassan was exempt from Shema on his wedding night, since he could not concentrate, and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said an ordinary groom who says it anyway is showing off. Today the halacha is the reverse. Our usual focus on Shema is so weak that skipping it would be the arrogant choice, as the article on Chullin 105a explains.
krias-shema/chassan-saying-shema-on-wedd.description: Does a chassan say Shema on his wedding night? Once exempt, and saying it was haughty; today he must, since skipping it is arrogant. See Chullin 105a.

krias-shema/interrupting-shema-for-busin.intro: Rav Safra was saying Shema when a customer walked into his store and made an offer. He did not answer, so the customer kept raising the price, thinking he wasn't interested. The Rashbam on Bava Basra 89a tells how Rav Safra finished Shema without interrupting, then sold at the first price.
krias-shema/interrupting-shema-for-busin.description: What if a customer makes an offer while you are saying Shema? Rav Safra stayed silent as the offers rose, a story the Rashbam tells on Bava Basra 89a.

berachos/answering-amen-to-a-childs-brac.intro: Should an adult answer amen when a young child makes a bracha? The Shulchan Aruch says not for a practice bracha, and the Mishnah Berurah adds not below the age of chinuch, but Rav Shlomo Zalman Auerbach held that teaching a child to say amen is itself chinuch. The article on Nedarim 7b shares his habit of saying amen without the final nun, and the Ohr L'tzion's idea of saying most of a pasuk silently.
berachos/answering-amen-to-a-childs-brac.description: Should you answer amen to a young child's bracha? The Shulchan Aruch, Mishnah Berurah and Rav Shlomo Zalman's creative solutions, on Nedarim 7b.

berachos/beracha-at-the-place-of-a-mirac.intro: One who passes a place where he was saved from danger says she'asah li neis ba'makom ha'zeh. The Shulchan Aruch says all his descendants say it too, while the Mishnah Berurah limits later generations to those alive because of the miracle. The Midrash says Yosef said this bracha at the pit on his way back from burying Yaakov, the scene behind Yevamos 65a.
berachos/beracha-at-the-place-of-a-mirac.description: Who says the bracha at the place of a miracle? The Shulchan Aruch, the Mishnah Berurah on descendants, and Yosef at the pit, tied to Yevamos 65a.

berachos/beracha-on-bran-products.intro: The Ran on Pesachim 36b notes that bread made only of bran would take a Shehakol, and the same is true of products like All-Bran cereal. Rabbi Binyamin Forst rules Shehakol on oat-bran cookies, unless they contain regular whole-wheat or oat flour, which makes them Mezonos. Rabbi Vozner notes that most bran bread is not pure bran and takes HaMotzi, while 100% bran bread needs only Shehakol and Borei Nefashos.
berachos/beracha-on-bran-products.description: Which bracha is said on bran cereal, oat-bran cookies or bran bread? Shehakol, Mezonos or HaMotzi, depending on the flour inside. Pesachim 36b.

berachos/berachah-hasemuchah-lechavertah.intro: Most long brachos open and close with Baruch atah, but the second bracha of bentching starts directly with Nodeh lecha. The reason is bracha hasemuchah l'chaveirta: a long bracha said right after another does not need its own opening. [On the Way](/daf/pesachim/104/on-the-way) on Pesachim 104b shows how this rule explains Shomeia Tefillah in Shemoneh Esrei and the opening of Tefillas HaDerech.
berachos/berachah-hasemuchah-lechavertah.description: Why do some long brachos skip the opening Baruch atah? The rule of a bracha that follows another, from bentching to Tefillas HaDerech. Pesachim 104b.

berachos/berachah-on-hearts-of-palm.intro: Hearts of palm are young shoots that would harden into a palm branch. Berachos 36 rules Shehakol, since no farmer would kill a branch and lose his dates. But today peach palms are grown mainly for the hearts, so the old reasoning may not hold, and poskim differ between Ha'adamah and Ha'eitz.
berachos/berachah-on-hearts-of-palm.description: What berachah do you make on hearts of palm? The Gemara says Shehakol, but modern farming leaves poskim split on Ha'adamah or Ha'eitz. From Berachos 36.

berachos/berachah-on-sugar-cane.intro: Sugar cane is not the fruit of a tree but the tree itself, so many Rishonim say its berachah is Ha'adamah. The Shulchan Aruch follows the Rambam, who says Shehakol, and the Mishnah Berurah and Aruch HaShulchan explain that the cane itself is not edible. [Fruits Of Our Labor](/daf/berachos/36/fruits-of-our-labor) uses this to weigh hearts of palm, building on Berachos 36.
berachos/berachah-on-sugar-cane.description: Is sugar cane Ha'adamah or Shehakol? Rishonim say it is the tree itself, while the Rambam calls it inedible. The sugar cane debate builds on Berachos 36.

berachos/berachah-when-eating-on-yom-kip.intro: A person told to eat small amounts on Yom Kippur is doing a mitzvah by guarding his health, so he makes a berachah, even though the Shitah Mekubetzes disagrees. Does he need a new berachah every nine minutes? In [A Minimalist Diet](/daf/chullin/86/a-minimalist-diet), the shochet's single berachah in Chullin 86b and Tosfos's view on davening lead Rav Shlomo Zalman to rule that one berachah carries over.
berachos/berachah-when-eating-on-yom-kip.description: Does someone allowed to eat on Yom Kippur make a berachah, and again every nine minutes? The shochet's one berachah in Chullin 86b guides the answer.

berachos/birchas-ilanos-in-the-southern-.intro: Birchas Ilanos is said on blossoming fruit trees in the spring, but south of the Equator spring comes in Tishrei. The Nitei Gavriel writes that those countries say the beracha in their own spring season. Rav Chaim Kanievsky was asked about a traveler who already said it in Nissan and then went to Australia, and he answered that he may not say it again in Tishrei.
berachos/birchas-ilanos-in-the-southern-.description: When is Birchas Ilanos said south of the Equator, and may someone who said it in Nissan say it again in Australia in Tishrei? Rav Chaim Kanievsky answers.

berachos/birchas-ilanos-on-blossoming-tr.intro: Birchas Ilanos is the blessing said on seeing fruit trees in bloom in the spring. Rav Chaim Kanievsky ruled that women are obligated when they see one, that one tree is enough by the letter of the law though the custom is two, and that it may be said on Shabbos. The custom is not to say it in Adar, yet Rav Moshe Feinstein was seen reciting it as late as Iyar.
berachos/birchas-ilanos-on-blossoming-tr.description: Who says Birchas Ilanos on blossoming fruit trees, and when and where? Rav Chaim Kanievsky on women, Shabbos, Adar, a minyan and how many trees are needed.

berachos/birchas-ilanos-on-potted-or-orl.intro: Can the blessing on blossoming trees be said over a tree in a pot, or one still in its orlah years? Rav Chaim Kanievsky allowed a potted tree with holes in the bottom, while his answers on a pot without holes are recorded as contradictory. For orlah he noted that some are lenient, Rebbe Akiva Eiger permits safek orlah outside Israel, and a tree planted without permission gets the beracha without Shem U'Malchus.
berachos/birchas-ilanos-on-potted-or-orl.description: May Birchas Ilanos be said on a potted tree, a young orlah tree, or a tree planted without permission? Rav Chaim Kanievsky's short answers on each case.

berachos/birkas-hagomel.intro: Rashi in Zevachim 7a lists four people who brought a korban todah: one who crossed the sea, crossed a desert, recovered from serious illness, or was freed from captivity. Today, without korbanos, Chazal set up birkas hagomel in its place. It thanks Hashem, Who bestows good things upon the guilty, and is usually said at krias haTorah before ten men.
berachos/birkas-hagomel.description: Birkas hagomel replaced the korban todah for those who survived the sea, a desert, illness or captivity, as Rashi explains it in Zevachim 7a.

berachos/birkas-hagomel-for-women.intro: Birkas hagomel is said before ten men, usually at krias haTorah, so how does a woman thank Hashem after danger? Some say before ten family members, others in the ezras nashim loud enough for the men to hear. Rav Shlomo Zalman suggested the last bracha of birkas hashachar, which ends with similar words, in a discussion of Zevachim 7a.
berachos/birkas-hagomel-for-women.description: How can a woman say birkas hagomel when it is said before a minyan? Customs and Rav Shlomo Zalman's suggestion, in a discussion growing out of Zevachim 7a.

berachos/borei-pri-haeitz-on-bushes-and-.intro: Blueberries grow on bushes, and kiwis and grapes grow on vines, yet the bracha on all of them is ha'eitz. The halachic idea of a tree does not match the English word: a plant that lives for many years while producing fruit counts as an eitz. Tied to Kiddushin 39, the article notes that one may even say Birkas Ha'ilanos on a flowering blueberry bush.
berachos/borei-pri-haeitz-on-bushes-and-.description: Why is the bracha on blueberries, grapes and kiwis ha'eitz when they grow on bushes and vines? The halachic idea of a tree, tied to Kiddushin 39.

berachos/bracha-acharonah-on-hot-coffee.intro: A berachah acharonah requires drinking a revi'is within a set time, but hot coffee is sipped slowly. Rav Yaakov Kuli proved from kutach haBavli in Pesachim 43 that the time frame never stretches, and the Mishnah Berurah notes the custom is not to say one, while the Minchas Chinuch disagrees. [Coffee Break](/daf/pesachim/43/coffee-break) shares the Mishnah Berurah's advice to leave three ounces and drink them once they cool.
berachos/bracha-acharonah-on-hot-coffee.description: Do you say a bracha acharonah on hot coffee you sip slowly? Rav Yaakov Kuli, the Minchas Chinuch and the Mishnah Berurah's advice. Pesachim 43.

berachos/bracha-on-charoses.intro: Tosfos and the Rambam hold that charoses at the Seder is a real mitzvah, not just a custom. So does it need its own bracha? The Rambam first wrote that one says Al achilas charoses but later ruled that no bracha is said, and the Tur explains, as discussed on Pesachim 116a, that the bracha on marror covers it, just as the bracha on the lulav covers the other species.
berachos/bracha-on-charoses.description: If charoses is a mitzvah, why is there no bracha on it? The Rambam's change of mind and the Tur's comparison to the lulav, on Pesachim 116a.

berachos/bracha-on-dessert-during-a-meal.intro: Why would a great rav in Europe always eat his watermelon with challah? The Chofetz Chaim first ruled that dessert in a bread meal needs its own bracha, then changed his mind once dessert became a normal part of meals. Rav Elyashiv advised eating dessert with bread to avoid the doubt, as the Brisker Rav did, in a discussion that starts in Chullin 44b.
berachos/bracha-on-dessert-during-a-meal.description: Does dessert after Hamotzi need its own bracha? The Chofetz Chaim changed his view, and some eat dessert with bread. Rav Moshe on ice cream. Chullin 44b.

berachos/bracha-on-seeing-a-rainbow.intro: The Gemara records two versions of the bracha on a rainbow: one says Hashem remembers the covenant, the other says He is trustworthy in His covenant and fulfills His word. Rav Papa rules that we say both, and the halacha follows him. A discussion that begins on Yoma 67a points to this as one of several places where Rav Papa joined opinions together.
berachos/bracha-on-seeing-a-rainbow.description: The bracha on a rainbow joins two versions in the Gemara, since Rav Papa said to say both. A pattern in his rulings, explored in a discussion of Yoma 67a.

berachos/doubt-between-haeitz-and-haadam.intro: When unsure whether a food is a tree fruit or a vegetable, the well-known rule is to say Ha'adamah. A Ha'adamah said on a fruit still counts, but a Ha'eitz said on a true vegetable does not. Building on Berachos 36, the Mishnah Berurah adds that even on sugar cane, Ha'eitz works after the fact.
berachos/doubt-between-haeitz-and-haadam.description: Unsure whether to say Ha'eitz or Ha'adamah? Why Ha'adamah covers you, and when Ha'eitz still works after the fact, per the Mishnah Berurah. Berachos 36.

berachos/forgot-to-say-asher-yatzar.intro: If someone forgot asher yatzar and then used the restroom again, the Shulchan Aruch says to recite it twice, since there were two reasons to give thanks. The Mishnah Berurah rules once and advises saying it right away so as not to lose the bracha, a case [Many Thanks Or Just One?](/daf/zevachim/7/many-thanks-or-just-one) uses to explore Zevachim 7a.
berachos/forgot-to-say-asher-yatzar.description: Forgot asher yatzar and used the restroom again: say it once or twice? The Shulchan Aruch and the Mishnah Berurah differ, in a discussion of Zevachim 7a.

berachos/gomel-for-several-dangers.intro: The Pri HaEitz discusses a man who crossed a desert, fell ill at sea and was captured by pirates, then went free. Should he say hagomel once or four times? Some Acharonim prove from Rashi in Zevachim 7a that one korban todah, and so one bracha, covers all, and the Mishnah Berurah rules to say it once.
berachos/gomel-for-several-dangers.description: Survived several dangers? Should you say hagomel once or for each one? Proofs from asher yatzar, bentching and Rashi in Zevachim 7a, and the ruling.

berachos/hatov-vehameitiv-on-a-new-menor.intro: Rav Dovid Feinstein noted that when a family receives a new Chanukah menorah as a gift, the husband should say HaTov VeHaMeitiv, the bracha for an item that benefits several people. Husband and wife share the mitzvah of Chanukah lights. The article on Menachos 75b asks if new candlesticks work the same way, and why Rav Mordechai Eliyahu had a kallah say Shehechiyanu on them.
berachos/hatov-vehameitiv-on-a-new-menor.description: Does a couple say HaTov VeHaMeitiv or Shehechiyanu on a new menorah or candlesticks? Rav Dovid Feinstein's ruling, in an article on Menachos 75b.

berachos/hefsek-after-a-berachah.intro: A real interruption between a berachah and its mitzvah can make the berachah wasted. Rashi rules that someone unsure which of two animals needs semichah makes no berachah, since leaning on the wrong one first would be a hefsek. The article on Eruvin 49 explains why picking up a doubtful esrog after the lulav is different: the mitzvah has already begun, so a short pause does not break it.
berachos/hefsek-after-a-berachah.description: When does an action between a berachah and its mitzvah count as a hefsek? Rashi on semichah and the doubtful esrog show the line, discussed on Eruvin 49.

berachos/hefsek-between-beracha-and-mitz.intro: If an unrelated action comes between a bracha and its mitzvah, the bracha may be wasted. Rashi rules that one unsure which of two animals is the shelamim leans on both without a bracha, since leaning on the wrong one first would be a hefsek. Rav Yitzchok Zev Soloveitchik distinguishes the four minim, where the mitzvah has already begun, in a discussion connected to Sukkah 46.
berachos/hefsek-between-beracha-and-mitz.description: When does an action between a bracha and the mitzvah make the bracha void? Rashi on semichah and Rav Yitzchok Zev Soloveitchik's answer, Sukkah 46.

berachos/order-of-berachos-on-foods.intro: The usual order of berachos runs from hamotzi and mezonos through ha'eitz, ha'adamah and shehakol, but a favorite food can come first, and the seven species win between two fruits. So what about an apple, a pickle and a grape, liked in that order? In [A Cornucopia of Blessings](/daf/gittin/83/a-cornucopia-of-blessings), tied to a paradox in Gittin 83a, the Steipler and Rav Wosner both start with the grape.
berachos/order-of-berachos-on-foods.description: Which berachah comes first with several foods on the table? Favorite foods, the seven species and an apple, pickle and grape puzzle, tied to Gittin 83a.

berachos/saying-berachos-near-a-bathroom.intro: At Camp Romimu, the back of each bunk held cubbies, sinks and commodes, separated only by partitions that did not reach the floor. Rabbi Shimon Eider ruled that these did not count as a halachic wall, so no brachos could be said there. In [Of Giving and Receiving](/daf/kiddushin/6/of-giving-and-receiving), tied to Kiddushin 6b, his solution was a tzuras ha'pesach to wall off the commodes.
berachos/saying-berachos-near-a-bathroom.description: May brachos be said near toilets behind partitions that do not reach the floor? Rabbi Shimon Eider's tzuras ha'pesach idea, in a piece on Kiddushin 6b.

berachos/saying-hashems-name-in-vain.intro: Nedarim 7b teaches that one who hears a friend say Hashem's name in vain must put him in excommunication, and the Ran adds that it violates the command to fear Hashem. [Not Saying Hashem’s Name in Vain](/daf/nedarim/7/not-saying-hashems-name-in-vain) shows how, according to Reish Lakish in Nedarim 10b, the Sages invented kinuyei nedarim, substitute words for vows, so people would not slip into using Hashem's name alone.
berachos/saying-hashems-name-in-vain.description: How serious is saying Hashem's name in vain? Nedarim 7b, and why the Sages created substitute words for vows according to Reish Lakish in Nedarim 10b.

berachos/shehecheyanu-at-a-bar-mitzvah.intro: Menachos 75b says one recites Shehechiyanu on bringing a mincha, and the manuscript Rashi applies this to a first-time mitzvah. The Pri Toar extends it to a bar mitzvah boy's first tefillin, though the Mishnah Berurah rules he should not. The solutions: a new suit, Rav Shlomo Zalman Auerbach's gift of tefillin, and Rav Mordechai Eliyahu's new candlesticks for a kallah.
berachos/shehecheyanu-at-a-bar-mitzvah.description: Should a bar mitzvah boy say Shehechiyanu at his first tefillin? The Pri Toar, the Mishnah Berurah and a new suit or gifted tefillin, from Menachos 75b.

berachos/shehecheyanu-on-a-first-time-mi.intro: Shehecheyanu is usually said on mitzvos that come at a set time of year, but what about doing an everyday mitzvah for the first time in one's life? A manuscript version of Rashi on Menachos 75 reads the Gemara this way, and the Rema rules that a shochet says it the first time he covers the blood. The Pri Chadash calls it a dispute and applies safek berachos l'hakeil.
berachos/shehecheyanu-on-a-first-time-mi.description: Does one say Shehecheyanu the first time he does an everyday mitzvah? The manuscript Rashi, the Rema on covering blood and the Pri Chadash, on Menachos 75.

berachos/shehecheyanu-on-the-lulav.intro: Sukkah 42a teaches that lifting the arba minim fulfills the mitzvah, but when is Shehechiyanu said: at binding the lulav or at first taking it? The Smag explains that one person may bind 100 lulavim for 100 people, so everyone says it at the first taking on Sukkos. The Ritva advises having someone else bind the lulav, staying clear of the doubt altogether.
berachos/shehecheyanu-on-the-lulav.description: Is Shehechiyanu on the lulav said when binding it or when first taking it on Sukkos? The Smag, the Ritva and the Mishnah Berurah, from Sukkah 42a.

berachos/shehecheyanu-on-the-sukkah.intro: Tosfos on Sukkah 46a hold that a Shehechiyanu said while building the sukkah covers the yom tov as well, though one said indoors on a rainy night does not cover the sukkah. [What Bracha Do You Make on the Sukkah?](/daf/sukkah/56/what-bracha-do-you-make-on-the-sukkah) also asks whether someone who forgot can still say it as late as Hoshana Rabba, and what happens when Kiddush is made in the sukkah during heavy rain.
berachos/shehecheyanu-on-the-sukkah.description: When is Shehechiyanu said on the sukkah: at building it, at Kiddush, in the rain, or on Hoshana Rabba? Tosfos and the Mishnah Berurah, from Sukkah 46a.

berachos/smelling-the-esrog-on-sukkos.intro: The Gemara permits smelling the esrog during Sukkos. So why refuse a friend who asks to smell a beautiful one? [Shaking Shailos](/daf/sukkah/42/shaking-shailos) explains, around Sukkah 42a, that the Shulchan Aruch raises a doubt whether the bracha on fragrant fruit is said on a mitzvah esrog, so it is better to wait until after Sukkos.
berachos/smelling-the-esrog-on-sukkos.description: May you smell your esrog during Sukkos? The Gemara allows it, but the Shulchan Aruch doubts the bracha on its fragrance. A look tied to Sukkah 42a.

berachos/time-limit-for-eating-a-kezayis.intro: A berachah rishonah is said even on a crumb, but a berachah acharonah requires a k'zayis eaten within k'dei achilas p'ras, somewhere between two and nine minutes. For drinks, the Mishnah Berurah understands the Shulchan Aruch to require a revi'is in two gulps, while the Vilna Gaon applies the same time as for food. The article on Pesachim 43 shows how the kutach dip suggests the time frame stays the same for every food.
berachos/time-limit-for-eating-a-kezayis.description: How fast must you eat a k'zayis or drink a revi'is to need a bracha acharonah? K'dei achilas p'ras for food, drinks and dips, from Pesachim 43.

hamotzi-and-bread/braiding-challah-on-yo.intro: When baking on Yom Tov, may you braid your challos? The Be'er Moshe says yes, since a braid is not a meaningful shape, but a challah shaped like a ladder or a key is not allowed, and the Chayei Adam forbids shaping it into a bird, by hand or with a mold. The rules grow from the discussion of shaping meat in Beitzah 28a.
hamotzi-and-bread/braiding-challah-on-yo.description: May challah be braided or shaped like a key or bird on Yom Tov? The Be'er Moshe and Chayei Adam separate plain from meaningful shapes, Beitzah 28a.

hamotzi-and-bread/burnt-challah-for-lech.intro: Lechem mishneh calls for two whole loaves, but what if part of a challah burned until it cannot be eaten? The Mekom Shmuel applies Ravina's rule from Chullin 70, that something destined to be cut off counts as already cut off, so such a loaf is not whole. The Mishnah Berurah is more lenient, and a small inedible spot is generally fine.
hamotzi-and-bread/burnt-challah-for-lech.description: Does a challah with a burnt, inedible spot still count as whole for lechem mishneh? The Mekom Shmuel applies Ravina's rule from Chullin 70 to the question.

hamotzi-and-bread/buying-bakery-challah-.intro: The Rema writes that one should not deviate from the custom of baking at home for Shabbos, and the Biur Halachah criticizes buying from a bakery. The Ohr L'Tzion says this was aimed at buying weekday bread from non-Jewish bakeries. Rav Elyashiv rules that one who enjoys bakery challah more is fulfilling oneg Shabbos in the best way, as the article on Menachos 96b explains.
hamotzi-and-bread/buying-bakery-challah-.description: Is buying bakery challah for Shabbos a slight to Shabbos? The Rema, Biur Halachah and Rav Elyashiv's oneg Shabbos ruling, in an article on Menachos 96b.

hamotzi-and-bread/clear-plastic-challah-.intro: Does a see-through challah cover do the job? If the covering shows the meal is for Shabbos, or recalls the dew over the manna, a clear plastic cover is fine. But [A Challah Covering Quiz](/daf/pesachim/100/a-challah-covering-quiz-pesachim-100) notes on Pesachim 100 that if the cover protects the challah from shame during Kiddush, Rav Nissim Karelitz rules a visible challah is not hidden, while Rav Shlomo Zalman disagrees.
hamotzi-and-bread/clear-plastic-challah-.description: Can you use a clear plastic challah cover? It depends on why we cover the challah, and Rav Nissim Karelitz and Rav Shlomo Zalman differ. Pesachim 100.

hamotzi-and-bread/covering-the-challah-d.intro: Why cover the challah during Kiddush? Tosfos on Pesachim 100a cites Rav Achai Gaon's reason of showing the meal is for Shabbos, and the reminder of the dew that protected the manna, while other Rishonim say it spares the challah the shame of its bracha coming after the wine. Each reason leads to different answers, from a kiddush with only cake to a guest's own roll at a large meal.
hamotzi-and-bread/covering-the-challah-d.description: Three reasons for covering the challah during Kiddush: kavod Shabbos, the dew on the manna and the challah's shame, and how they differ. Pesachim 100a.

hamotzi-and-bread/dipping-challah-in-sal.intro: Many people dip the piece of challah in salt three times after Hamotzi. The Mishnah Berurah cites this as a custom al pi Kabbalah. [Worth Its Salt](/daf/menachos/20/worth-its-salt-menachos-20) ties it to the salt placed on every korban in Menachos 20a, and adds that the mitzvah is fulfilled just by having salt on the table, even without putting any on the challah.
hamotzi-and-bread/dipping-challah-in-sal.description: Why do many dip challah in salt three times after Hamotzi? The Mishnah Berurah's kabbalistic custom and the salt of the korbanos in Menachos 20a.

hamotzi-and-bread/hamotzi-on-a-whole-loa.intro: Even on a weekday, there is a mitzvah to say Hamotzi over a whole loaf and slice it only afterward. The Rokeach takes Rav Chisda's toothpick idea from Eruvin 81, and the Shulchan Aruch rules that a roll cut in two should be pinned together to look whole. The Magen Avraham questions whether this effort is really needed on an ordinary day.
hamotzi-and-bread/hamotzi-on-a-whole-loa.description: Should Hamotzi be said over a whole loaf even on a weekday? The Rokeach, the Shulchan Aruch and the Magen Avraham on a toothpick fix, drawn from Eruvin 81.

hamotzi-and-bread/interruption-between-h.intro: Uncle Dov makes Hamotzi and only then spots the saltshaker at the far end of the table, so may he ask for it? The Vilna Gaon explains that salt must be on the table beforehand so no one says pass the salt, an interruption between the bracha and eating. Bedieved the bracha still stands, but the Mishnah Berurah says to eat right away, as the article on Menachos 20a explains.
hamotzi-and-bread/interruption-between-h.description: May one ask for salt after Hamotzi before eating? The Vilna Gaon and Mishnah Berurah on avoiding a hefsek, with a Shabbos table story on Menachos 20a.

hamotzi-and-bread/keeping-challah-warm-f.intro: Many leave the challah in the oven on Friday so it is warm for the meal. Menachos 96b describes the Lechem Hapanim staying warm all week by a miracle, and Tosafos in Chagigah suggests it was kept in the oven until it was placed on the Shulchan. Since kabbalistic sources see our challah as a reminder of the Lechem Hapanim, the warm challah becomes a small reenactment of the Mikdash.
hamotzi-and-bread/keeping-challah-warm-f.description: Why keep challah warm in the oven on Friday? The Lechem Hapanim stayed warm by a miracle, and Tosafos says it was kept in the oven, from Menachos 96b.

hamotzi-and-bread/machine-matzah-for-lec.intro: Machine matzos are baked joined together and broken apart right after. Are they whole loaves for lechem mishneh? [Piecing It Together](/daf/shevuos/42/piecing-it-together) uses Rebbe Meir's idea in Shevuos 42b, that what is meant to be cut is seen as cut, so the Yerushah Pleitah counts them as whole, and Rav Simcha Bunim Cohen extends this to pieces of a sectional challah.
hamotzi-and-bread/machine-matzah-for-lec.description: Do machine matzos or pieces of a sectional challah count as whole loaves for lechem mishneh? The Yerushah Pleitah's view, building on Shevuos 42b.

hamotzi-and-bread/salt-on-the-table-at-h.intro: The Shulchan Aruch HaRav says salt belongs on the table before Hamotzi for the honor of the bracha, and the Vilna Gaon says it prevents an interruption. The Rema adds that our table is compared to the mizbe'ach, where every korban was salted, as Menachos 20a teaches. He calls it a mitzvah and a segulah for protection.
hamotzi-and-bread/salt-on-the-table-at-h.description: Why is salt placed on the table before Hamotzi? The honor of the bracha, avoiding a hefsek, and the table as a mizbe'ach, all tied to Menachos 20a.

hamotzi-and-bread/sliced-bread-for-leche.intro: Can a full bag of sliced challah count as a whole loaf for lechem mishneh? The Netziv says yes, since the bag joins the slices into one unit, but Rav Shlomo Zalman Auerbach says not to rely on it unless there is no other choice, a debate that [The Greatest Article Since Sliced Bread?](/daf/zevachim/105/the-greatest-article-since-sliced-bread) traces to Tosafos in Zevachim 105b.
hamotzi-and-bread/sliced-bread-for-leche.description: Does a full bag of sliced challah count as whole for lechem mishneh? The Netziv, Rav Shlomo Zalman and Tosafos in Zevachim 105b on toothpicks and slices.

hamotzi-and-bread/throwing-challah-at-th.intro: May a father toss challah to his family to speed things up? The Shulchan Aruch forbids throwing food, and the Magen Avraham says not to throw bread even onto a clean table, while the K'sav Sofer regularly tossed challah since it would not be ruined. His son even argued from Zevachim 62b, where sacrificial parts were thrown onto the Altar, that tossing is preferred.
hamotzi-and-bread/throwing-challah-at-th.description: May you toss challah to people at the Shabbos table? The Magen Avraham, the K'sav Sofer's practice and a novel proof from the Altar in Zevachim 62b.

hamotzi-and-bread/throwing-pastries-at-a.intro: Throwing bread is disrespectful no matter how you slice it. [The Friday Night Food Fight](/daf/zevachim/62/the-friday-night-food-fight) cites Rav Elyashiv, who says mini cakes, pastries and cookies should not go into aufruf bags, even wrapped, while a view based on the Vilna Gaon limits the stringency to actual bread, in a discussion tied to Zevachim 62b.
hamotzi-and-bread/throwing-pastries-at-a.description: May wrapped cakes and pastries be thrown at a chasan at an aufruf? Rav Elyashiv says no, while a view based on the Vilna Gaon differs, from Zevachim 62b.

hamotzi-and-bread/toothpicks-for-lechem-.intro: Can two halves of a roll joined with toothpicks count as a whole loaf for lechem mishneh? The Shulchan Aruch says yes, but others argue that toothpicks only fool the neighbors in Rav Chisda's eruv case in Eruvin 81, not Hashem. The Chelkas Yaakov says a whole loaf is about appearance, and the Elyah Rabba allows it only when no real whole loaf is available.
hamotzi-and-bread/toothpicks-for-lechem-.description: Do two halves of a roll joined with toothpicks count as whole for lechem mishneh? The Shulchan Aruch, the Chelkas Yaakov and others, based on Eruvin 81.

hamotzi-and-bread/washing-hands-for-wet-.intro: Wet foods are more prone to tumah, so the rabbis required washing before eating food dipped in one of the seven liquids, as Pesachim 115a records. Some Rishonim disagree, and the Lechem Chamudos says the custom was lenient. The Mishnah Berurah still says to wash without a berachah, but food usually eaten with a fork needs no washing, even when eaten by hand.
hamotzi-and-bread/washing-hands-for-wet-.description: Do we still wash before food dipped in the seven liquids? The Shulchan Aruch, Lechem Chamudos and Mishnah Berurah on wet food, from Pesachim 115a.

hamotzi-and-bread/washing-hands-for-wet-.intro: Chullin 106a rules that washing for dry fruit is forbidden as haughty. But Pesachim 115a requires washing before food dipped in a liquid, and the Mishnah Berurah says to wash without a berachah. In [In a Pickle](/daf/chullin/106/in-a-pickle), the Aruch HaShulchan notes most people did not wash for wet pickles, and Rav Shlomo Zalman exempts a pickle eaten with kugel.
hamotzi-and-bread/washing-hands-for-wet-.description: Must you wash your hands before eating a wet pickle? The Shulchan Aruch, Vilna Gaon and Aruch HaShulchan on wet foods, from Pesachim 115a and Chullin 106a.

hamotzi-and-bread/where-to-cut-the-chall.intro: Where should you start cutting the bread after Hamotzi? On Sanhedrin 102b, King Menashe appears to Rav Ashi in a dream and teaches that one cuts from where it begins to bake. The Toras Chaim gives the practice symbolic meaning even on Shabbos, while the Aruch HaShulchan rules that evenly baked rolls need no incision.
hamotzi-and-bread/where-to-cut-the-chall.description: Where do you start cutting the challah? King Menashe taught Rav Ashi in a dream on Sanhedrin 102b, and the poskim discuss the incision on Shabbos.

birkas-hamazon/birshus-hakohanim-in-zimu.intro: A non-kohen who leads bentching shows respect by announcing that he does so with the consent of the kohanim present. At one pidyon haben, the leader skipped it, saying he did not know a kohen was there. In [Do You Need a Kohein to Perform a Pidyon HaBen?](/daf/kiddushin/8/do-you-need-a-kohein-to-perform-a-pidyon-haben), tied to Kiddushin 8a, the Chasam Sofer came to his defense with a quip.
birkas-hamazon/birshus-hakohanim-in-zimu.description: Why does a non-kohen leading bentching say birshus hakohanim, and must he at a pidyon haben? A quip of the Chasam Sofer, in a story tied to Kiddushin 8a.

birkas-hamazon/fourth-berachah-of-bentch.intro: The fourth berachah of bentching was added later, to thank Hashem that the victims of Beitar were allowed burial. Berachos 49 says Hashem's kingship is mentioned extra times in it, because the third berachah, which speaks of the kingdom of David, does not mention it. Its three mentions are Melech HaOlam, Malkeinu and HaMelech HaTov.
birkas-hamazon/fourth-berachah-of-bentch.description: Why does HaTov VeHaMeitiv mention Hashem's kingship three times? The fourth berachah of bentching, added after Beitar, makes up for the third. Berachos 49.

birkas-hamazon/hat-and-jacket-for-bentch.intro: A businessman who wore a hat and jacket for bentching felt awkward doing so after meals at restaurant meetings. Rav Chaim Kanievsky told him to keep the custom, citing the Mishna Berura that this is proper attire for bentching, and added that it is a segulah for wealth. Soon after, standing up to get his hat closed a real estate deal, when the other side thought he was walking away.
birkas-hamazon/hat-and-jacket-for-bentch.description: Should a businessman wear a hat and jacket to bentch at a restaurant meeting? Rav Chaim Kanievsky's answer, the Mishna Berura, and a segulah for wealth.

birkas-hamazon/leaving-before-sheva-brac.intro: One should not leave a Sheva Brachos meal before bentching and the blessings, and Rav Moshe Feinstein noted this applies to men and women alike. If someone must leave early, there is room to be lenient based on the Aruch HaShulchan. Tied to Kesubos 8, the Sovaya Semachos offers a series of ways to plan ahead, such as not eating bread or finishing and bentching before the others.
birkas-hamazon/leaving-before-sheva-brac.description: May a guest leave a Sheva Brachos meal before bentching? Rav Moshe Feinstein, the Aruch HaShulchan and ways to plan ahead, tied to Kesubos 8.

birkas-hamazon/melech-in-yaaleh-veyavo-i.intro: The Shulchan Aruch warns against equating David's kingship with Hashem's in the third berachah of bentching. The Rema cites those who skip Melech at the end of Yaaleh VeYavo, and the Mishnah Berurah quotes the Magen Avraham not to object to those who say it. That is why some bentchers print the word in parentheses, building on Berachos 49.
birkas-hamazon/melech-in-yaaleh-veyavo-i.description: Should you skip Melech in Yaaleh VeYavo in bentching? The Rema, Magen Avraham and Mishnah Berurah, and why it is in parentheses. Building on Berachos 49.

birkas-hamazon/shehasimcha-bimono-at-a-s.intro: The Maharshal was so sure a siyum is a seudas mitzvah that he ruled to add shehasimcha bimono to bentching there, as at a wedding. At the first siyum where he tried it, something unpleasant happened, and he saw it as punishment for a new halacha with no source in earlier poskim. [The Simcha of a Siyum](/daf/taanis/26/the-simcha-of-a-siyum) explains why he retracted, in a discussion that begins on Taanis 26b.
birkas-hamazon/shehasimcha-bimono-at-a-s.description: Should shehasimcha bimono be said in bentching at a siyum? The Maharshal ruled it should, then retracted after his first try. A look from Taanis 26b.

birkas-hamazon/unsure-if-you-bentched.intro: A man who ate a satisfying bread meal has a Torah obligation to bentch, so if he is unsure whether he did, he must bentch. For a woman, Rebbe Akiva Eiger applies a double doubt and says she should not, while the Mishnah Berurah says she does not lose by bentching. The article on Nedarim 80b notes that Rav Shlomo Zalman rules that both men and women should bentch while the time has not passed.
birkas-hamazon/unsure-if-you-bentched.description: Not sure if you bentched after bread? Why a man must bentch again, and the debate over women, from Rebbe Akiva Eiger to Rav Shlomo Zalman. Nedarim 80b.

birkas-hamazon/womens-obligation-in-bent.intro: The Gemara in Berachos leaves open whether women are obligated in bentching by Torah law, perhaps because only those obligated in bris milah have a Torah obligation. Women certainly have at least a rabbinic obligation. The article on Nedarim 80b shows how this unresolved doubt shapes what a woman should do when she cannot remember whether she bentched.
birkas-hamazon/womens-obligation-in-bent.description: Are women obligated in Birkas HaMazon by Torah law or only rabbinically? The Gemara leaves it open, with practical results discussed on Nedarim 80b.

kiddush-and-havdalah/chamar-medina-for-k.intro: When wine is not used, Kiddush on Shabbos day may be made on chamar medina, a respected local drink. The Chazon Ish and Ketzos HaShulchan held no drink today truly qualifies, but Rav Moshe Feinstein ruled that beer and liquor in America do. Orange juice, coffee, milk and soda are less clear, says a discussion of Kiddush tied to Zevachim 31b, so ask a rav.
kiddush-and-havdalah/chamar-medina-for-k.description: Which drinks count as chamar medina for Kiddush? The Chazon Ish, and Rav Moshe Feinstein on beer and liquor in America, in a discussion of Zevachim 31b.

kiddush-and-havdalah/children-and-late-h.intro: In summer, Havdalah can come long after a child's bedtime. The Mishna Berura says a child who understands Shabbos should be trained to hear it, but waking him goes against chinuch, which does not demand physical discomfort. Rav Chaim Kanievsky ruled that such children are exempt from Havdalah, in a discussion tied to Bava Metzia 5a.
kiddush-and-havdalah/children-and-late-h.description: What should parents do when Havdalah falls after a child's bedtime? Early Havdalah, Sunday Havdalah or none at all, in an article on Bava Metzia 5a.

kiddush-and-havdalah/delaying-kiddush-on.intro: Is it better to make Kiddush right at nightfall on Friday night, or to wait until one is hungry? In the Mishnah Berurah, the Chofetz Chaim allows a delay for greater Oneg Shabbos, but not when it hurts shalom bayis or keeps staff or guests waiting. [Be Our Guest](/daf/rosh-hashanah/6/be-our-guest) connects this to Rava's rule on Rosh Hashanah 6a about delaying tzedakah.
kiddush-and-havdalah/delaying-kiddush-on.description: May Kiddush be delayed on Friday night to enjoy the meal more? The Chofetz Chaim's limits for guests, family and staff, and Rava in Rosh Hashanah 6a.

kiddush-and-havdalah/havdalah-after-plag.intro: The Shulchan Aruch allows an adult in a pressing case to say Havdalah after plag hamincha, though he may not do melacha until night and so skips the candle. The Mishna Berura discourages it, since it looks strange in daylight and he may forget it is still Shabbos. [Children and Havdalah](/daf/bava-metzia/5/children-and-havdalah), filed on Bava Metzia 5a, asks whether children should use it.
kiddush-and-havdalah/havdalah-after-plag.description: May Havdalah be said after plag hamincha, before Shabbos ends? The Shulchan Aruch allows it in a pinch, but the Mishna Berura warns, Bava Metzia 5a.

kiddush-and-havdalah/havdalah-on-sunday.intro: Someone who missed Havdalah on Motzei Shabbos says it on Sunday, without the spices or candle, and Rav Elyashiv reportedly advised this for children. The B'tzel Hachochma, based on Bava Metzia 5a, argues that Chazal never obligated children in make-up mitzvos. Rabbi Simcha Bunim Cohen reports that the widespread custom is that children skip it.
kiddush-and-havdalah/havdalah-on-sunday.description: Can a missed Havdalah be said on Sunday, and must children make it up? Rav Elyashiv and the B'tzel Hachochma differ, based on Bava Metzia 5a.

kiddush-and-havdalah/how-much-to-drink-f.intro: After Kiddush, a cheekful must be drunk within k'dei achilas p'ras, and if several listeners share it, the Mishnah Berurah says they must all finish in that same time. The Afikei Yam finds this odd, since separate people drink separately. In [The Kiddush Cup Runneth Over](/daf/zevachim/31/the-kiddush-cup-runneth-over), the Biur Halachah answers from Zevachim 31b, where two people's half-kezayis intentions combine.
kiddush-and-havdalah/how-much-to-drink-f.description: How much Kiddush wine must be drunk, how fast, and may listeners share it? The Mishnah Berurah's time limit, defended with a proof from Zevachim 31b.

kiddush-and-havdalah/kiddush-cup-size.intro: How big must a Kiddush cup be? A revi'is is at least 2.9 ounces, 3.3 is more mainstream, and many use about 4.5 ounces on Friday night. The Mishnah Berurah quotes no one who disputes the need for a revi'is, but the Taz allows a one-ounce shot of schnapps, a view many chassidic masters followed, in a discussion tied to Zevachim 31b.
kiddush-and-havdalah/kiddush-cup-size.description: How much must a Kiddush cup hold in ounces, and is a shot glass enough for schnapps? The Mishnah Berurah and the Taz, in a discussion tied to Zevachim 31b.

kiddush-and-havdalah/kiddush-on-liquor.intro: Many chassidim make Shabbos morning Kiddush on liquor, while Litvishe custom sticks to wine or grape juice. The Mishnah Berurah allows liquor for the daytime Kiddush, even for one who simply prefers it, and Rav Moshe Feinstein counts liquor as chamar medina. [Analysis of Halachic Requirements for Kiddush on Liquor](/daf/zevachim/31/analysis-of-halachic-requirements-for-kiddush-on-liquor) adds the conditions, with a proof from Zevachim 31b.
kiddush-and-havdalah/kiddush-on-liquor.description: May Shabbos morning Kiddush be made on whiskey? The Mishnah Berurah and Rav Moshe allow it, with conditions on cup size and drinking, tied to Zevachim 31b.

kiddush-and-havdalah/kiddush-on-yom-kipp.intro: Does a sick person who must eat on Yom Kippur make Kiddush? The Magen Avraham says no, but in 1848 Yom Kippur fell on Shabbos, and Rebbe Akiva Eiger suggests the weekly Shabbos Kiddush may then apply to those who eat. In [Required Eating on Yom Kippur?](/daf/shevuos/28/required-eating-on-yom-kippur), filed on Shevuos 28, this helps judge the story of Rav Yisrael Salanter's Kiddush.
kiddush-and-havdalah/kiddush-on-yom-kipp.description: Does someone who must eat on Yom Kippur make Kiddush? The Magen Avraham and Rebbe Akiva Eiger on Yom Kippur that falls on Shabbos, from Shevuos 28.

kiddush-and-havdalah/kiddush-wine-with-a.intro: The Rambam rules that Kiddush may be made only on wine fit for the mizbeach, so wine mixed with honey is out, while the Ramban, Rashba and others allow it. The Pri Megadim says the Rambam would forbid added sugar too. Building on Menachos 58a, [Wine and Honey](/daf/menachos/58/wine-and-honey) explains chaptalization and why wine without added sugar may be a hiddur.
kiddush-and-havdalah/kiddush-wine-with-a.description: Is wine with added honey or sugar fit for Kiddush? The Rambam, Shulchan Aruch and Pri Megadim, plus how wine is made, building on Menachos 58a.

kiddush-and-havdalah/light-bulb-for-havd.intro: The Gemara in Pesachim 8a prefers a torch for borei me'orei ha'eish, and the Mishnah Berurah explains that it is bright. Rav Chaim Ozer Grodzinski ruled that an incandescent bulb may be used for Havdalah, to stress that turning one on is lighting a fire on Shabbos. His ruling was not universally accepted, and Rav Nissim Karelitz held that today even he would want real fire.
kiddush-and-havdalah/light-bulb-for-havd.description: Can a light bulb serve as the fire for Havdalah? Rav Chaim Ozer's ruling, Rav Nissim Karelitz's view, and why a torch is preferred in Pesachim 8a.

kiddush-and-havdalah/non-mevushal-wine-f.intro: The Shulchan Aruch writes that one should ideally use non-mevushal wine for Kiddush and the four cups. Since Rav Moshe Feinstein counts pasteurized wine as cooked, Kedem grape juice is mevushal by American standards. Rav Shmuel Kamenetsky and the gedolim who reject pasteurization would treat it as not mevushal, so their stringency about the leniency on Avodah Zarah 30a becomes a leniency for Kiddush.
kiddush-and-havdalah/non-mevushal-wine-f.description: Should Kiddush and the four cups use non-mevushal wine, and may pasteurized grape juice count? Rav Shmuel Kamenetsky's view, built on Avodah Zarah 30a.

kiddush-and-havdalah/order-of-leishev-ba.intro: At Kiddush on the first night of Sukkos, which comes first, Leishev BaSukkah or Shehechiyanu? Rabba bar bar Channah would put the more common bracha first, but on Sukkah 56a the halacha follows Rav: the sukkah bracha first, since Shehechiyanu covers the sukkah too. On the second night the order is reversed, though the Mishnah Berurah allows keeping the first night's order, as long as families sharing one sukkah agree.
kiddush-and-havdalah/order-of-leishev-ba.description: Leishev BaSukkah or Shehechiyanu first at Kiddush? Rav's ruling on Sukkah 56a, the reversed order on the second night, and family customs that differ.

kiddush-and-havdalah/plastic-cups-for-ki.intro: In Europe, a one-ounce Kiddush cup was made of metal or glass. Today some use disposable plastic, and there is a debate over whether such a cup has enough importance for Kiddush. A plastic shot glass may be worse than a larger cup, since it is used only once, yet the custom now is to be lenient, notes a discussion tied to Zevachim 31b.
kiddush-and-havdalah/plastic-cups-for-ki.description: May Kiddush be made on a disposable plastic cup or plastic shot glass? The debate and today's lenient custom, in a discussion tied to Zevachim 31b.
