kiddush-and-havdalah/size-of-the-kiddush.intro: The Mishnah Berurah says that even with liquor, the Kiddush cup must hold a revi'is, between 2.9 and 3.3 ounces, and a cheekful must be drunk. The Taz disagrees: for strong drink, the measure is a normal local serving, about a one-ounce shot. Many chassidic Rebbes followed the Taz, in a discussion that cites Zevachim 31b.
kiddush-and-havdalah/size-of-the-kiddush.description: Must a Kiddush cup hold a revi'is even for liquor? The Mishnah Berurah says yes, but the Taz allows a one-ounce shot, in a discussion citing Zevachim 31b.

kiddush-and-havdalah/spilling-wine-at-ha.intro: The Rema mentions a custom to spill some wine at Havdalah as a good sign for the week, while many Acharonim object that it is wasteful. The Rema says to spill it in the middle of the berachah. In [Don’t Cry Over Spilled Wine](/daf/eruvin/65/dont-cry-over-spilled-wine), on Eruvin 65a, the Taz disagrees but still keeps the custom by letting the cup overflow as he fills it.
kiddush-and-havdalah/spilling-wine-at-ha.description: Why do many spill wine at Havdalah, and when should it be spilled? The Rema and the Taz disagree over a custom drawn from the Gemara in Eruvin 65a.

hallel/half-hallel-on-pesach.intro: Why is only half Hallel said on Chol HaMoed and the last days of Pesach? Arachin 10a explains that Pesach's Mussaf korbanos are the same each day, unlike those of Sukkos. The Mishnah Berurah cites a Midrash based on Sanhedrin 39b, where Hashem stopped the angels from singing as the Egyptians drowned, and the Kollel Iyun HaDaf shows how the two reasons fit together.
hallel/half-hallel-on-pesach.description: Why only half Hallel on the later days of Pesach? Arachin 10a on the identical korbanos, and a Midrash on the drowning Egyptians from Sanhedrin 39b.

hallel/half-hallel-on-rosh-chodesh.intro: Hallel on Rosh Chodesh is only a custom, so verses are skipped to set it apart from days when Hallel is required. Half Hallel is really closer to 85 percent, since we leave out the first 11 pesukim of chapters 115 and 116. Arachin 10a explains why only half Hallel is said on the last days of Pesach, and the Rambam said no bracha over it on Rosh Chodesh.
hallel/half-hallel-on-rosh-chodesh.description: Why is only half Hallel said on Rosh Chodesh, which verses are skipped, and is a bracha said? The custom explained, with Pesach in Arachin 10a.

hallel/hallel-after-chatzos-on-seder-nig.intro: The Korban Pesach was eaten with Hallel, so should Hallel at the Seder be finished by chatzos? In Machaneh Yisrael the Chofetz Chaim said the closing bracha is lost after midnight, but in the Mishnah Berurah he allows it. [Racing Towards Chatzos](/daf/zevachim/56/racing-towards-chatzos) adds the Rema and the Gra on Hallel and the four cups, tied to Zevachim 56b.
hallel/hallel-after-chatzos-on-seder-nig.description: Must Hallel and the four cups be done before chatzos on Seder night? The Chofetz Chaim, the Rema and the Gra, in a Seder dialogue built on Zevachim 56b.

hallel/hallel-in-shul-on-seder-night.intro: The Beis Yosef says to recite Hallel in shul on the first night of Pesach, while the Rema says that is not our minhag. When the Baal HaTanya, visiting another town, said Hallel after everyone left, the rav came to protest. [Do We Need to Suffer for Torah?](/daf/bava-kamma/61/do-we-need-to-suffer-for-torah), on Bava Kamma 61b, retells his clever reply about how the Rema may have meant it.
hallel/hallel-in-shul-on-seder-night.description: Do we say Hallel in shul on the first night of Pesach? The Beis Yosef says yes, the Rema says not our minhag, and the Baal HaTanya's reply. Bava Kamma 61b.

hallel/hallel-on-purim.intro: If we say Hallel on Pesach for our freedom, why not on Purim, when we were saved from death? Megillah 14a gives two answers. Rav Nachman says reading the Megillah is itself like Hallel, while Rava says Hallel does not fit because the Jews were still Achashverosh's subjects, and Rabbi Yechezkel Roter explains that the Megillah thanks Hashem for hidden miracles.
hallel/hallel-on-purim.description: Why isn't Hallel said on Purim? Rav Nachman and Rava give two reasons in Megillah 14a, and whether the Megillah reading takes the place of Hallel.

hallel/saying-hallel-out-of-order.intro: Just like the Megillah, Hallel said out of order does not count, and many Acharonim apply this even to whole paragraphs. The Chofetz Chaim asks how this can apply on Rosh Chodesh, when any verse may be skipped. In a discussion tied to Megillah 17, he suggests that skipping a verse is fine, but saying it later in the wrong place breaks the order and ruins the custom.
hallel/saying-hallel-out-of-order.description: Has one fulfilled the obligation if Hallel's verses are said out of order? The Chofetz Chaim on skipped verses on Rosh Chodesh, tied to Megillah 17.

krias-hatorah/aliyos-when-there-is-no-le.intro: The usual order of aliyos is Kohen, Levi, Yisrael, so what happens when no Levi is in shul? Rashi in Kesubos 25b seems to call two kohanim, but the accepted halacha is that the same kohen takes the second aliyah too. In [Kohen Conundrums](/daf/kesubos/25/kohen-conundrums), the Minchas Elazar explains why the Munkacser beis midrash sometimes called a Yisrael first.
krias-hatorah/aliyos-when-there-is-no-le.description: How are aliyos given when no Levi is in shul? Rashi in Kesubos 25b, the Shulchan Aruch and the Minchas Elazar on whether the kohen takes the second aliyah.

krias-hatorah/chazak-aliyah.intro: Two Leviim with yahrzeit on the same Shabbos drew lots for sheini, and the one who had bought rights to acharon won it. Then he realized it was Shabbos Chazak, when acharon is the last regular aliyah of the sefer and everyone blesses the one who receives it. The Harei BaShamayim ruled he could take back acharon, since the lottery rested on a mistake, one of the cases [Win Or Lose](/daf/bava-basra/106/win-or-lose) brings beside Bava Basra 106b.
krias-hatorah/chazak-aliyah.description: Two Leviim drew lots for an aliyah and the winner realized it was Shabbos Chazak. Could he take back the Chazak aliyah? A ruling tied to Bava Basra 106b.

krias-hatorah/four-aliyos-on-rosh-chodes.intro: Megillah 21b says four people get aliyos on Rosh Chodesh because people will not be late for work, while Mondays and Thursdays have only three. But why is Rosh Chodesh not a workday? Rashi says it is a holiday for women, while the Turei Even suggests that when the Korban Mussaf was brought for all of Klal Yisrael, Rosh Chodesh was a holiday for everyone, and the fourth aliyah remains from then.
krias-hatorah/four-aliyos-on-rosh-chodes.description: Why are four people called to the Torah on Rosh Chodesh? Megillah 21b links it to work, with Rashi and the Turei Even on whether it was a day off.

krias-hatorah/minimum-length-of-the-haft.intro: The Gemara on Megillah 23 says a haftarah needs at least 21 pesukim, unless the topic ends sooner, but Rebbe Yochanan let ten verses suffice where there was a translator. The Ran explains that ten verses plus their translations, with the last verse repeated, make 21. But the Magen Giborim says the short haftarah was simply a break for shuls whose Torah reading took twice as long.
krias-hatorah/minimum-length-of-the-haft.description: How many pesukim must a haftarah have? The rule of 21 verses, the topic exception and the translator, with the Ran and Magen Giborim on Megillah 23.

krias-hatorah/seven-aliyos-on-shabbos.intro: Why are seven people called to the Torah on Shabbos? As with the seven judges of Sanhedrin 10b, one view links them to the seven words of Birkas Kohanim's third verse and another to seven royal advisers. Rashi says these are Achashveirosh's advisers, Tosfos objects, and the Rema explains that we ask Hashem to annul the plans of the wicked seven.
krias-hatorah/seven-aliyos-on-shabbos.description: Why seven aliyos on Shabbos? Birkas Kohanim's third verse or seven royal advisers; Rashi, Tosfos and the Rema debate whose advisers, with Sanhedrin 10b.

krias-hatorah/shabbos-rosh-chodesh-chanu.intro: On Shabbos Rosh Chodesh Chanukah three sifrei Torah come out. The Chanukah haftorah is read, since publicizing the miracle beats tadir when only one can be chosen. But for the Torah readings, where both are read anyway, the more frequent Rosh Chodesh reading comes before Chanukah, as the principle in Zevachim 89 teaches.
krias-hatorah/shabbos-rosh-chodesh-chanu.description: When Shabbos, Rosh Chodesh and Chanukah coincide, which reading comes first and which haftorah is read? Tadir and pirsumei nisa, from Zevachim 89.

krias-hatorah/translating-the-torah-read.intro: In the times of the Gemara, someone would translate the Torah and haftarah into Aramaic as they were read, a practice mentioned on Megillah 23. Why was it dropped? Tosfos note that even then some places had no translator, and the Rosh adds that people no longer understand Aramaic, and a French translation would be improper, since Onkelos was written with ruach hakodesh.
krias-hatorah/translating-the-torah-read.description: Why was the Torah reading once translated into Aramaic, and why is it no longer done? Tosfos and the Rosh explain, in an article on Megillah 23.

krias-hatorah/walking-to-the-bimah-for-a.intro: Someone called for an aliyah should take the shortest route to the bimah, the Shulchan Aruch rules, so as not to keep the tzibbur waiting and to show his eagerness for the Torah. When both paths are equal, he goes up on the right, since the bimah represents the mizbeach of Yoma 17b. The Vilna Gaon says to go right even if it is longer, but the Mishnah Berurah does not mention his view.
krias-hatorah/walking-to-the-bimah-for-a.description: Which way should you walk to the bimah for an aliyah? The Shulchan Aruch's shortest route, the Vilna Gaon's right turn, and the mizbeach of Yoma 17b.

shul/bringing-a-weapon-into-shul.intro: The Shulchan Aruch records that some say not to enter a shul with a long knife. This comes not from the Gemara on Sanhedrin 82 about swords in the Beis Medrash, but from the Maharam M'Rottenberg. He explains that prayer lengthens a person's life while a knife can shorten it, so a blade does not belong in a place of prayer.
shul/bringing-a-weapon-into-shul.description: Why not bring a long knife into shul? The Shulchan Aruch's custom, the Maharam M'Rottenberg's reason, and the swords of the Beis Medrash on Sanhedrin 82.

shul/building-an-office-inside-a-shul.intro: May a shul lower the back of its 20-foot ceiling and build offices above? Reuven argues that holiness extends upward, citing Zevachim 87b on the airspace above the Mizbeach. The Beis Shlomo says a ceiling in between blocks that holiness, while the Imrei Yosher rules that a shul's airspace is holy and a floor may not be added.
shul/building-an-office-inside-a-shul.description: May a shul lower its ceiling and build offices above? The Beis Shlomo and Imrei Yosher disagree, based on the Altar's airspace in Zevachim 87b.

shul/chazzan-with-a-pleasant-voice.intro: Tosfos on Rosh Hashanah 8a tells of the son of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, chosen as chazzan on Rosh Hashanah for his nice voice. The Shearim Metzuyanim B'Halacha calls this perhaps the earliest source that a chazzan should sound pleasant. Rashi on Mishlei explains that honoring Hashem with your wealth includes any talent, even a voice.
shul/chazzan-with-a-pleasant-voice.description: Should a chazzan have a pleasant voice? Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's son, chosen to lead on Rosh Hashanah, and serving Hashem with talent, Rosh Hashanah 8a.

shul/choosing-which-shul-to-attend.intro: If two shuls both fit, the Magen Avraham says to go to the farther one, for the reward of each step, learned from a widow who walked to Rebbe Yochanan's beis midrash. The Geza Yishai objects that this passes over a mitzvah. [A Mitzvah for Each Footstep](/daf/zevachim/51/a-mitzvah-for-each-footstep) shows how Tosfos in Zevachim 51a answers him, though a makom kavuah still comes first.
shul/choosing-which-shul-to-attend.description: Which of two shuls should you attend? The Magen Avraham says the farther one, for each step, and Tosfos in Zevachim 51a answers the Geza Yishai.

shul/demolishing-a-shul.intro: The Torah's command not to destroy the Beis HaMikdash extends to a shul or beis midrash, and the halacha says one may not destroy a shul. The Chofetz Chaim adds that this includes its tables and benches. Still, a shul may be torn down to build a nicer one, a point [Getting A Handle On Shul Rules](/daf/zevachim/98/getting-a-handle-on-shul-rules) explores in connection with Zevachim 98.
shul/demolishing-a-shul.description: May a shul or its furniture be destroyed? The ban learned from the Beis HaMikdash, and the exception for building a nicer shul, discussed with Zevachim 98.

shul/drawing-lots-for-shul-honors.intro: If two people in shul both want to be chazzan or get an aliyah, may they draw lots? Tosfos quotes a Sifri that calls lotteries a form of divination, but the Shevet HaLevi says that only means predicting the future. Settling a dispute by gorel is fine, and the winner needs no kinyan, a point tied to Zevachim 119b and the Zichron Yosef's view that everyone shares in the kibbudim.
shul/drawing-lots-for-shul-honors.description: May a shul use a lottery to decide who gets an aliyah or leads davening? The Shevet HaLevi and Zichron Yosef on the gorel, discussed with Zevachim 119b.

shul/eating-in-shul.intro: Megillah 28a says one may not eat or drink in shul, yet Babylonian shuls were built with certain conditions. Tosfos limit this to a shul no longer in use, while the Ramban and Rashba allow limited use for a real need, such as feeding the poor. In [Don’t Talk, Just Daven](/daf/megillah/28/dont-talk-just-daven), Rav Moshe Feinstein explains that shuls serving seudah shelishis follow Rashi and the Ohr Zarua.
shul/eating-in-shul.description: May food be served in shul, like a kiddush or seudah shelishis? Tosfos, the Rashba and Rav Moshe Feinstein on the condition in Megillah 28a.

shul/facing-away-from-the-aron-kodesh.intro: The Kohen Gadol walked backwards out of the Kodesh HaKedoshim so as not to turn his back on the Aron, as Yoma 52b describes. Yet kohanim bless the people facing away from the Aron Kodesh, and the Taz lets rabbanim give sermons that way, since the sifrei Torah sit above ten tefachim. The Shaarei Efraim warns that a speaker seeking only glory or pay will be punished.
shul/facing-away-from-the-aron-kodesh.description: Why may kohanim bless and rabbanim speak with their backs to the Aron Kodesh? The Rambam, the Taz and a sharp warning from the Shaarei Efraim, on Yoma 52b.

shul/kedushah-of-a-shuls-airspace.intro: Shevuos 17 asks whether the air above the Beis HaMikdash is as holy as the ground. [Clearing the Air](/daf/shevuos/17/clearing-the-air) turns that into a shul debate: may a congregation build a floor across the back of a tall sanctuary for offices? The Maharsham allowed a new floor for an Ezras Nashim and the Beis Shlomo allows offices, but the Imrei Yosher says a shul's airspace is holy.
shul/kedushah-of-a-shuls-airspace.description: Does a shul's holiness reach up through the open space under its ceiling? Shevuos 17 and the Beis Shlomo and Imrei Yosher on building a new floor inside.

shul/making-holes-in-a-shul-wall.intro: A student put a handle on a beis midrash door with two screws. Does that break the ban on damaging a shul? The Taz objected to a hole made in a shul wall for a shtender, but the Maamar Mordechai, Beis Shearim and Elya Rabba all find reasons to permit it, and the Mishnah Berurah seems to agree, in a discussion of Zevachim 98.
shul/making-holes-in-a-shul-wall.description: May you drill holes in a shul wall or door for a fixture? The Taz forbids it, while the Elya Rabba and Mishnah Berurah permit it, in light of Zevachim 98.

shul/reward-for-steps-to-shul.intro: Rebbe Yochanan learned from a widow that each extra step to shul brings more reward. The Mishna Berura rules that, all else being equal, one should daven at the farther shul, and the Maharal explains that the effort deepens one's bond with Hashem where His Shechina rests. [Walks of Life](/daf/bava-metzia/113/walks-of-life) sets this beside Bava Metzia 113b.
shul/reward-for-steps-to-shul.description: Does walking farther to shul earn more reward? Rebbe Yochanan learned it from a widow, and the Mishna Berura and Maharal explain, beside Bava Metzia 113b.

shul/shul-as-the-tallest-building.intro: Rav taught that a city whose houses are taller than its shul will become desolate, and the Chofetz Chaim says one should keep this as far as possible, even though many ignore it today. [Reaching New Heights](/daf/shabbos/11/reaching-new-heights) looks at Shabbos 11 and at Rabbeinu Tam's advice to raise one corner of the shul. Does a plain pole on the roof count, or only a decorative part of the building?
shul/shul-as-the-tallest-building.description: Must a shul be the tallest building in town? Rav's warning in Shabbos 11, Rabbeinu Tam's fix, and whether a pole on the roof counts toward the height.

shul/talking-in-shul.intro: Strictly speaking, any talk in shul that is not about a mitzvah is forbidden, and some Acharonim even forbid saying gezunteit. Rav Shlomo Zalman explains that people chat after davening because they rely on Rashi and the Ohr Zarua, who read the condition in Megillah 28a broadly. Talking during davening is a different matter, and one gadol blamed the massacres of Tach V'Tat on it.
shul/talking-in-shul.description: Why do many talk in shul after davening when it is forbidden, and why is talking during davening so serious? Rav Shlomo Zalman on Megillah 28a.

shul/ten-commandments-display-in-shul.intro: May a shul hang a display of the Aseres HaDibros? The Mishnah Berurah warns against it, lest people think there are only ten mitzvos. In [Fair and Square](/daf/bava-basra/14/fair-and-square), connected to the Luchos on Bava Basra 14a, Rav Moshe Sternbuch rules that an artistic picture of the Luchos is different, though for peace in one South African shul he advised squaring off the rounded tops.
shul/ten-commandments-display-in-shul.description: May a shul display the Aseres HaDibros on artistic Luchos? The Mishnah Berurah's concern and Rav Moshe Sternbuch's ruling, connected to Bava Basra 14a.

shul/using-an-abandoned-shul.intro: Megillah 28a says Babylonian shuls were built on certain conditions. Tosfos explain that the condition allowed a shul to be used for other purposes once it fell out of use. The Shulchan Aruch rules this way, but adds that even then it may not be used for something disgraceful, like planting, and that in Eretz Yisrael no condition works at all.
shul/using-an-abandoned-shul.description: May a shul no longer in use serve other purposes? How a condition made when it was built works outside Eretz Yisrael, from Tosfos on Megillah 28a.

shul/wearing-shoes-in-shul.intro: A shul is called a small Beis HaMikdash, and no one wore shoes in the Beis HaMikdash. Rabbeinu Chananel took this seriously enough to ask whether shoes are allowed in shul. He proves from Sotah 39b, where kohanim must take off their shoes before duchening, that they had been wearing them in shul until then, so shoes are permitted.
shul/wearing-shoes-in-shul.description: If a shul is like a small Beis HaMikdash, should shoes come off there? Rabbeinu Chananel proves from Sotah 39b that shoes may be worn in shul.

zmanim/davening-maariv-after-chatzos.intro: A traveler can daven Maariv now while sitting, or wait until after chatzos and daven standing. One rav, citing the Mishnah Berurah, preferred standing after chatzos. Rav Shlomo Zalman ruled the opposite, and the article reads the Mishnah Berurah on a traveler heading to an inn as agreeing with him, building on the rules of davening on the road in Berachos 30a.
zmanim/davening-maariv-after-chatzos.description: Is it better to daven Maariv standing after chatzos or sitting before it while traveling? Rav Shlomo Zalman and the Mishnah Berurah, from Berachos 30a.

zmanim/earliest-time-for-minchah.intro: According to the Shulchan Aruch, Minchah should not be davened before nine and a half halachic hours, Minchah ketanah, since that is when the afternoon Tamid was usually brought. Rebbe Akiva Eiger adds that one should ideally daven exactly then. Discussing Pesachim 65a, the Mishnah Berurah cites the Rosh and Tur, who allow davening from a half hour after midday, and says one may rely on them before a big meal or a trip.
zmanim/earliest-time-for-minchah.description: When is the earliest time to daven Minchah? Minchah ketanah and the Tamid, versus a half hour after midday per the Rosh and Tur. Pesachim 65a.

zmanim/rabbeinu-tam-zman-for-ending-shab.intro: When does Shabbos end? The Gra holds that only until sunset is it surely day, while Rabbeinu Tam in Tosfos on Pesachim 94a extends daytime much longer, with night certain at 72 minutes after sunset. Rav Moshe Feinstein held that in New York, 50 minutes would suffice, and that is a common custom there, though careful people wait 72.
zmanim/rabbeinu-tam-zman-for-ending-shab.description: Rabbeinu Tam in Tosfos on Pesachim 94a puts nightfall 72 minutes after sunset. How it differs from the Vilna Gaon, and the 50-minute New York custom.

tefillin/checking-tefillin-in-a-mirror.intro: Should one use a mirror to make sure the head tefillin sit in the right place? The Divrei Chaim of Sanz said no, since there is enough room on the head, and called someone who checks an am ha'aretz. The Brisker Rav answered that he would rather be called that and know his tefillin were correct, and [A Moment of Reflection](/daf/avodah-zarah/29/a-moment-of-reflection) ties the question to the mirror sugya on Avodah Zarah 29a.
tefillin/checking-tefillin-in-a-mirror.description: Should one check head tefillin in a mirror? The Divrei Chaim of Sanz, the Brisker Rav and Rav Henoch Leibowitz, tied to the sugya on Avodah Zarah 29a.

tefillin/shehecheyanu-on-bar-mitzvah-tef.intro: The Pri Toar rules that a bar mitzvah boy should say Shehecheyanu the first time he puts on tefillin, covering all his new mitzvos. The Mishnah Berurah disagrees, but suggests he wear a new suit and have tefillin in mind. In [Attitude Of Gratitude](/daf/menachos/75/attitude-of-gratitude), on Menachos 75, HaRav Shlomo Zalman advises a father to lend the tefillin and then give them as a gift.
tefillin/shehecheyanu-on-bar-mitzvah-tef.description: Does a bar mitzvah boy say Shehecheyanu on his first tefillin? The Pri Toar, the Mishnah Berurah's new suit and Rav Shlomo Zalman's gift, on Menachos 75.

tefillin/shin-on-the-tefillin-shel-rosh.intro: Menachos 35 records a Halacha L'Moshe MiSinai that a shin must be embossed on the tefillin shel rosh. Rashi says the shin joins the daled and yud of the knots to spell Hashem's Name, while Tosafos disagrees. The Orchos Chaim notes that shin equals 300, about the number of days a man wears tefillin each year, and the Ateres Zekeinim says the math works only with Chol HaMoed.
tefillin/shin-on-the-tefillin-shel-rosh.description: Why is a shin embossed on the head tefillin? Rashi links it to Hashem's Name, and the Orchos Chaim counts 300 tefillin days a year, from Menachos 35.

tefillin/tallis-or-tefillin-first.intro: Normally the tallis goes on before the tefillin, but the Shulchan Aruch says that whoever reaches his tefillin first puts them on first. If he already walked past them, the Kohen Gadol in Yoma 58b, who went back to the corner of the Altar he had passed, suggests going back. The Mishnah Berurah adds that once the tallis is in hand, it should not be put down.
tefillin/tallis-or-tefillin-first.description: Tallis or tefillin first, and what if you passed your tefillin already? The Kohen Gadol at the Altar in Yoma 58b and the Mishnah Berurah's ruling.

tefillin/tefillin-for-a-lefty.intro: Righties put tefillin on the left arm, because the Torah calls for the weaker arm, and lefties put them on the right arm for the same reason. The Tur uses this to say a left-footed yavam should have the shoe removed from his left foot at chalitzah. The Yam Shel Shlomo disagrees, as [Left Foot, Right Foot](/daf/yevamos/104/left-foot-right-foot) on Yevamos 104 explains: for tefillin the Torah asks for the weaker arm, but for chalitzah it simply names the right foot.
tefillin/tefillin-for-a-lefty.description: Why does a lefty put tefillin on the right arm? The Torah's call for the weaker arm, and how the Tur applies the idea to chalitzah, from Yevamos 104.

tefillin/tefillin-on-chol-hamoed.intro: Some men put on tefillin on Chol HaMoed and some do not, and shuls handle the divide in different ways, even with a special mechitza. [The Great Tefillin Divide](/daf/chagigah/18/the-great-tefillin-divide) links the split to Chagigah 18a and whether the holiness of Chol HaMoed is from the Torah. The Shulchan Aruch rules that tefillin should not be worn, perhaps because of the Zohar.
tefillin/tefillin-on-chol-hamoed.description: Should tefillin be worn on Chol HaMoed? The split customs, the mechitza in some shuls, and the Shulchan Aruch's view, linked to the debate in Chagigah 18a.

tefillin/tefillin-when-lost-track-of-sha.intro: A traveler lost in the desert does not know which day is Shabbos, so he does only the labor he needs to survive and picks one day for Kiddush and Havdalah. The Mishna Berura rules that he wears tefillin on that day, since his chosen day has no unique os. [Mordechai’s Tefillin](/daf/menachos/35/mordechais-tefillin) uses this case to explain Mordechai's tefillin, from Menachos 35.
tefillin/tefillin-when-lost-track-of-sha.description: Should a traveler lost in the desert wear tefillin on the day he picks as Shabbos? The Mishna Berura's ruling and the os of the day, from Menachos 35.

tefillin/wearing-rashi-and-rabbeinu-tam-.intro: The Shulchan Aruch allows wearing Rashi and Rabbeinu Tam tefillin at the same time, but why is that not baal toseif, adding to a mitzvah? In [The Tiff Over Two Tefillin](/daf/menachos/34/the-tiff-over-two-tefillin-menachos-34), filed on Menachos 34, the Chofetz Chaim explains that one pair is surely invalid. To avoid even the look of adding, one stipulates that he means to fulfill the mitzvah only with whichever pair is kosher.
tefillin/wearing-rashi-and-rabbeinu-tam-.description: May one wear Rashi and Rabbeinu Tam tefillin at once without baal toseif? The Chofetz Chaim on intention and the invalid pair, from Menachos 34.

mezuzah/fallen-mezuzah-on-shabbos.intro: If a mezuzah falls on Shabbos, all agree it may be picked up and put somewhere safe, though some say it is muktzeh after that. It usually cannot be put back until after Shabbos. In [Muktzeh Marvels](/daf/gittin/77/muktzeh-marvels), filed on Gittin 77, the Aruch HaShulchan says to stay out of that room if possible, while Rebbe Zalman of Vilna went much further.
mezuzah/fallen-mezuzah-on-shabbos.description: What should you do if a mezuzah falls on Shabbos? Handling it, putting it back and using the room, with the Aruch HaShulchan's ruling, from Gittin 77.

mezuzah/mezuzah-for-a-left-footed-person.intro: The mezuzah goes on the right doorpost because most people step in with the right foot first. So what about a home where everyone is left-footed? The Mordechai says to follow the majority of residents, implying the left doorpost, but the Shach rules it must always go on the right, and adds that this is the custom, in a discussion tied to Yevamos 104.
mezuzah/mezuzah-for-a-left-footed-person.description: Should a left-footed household put the mezuzah on the left doorpost? The Mordechai follows the residents; the Shach says always the right. Yevamos 104.

mezuzah/mezuzah-for-renters.intro: Menachos 44a links borrowed tzitzis to a rented home: after thirty days, a renter looks like an owner and must put up a mezuzah, and Tosafos offers two reasons, appearance or a temporary dwelling. For a one-year lease, the Pischei Teshuvah says to wait thirty days and the Aruch HaShulchan says to affix right away. Rav Moshe Feinstein suggests putting it up at once but waiting on the bracha.
mezuzah/mezuzah-for-renters.description: When must a renter put up mezuzos, and does a one-year lease change the thirty days? Tosafos, the Aruch HaShulchan and Rav Moshe, from Menachos 44a.

mezuzah/mezuzah-in-a-summer-bungalow.intro: An old painted-over mezuzah sits beside a new one on a Catskills bungalow, and in [Multiple Mezuzos?](/daf/yoma/57/multiple-mezuzos) Boruch and Shimon ask whether that breaks bal tosif. The Pischei Teshuva and Rav Moshe Feinstein say to remove and check the old one rather than add another, though the Minchas Elazar once added a mezuzah where most were known to be invalid, in a talk that opens on Yoma 57a.
mezuzah/mezuzah-in-a-summer-bungalow.description: Should you add a new mezuzah beside an old one on a bungalow doorpost? The Pischei Teshuva and Rav Moshe Feinstein weigh in, starting from Yoma 57a.

mezuzah/mezuzah-on-a-tiny-house.intro: Does a tiny house need a mezuzah? Sukkah 3a exempts a house smaller than four amos by four, and even a 65-square-foot model passes under one measure. The Chazon Ish says built-in furniture can bring the space below the minimum, while Rav Moshe sets four by four amos at about 49 square feet, which leaves the question open.
mezuzah/mezuzah-on-a-tiny-house.description: Does a tiny house need a mezuzah? Sukkah 3a sets a minimum of four by four amos; the Chazon Ish and Rav Moshe on built-in furniture and measurements.

mezuzah/mezuzah-on-a-walk-in-closet.intro: Does a walk-in closet need a mezuzah, and on which side? The Maharam Shik links the question to Bava Basra 61a, about whether a small room counts as significant. [Small Talk](/daf/bava-basra/61/small-talk) explains how the Chamudei Daniel and Rebbe Akiva Eiger would put it on opposite doorposts, and why Rav Moshe Feinstein ruled that none is needed.
mezuzah/mezuzah-on-a-walk-in-closet.description: Does a walk-in closet need a mezuzah, and on which side? The Chamudei Daniel, Rebbe Akiva Eiger and Rav Moshe weigh in, tied to Bava Basra 61a.

mezuzah/replacing-a-mezuzah-with-a-nicer.intro: May you take down a perfectly kosher mezuzah to put up a more mehudar one? Following Rav Achai Gaon, the Mezuzos Melachim says sending a kosher mezuzah to a drawer may be a disgrace. In [Removing a House’s Mezuzos](/daf/bava-metzia/102/removing-a-houses-mezuzos), tied to Bava Metzia 102a, the suggestion is to give the older one away or sell it so it stays in use.
mezuzah/replacing-a-mezuzah-with-a-nicer.description: May a kosher mezuzah be swapped for a nicer one? The Mezuzos Melachim fears disgracing the old one and suggests giving it away, from Bava Metzia 102a.

mezuzah/taking-down-mezuzos-for-checking.intro: Leaving a home without mezuzos for a long time while they are checked is a mistake. In the Five Towns, Rabbi Naftali Jaeger set up a free gemach that lends mezuzos to put up as soon as one's own come down. As the article on Gittin 77 notes, a sofer who makes house calls helps too, while declaring the house ownerless works for only 30 days.
mezuzah/taking-down-mezuzos-for-checking.description: How can you check your mezuzos without leaving doorways bare? A mezuzah gemach, a sofer who makes house calls and other options, from Gittin 77.

mezuzah/taking-mezuzos-when-moving-out.intro: Bava Metzia 102a says a renter may not take his mezuzos when he moves out, and tells of a tenant who did so with disastrous results. Tosfos says the mezuzah protects the next residents, the Ritva speaks of sanctity on the home, and the Birchei Yosef fears the new tenant will be negligent. Rav Moshe allows removing them when the apartment is painted.
mezuzah/taking-mezuzos-when-moving-out.description: May a tenant take his mezuzos when he moves out? Tosfos, the Ritva, the Birchei Yosef and Rav Moshe weigh in on painting and moving, from Bava Metzia 102a.

mezuzah/thirty-days-to-put-up-a-mezuzah.intro: Many people think everyone has 30 days before putting up mezuzos, but that leniency is only for a renter outside of Israel. A buyer must put them up right away, and a fallen mezuzah must be returned immediately. The Aruch HaShulchan rules one may not delay even a moment, as the article on Gittin 77 explains.
mezuzah/thirty-days-to-put-up-a-mezuzah.description: Who really has thirty days to put up a mezuzah? Only renters outside Israel; homeowners must act at once, as the Aruch HaShulchan rules, from Gittin 77.

mezuzah/two-mezuzos-on-one-doorpost.intro: If Rashi wants a mezuzah vertical and Rabbeinu Tam wants it horizontal, why not put up two? The Birur Halacha compares it to wearing two pairs of tefillin, but the Mezuzos Melachim warns it may be baal toseif. Rav Moshe Feinstein rules that one may not add a second mezuzah just because he is unsure of the first, as the article on Menachos 34 explains.
mezuzah/two-mezuzos-on-one-doorpost.description: May one put two mezuzos on one doorpost, one vertical and one horizontal, or add one when unsure? Rav Moshe and others on baal toseif, from Menachos 34.

mezuzah/why-the-mezuzah-is-slanted.intro: Rashi holds a mezuzah should stand upright, and Rabbeinu Tam says it should lie flat. Ashkenazim place it at an angle as a compromise between the two, and it is said this teaches that compromise belongs in every Jewish home. [The Right Angle](/daf/bava-basra/14/the-right-angle) opens with a mezuzah in a Super Bowl ad and goes on to Bava Basra 14a.
mezuzah/why-the-mezuzah-is-slanted.description: Why do Ashkenazim put the mezuzah on a slant? Rashi says upright and Rabbeinu Tam says flat, so we compromise. A look at the dispute, with Bava Basra 14a.

tzitzis/age-to-start-wearing-tzitzis.intro: Sukkah 42a says a minor who knows how to wrap himself in tzitzis is obligated in tzitzis. The Meiri notes that, unlike tefillin, a father need not buy tzitzis, but the Bach explains we buy them since we all wear a tallis katan. On age, the Tur says nine, the Bach six or seven, and the Eliyahu Rabbah three.
tzitzis/age-to-start-wearing-tzitzis.description: At what age should a boy start wearing tzitzis, and must his father buy them? Sukkah 42a, the Meiri, the Bach and the Tur all weigh in on the question.

tzitzis/beautifying-the-tallis-garment.intro: Nazir 2b lists beautiful tzitzis among the ways to beautify a mitzvah, and Rashi in Bava Kama includes the tallis itself. But must one beautify any four-cornered garment, even a poncho? Rav Moshe Feinstein rules that hiddur applies to the garment only when it is worn to fulfill the mitzvah of tzitzis, as our tallis and tzitzis are.
tzitzis/beautifying-the-tallis-garment.description: Does hiddur mitzvah apply to the tallis garment or only the strings? Rashi and Rav Moshe Feinstein on when a nice garment is a mitzvah, from Nazir 2b.

tzitzis/bracha-on-borrowed-tzitzis.intro: A borrowed four-cornered garment has no Torah obligation of tzitzis, so a borrower does not recite a bracha unless he receives it as a gift on condition that it be returned. In [On Borrowed Time](/daf/menachos/44/on-borrowed-time), Menachos 44a adds a twist: after thirty days the garment starts to look like his, and he must affix tzitzis. The Rosh's view that a bracha is not lost is not accepted.
tzitzis/bracha-on-borrowed-tzitzis.description: Does one say a bracha on borrowed tzitzis, and when does a borrowed garment need tzitzis? The thirty-day rule and matanah al menas, from Menachos 44a.

tzitzis/moving-tzitzis-strings-to-anothe.intro: Shmuel rules that tzitzis strings may be taken off one garment and tied onto another. So why can't a renter move his mezuzos? On Bava Metzia 102a, the Rishonim answer that tzitzis protect no one else and bring no sanctity to the garment, and the Mishna Berura even allows removing kosher strings to replace them with nicer ones.
tzitzis/moving-tzitzis-strings-to-anothe.description: Tzitzis strings may move to another garment, but mezuzos must stay. Shmuel's rule and the Rishonim's reasons for the difference, from Bava Metzia 102a.

tzitzis/silk-tzitzis.intro: Silk comes from insect larvae, which are not kosher. The Torah Lishmah suggests that according to the Magen Avraham, someone who usually wears cotton should not switch to silk tzitzis, since tzitzis can be made from kosher materials. In this article on Sukkah 23 he concludes that by the letter of the law there is no concern, but one should use kosher-animal products where possible.
tzitzis/silk-tzitzis.description: Should you wear silk tzitzis or a silk tallis if wool or cotton is available? The Torah Lishmah on the Magen Avraham's view, in an article on Sukkah 23.

tzitzis/symbolism-of-tzitzis-strings-and.intro: The Yerushalmi says Menashe's soldiers found Yeshaya hidden in a cedar tree because his tzitzis were sticking out. The Ben Yehoyada explains why: each corner's 8 strings and 5 knots make 13, and four corners make 52, the gematria of ben, son. [The Good In The Bad](/daf/yevamos/49/the-good-in-the-bad) on Yevamos 49 adds that two corners in front and two in back show Hashem loves us as children whether we act well or not.
tzitzis/symbolism-of-tzitzis-strings-and.description: What do the strings and knots of tzitzis stand for? The Ben Yehoyada's count of 13 and 52, and Hashem's love for His children, from Yevamos 49.

tzitzis/tzitzis-dragging-on-the-floor.intro: The Shulchan Aruch says to keep tzitzis strings from dragging on the ground, yet in Berachos 18 Rebbe Chiya only objected when they dragged over graves. The Yad Aharon limits the rule to a tallis gadol. The Magen Avraham limits it to the moment of the berachah, and the Aruch HaShulchan says an occasional touch of the floor is no concern.
tzitzis/tzitzis-dragging-on-the-floor.description: Must tzitzis strings be kept off the floor? The Yad Aharon, Magen Avraham and Aruch HaShulchan on a tallis versus daily tzitzis, from Berachos 18.

tzitzis/tzitzis-for-idf-soldiers.intro: A commando unit disguised as the enemy waited on a roof for rescue, while the pilot, never told of the disguise, prepared to fire. [Strings Attached](/daf/sanhedrin/72/strings-attached), built on a question tied to Sanhedrin 72b, tells how the soldiers waved the tzitzis they had received from American donors, and the pilot spotted them in time. The article notes it could not confirm the story, but One Israel Fund does run such a tzitzis program.
tzitzis/tzitzis-for-idf-soldiers.description: Did waving tzitzis save a disguised IDF commando unit? A reported story, a program that sends tzitzis to soldiers, and the rodef question of Sanhedrin 72b.

tzitzis/tzitzis-in-a-cemetery.intro: Rebbe Chiya and Rebbe Yonasan were walking in a cemetery, and Rebbe Yonasan's tzitzis were dragging over the graves. Rebbe Chiya told him to lift them, since the dead can no longer do mitzvos and would feel mocked. In [Do Knot Disturb](/daf/berachos/18/do-knot-disturb), Berachos 18 also raises how Rebbe Yonasan, a kohein, could be there at all.
tzitzis/tzitzis-in-a-cemetery.description: Why lift your tzitzis in a cemetery? Rebbe Chiya warns of mocking the dead, who can no longer do mitzvos, and asks which Rebbe Yonasan it was. Berachos 18.

tzitzis/wearing-a-tallis-without-intent.intro: A man called for an aliyah at Minchah on Shabbos quickly throws on a tallis, likely with no thought of the mitzvah. Since tzitzis is a biblical mitzvah that requires intent, he may not fulfill it at all. Worse, the Biur Halachah suggests he may be considered mevateil mitzvas aseh, wearing a kosher tallis without the mitzvah, a case raised alongside Yevamos 55.
tzitzis/wearing-a-tallis-without-intent.description: Does a man who grabs a tallis for an aliyah without intent fulfill tzitzis? The Biur Halachah's warning about mevateil mitzvas aseh, from Yevamos 55.

tzitzis/wool-tzitzis-on-a-linen-garment.intro: The Torah places the shatnez prohibition right next to tzitzis, and Yevamos 4a learns that in the days of techeiles, wool strings could go on a linen garment. Since we no longer have definite techeiles, the Shulchan Aruch rules that a linen garment now takes linen strings. Rabbi Akiva Eiger adds that even then, a garment made of wool and linen itself was never allowed.
tzitzis/wool-tzitzis-on-a-linen-garment.description: Could wool tzitzis go on a linen garment? Yevamos 4a, the role of techeiles, the Shulchan Aruch today, and Rabbi Akiva Eiger on shatnez garments.

sefer-torah/last-eight-pesukim-of-the-to.intro: Menachos 30a teaches that a special halacha applies to the last eight pesukim of the Torah, which describe Moshe Rabbeinu's death. Rebbe Yehuda says Yehoshua wrote them, while Rebbe Shimon says Moshe wrote them with tears. Opinions differ on the halacha too: one aliyah, no ba'al korei reading with the oleh, no minyan, or an honor for the greatest scholar.
sefer-torah/last-eight-pesukim-of-the-to.description: Who wrote the last eight pesukim of the Torah, Moshe or Yehoshua, and what special halacha applies when reading them? The debate in Menachos 30a.

sefer-torah/presidential-autopen.intro: The presidential autopen signs documents with a motorized arm, and the signature counts as the President's own. [The Modern Autopen](/daf/menachos/30/the-modern-autopen-menachos%20-30) finds an ancient parallel. Starting from Menachos 30a, it brings the Shelah HaKadosh's view that Moshe wrote the Sefer Torah through hashbuas kulmus, animating the pen by hidden forces, which explains how he could write on the Shabbos of his death.
sefer-torah/presidential-autopen.description: Did Moshe write the Torah with an ancient autopen? The Shelah's hashbuas kulmus explains writing on Shabbos, from the last pesukim in Menachos 30a.

sefer-torah/sefer-torah-position-in-the-.intro: Rabbeinu Tam held that sifrei Torah should lie flat in the aron kodesh, like the Luchos and the sefer Torah in the Aron on Bava Basra 14a. He even regretted not building his aron wide enough. The Radvaz defends standing them up, since we read from them often, they are round, and we daven facing them, calling the custom of our fathers Torah.
sefer-torah/sefer-torah-position-in-the-.description: Should a sefer Torah stand or lie flat in the aron kodesh? Rabbeinu Tam says flat, and the Radvaz defends our custom of standing it. From Bava Basra 14a.

sefer-torah/turning-your-back-on-a-sefer.intro: When the Kohen Gadol left the Holy of Holies, he walked backwards, never turning his back on the Aron. [Back to Respect](/daf/yoma/52/back-to-respect) shows how Yoma 52b learns this from Shlomo HaMelech leaving the Mishkan in Givon. The Rambam and Shulchan Aruch apply the rule to a sefer Torah, but a scroll raised above ten tefachim is already honored enough.
sefer-torah/turning-your-back-on-a-sefer.description: One should not turn his back on a sefer Torah. Yoma 52b learns it from the Kohen Gadol and Shlomo HaMelech, and the Rambam explains when it does not apply.

sefer-torah/which-sefer-torah-to-read-fr.intro: A gabbai thought a sefer Torah was pasul, so a second scroll was taken out, until the rav found that shadows and dirt had fooled him. The Torah Lishmah rules that the first scroll must be read, since it was picked first. In [What Came First?](/daf/yoma/64/what-came-first), Shimon explains why this differs from the two korbanos of Yoma 64a: the first scroll was never really disqualified.
sefer-torah/which-sefer-torah-to-read-fr.description: A sefer Torah wrongly thought pasul was replaced. Must the shul read the first one? The Torah Lishmah's ruling, compared with the korbanos of Yoma 64a.

sefer-torah/writing-a-sefer-torahs-final.intro: When a sefer Torah is completed, many people are honored with writing one of the final letters. The Chasam Sofer used this custom to check whether a scroll was written by a Jew: uneven writing in the last column shows the minhag was followed. As the article on Gittin 33 explains, scribes now leave out a drop of ink in each final letter to keep the writing uniform.
sefer-torah/writing-a-sefer-torahs-final.description: Why are people honored with writing a new sefer Torah's last letters, and how do scribes keep them uniform? The Chasam Sofer's test, as told on Gittin 33.

sefer-torah/writing-pesukim-outside-a-se.intro: Queen Hilney gave the Beis HaMikdash a golden tablet with parashas Sotah, and Yoma 37a asks whether a single portion of Torah may be written on its own. Rabba rules it forbidden, and the Rambam codifies this, even objecting to pesukim embroidered on a tallis bag. The Rif permits writing pesukim for learning, and the Shach says the custom follows him, so a rebbe may write a pasuk on the board.
sefer-torah/writing-pesukim-outside-a-se.description: May Torah verses be written on their own, on a board or worksheet? The golden tablet of Yoma 37a, Rabba and the Rambam, and the Rif's view for learning.

tashmishei-kedushah/disposing-of-old-tzi.intro: What do you do with tzitzis strings that are no longer kosher? The Shulchan Aruch allows throwing them in the trash, the Rema says that is degrading, and the Maharil says to hide them. The article on Sukkah 42a notes that many wrap them in a bag first, and that leaving them on the ground is only a problem if one steps on them.
tashmishei-kedushah/disposing-of-old-tzi.description: May old tzitzis be thrown out, or should they be hidden? The Shulchan Aruch, the Rema and the Maharil disagree, in an article filed on Sukkah 42a.

tashmishei-kedushah/repurposing-garments.intro: Can a cloak once worn by a French emperor become a paroches? Menachos 22b says wood already used for a house may not go on the Mizbeach. The Magen Avraham rules that once an item's form is changed it counts as new, and the Mishnah Berurah notes that the common practice is lenient when a garment is physically remade into something else.
tashmishei-kedushah/repurposing-garments.description: May a garment worn for ordinary use become a paroches? The Magen Avraham says changing its form makes it new, building on Menachos 22b and used wood.

tashmishei-kedushah/reusing-mitzvah-obje.intro: It is good to reuse an object from one mitzvah for another, like the worn priestly garments made into wicks for Simchas Beis HaShoevah. The Maharil suggests old tzitzis as a bookmark in a sefer, and the Yad Chanoch suggests using your esrog for charoses. The article on Sukkah 42a also notes the Rema's minhag of using hoshanos to bake matzah, while the Mishnah Berurah mentions burning chametz with them.
tashmishei-kedushah/reusing-mitzvah-obje.description: Can an item from one mitzvah be used for another, like an esrog for charoses or hoshanos for chametz? The customs, in an article on Sukkah 42a.

tashmishei-kedushah/used-items-for-a-sef.intro: Someone offers an old velvet sofa cover or a designer jacket to make a mantle for a Sefer Torah. The Agudah, building on the used wood of Menachos 22b, says items for a Sefer Torah should be new, while the Chavos Yair permits used clothing. The Rama and Shulchan Aruch follow the Agudah, and the Darchei Moshe prefers a simple new cover over a nicer used one.
tashmishei-kedushah/used-items-for-a-sef.description: May old fabric or a used garment become a Sefer Torah cover? The Agudah, Chavos Yair, Rama and Mishnah Berurah weigh in, drawing on Menachos 22b.

mitzvah-principles/acting-on-inspiration.intro: A wealthy man asked Rebbe Elazar bar Tzadok whether his workers could take Shemittah olives as pay, then left abruptly when told no. Rav Yisrael Salanter explains on Sukkah 44a that he rushed off to stop the practice at once, and that zeal is what impressed Rebbe Elazar. [Without Delay](/daf/sukkah/44/without-delay) draws the lesson: a commitment made in a moment of inspiration must be acted on right away.
mitzvah-principles/acting-on-inspiration.description: Why act on inspiration right away? Rav Yisrael Salanter on the man who left Rebbe Elazar mid-talk, and the ram at the Akeidah, from Sukkah 44a.

mitzvah-principles/bal-tosif-adding-to-m.intro: The Torah forbids adding to a mitzvah, like a fifth parsha in tefillin, yet in Yoma 57a the Kohen Gadol sprinkles three sets of blood when the bull and goat blood got mixed up. The Tosfos Yeshanim explains that the extra set is only a way out of doubt, not an addition. The same question returns with two mezuzos, two sets of tzitzis, and Rashi and Rabbeinu Tam tefillin.
mitzvah-principles/bal-tosif-adding-to-m.description: When is doing something extra a ban of bal tosif? The Kohen Gadol's third sprinkling in Yoma 57a, and how the rule applies to mezuzos, tzitzis, tefillin.

mitzvah-principles/choosing-a-day-of-fur.intro: A prisoner was allowed out of jail one day a year and asked which day to pick, and another rav told him Yom Kippur or Purim. The Radvaz strongly disagreed: based on ein ma'avirin al ha'mitzvos, he should take the first day with a mitzvah he cannot do in jail. The case appears in a discussion of Yoma 58b, alongside the Magen Avraham's reason for the rule.
mitzvah-principles/choosing-a-day-of-fur.description: A prisoner may leave jail one day a year: which should he pick? The Radvaz rules to grab the first mitzvah day, not Yom Kippur, discussed with Yoma 58b.

mitzvah-principles/do-pomegranates-have-.intro: Every preschooler learns that a pomegranate has 613 seeds, but Rabbi Shlomo Zalman Ehrenreich would accept that only if it had a valid source. [Sowing The Seeds For Mitzvos](/daf/pesachim/74/sowing-the-seeds-for-mitzvos) on Pesachim 74 tells of a student whose pomegranate had exactly 613, and of a Columbia study whose counts ranged from 286 to 1,370. The average of all 206 pomegranates came out to 613.
mitzvah-principles/do-pomegranates-have-.description: Does a pomegranate really have 613 seeds? The sources for the belief, a Michigan student's count and a 206-pomegranate study, told on Pesachim 74.

mitzvah-principles/doing-a-mitzvah-yours.intro: Should you write a plain Sefer Torah yourself or hire an expert scribe to write a beautiful one? The Chaya Adam left it open, but the Doveiv Meisharim and Rav Vozner chose the nicer mitzvah. Building on the Mishna in Shevuos 27 about building a sukkah, the article adds rulings on Chanukah lights by an agent and on a white challah given up out of kindness.
mitzvah-principles/doing-a-mitzvah-yours.description: Is it better to do a mitzvah yourself or have it done more beautifully by an agent? Poskim on a Sefer Torah, Chanukah lights and sukkahs, from Shevuos 27.

mitzvah-principles/doing-part-of-a-mitzv.intro: Dovid HaMelech could not build the Beis HaMikdash, yet he bought the site, drew plans, gathered materials and sanctified the floor discussed in Zevachim 24. Moshe Rabbeinu set aside three cities of refuge, knowing they would not work in his lifetime. [Reach Out and Grab a Mitzvah](/daf/zevachim/24/reach-out-and-grab-a-mitzvah) draws the lesson: when the whole is out of reach, grab whatever part you can.
mitzvah-principles/doing-part-of-a-mitzv.description: When you cannot do a whole mitzvah, do the part you can. Dovid HaMelech and the Beis HaMikdash floor in Zevachim 24, and Moshe with the cities of refuge.

mitzvah-principles/ein-maavirin-al-hamit.intro: We do not pass over a mitzvah, so a man reaching into his bag should not reach over his tefillin to get his tallis. Does that rule apply when choosing where or how to do one mitzvah? Tosfos in Zevachim 51a says no: it applies only when two mitzvos compete, which is why the Levushei Mordechai lets a person walk past one shul to reach another.
mitzvah-principles/ein-maavirin-al-hamit.description: Ein maavirin al hamitzvos: when must you take the first mitzvah in front of you? Tosfos in Zevachim 51a says it applies only when two mitzvos compete.

mitzvah-principles/hiddur-mitzvah-versus.intro: Lighting the Chanukah menorah with olive oil is a hiddur mitzvah, but mitzvos should also be done at the first chance. If only wax candles are on hand and oil is on its way, should one wait? Rav Shlomo Zalman left the question open, and the article on Shevuos 11b goes on to the Parah Adumah, where a nicer animal replaces the first.
mitzvah-principles/hiddur-mitzvah-versus.description: Should you wait for olive oil for the menorah or light right away with wax? Rav Shlomo Zalman weighs hiddur against zerizus, in an article on Shevuos 11b.

mitzvah-principles/is-a-beautiful-house-.intro: A wealthy man wants to build the biggest mansion in the city and wonders if it is a hiddur mitzvah, since the house will hold a mezuzah. In [Hiddur Miss](/daf/nazir/2/hiddur-miss), on Nazir 2b, Rav Moshe Feinstein's ruling on the tallis says no. A building made for a mitzvah, like a shul or yeshiva, should be beautified, but a home built for oneself is not.
mitzvah-principles/is-a-beautiful-house-.description: Is building a lavish home a mitzvah because it holds a mezuzah? Rav Moshe Feinstein says no, but a shul or yeshiva is, from an article on Nazir 2b.

mitzvah-principles/joining-others-in-a-m.intro: Rebbe Akiva in Makkos 5b learns from a third false witness that anyone who joins sinners shares their punishment, however small his part. The flip side is that one who joins people doing a mitzvah shares the full reward, and Chazal say the reward is 500 times greater. Rabbeinu Yonah rules this way, so one who helps at a bris is as if he did the bris himself.
mitzvah-principles/joining-others-in-a-m.description: Does someone who joins others in a mitzvah share the full reward, even with a small part? Rebbe Akiva's lesson and Rabbeinu Yonah's ruling, Makkos 5b.

mitzvah-principles/maakeh-roof-railing.intro: A man with a flat roof knew the Torah requires a protective fence, a ma'akeh, around it. To save money, he asked Rav Moshe Feinstein whether poles at the corners joined by a string would do, and Rav Moshe answered that a tzuras ha'pesach won't prevent you from falling. Tied to Kiddushin 6b, the lesson is that a halachic concept found in one place does not apply everywhere.
mitzvah-principles/maakeh-roof-railing.description: Can a symbolic string doorframe count as a ma'akeh around a roof? Rav Moshe Feinstein says it won't stop a fall, in an article tied to Kiddushin 6b.

mitzvah-principles/mitzvah-items-from-no.intro: Tefillin must be made from kosher animals. The Magen Avraham reads the Rema as saying that every mitzvah item that can come from a kosher animal must, which would raise questions about silk tzitzis or whale oil for Chanukah. The Torah Lishmah, in an article on Sukkah 23, holds that the rule is only for tefillin and perhaps shofar, so a non-kosher elephant could even serve as a sukkah wall.
mitzvah-principles/mitzvah-items-from-no.description: Must every mitzvah item come from a kosher animal, as with tefillin? The Magen Avraham and Torah Lishmah weigh in, in an article on Sukkah 23.

mitzvah-principles/mitzvah-preparation-c.intro: The river in Chullin 7a refused to split for R' Pinchas ben Yair, saying his mission to redeem captives might fail. But he also had it split for a man carrying wheat for matzos. The Rivash learns that someone doing even a preparatory step is already engaged in a mitzvah, so R' Pinchas was in the middle of a mitzvah whether or not he succeeded.
mitzvah-principles/mitzvah-preparation-c.description: Is preparing for a mitzvah already a mitzvah? The Rivash learns it from a man carrying wheat for matzos, for whom the river split. From Chullin 7a.

mitzvah-principles/not-delaying-mitzvos.intro: The Korban Pesach was offered in three shifts, and the last one was called the lazy shift. In Pesachim 65a the Gemara asks why they are called lazy, since someone has to be last, and answers that it does not have to be you. The Maharit applies this to Minchah: one fulfills the mitzvah until sunset, but a person should always try to do mitzvos while plenty of time remains.
mitzvah-principles/not-delaying-mitzvos.description: Someone has to be last, but it does not have to be you. The lazy shift of the Korban Pesach in Pesachim 65a teaches not to push mitzvos off.

mitzvah-principles/reward-for-inspiring-.intro: Yoma 28a calls Mincha the prayer of Avraham, though Yitzchak instituted it. The Ben Yehoyada explains that Avraham's morning prayer inspired Yitzchak to enact the afternoon one, and whoever inspires another to do a mitzvah shares in its credit. [Mincha Motivation](/daf/yoma/28/mincha-motivation) concludes that each mitzvah we do is also done for all those watching.
mitzvah-principles/reward-for-inspiring-.description: Do you earn credit for mitzvos others do because of you? Why Yoma 28a calls Mincha Avraham's prayer, and the Ben Yehoyada's explanation of it.

mitzvah-principles/searching-for-reasons.intro: The Rambam explains that cutting peyos is forbidden because idol worshippers did it, and the Tur replies that we need not seek reasons for mitzvos. In [Peyos Prohibitions](/daf/makkos/20/peyos-prohibitions), filed on Makkos 20, the Beis Yosef defends giving reasons where possible. The Rema says the Tur's real concern was that a stated reason might wrongly limit when the prohibition applies.
mitzvah-principles/searching-for-reasons.description: Should we look for reasons behind mitzvos, and can a reason limit a mitzvah? The Rambam, Tur, Beis Yosef and Rema on peyos, tied to Makkos 20.

mitzvah-principles/selling-the-reward-fo.intro: Shevna offered his brother Hillel half his wealth for half of Hillel's reward for learning, and a Heavenly voice scorned him, as Sotah 21a tells. The Meiri and the Tashbetz explain why a supporter can share in Torah only by making it possible from the start. Rav Shlomo Kluger adds that reward for mitzvos is a gift from Hashem, and a gift cannot be passed on to someone else.
mitzvah-principles/selling-the-reward-fo.description: Can the reward for a mitzvah be sold to someone else? Sotah 21a tells of Hillel and Shevna, and Rav Shlomo Kluger says reward is a gift from Hashem.

mitzvah-principles/sinning-to-help-anoth.intro: The Gemara in Shabbos says one may not take dough out of an oven, a rabbinic prohibition, to save a forgetful baker from a Torah violation. Yet the Mishnah in Gittin 41a forces a master to free a half-slave, breaking a mitzvah so the slave can marry. Tosfos answers that marriage is a mitzvah rabbah, or that the half-slave, unlike the baker, did nothing wrong.
mitzvah-principles/sinning-to-help-anoth.description: May you commit a lesser sin to help another do a mitzvah? Tosfos compares the half-slave in Gittin 41a with the baker who put dough in the oven on Shabbos.

mitzvah-principles/sinning-to-save-anoth.intro: May a person commit a small sin to save someone else from a big one? The Gemara in Shabbos says no, which makes Aharon's role in the Golden Calf, discussed on Sanhedrin 7a, hard to explain. Rav Gavriel Zev Margoliyos answers from Tosfos that a great mitzvah allows a minor sin, and the Beis Yosef applies this to rescuing a kidnapped daughter even on Shabbos.
mitzvah-principles/sinning-to-save-anoth.description: May one sin to save another from a greater sin? Tosfos on a mitzvah rabbah, Aharon's choice in Sanhedrin 7a and saving a child from conversion on Shabbos.

mitzvah-principles/spending-money-to-avo.intro: A kohen learned his cheap flight home would pass over a cemetery, and a new ticket would cost an extra $1,000. His posek ruled that he must pay, since one must use all he has to avoid a lav, while the twenty percent limit applies only to a mitzvas asei. [When The Sky Is Not The Limit](/daf/nazir/55/when-the-sky-is-not-the-limit), on Nazir 55, adds the Chofetz Chaim on lashon ha'ra.
mitzvah-principles/spending-money-to-avo.description: Must one spend everything to avoid a sin, but only twenty percent on a mitzvah? A kohen's $1,000 flight and the Chofetz Chaim, in an article on Nazir 55.

mitzvah-principles/switching-to-a-nicer-.intro: Suppose you set up your Chanukah menorah with wax candles and then find olive oil, which is more mehudar. The Shvua Yaakov says you should stay with what you chose first, but the Chacham Tzvi disagrees and says to use the finer oil. The question grows out of Yoma 64a, where a korban picked first does not always get priority.
mitzvah-principles/switching-to-a-nicer-.description: May you swap a mitzvah item you already picked for a nicer one? The Shvua Yaakov and the Chacham Tzvi on wax candles and olive oil, from Yoma 64a.

mitzvah-principles/tadir-kodem.intro: Zevachim 89 teaches tadir kodem: the more frequent mitzvah comes first. On Rosh Chodesh Elul, Borchi Nafshi, said at least eleven times a year, comes before L'Dovid, said only one season a year. But Sefiras HaOmer comes before Kiddush Levana, since ein maavirin al hamitzvos means doing the mitzvah right in front of you.
mitzvah-principles/tadir-kodem.description: Tadir kodem: the more frequent mitzvah comes first. Borchi Nafshi and L'Dovid, Sefirah and Kiddush Levana, and other cases built on Zevachim 89.

bris-milah/bris-for-a-baby-born-at-twili.intro: A baby born during twilight on Friday may have been born on Friday or on Shabbos. Friday may be only day seven, and Shabbos may be day nine, when a bris cannot override Shabbos, so the bris moves to Sunday. Yoma 64a then helps decide whether this baby goes before another one having a bris that same day.
bris-milah/bris-for-a-baby-born-at-twili.description: When a baby is born at twilight on Friday, why is his bris on Sunday? The doubt between day seven and day nine explained, with a lesson from Yoma 64a.

bris-milah/bris-yitzchak-night-before-th.intro: A Sefardi father once told a friend that his family does not make a shalom zachar, but holds a meal on the night before the bris instead. Is that gathering really a stand-in for the Friday night one? The Noda BeYehuda reads the Tosfos on Bava Kamma 80a as describing a thanksgiving meal tied to the bris itself, held the night before it.
bris-milah/bris-yitzchak-night-before-th.description: Is the Sefardi meal on the night before the bris like a shalom zachar? The Noda BeYehuda ties the thanksgiving meal to the bris, from Bava Kamma 80a.

bris-milah/lighting-candles-at-a-bris-mi.intro: Sanhedrin 32b tells that during a decree against Jewish weddings and bris milah, candles lit by day and a millstone's grinding signaled a celebration. Tosfos notes a custom in his day to light candles at a bris, and the Shibolei HaLeket gives two reasons: candles are festive, and they recall the time of persecution. The Be'er Moshe argues they were chosen only because they were an oddity.
bris-milah/lighting-candles-at-a-bris-mi.description: Why light candles at a daytime bris milah? Sanhedrin 32b's secret signals in times of persecution, Tosfos's custom and the Shibolei HaLeket's two reasons.

bris-milah/no-bris-milah-in-the-midbar.intro: Yevamos 71b says bris milah was not done during the years in the desert, since travel and harsh weather made it dangerous for babies. Uncircumcised males cannot eat the Korban Pesach, and Rashi adds that their parents cannot either. Tosfos say the harsh weather was itself a punishment for the spies, so the people were held responsible for a situation they never imagined.
bris-milah/no-bris-milah-in-the-midbar.description: Why was there no bris milah in the desert? Danger from travel and harsh weather, and how Tosfos tie it to the sin of the spies, from Yevamos 71b.

bris-milah/order-of-two-brissim-in-one-s.intro: Two babies, one mohel, one shul: who goes first? Using Yoma 64a, where two korbanos became fit at the same moment, Shimon argues that babies born the same day have no order, since both obligations start on the morning of the eighth day. The Birchas Avrohom adds that the firstborn goes first if there would be strife, and the Chelkas Yaakov puts a delayed bris second.
bris-milah/order-of-two-brissim-in-one-s.description: Two brissim in one shul: which baby goes first? The Birchas Avrohom and Chelkas Yaakov decide based on when each obligation began, using Yoma 64a.

bris-milah/shalom-zachar-origin.intro: The Gemara never mentions a shalom zachar. On Bava Kamma 80a, though, Tosfos explains a Yeshua HaBen as a party thanking Hashem that mother and baby survived childbirth, and the Terumas HaDeshen calls this the source. In [Shalom, Zachor!](/daf/bava-kamma/80/shalom-zachor), other views follow: the Maharshal says guests come to comfort the baby for the Torah he forgot.
bris-milah/shalom-zachar-origin.description: Where does the Friday night shalom zachar come from? The Terumas HaDeshen points to Tosfos on Bava Kamma 80a, and others say it comforts the baby.

pidyon-haben/bas-kohens-husband-at-pidyo.intro: At a pidyon haben seudah, a guest who led bentching was scolded for not saying birshus hakohanim. The Chasam Sofer quipped that perhaps no kohen was there, only a Yisrael who took the money for his kohen wife, as one answer in Tosfos on Kiddushin 8a explains Rav Kahane. When people began quoting this as halacha, he was horrified and wrote that the Rav Kahane there was a kohen.
pidyon-haben/bas-kohens-husband-at-pidyo.description: May a Yisrael married to a kohen's daughter accept pidyon haben money for her? The Chasam Sofer's quip and his later correction, on Kiddushin 8a.

pidyon-haben/firstborns-offering-korbano.intro: Before the Mishkan, the avodah was done by firstborns, and the Rambam says this was true from Adam HaRishon until Moshe. But were all the Avos bechoros? [Firstborn Offerings](/daf/zevachim/112/firstborn-offerings) shows how Avraham and Shem were given the status for their righteousness, Yitzchak was his mother's firstborn, and Yaakov bought it from Esav, in a discussion of Zevachim 112.
pidyon-haben/firstborns-offering-korbano.description: Firstborns did the avodah before the Mishkan. How could the Avos and Shem offer korbanos? The Rambam and the commentators, in a discussion of Zevachim 112.

pidyon-haben/pidyon-haben-on-shabbos.intro: Pidyon haben is not done on Shabbos, because transactions are restricted then. Could a father give the kohen five coins on Friday, so that the kohen acquires them only on Shabbos? The Terumas HaDeshen says it would work but the father would lose the bracha, while Rebbe Akiva Eiger, building on Yoma 13b, would forbid it.
pidyon-haben/pidyon-haben-on-shabbos.description: Can a pidyon haben be set up on Friday to take effect on Shabbos? The Terumas HaDeshen, the lost bracha, and Rebbe Akiva Eiger, from Yoma 13b.

pidyon-haben/pidyon-haben-without-a-kohe.intro: Can a pidyon haben be done without a kohen? Tosefos on Kiddushin 8a suggest Rav Kahane accepted the redemption for his kohen wife, but they also say this Rav Kahane may simply have been a kohen. The Chasam Sofer concluded that a Yisrael married to a bas kohen may fill in only if no kohen is around on the day, and the baby must be redeemed again later.
pidyon-haben/pidyon-haben-without-a-kohe.description: Can a Yisrael married to a kohen's daughter do a pidyon haben when no kohen is found? The Chasam Sofer's ruling, drawing on Tosefos in Kiddushin 8a.

kibbud-av-vaem/calling-a-parent-by-first.intro: May a child call his father Abba if that is his father's actual name? On Yevamos 57b, Shmuel calls Rav Abba, and Rashi and Tosfos argue whether that was an endearing title or Rav's real name. The Chida suggests a son might use Abba as a term of endearment, but warns not to rush to rely on it, and the Shem HaGedolim agrees with the stricter view.
kibbud-av-vaem/calling-a-parent-by-first.description: May a child call a father named Abba by that word? Rashi and Tosfos on Shmuel's name for Rav in Yevamos 57b, the Chida, and the Shem HaGedolim.

kibbud-av-vaem/friend-with-a-parents-nam.intro: The Shulchan Aruch rules that if your father has a rare name, you should not call a friend with that name by his first name in your father's presence. The Aruch traces this to Abaye, whose uncle Rabbah would not call out his own father's name, Nachmani. [When a Father Is Named “Abba”](/daf/chullin/35/when-a-father-is-named-abba) applies it to Shmuel, whose father was also Abba, building on Chullin 35.
kibbud-av-vaem/friend-with-a-parents-nam.description: May you call a friend by your father's rare name in front of him? The Shulchan Aruch, the Aruch on Abaye, and Shmuel calling Rav Abba. From Chullin 35.

kibbud-av-vaem/fulfilling-a-parents-last.intro: A son has a special mitzvah to carry out his parents' wishes after they pass away. A dying mother asked her children to settle any inheritance dispute before a relative, and one son later refused. The Chashukei Chemed on Bava Basra 147b brings the Shvus Yaakov, who says the oath Yosef swore to Yaakov Avinu shows that a promise turns this mitzvah into an absolute obligation.
kibbud-av-vaem/fulfilling-a-parents-last.description: Must a son keep a promise he made to his dying mother? The Shvus Yaakov says an oath makes a parent's last wish binding. From Bava Basra 147b.

tzedakah/anonymous-giving.intro: At the cornerstone ceremony for the Maharsha's new yeshiva, a man won the honor with a bid of 500 rubles, and asked that no one learn who he was. He even gave the honor to the Maharsha, and only the Maharsha was told, since the man was poor and the money was nearly all he had. [Bidding on Buildings and Baby Boys](/daf/moed-katan/9/bidding-on-buildings-and-baby-boys) ties the story to Moed Katan 9a.
tzedakah/anonymous-giving.description: A poor man secretly gave nearly all he had for the Maharsha's yeshiva cornerstone. A story of hidden tzedakah, tied to the Gemara in Moed Katan 9a.

tzedakah/camp-nageela-founding-story.intro: JEP of Long Island hoped for a bequest that objectors were holding up, and a local rosh yeshiva agreed to help. That same day his yeshiva got a $100,000 pledge, and the amounts kept matching almost to the dollar. In [Putting You First](/daf/bava-kamma/92/putting-you-first), the rosh yeshiva credits the teaching of Bava Kamma 92, and the money built Camp Nageela.
tzedakah/camp-nageela-founding-story.description: A rosh yeshiva helped JEP win a bequest, and matching gifts reached his own yeshiva first. The story behind Camp Nageela, tied to Bava Kamma 92.

tzedakah/charity-for-ulterior-motives.intro: Nakdimon ben Gurion gave huge sums to the poor, yet Kesubos 66b says he lost his fortune because he gave for his own honor. But isn't charity given for a personal reason still a mitzvah? In [Charity with Uncharitable Intentions](/daf/kesubos/66/charity-with-uncharitable-intentions), the Maharsha says giving for honor is a disgraceful motive, while the Hafloah says it is a full mitzvah that simply does not protect one's wealth.
tzedakah/charity-for-ulterior-motives.description: Is tzedakah given for honor still a full mitzvah? The Maharsha and the Hafloah explain why Nakdimon ben Gurion lost his wealth in Kesubos 66b.

tzedakah/delaying-a-tzedakah-pledge.intro: Rava says on Rosh Hashanah 6a that one who pledges money to the poor and does not pay right away violates the ban on delaying vows. The Dvar Avraham applies this to inviting poor guests for Friday night: the invitation is a pledge of food, so keeping them waiting may be a problem. HaRav Elchonon Peretz asks whether a family meal counts too, but the Taz suggests feeding one's children is not tzedakah in this sense.
tzedakah/delaying-a-tzedakah-pledge.description: Delaying a tzedakah pledge violates a Torah ban, says Rava in Rosh Hashanah 6a. Can keeping poor guests waiting for their Friday night meal do the same?

tzedakah/does-tzedakah-protect-your-weal.intro: A young man turned $3,000 into nearly a million dollars and gave tzedakah generously, then lost it all on bad trades. He asked Rav Pinchas Scheinberg whether tzedakah is supposed to protect one's wealth. The article on Nedarim 50b records the answer: either the money would return, or it was taken in place of his life, and his rebbe added that the loss may have been a kapparah to merit finding his wife.
tzedakah/does-tzedakah-protect-your-weal.description: If tzedakah protects your money, how can a generous giver lose it all? Rav Pinchas Scheinberg's answer to a young investor, told on Nedarim 50b.

tzedakah/giving-more-than-twenty-percent.intro: The Gemara in Kesubos 50a records the enactment at Usha not to give away more than a fifth of one's money, even to tzedakah. Yet Ben Kalba Savua gave Rebbe Akiva half his money in Kesubos 63a, and Mar Ukva gave away half as he was dying. In [More Than Twenty Percent](/daf/kesubos/63/more-than-twenty-percent), the limit is shown not to apply to the dying, to supporters of Torah, or perhaps to the very wealthy.
tzedakah/giving-more-than-twenty-percent.description: May you give more than a fifth of your money to tzedakah? The Usha enactment in Kesubos 50a, and exceptions for the dying, the rich and Torah supporters.

tzedakah/merit-of-supporting-those-who-s.intro: Dovid HaMelech learned through the Urim v'Tumim that one cause of a famine was Shaul's role in the deaths of the Givonim, as Yevamos 78b relates. The Maharsha explains that the Givonim supplied food and water to Nov, a city of people serving Hashem, and that mitzvah was the merit that sustained them. When Nov was destroyed, they lost that merit, and seven of them perished.
tzedakah/merit-of-supporting-those-who-s.description: Does supporting those who serve Hashem bring merit? The Maharsha on the Givonim who supplied Nov and lost their merit when it fell, Yevamos 78b.

tzedakah/paying-a-yizkor-tzedakah-pledge.intro: A tzedaka pledge made at Yizkor must actually be paid, and the Kav V'Yashar warns that failing to do so can harm the neshama. The Terumas HaDeshen would not eat the day after Yom Kippur until he paid his pledge. The article on Nazir 31 ends with a story of a granddaughter who kept dreaming of her grandmother asking about unpaid tzedaka pledges.
tzedakah/paying-a-yizkor-tzedakah-pledge.description: How soon must a Yizkor tzedaka pledge be paid? The Kav V'Yashar, the Terumas HaDeshen and a striking dream story, in an article on Nazir 31.

tzedakah/rebbe-meir-baal-hanes-tzedakah.intro: On Avodah Zarah 18, Rebbe Meir rescued Bruriah's sister and taught her guard to call out to the G-d of Meir, words that later saved him from execution. That story is the basis for giving tzedakah in memory of Rebbe Meir Baal Hanes to find a lost item. The Me'il Tzedakah writes that the gift should ideally be oil or candles for light, though most people today give to any tzedakah.
tzedakah/rebbe-meir-baal-hanes-tzedakah.description: Why people give tzedakah in memory of Rebbe Meir Baal Hanes when something is lost, and why oil or candles are ideal, from the story on Avodah Zarah 18.

tzedakah/sparing-the-poor-from-embarrass.intro: When a korban Pesach became tamei, its owner had to burn it in public, in front of the Beis HaMikdash. Pesachim 85b rules that even a rich man must use the Mikdash's wood, so a poor man who cannot afford his own is not shamed. The Tosfos Yom Tov adds that Chazal would even give up hiddur mitzvah to protect the poor, if not for the honor of the Beis HaMikdash.
tzedakah/sparing-the-poor-from-embarrass.description: Why must even a rich man use Temple wood to burn his tamei korban? Pesachim 85b shows how Chazal guarded the poor from shame, even above hiddur mitzvah.

tzedakah/tzedakah-as-a-segulah-for-child.intro: A childless man secretly gave nearly all he owned for the Maharsha's new yeshiva, and the Maharsha blessed him with a son who would learn there. Rav Moshe Dov HaLevi Soloveichik explains the blessing from Moed Katan 9a, where all who joined the Beis HaMikdash celebration had a baby boy. A Midrash Tanchuma promises a son to one who pays Torah teachers' wages.
tzedakah/tzedakah-as-a-segulah-for-child.description: Can tzedakah for Torah bring the blessing of children? The Maharsha's blessing for a son, based on Moed Katan 9a, and a Midrash about paying rebbeim.

tzedakah/tzedakah-pledges-and-vows.intro: When it comes to mitzvos, what counts as a vow is broader than usual, so a pledge to tzedakah can easily become binding. That is why, when someone makes a Mi Sheberach and pledges charity, it is wise to add bli neder. [No Promises](/daf/shevuos/36/no-promises), filed on Shevuos 36, explains why this phrase matters more than people think.
tzedakah/tzedakah-pledges-and-vows.description: Why can a pledge to tzedakah become a vow so easily, and how do you pledge without one? Saying bli neder at a Mi Sheberach, from an article on Shevuos 36.

tzedakah/yeshiva-donations-from-non-obse.intro: Rebbe Chiya planted flax and hunted deer to make his own parchment, and the Maharsha says a Torah project with a pure foundation is more successful. For the same reason, the Chofetz Chaim would not accept yeshiva donations from people who did not keep Shabbos. Rav Henoch Leibowitz said such funds could go to a secular studies department, in an article on Bava Metzia 85b.
tzedakah/yeshiva-donations-from-non-obse.description: Should a yeshiva take money from donors who don't keep Shabbos? The Chofetz Chaim refused, and Rav Henoch Leibowitz found a use, from Bava Metzia 85b.

chesed/bikur-cholim-benefits-the-visitor.intro: Visiting the sick is not only a kindness to the patient. In [The Power of Bikur Cholim](/daf/nedarim/39/the-power-of-bikur-cholim), the Kli Yakar teaches, on the hint to bikur cholim in Nedarim 39b, that the visitor sees how fragile life is and takes his own life more seriously. Like Shlomo HaMelech's house of mourning, that soul searching becomes a great merit for the choleh who inspired it.
chesed/bikur-cholim-benefits-the-visitor.description: Bikur cholim helps the visitor too: the Kli Yakar on Nedarim 39b explains how seeing illness leads to lasting change and earns merit for the patient.

chesed/bikur-cholim-by-phone.intro: Does a phone call count as visiting the sick? The Beer Moshe and Rav Elyashiv say no, since the verse on Bava Metzia 30b speaks of walking, and in person you can see what the patient needs. In [Visiting the Sick](/daf/bava-metzia/30/visiting-the-sick), Rav Moshe Feinstein holds that a call fulfills the mitzvah to some degree, though one should still try to visit.
chesed/bikur-cholim-by-phone.description: Does calling a sick person fulfill bikur cholim? The Beer Moshe and Rav Elyashiv say no, while Rav Moshe says partly, based on Bava Metzia 30b.

chesed/chesed-and-long-life.intro: Eli's descendants were cursed to die young, yet Rabbah, who learned and taught Torah, lived to 40, and Abaye, who added acts of kindness, lived to 60, as Yevamos 105a relates. Rabbeinu Elchanan in Tosfos explains that Rabbah surely did chesed too, but did not reach Abaye's level. The Chofetz Chaim adds that Abaye's extra years made up for the learning time he gave away.
chesed/chesed-and-long-life.description: Can chesed add years to a life? Rabbah lived to 40 and Abaye to 60, explains Yevamos 105a, with Rabbeinu Elchanan and the Chofetz Chaim on why.

chesed/delivering-a-package-for-someone.intro: A traveler agreed to bring a package of clothing to Eretz Yisrael, then left the relative waiting for months. When asked why, he replied, where does it say in the Torah you have to be nice? [The Fifth Shulchan Aruch](/daf/nazir/45/the-fifth-shulchan-aruch), filed on Nazir 45a, shows that taking on such a favor brings a real duty to act decently, even without a written rule.
chesed/delivering-a-package-for-someone.description: What do you owe someone after agreeing to carry a package for them? A traveler who made a relative wait months, and the duty to be decent, from Nazir 45a.

chesed/hachnasas-orchim-before-shalom-al.intro: When the Chofetz Chaim brought hungry travelers home for Friday night, he made Kiddush at once and sang Shalom Aleichem later. If hosting guests is greater than greeting the Divine Presence, he explained, it surely comes before greeting angels, who are not hungry. The Dvar Avraham adds a reason from Rosh Hashanah 6a, while Rav Moshe Sternbuch says a starving guest must be fed right away.
