chesed/hachnasas-orchim-before-shalom-al.description: Should hungry Friday night guests eat before Shalom Aleichem? The Chofetz Chaim's practice, the Dvar Avraham and Rosh Hashanah 6a on making guests wait.

chesed/helping-others-brings-help-to-you.intro: The K'sav Sofer says Hashem rewards measure for measure: one who tries to help another is helped. A local rosh yeshiva taught from this that the blessing of Bava Kamma 92 is not limited to prayer. Whenever a person helps a friend with a need he shares, Hashem helps the helper first, and then the friend.
chesed/helping-others-brings-help-to-you.description: Is being answered first only for prayer? The K'sav Sofer's measure for measure suggests helping a friend with a shared need also works, Bava Kamma 92.

chesed/hosting-guests-greater-than-greet.intro: Rav teaches that hosting guests is greater than greeting the Divine Presence, learned from Avraham, who left his conversation with Hashem to greet three travelers. The Baal Shem Tov asked why, since any mitzvah is like greeting the Shechinah. In a piece tied to Kiddushin 31, the Naharos Eisan explains that idle chatter with a guest on Shabbos is still hachnasas orchim, even though it is not greeting the Shechinah.
chesed/hosting-guests-greater-than-greet.description: Why is hosting guests greater than greeting the Shechinah? The Baal Shem Tov's question and who counts as a guest, in an article tied to Kiddushin 31.

chesed/how-to-make-a-shivah-call.intro: What does the mitzvah of nichum aveilim really involve? Rav Moshe Feinstein writes that it is done mainly by talking with the mourner and easing some of his pain, while the Perisha suggests that just sitting with him also counts. [A Halacha That’s Clear-Cut](/daf/moed-katan/28/a-halacha-thats-clear-cut) adds that, per Moed Katan 28b, visitors wait for the mourner to speak first.
chesed/how-to-make-a-shivah-call.description: What does comforting mourners involve, sitting quietly or talking with them? Rav Moshe and the Perisha on nichum aveilim, from Moed Katan 28b.

chesed/is-bikur-cholim-a-torah-mitzvah.intro: Rav Yosef's beraisa on Bava Metzia 30b reads visiting the ill into the words "they shall walk" in a verse about kindness. The Ramban therefore counts bikur cholim as a Torah mitzvah, while the Rambam calls it rabbinic, though it still fulfills the Torah mitzvah of chessed. The Tur gives two purposes: caring for the patient's needs and praying for him.
chesed/is-bikur-cholim-a-torah-mitzvah.description: Is visiting the sick a Torah or rabbinic mitzvah? The Ramban and Rambam read Rav Yosef's beraisa in Bava Metzia 30b differently, and the Tur explains why.

chesed/korach-and-bikur-cholim.intro: Moshe told Korach's followers that if they died like all men, with "pekudas kol ha'adam" upon them, then Hashem had not sent him. Nedarim 39b finds a hint to bikur cholim in those words. [Visitor Rewards](/daf/nedarim/39/visitor-rewards) asks why Moshe brought up visiting the sick at all, and the Kli Yakar answers that people whose illness inspires their visitors to grow must be righteous.
chesed/korach-and-bikur-cholim.description: Nedarim 39b finds a hint to bikur cholim in Moshe's words to Korach. The Kli Yakar explains why Moshe mentioned visiting the sick at that moment.

chesed/where-to-sit-when-visiting-the-si.intro: When visiting a sick person, where should you sit? Rashi teaches that the Divine Presence rests at the head of a sick person, and the Beis Hillel learns from this not to sit by the patient's head or feet. [Sworn Statements](/daf/bava-basra/147/sworn-statements), on Bava Basra 147b, adds that the most important thing is what makes the patient feel comfortable.
chesed/where-to-sit-when-visiting-the-si.description: Where should a visitor sit by a sick person's bed? Not by the head, where the Shechinah rests, but comfort comes first. A note from Bava Basra 147b.

talmud-torah/analytical-gemara-learning.intro: Rabbi Shmuel Niman's morning shiur at Yeshivas Chofetz Chaim did not try to cover ground; it took one sugya and studied it intensely. Every sugya faced his five questions: the hava amina, the maskana, the movement between them, the pivot that movement depends on, and finally what the sugya means as a whole. On some mornings the commentary of the day was the Rosh, meaning students had to use their own heads.
talmud-torah/analytical-gemara-learning.description: Rabbi Shmuel Niman's five questions for learning a sugya in depth: the hava amina, the maskana, the movement between them, and the pivot it turns on.

talmud-torah/baby-learning-torah-in-the-.intro: Rebbe Simlai says a baby learns the whole Torah in the womb, and then an angel strikes its mouth at birth and it forgets everything. Why teach it only to have it lost? The answer given is that the loss leaves a thirst that drives the child to toil in Torah, and the Gemara's word "found" fits this reading of Niddah 30b.
talmud-torah/baby-learning-torah-in-the-.description: Why does a baby learn the whole Torah in the womb only to forget it at birth? Rebbe Simlai's teaching in Niddah 30b leaves a lifelong thirst for Torah.

talmud-torah/balancing-kiruv-and-persona.intro: Teaching Torah and kiruv need not cost a person his own growth, and the Chasam Sofer promises that Hashem will make up the lost time. But the article on Niddah 14b adds a warning from the author's rosh yeshiva: the promise holds only for those who still set aside time for intensive Torah and mussar study. A professional who keeps no personal learning time will not see these results.
talmud-torah/balancing-kiruv-and-persona.description: Do teachers and kiruv workers still need their own learning time? The Chasam Sofer's promise and a rosh yeshiva's warning, discussed on Niddah 14b.

talmud-torah/buying-seforim.intro: When Rav Kahaneman and Reb Elchonon asked to borrow an obscure sefer, the Chofetz Chaim said he did not own it and was already pained by the seforim he had. Seforim cost money, money costs time, and time is life itself. In [Life is Precious](/daf/gittin/47/life-is-precious), he finds this lesson in Gittin 47a.
talmud-torah/buying-seforim.description: Why was the Chofetz Chaim pained by the seforim he owned? Money is time and time is life, a lesson he drew from Reish Lakish's saffron in Gittin 47a.

talmud-torah/chevrah-shas-group-siyum.intro: In the old chevrah haShas, each member of a shul took one masechta, and together they made a siyum haShas, though no single person had finished Shas. The Nachalah L'Yisrael answers from Rebbe Akiva in Makkos 5b: whoever joins others in a mitzvah gets credit for all of it. The Beis Ephraim applies the same idea to people who write a sefer Torah together.
talmud-torah/chevrah-shas-group-siyum.description: Can a shul that divides the masechtos among its members make a siyum haShas together? The Nachalah L'Yisrael explains, from Rebbe Akiva in Makkos 5b.

talmud-torah/choosing-a-gemara-learning-.intro: Daf Yomi, Amud Yomi, Oraysah and Daf HaShavua move at very different speeds, and those on slower cycles may feel they finish less. At the Darchei Yovel Dinner, Rav Reuven Feinstein stressed that reward for Torah study is based on the time and effort invested, not on masechtos finished. The article on Nazir 2b says two hours of Daf HaShavua beats a rushed half-hour of daf.
talmud-torah/choosing-a-gemara-learning-.description: Daf Yomi, Amud Yomi or a slower cycle? Rav Reuven Feinstein says reward follows the time and effort, not pages done, in an article on Nazir 2b.

talmud-torah/fox-and-the-fish-parable.intro: When the Romans banned Torah study, Rebbe Akiva compared the Jews to fish fleeing nets. A fox invited them onto land, but the fish knew they would die there, and a Jew without Torah is like a fish on land. Rav Meir Shapiro told this parable at a yeshiva opening to explain why Rav signed with a fish on Bava Basra 161b.
talmud-torah/fox-and-the-fish-parable.description: Why is a Jew without Torah like a fish on dry land? Rebbe Akiva's parable of the fox and the fish, used to explain Rav's signature on Bava Basra 161b.

talmud-torah/increasing-torah-study-afte.intro: Hillel taught that one who does not increase, decreases. Rashi links this to the season of Tu B'Av, when nights grow longer and workers come home earlier, so whoever fails to add Torah study in those evenings will suffer for it. The idea opens an article filed on Bava Kamma 77a about using every spare hour for learning.
talmud-torah/increasing-torah-study-afte.description: Longer nights after Tu B'Av mean more time to learn. Rashi explains Hillel's warning that one who does not increase decreases, in Bava Kamma 77a.

talmud-torah/interrupting-torah-study-fo.intro: If someone else can do a mitzvah for him, must a talmid chacham stop learning to do it himself? The Mishnah Berurah leaves the question open, and the Machzik Berachah says a scholar need not leave his learning to prepare a wedding feast. In a discussion filed on Makkos 19, Rav Chaim Kanievsky remarks that he is at least allowed to stop and do the mitzvah himself.
talmud-torah/interrupting-torah-study-fo.description: Must a talmid chacham stop learning to do a mitzvah himself when an agent could do it? The Mishnah Berurah and Rav Chaim Kanievsky, tied to Makkos 19.

talmud-torah/interrupting-torah-study-to.intro: Many sources say that if someone interrupts your learning with small talk, you should politely but firmly explain that you cannot talk now. Learning Torah is equal to all other mitzvos, and bittul Torah is a serious sin. Yet a rosh yeshiva quoted in [Word To The Wise](/daf/kiddushin/31/word-to-the-wise), filed on Kiddushin 31, cautioned that people today are more easily hurt, and the one interrupting may be feeling low.
talmud-torah/interrupting-torah-study-to.description: How should one respond when someone interrupts Torah learning with small talk? A rosh yeshiva's caution about hurt feelings, tied to Kiddushin 31.

talmud-torah/joy-in-learning-torah.intro: When Yosef the Babylonian heard a single ruling from Rebbe Elazar ben Shamua, his face lit up with joy, and his teacher wept and quoted the pasuk Mah ahavti Torasecha. Menachos 18a records the scene. The Ben Yehoyada explains that the word Mah hints at something small: a person should love every piece of Torah, no matter how small.
talmud-torah/joy-in-learning-torah.description: Why did Rebbe Elazar ben Shamua weep when his student's face lit up over one ruling? The Ben Yehoyada on loving even small Torah, from Menachos 18a.

talmud-torah/learning-only-easy-material.intro: A person can learn without stopping and still be guilty of bitul Torah. The Shulchan Aruch HaRav writes that choosing to study only easy parts of the Torah counts as neglecting it. Tied to Megillah 3, the Rashash says the Torah expects a person to use his full mind, so leaving hard study just to hear verses read would be bitul Torah, if not for the Sages' decree.
talmud-torah/learning-only-easy-material.description: Can learning only easy Torah material count as bitul Torah? The Shulchan Aruch HaRav and the Rashash on using one's full mind, tied to Megillah 3.

talmud-torah/learning-torah-alone.intro: Taanis 7a compares two sages learning together to iron sharpening iron, and warns that those who learn alone become foolish. The Maharsha explains that Torah's deep sevaros need real give-and-take, but Rav Yaakov Emden shows from Pirkei Avos that one with no chaburah is rewarded for learning alone. [Sky-High Sevaros](/daf/taanis/7/sky-high-sevaros) uses a 1980 flight that lost all three engines to show how a lone learner can repeat one mistake.
talmud-torah/learning-torah-alone.description: Is it wrong to learn Torah alone? Taanis 7a on iron sharpening iron, the Maharsha, Rav Yaakov Emden, and when learning alone is better after all.

talmud-torah/learning-torah-at-night.intro: Why was Tu B'Av a day of joy? Rabbeinu Gershom explains that once the wood-cutting for the altar ended, people were free to learn, and the nights were getting longer. [The Simcha of a Siyum](/daf/bava-basra/121/the-simcha-of-a-siyum-2024) shows how the Vilna Gaon finds here, on Bava Basra 121a, the source for teaching children to learn at night too.
talmud-torah/learning-torah-at-night.description: Why do the longer nights after Tu B'Av call for more Torah learning? Rabbeinu Gershom and the Vilna Gaon on learning after dark, from Bava Basra 121a.

talmud-torah/learning-torah-in-comfort.intro: When Rav Meir Shapiro raised money for a yeshiva with a dining room and dorm, donors objected that Torah requires hardship. He answered that one should kill oneself for the Torah itself, not for finding meals and lodging. Building on Bava Kamma 61b, he read the Mishna in Avos about bread and salt as a lament about how Torah learners live, not a demand that they suffer.
talmud-torah/learning-torah-in-comfort.description: Must Torah students suffer, or should they learn in comfort? Rav Meir Shapiro defends giving yeshiva boys meals and lodging, building on Bava Kamma 61b.

talmud-torah/learning-torah-no-longer-re.intro: Chullin 17a asks whether meat slaughtered without shechitah in the desert became forbidden once it entered Eretz Yisrael, and leaves it unresolved. Rashi asks why we discuss a question that no longer matters, and answers that we are rewarded for learning Torah even when it has no practical use. The Rosh agrees, but finds a practical case anyway.
talmud-torah/learning-torah-no-longer-re.description: Why study laws that no longer apply? Rashi says Torah learning is rewarded even without practical use, while the Rosh finds a case. From Chullin 17a.

talmud-torah/learning-with-a-chavrusa.intro: One mechanic made the same mistake on all three engines of Eastern Airlines Flight 885, and the plane nearly crashed. Taanis 7a teaches that two scholars sharpen each other like iron, and Makkos 10a praises learning in a group. In [Soaring to New Heights](/daf/makkos/10/soaring-to-new-heights), the Maharsha warns that a lone learner can build on one mistake, though Rav Yaakov Emden values solo study when no chavrusa is found.
talmud-torah/learning-with-a-chavrusa.description: Why does the Gemara stress learning Torah with a chavrusa or a group, not alone? The Maharsha's warning and Rav Yaakov Emden on Taanis 7a and Makkos 10a.

talmud-torah/living-in-a-makom-torah.intro: Rebbi Yose ben Kisma refused a fortune to move to a town without Torah, insisting on living only in a makom Torah. Why not use the money to build a yeshiva there? The Chofetz Chaim says the man only wanted the honor, the Maharal says not every place is fit for a yeshiva, and Rav Henoch Leibowitz adds that every place is fit for a Torah day school, in a discussion tied to Yoma 18a.
talmud-torah/living-in-a-makom-torah.description: Should one live only in a makom Torah? Rebbi Yose ben Kisma's refusal, the Chofetz Chaim, the Maharal and Rav Henoch Leibowitz, tied to Yoma 18a.

talmud-torah/making-a-siyum-on-a-masecht.intro: Finishing a masechta is a time to celebrate with a festive meal. The Rashbam on Bava Basra 121a says the people rejoiced on Tu B'Av because they had completed a mitzvah, and the Nemukei Yosef calls this the source for a siyum seudah. The Rema codifies it, and the Maharshal tells how he tried, then dropped, a special addition to bentching at a siyum.
talmud-torah/making-a-siyum-on-a-masecht.description: Where does the seudah for finishing a masechta come from? The Rashbam, Nemukei Yosef and Rema on the joy of a siyum, traced to Bava Basra 121a.

talmud-torah/meaning-of-the-word-kivyach.intro: Many assume kivyachol simply marks a statement about Hashem as allegory. On Yoma 3b, Rashi offers two precise meanings: if it were possible, or a signal that we may say this only because the Torah says it. Tosfos Rabbeinu Peretz reads it as kv, 22, for the Torah's 22 letters, plus yachol, and the Tosfos Shantz sees it as an abbreviation.
talmud-torah/meaning-of-the-word-kivyach.description: What does kivyachol really mean? Rashi's two explanations on Yoma 3b, plus Tosfos Rabbeinu Peretz on the Torah's 22 letters and the Tosfos Shantz.

talmud-torah/order-of-masechtos-in-daf-y.intro: In a standard Vilna Shas, Rosh Hashanah comes right after Shekalim, yet Daf Yomi goes from Shekalim to Yoma. Rav Sherira Gaon explains the Mishna's order, and Rav Reuvain Margoliyos notes that longer masechtos come first. In [Out of Order](/daf/beitzah/37/out-of-order), filed on Beitzah 37, Rebbe Meir Shapiro built the calendar on the Slavuta Shas, which follows the Mishna.
talmud-torah/order-of-masechtos-in-daf-y.description: Why does Daf Yomi study Yoma after Shekalim when the Vilna Shas prints Rosh Hashanah next? The Slavuta Shas explains it, in an article on Beitzah 37.

talmud-torah/order-of-the-masechtos-in-d.intro: In the Vilna Shas, Rosh Hashanah comes before Yoma, so why does Daf Yomi go straight from Shekalim to Yoma? [K’vyachol](/daf/yoma/3/kvyachol), written on Yoma 3b, brings Rabbi David Feder's answer: in the Slavuta Shas, Yoma follows Shekalim, and Rav Meir Shapiro, founder of Daf Yomi, was a cousin of its printers. The order also matches the Mishnayos, the Rambam and Rav Sherira Gaon.
talmud-torah/order-of-the-masechtos-in-d.description: Why does Daf Yomi learn Yoma right after Shekalim? The Slavuta Shas, Rav Meir Shapiro's family tie to its printers, and the Rambam, from Yoma 3b.

talmud-torah/reviewing-learning-101-time.intro: Chagigah 9b says that one who reviews his learning 100 times is called someone who does not serve Hashem, while one who reviews it 101 times does. Rav Itzele Peterburger explains the harsh title: true learning would have brought such joy that he could not skip the last review. The Chofetz Chaim says the last step completes the mitzvah, and Rav Avrohom Kalmanowitz faults treating any part as small.
talmud-torah/reviewing-learning-101-time.description: Why is reviewing learning 100 times not enough? Rav Itzele Peterburger, the Chofetz Chaim and Rav Kalmanowitz on review 101, from Chagigah 9b.

talmud-torah/risking-your-life-for-torah.intro: Three warriors crossed enemy lines to bring Dovid HaMelech's halachic questions to the Sanhedrin, but Dovid would not let their answers be said in their names. Bava Kamma 61b shows that one should not risk his life just to find answers to Torah questions. Rebbe Akiva is praised for risking his life, because he was teaching Torah to the public.
talmud-torah/risking-your-life-for-torah.description: When is risking your life for Torah praised? Rebbe Akiva taught the public, but Dovid's warriors only sought answers to questions. From Bava Kamma 61b.

talmud-torah/seudas-siyum.intro: Why was Tu B'Av such a joyous day? Rabba and Rav Yosef on Taanis 31a say it was when wood-cutting for the mizbeach ended, and the Rashbam explains that finishing a mitzvah is cause for celebration. The Nimukei Yosef calls this the source for a seudah on completing a masechta, and Rav Moshe Feinstein once told a student to make a siyum on a single daf.
talmud-torah/seudas-siyum.description: Where does the seudas siyum come from? Tu B'Av, the Rashbam, the Nimukei Yosef, and Rav Moshe Feinstein's siyum on one daf, from Taanis 26b and 31a.

talmud-torah/signatures-of-the-amoraim.intro: Some Amoraim signed documents with a picture instead of their name. Bava Basra 161b says Rav drew a fish, Rabbi Chanina a palm branch, and Rava bar Rav Huna a ship's mast. [Sign Up](/daf/bava-basra/161/sign-up) shares the meanings found in them, from the Rashbam's simple reason to the Maharshal's idea that each sign recalled a food bought for Shabbos.
talmud-torah/signatures-of-the-amoraim.description: Why did Rav sign with a fish and Rabbi Chanina with a palm branch? The signatures of the Amoraim in Bava Basra 161b and the meanings found in them.

talmud-torah/simchas-torah-honors-bought.intro: In some yeshivos, Simchas Torah honors are sold for pledges of learning, and one bachur won by promising 1,000 blatt Gemara. Must they all be new pages, or may he review 200 pages five times? In [Another Repeat](/daf/megillah/23/another-repeat), Rav Yitzchok Zilberstein looks for an answer in the haftarah rule on Megillah 23, and advises the gabbai to spell it out at the auction.
talmud-torah/simchas-torah-honors-bought.description: If a bachur pledges 1,000 blatt for a Simchas Torah honor, does review count? Rav Zilberstein looks to the haftarah rule in Megillah 23 for an answer.

talmud-torah/siyum-daily-app.intro: A young man on the train glances at a businessman's phone and finds him using Siyum Daily. The free app, created by Rabbi Mordechai Groner, gives each user one Mishnah a day, so that thousands of users finish all of Shas every day. In [App-ortioned Learning](/daf/makkos/5/app-ortioned-learning), Rebbe Akiva's teaching in Makkos 5b about joining others in a mitzvah explains the reward.
talmud-torah/siyum-daily-app.description: A free app gives each user one Mishnah a day so thousands finish all of Shas daily. Rebbe Akiva's lesson in Makkos 5b explains each learner's reward.

talmud-torah/sons-of-rav-papa-at-a-siyum.intro: Why are Rav Papa's sons named at every siyum? Rav Shimshon Aharon Polinsky notes that in about ten places Rav Papa says to recite both or all opinions, so as not to dismiss any Torah scholar. In that merit he had ten sons who were scholars, an idea the article reaches from Rav Nachum Bar Papa in Yoma 67a.
talmud-torah/sons-of-rav-papa-at-a-siyum.description: Why are Rav Papa's ten sons named at every siyum? His habit of honoring every scholar's opinion, as Rav Polinsky explains, starting from Yoma 67a.

talmud-torah/source-hunting-versus-deep-.intro: Rav Yitzchak Hutner lamented that his generation had swapped yegiyas haTorah for mere source-hunting, finding where the Chasam Sofer speaks without truly understanding him. But Menachos 7a, where Avimi walks to Rav Chisda, shows that even preparation counts as toil. [Torah Toil](/daf/menachos/7/torah-toil) suggests source-hunting counts only when it ends in real study.
talmud-torah/source-hunting-versus-deep-.description: Does looking up sources count as toiling in Torah? Rav Hutner's warning about source-hunting meets Avimi's walk to Rav Chisda in Menachos 7a.

talmud-torah/supporting-a-kollel-son-in-.intro: Kiddushin 70a warns about marrying a woman for her money, but does that include a young man who needs his in-laws' help to learn in kollel? The Aruch HaShulchan writes that for a Torah scholar it is fitting. Good families have long taken a scholar as a son-in-law and supported him for some years so he can learn, and he writes that there is no greater mitzvah than this.
talmud-torah/supporting-a-kollel-son-in-.description: Is it wrong for a Torah scholar to marry with parental support so he can learn? The Aruch HaShulchan praises supporting a kollel son-in-law, Kiddushin 70a.

talmud-torah/swords-in-the-beis-midrash.intro: Pinchas left his sword outside the Beis Medrash, and the Gemara on Sanhedrin 82 says a sword may not be brought in, yet Amasa ben Yeter, Chizkiya and Beis Shammai all placed swords in or by the study hall. [To Live By the Sword?](/daf/sanhedrin/82/to-live-by-the-sword) brings Rav Yitzchok Zilberstein's answer: a sword may come in when it serves Torah study.
talmud-torah/swords-in-the-beis-midrash.description: Pinchas left his sword outside, yet others planted swords in the Beis Medrash. Rav Zilberstein on when a weapon may serve Torah study, from Sanhedrin 82.

talmud-torah/teaching-torah-makes-you-gr.intro: Rebbe Yossi was once Rebbe Yehudah haNasi's rebbe, yet the Gemara suggests he would later have accepted his student's rulings. Tosfos on Niddah 14b explains that Rebbe Yehudah haNasi grew greater by teaching the many students of his yeshiva. [When The Student Becomes The Rebbe](/daf/niddah/14/when-the-student-becomes-the-rebbe) adds the Chasam Sofer's teaching that one learns most of all from his students.
talmud-torah/teaching-torah-makes-you-gr.description: Does teaching Torah take away from your own learning? Tosfos on Niddah 14b shows how Rebbe Yehudah haNasi surpassed his rebbe by teaching students.

talmud-torah/teaching-torah-out-of-town.intro: Reish Lakish could not find Rebbe Chiya's grave, and a Heavenly voice told him he had learned like Rebbe Chiya but had not spread Torah like him. Bava Metzia 85b says Rebbe Chiya has a special chariot in Shamayim. In [Rebbe Chiya: The Ultimate Teacher](/daf/bava-metzia/85/rebbe-chiya-the-ultimate-teacher), Rav Gifter says his three years as a rav in Waterbury brought more kavod Shamayim than decades in Telshe.
talmud-torah/teaching-torah-out-of-town.description: Is spreading Torah in a small town greater than leading a big yeshiva? Rebbe Chiya's reward and Rav Gifter's view, in an article on Bava Metzia 85b.

talmud-torah/toiling-in-torah.intro: When Avimi forgot Maseches Menachos, he traveled to his own student, Rav Chisda, to relearn it, and Rashi explains that he wanted to fulfill I toiled and found. Building on Menachos 7, [Toil For Torah](/daf/menachos/7/toil-for-torah) brings the Vilna Gaon's point that success in Torah is a gift, not a direct result, so even effort spent getting to the learning brings success.
talmud-torah/toiling-in-torah.description: Does effort in Torah guarantee success, even effort spent traveling to learn? Avimi goes to his student, with Rashi and the Vilna Gaon, in Menachos 7.

talmud-torah/torah-belongs-to-every-jew.intro: Rav applies the verse our water we drank for money to scholars who had to pay 400 zuz to ask Rebbe Akiva a question in prison. Why call Rebbe Akiva's Torah our water, when he earned it through his own toil? [Still Waters Run Deep](/daf/yevamos/78/still-waters-run-deep), filed on Yevamos 78b, brings Rav Henoch Leibowitz's answer: even the loftiest Torah is every Jew's birthright.
talmud-torah/torah-belongs-to-every-jew.description: Is the deepest Torah the inheritance of every Jew? Rav's reading of our water in Eichah and Rav Henoch Leibowitz's lesson, from Yevamos 78b.

talmud-torah/torah-lishmah.intro: During the dispute on Bava Metzia 59b, the walls of the beis midrash leaned but did not fall. The Maharsha says Rebbe Eliezer was charging that the Sages learned only to argue, and the slanted walls show that every generation has those who learn lishmah and those who do not. Tosfos elsewhere says learning for reward or honor is acceptable, but learning just to argue is wrong.
talmud-torah/torah-lishmah.description: Is learning Torah for honor or argument acceptable? The Maharsha reads the slanted walls of Bava Metzia 59b as a lesson about Torah lishmah.

talmud-torah/torah-study-protecting-from.intro: The Malach HaMaves could not take Rav Chisda because he never stopped learning, until a pillar snapped and startled him. The Ben Ish Chai asks why the Gemara uses this story and not a similar one about Dovid HaMelech. In [Lifelong Goal](/daf/makkos/10/lifelong-goal), filed on Makkos 10, he answers that Rav Chisda was no king or prophet and died in Bavel on a weekday, so Torah alone protected him.
talmud-torah/torah-study-protecting-from.description: Why couldn't the Malach HaMaves take Rav Chisda while he learned? The Ben Ish Chai on the protective power of Torah, in an article on Makkos 10.

talmud-torah/torah-study-versus-acts-of-.intro: Torah learning takes precedence over chesed that others can do, but chesed that no one else will do comes first. So why did Abaye leave his learning to do kindness, while Rabbah did not? [Keep Calm And Chesed On](/daf/yevamos/105/keep-calm-and-chesed-on) brings the Chofetz Chaim's view on Yevamos 105a that a gadol leading a chesed effort inspires others, and Rav Henoch Leibowitz's warning not to use the rule as an excuse.
talmud-torah/torah-study-versus-acts-of-.description: When should one stop learning Torah to do chesed? Abaye and Rabbah, the Chofetz Chaim, and Rav Henoch Leibowitz's caveat, from Yevamos 105a.

talmud-torah/understanding-fantastical-a.intro: A poetic recap of a Ravens-Falcons football game sounds like fantasy unless you know the code. The same is true of Rabba bar bar Channa's tale of a one-day-old Re'em as big as Mount Tabor, whose waste dammed the Jordan. The Ben Ish Chai says it appears in Zevachim 113b to sharpen students' minds, and the Vilna Gaon reads it as a carefully built metaphor.
talmud-torah/understanding-fantastical-a.description: How should we read the Gemara's fantastical tales? Rabba bar bar Channa's giant Re'em in Zevachim 113b, decoded by the Vilna Gaon and the Ben Ish Chai.

talmud-torah/understanding-the-words-whe.intro: Does reading Torah text without understanding it count as learning? The Mishnah Berurah says Mishnah and Gemara must be understood, unlike tefillah, which can work without it. The Shulchan Aruch HaRav says reading pesukim counts even without knowing their meaning, and the Shelah adds that one must at least be aware, in a discussion of Zevachim 47a.
talmud-torah/understanding-the-words-whe.description: Does reading Torah without understanding count as learning? The Mishnah Berurah, Shulchan Aruch HaRav and Shelah on pesukim and Mishnah, from Zevachim 47a.

talmud-torah/using-free-time-for-torah.intro: During the conquest of Eretz Yisrael, an angel rebuked Yehoshua for not learning at night, even though the soldiers were exhausted from battle. The Minchas Elazar adds the exiles who debated Torah while in chains. [A Time for Torah](/daf/bava-kamma/77/a-time-for-torah) asks, from Bava Kamma 77a, what excuse remains for wasting free time.
talmud-torah/using-free-time-for-torah.description: Weary soldiers and chained exiles still learned deep Torah. The Minchas Elazar asks what excuse we have for idle hours, in an article on Bava Kamma 77a.

talmud-torah/vowing-to-learn-torah.intro: Rav Gidal quoted Rav that one who says he will rise early and learn a chapter has made a great neder to Hashem. The Ran and Tosfos on Nedarim 8 explain that the person must have used the language of a shevuah, but the Shulchan Aruch rules that simply saying one will learn a perek obligates him like a vow for tzedakah. The Rema extends this to every mitzvah, which is why people say b'li neder.
talmud-torah/vowing-to-learn-torah.description: Is a promise to learn a chapter or tractate a binding vow? Rav Gidal, the Ran and the Shulchan Aruch on Nedarim 8, and why we say b'li neder.

talmud-torah/why-yevamos-is-so-difficult.intro: The Zohar reads ani, a pauper, as an acronym for Eiruvin, Niddah and Yevamos, among the hardest masechtos in Shas. Rav Yaakov Emden says the challenge of Yevamos is not its complicated cases but the fine reasoning behind them. [Yibum and Tzitzis](/daf/yevamos/4/yibum-and-tzitzis), written as Daf Yomi reached Yevamos 4a, notes that the Mesivta Gemara needs 168 pages of diagrams for the first 19 blatt.
talmud-torah/why-yevamos-is-so-difficult.description: Why is Masechta Yevamos so hard to learn? The Zohar's acronym, Rav Yaakov Emden on its fine reasoning, and pages of diagrams, from Yevamos 4a.

talmud-torah/yissachar-zevulun-partnersh.intro: In a Yissachar-Zevulun partnership, the working Zevulun supports the full-time learner Yissachar, and both share the reward. But if reward for a mitzvah cannot be sold, as the Netziv rules, how can Zevulun get a share? [Is Olam Habah for Sale?](/daf/shekalim/14/is-olam-habah-for-sale), filed on Shekalim 14a, answers that it is about timing: Zevulun makes the learning happen, but he cannot pay for it afterward.
talmud-torah/yissachar-zevulun-partnersh.description: How can a supporter share the reward of Torah he funds if mitzvos can't be sold? The Yissachar-Zevulun partnership and why timing matters, Shekalim 14a.

talmud-torah/zoom-shiur-versus-attending.intro: Should a person join a shiur on Zoom or travel to hear it in person? Menachos 7a and Rashi show that even walking to learn counts as yegiyas haTorah, which brings success. Pirkei Avos and the Chofetz Chaim add that learning in a group brings the Shechinah and greater honor to Heaven, so the article favors making the trip.
talmud-torah/zoom-shiur-versus-attending.description: Is it better to travel to a shiur than join on Zoom? Avimi's walk in Menachos 7a and the Chofetz Chaim on learning in a group point to the trip.

eretz-yisrael-mitzvos/bikkurim-declarati.intro: A farmer bringing bikkurim recites a pasuk thanking Hashem for the soil He has given him. But what if he bought trees from a neighbor and is unsure whether he owns the land under them? Bava Basra 82a says he brings the fruit without the declaration, since saying it might be a falsehood, and the Rashbam cites a verse in Tehillim against speaking lies.
eretz-yisrael-mitzvos/bikkurim-declarati.description: Why does someone unsure he owns the land bring bikkurim without the declaration? Bava Basra 82a and the Rashbam on avoiding even a doubtful falsehood.

eretz-yisrael-mitzvos/feeding-untithed-p.intro: R' Pinchas ben Yair's donkey would not eat barley at an inn until the maaser was taken. In Chullin 7a, the Gemara asks why, since demai may be fed to animals. The Maharsha says it was an ordinary donkey that Hashem protected for its owner's sake, while the Yerushalmi says the donkey took on a stringency of its own.
eretz-yisrael-mitzvos/feeding-untithed-p.description: May demai be fed to animals? The donkey of R' Pinchas ben Yair refused untithed barley, and the Maharsha and the Yerushalmi explain why. From Chullin 7a.

eretz-yisrael-mitzvos/orlah-on-blueberry.intro: Kiddushin 39 teaches that orlah, the ban on fruit from a tree's first three years, applies outside Eretz Yisrael as well. Most fruit trees take longer than that to bear fruit, but a blueberry bush from a garden center is often sold as a one-year plant and may fruit in its second year. In [Barking Up the Wrong Tree](/daf/kiddushin/39/barking-up-the-wrong-tree), pomegranate shrubs face the same issue.
eretz-yisrael-mitzvos/orlah-on-blueberry.description: Can a young blueberry or pomegranate bush from a garden center produce orlah fruit? The ban on fruit from the first three years, from Kiddushin 39.

eretz-yisrael-mitzvos/paying-workers-wit.intro: A landowner told Rebbe Elazar bar Tzadok that during Shemittah, villagers worked his vineyards and took olives as payment. Since the fruits of Shvi'is are meant to be ownerless and free for anyone, Rebbe Elazar ruled the practice improper, as Sukkah 44a records. The man's swift response earned rare praise: in 40 years, Rebbe Elazar said, he had never seen someone follow the proper path like this.
eretz-yisrael-mitzvos/paying-workers-wit.description: May workers be paid with Shemittah olives? Rebbe Elazar bar Tzadok rules it improper, since Shvi'is fruit is ownerless, in a story on Sukkah 44a.

eretz-yisrael-mitzvos/separating-maaser-.intro: Terumah and maaser are meant to be designated only for produce that is nearby. Rebbe Yannai did it for a gift of fruit whose whereabouts he did not know, then dreamed of a splintered reed and feared he had erred. On Yevamos 93a, Rebbe Chiya reads the dream as a sign that he ruled truly, since for oneg Shabbos this leniency is allowed.
eretz-yisrael-mitzvos/separating-maaser-.description: May terumah and maaser be designated for fruit not nearby? Rebbe Yannai's Shabbos fruit, his dream, and Rebbe Chiya's answer, from Yevamos 93a.

eretz-yisrael-mitzvos/who-receives-maase.intro: After terumah, a farmer gave a tenth of his produce, Maaser Rishon, to a Levi. Yevamos 86b records that Rebbe Elazar ben Azariah, a kohen, held it could go to any member of Shevet Levi and took it from a certain garden. Rebbe Akiva disagreed, noting that since Ezra's time Maaser Rishon was given to the poor, and he arranged for the garden's new entrance to lead through a cemetery.
eretz-yisrael-mitzvos/who-receives-maase.description: Who receives Maaser Rishon, only Levi'im or kohanim too? Rebbe Akiva and Rebbe Elazar ben Azariah's dispute over a garden's tithe, Yevamos 86b.

shatnez/shatnez-in-suits.intro: Many men's suits hide linen in the collar stiffeners and shoulder pads, even when the main fabric is fine. A sha'atnez lab found it in famous brands, and a lawyer's ten custom-made Hong Kong suits all turned out to be shatnez, as did two replacements promised to be linen-free. [Match But Don’t Mix](/daf/yevamos/4/match-but-dont-mix), on Yevamos 4a, concludes that every suit must be checked.
shatnez/shatnez-in-suits.description: Why must every suit be checked for shatnez? Linen collar stiffeners, shoulder pads from scraps, and a lawyer's ten suits, tied to Yevamos 4a.

shatnez/shatnez-in-ties-and-costumes.intro: Shatnez can hide in places people rarely suspect. Rabbi Yosef Sayagh warns that the stiffener inside a wool or linen tie is often wool or linen, and appliqué on children's clothing can cause problems too. Purim costumes, Russian hats, uniforms and tuxedos may also contain shatnez, a practical point raised alongside the Gemara on Yevamos 4a.
shatnez/shatnez-in-ties-and-costumes.description: Can a tie, a child's outfit or a Purim costume contain shatnez? Rabbi Yosef Sayagh's warnings about hidden linen and wool, tied to Yevamos 4a.

shatnez/wearing-shatnez-in-mortal-danger.intro: May a Jew wear a non-Jew's garment with shatnez to hide his identity and save his life? The Rema permits it, reasoning that if creating a non-Jewish impression is allowed, an ordinary lav like shatnez surely gives way to saving life. The Bach forbids setting out on a dangerous route planning to need it, and [Keeping the Faith](/daf/avodah-zarah/26/keeping-the-faith) weighs these views alongside Rebbe Meir's escape on Avodah Zarah 18b.
shatnez/wearing-shatnez-in-mortal-danger.description: May a Jew wear shatnez as a disguise to escape danger, or set out on a route where he will need it? The Rema, Bach and Shach, from Avodah Zarah 18b.

shatnez/which-fibers-are-shatnez.intro: Not every wool or linen look-alike is shatnez. Rabbi Avrom Pollack of the Star-K explains that wool means only sheep or lamb wool, so camel's wool, mohair, cashmere and angora are fine, and linen means only flax. Ramie, though, is hard to tell from linen even under a microscope, so clothing of wool and ramie needs an expert's check, a caution noted with Yevamos 4a.
shatnez/which-fibers-are-shatnez.description: Which fibers count as wool or linen for shatnez? Cashmere, mohair, hemp, and why ramie needs an expert's check, per the Star-K, with Yevamos 4a.

shiluach-haken/birds-eligible-for-shilua.intro: Shiluach haken applies only to kosher birds, and only the mother must be sent away. A mourning dove nesting outside a window raised both questions in [The Test Of A Nest](/daf/chullin/138/the-test-of-a-nest). The father sits on the eggs by day, so the evening bird is likely the mother, and a bird not known to be non-kosher may be sent, without a berachah, building on Chullin 138.
shiluach-haken/birds-eligible-for-shilua.description: Which birds qualify for shiluach haken, and how do you tell the mother from the father? A mourning dove and birds without a tradition. From Chullin 138.

shiluach-haken/bracha-on-shiluach-haken.intro: Shimon proudly recited the rare bracha before sending away a mother bird, but Boruch has bad news. Some Rishonim hold that the mitzvah only fixes the sin of taking the eggs, so like returning stolen property, it has no bracha. In [Talking Turkey About Shiluach Hakein](/daf/chullin/140/talking-turkey-about-shiluach-hakein), Rav Elyashiv, Rav Scheinberg and Rav Chaim Kanievsky rule against the bracha, building on Chullin 140.
shiluach-haken/bracha-on-shiluach-haken.description: Is a bracha said on shiluach haken? Some Rishonim say it only fixes a sin, and Rav Elyashiv and Rav Chaim Kanievsky say no bracha. Building on Chullin 140.

shiluach-haken/how-to-send-away-the-moth.intro: If the mother bird flies off before you reach her, has the mitzvah been done? Rav Chaim Kanievsky says to intend that any act that scares her fulfills it, while Rashi and the Rambam seem to require actively shooing her. Yet the Aruch L'ner warns that grabbing her may be forbidden, and the Chasam Sofer says both views cannot be met, building on Chullin 140.
shiluach-haken/how-to-send-away-the-moth.description: How must the mother bird be sent away? Rav Chaim Kanievsky, Rashi, the Rambam, the Aruch L'ner and Rav Moshe Shternbach disagree. Building on Chullin 140.

shiluach-haken/shiluach-haken-and-tzaar-.intro: Shiluach haken is only required when a person actually wants the eggs. The Chasam Sofer warns that chasing a mother bird without a clear mitzvah may cause tzaar baalei chaim. Rav Chaim Kanievsky encourages the mitzvah when possible, but not when no eggs are taken, and Rav Dovid Feinstein reportedly said to leave a park goose alone, building on Chullin 140.
shiluach-haken/shiluach-haken-and-tzaar-.description: Can chasing a mother bird without a clear mitzvah be tzaar baalei chaim? The Chasam Sofer, Rav Chaim Kanievsky and Rav Dovid Feinstein. From Chullin 140.

shiluach-haken/shiluach-haken-on-your-ow.intro: The Mishnah says the mitzvah cannot be done with your own birds, and a person's property can acquire eggs for him without his knowledge. Building on Chullin 138, Rav Chaim Kanievsky says nobody really wants eggs laid in his tree, and Rav Moshe Feinstein says a later statement works retroactively. The best advice is a one-time declaration that you never want such eggs.
shiluach-haken/shiluach-haken-on-your-ow.description: Is a nest in your own tree or air conditioner yours? Rav Chaim Kanievsky and Rav Moshe Feinstein on making the eggs ownerless. Building on Chullin 138.

kilayim/grafted-fruit-trees.intro: Nearly every fruit tree sold today is grafted, since that is the only way to be sure of the exact fruit it will produce. Kiddushin 39 teaches that kilayim of trees applies outside Eretz Yisrael. According to some Rishonim, one may not water or fertilize a fruit cocktail tree or an almond on peach roots even if it was bought already grafted, though its fruit may be eaten.
kilayim/grafted-fruit-trees.description: Can one grow a fruit cocktail tree or an almond grafted onto peach roots? Kilayim of trees outside Eretz Yisrael, and eating the fruit, from Kiddushin 39.

kilayim/horse-and-mule-pulling-a-wagon.intro: A wagon pulled by a horse and a mule together raises a kilayim problem, since different species may not be worked as one team. The Mordechai tells how the Rashbam nearly boarded such a wagon until Rabbeinu Tam stopped him, and he asks whether the issur is from the Torah or only Rabbinic. Rav Nosson Gestetner ties the story to the Rashbam's words on Bava Basra 133b.
kilayim/horse-and-mule-pulling-a-wagon.description: Is riding a wagon pulled by a horse and a mule kilayim? The Mordechai asks if it is Torah law, in a story of the Rashbam tied to Bava Basra 133b.

kilayim/pluots-and-hybrid-fruits.intro: Pluots, apriums and plumcots are crosses of plums and apricots, and many assume they come from forbidden methods. Tied to Kiddushin 39, [Barking Up the Wrong Tree](/daf/kiddushin/39/barking-up-the-wrong-tree) explains that the first stage, cross-pollinating a bloom and planting the seed, is permitted. The Torah prohibition comes later, when branches or buds are grafted onto other trees to grow the fruit commercially.
kilayim/pluots-and-hybrid-fruits.description: Do pluots, apriums and plumcots involve forbidden mixing of species? Which step of making these hybrid fruits raises a kilayim issue, from Kiddushin 39.

bal-tashchis/cutting-branches-from-a-fru.intro: The Korban Pesach was roasted on a spit of pomegranate wood, which raises the ban on destroying fruit trees. As the article on Pesachim 82 presents it, some say pruning a fruit tree is never a problem, even when it does not benefit the tree. Others say branches may be cut from a fruit tree for the sake of a great mitzvah such as roasting the Korban Pesach.
bal-tashchis/cutting-branches-from-a-fru.description: May you cut branches from a fruit tree for a mitzvah or other need? Two views on pruning and the pomegranate spit of the Korban Pesach. Pesachim 82.

bal-tashchis/cutting-down-a-fruit-tree.intro: The Torah forbids cutting down fruit trees, yet Bava Kamma 91b allows it when the wood is worth more than the fruit. Shmuel and Rav Chisda had date palms cut down to protect their vines. In [A Fruity Matter](/daf/bava-kamma/91/a-fruity-matter), the Be'er Sheva allows it for a mitzvah, but Rabbi Chanina's son died for cutting a fig tree too early, so people still hold back.
bal-tashchis/cutting-down-a-fruit-tree.description: When may a fruit tree be cut down? Ravina allows it if the wood is worth more, but Rabbi Chanina's story keeps people cautious, in Bava Kamma 91b.

bal-tashchis/throwing-away-food-and-bal-.intro: If you keep pas Yisrael only during the Ten Days, may you throw away a cake that will go stale? Dayan Weiss, the Minchas Yitzchak, said discarding pas palter is not bal tashchis, since it is done for a mitzvah, not for no reason. [The Noble Pas Price](/daf/bava-kamma/91/the-noble-pas-price) links this to the fruit-tree rule of Bava Kamma 91b.
bal-tashchis/throwing-away-food-and-bal-.description: Is it bal tashchis to throw out food you won't eat for a mitzvah? The Minchas Yitzchak says no when there is a purpose, building on Bava Kamma 91b.

haircuts-and-peyos/haircuts-and-shaving-.intro: The Sages forbade haircuts on chol ha'moed, though a mustache may be trimmed, and Rav Moshe Feinstein allows a daily shaver to shave in great need. The Shulchan Aruch lists exceptions such as a freed prisoner, and the Gemara adds a nazir who finished his nezirus. The article on Nazir 38 shows how the poskim allow a haircut for a mitzvah need, like hair blocking tefillin.
haircuts-and-peyos/haircuts-and-shaving-.description: Why are haircuts restricted on Chol HaMoed, and who may cut hair then? A freed prisoner, a nazir and haircuts for a mitzvah, from an article on Nazir 38.

haircuts-and-peyos/peyos-of-the-head-and.intro: The Rambam holds that the peyos of the head follow the same rules as the corners of the beard, so whatever cut is banned for one is banned for the other. The Rosh is stricter: the head peyos may not be cut close at all, even without a razor. Tied to Makkos 20, the Shulchan Aruch seems to rule like the Rambam but urges everyone to follow the Rosh, and that is the custom.
haircuts-and-peyos/peyos-of-the-head-and.description: Do the peyos of the head follow the same rules as the corners of the beard? The Rambam and the Rosh differ, and the custom follows, tied to Makkos 20.

haircuts-and-peyos/trimming-peyos-near-t.intro: Many people do not realize that the peyos of the head cover the whole area above the ear and somewhat around it. Barbers often like to shave a clean circle around the ear, but that would not comply with the Rosh. In [Peyos Prohibitions](/daf/makkos/20/peyos-prohibitions), tied to Makkos 20, the advice is to insist on a number 2 guard or scissors near the ear.
haircuts-and-peyos/trimming-peyos-near-t.description: How close may a barber cut the hair around the ears? Why a clean shaved circle around the ear is a problem for peyos, in an article tied to Makkos 20.

haircuts-and-peyos/using-a-non-jewish-ba.intro: The Mishnah forbids using a non-Jewish barber, and Tosfos on Avodah Zarah 29a explains that a barber holding a razor could easily kill his patron. The Gemara advises a Jew who does use one to watch in a mirror. That would not give him time to react, but the barber would assume so careful a patron must have government ties, and [Mirror Image](/daf/avodah-zarah/29/mirror-image) shows why this is a requirement, not a permit.
haircuts-and-peyos/using-a-non-jewish-ba.description: Why did the Gemara caution against a non-Jewish barber, and how did watching in a mirror protect the patron? Tosfos explains it all on Avodah Zarah 29a.

tattoos/temporary-tattoos.intro: A permanent tattoo is forbidden by the Torah, but what about a temporary one? Just as temporary writing is forbidden rabbinically on Shabbos, the Minchas Chinuch reads Tosfos in Gittin 20b as extending a rabbinic ban to skin writing. Rav Vozner and Rav Chaim Kanievsky disagree, and the article concludes that the modern poskim seem to permit temporary tattoos.
tattoos/temporary-tattoos.description: Are temporary tattoos permitted when a permanent tattoo is forbidden? The Minchas Chinuch, Tosfos in Gittin 20b, Rav Vozner and Rav Chaim Kanievsky.

tattoos/writing-on-your-hand.intro: Sarah Palin famously wrote speech notes on her hand, but is this allowed in halacha? In [The Rights and Wrongs of Writing](/daf/gittin/20/the-rights-and-wrongs-of-writing), on Gittin 20b, the Mishnas Chachamim notes that Jews commonly wrote reminders on their skin. The Minchas Chinuch forbids only permanent writing on the skin, which may mean avoiding a Sharpie.
tattoos/writing-on-your-hand.description: Is it permitted to write notes on your hand in ink? The Minchas Chinuch and the Mishnas Chachamim weigh a rabbinic tattoo ban, discussed on Gittin 20b.

lo-yilbash/men-looking-in-a-mirror.intro: Tosfos on Avodah Zarah 29a infers that a man may look in a mirror only in special cases, since beautifying oneself in a mirror is a feminine act under lo yilbash. He permits it for shaving or an eye problem, and the Shulchan Aruch rules this way. The Ran and the Rema allow men to use mirrors where that is the local custom, and most American Jews follow the Rema.
lo-yilbash/men-looking-in-a-mirror.description: May a man look in a mirror? Tosfos on Avodah Zarah 29a links it to lo yilbash, allowing shaving and health needs, while the Rema follows local custom.

lo-yilbash/woman-wearing-a-mans-raincoat.intro: The Maharsham notes a dispute among poskim about whether a woman may wear a man's raincoat simply to stay dry. If it is allowed for a practical purpose, he asks, why couldn't Yael use a man's sword against Sisera? He answers that she had another option, the tent peg, so the sword was not needed, as the article on Nazir 59a explains.
lo-yilbash/woman-wearing-a-mans-raincoat.description: May a woman wear a man's raincoat just to keep dry? The Maharsham notes the dispute and compares it to Yael's choice of a tent peg, from Nazir 59a.

lo-yilbash/women-carrying-weapons.intro: The plain meaning of a man's utensils should not be on a woman is that a woman may not wear men's clothing. In Nazir 59a, Rebbe Eliezer ben Yaakov reads the verse as teaching that a woman should not go out to war with weapons, and [What’s at Stake?](/daf/nazir/59/whats-at-stake) follows how this reading shaped the story of Yael.
lo-yilbash/women-carrying-weapons.description: Does the ban on a woman wearing men's garments include weapons of war? Rebbe Eliezer ben Yaakov reads the verse that way in Nazir 59a, with Yael's story.

lo-yilbash/yael-and-the-tent-peg.intro: Why did Yael kill Sisera with a tent peg and not a sword? The Mefaresh on Nazir 59a says she would not wield a man's weapon, and the Tiferes Tzion says she took a real risk by doing so. The Avnei Tzedek argues that with lives at stake she would have used a sword, but as a man's tool she simply had none at hand.
lo-yilbash/yael-and-the-tent-peg.description: Why did Yael kill Sisera with a tent peg rather than a sword? The Mefaresh, the Tiferes Tzion and the Avnei Tzedek weigh in, from Nazir 59a.

hafrashas-challah/baking-challah-every-w.intro: Is it better to bake a large batch every few weeks to separate challah and freeze it, or bake fresh challah weekly without the mitzvah of hafrashas challah? [Fresh, Hot Challah](/daf/menachos/96/fresh-hot-challah) weighs the Rema's custom against oneg Shabbos. Based on Rav Elyashiv, the article concludes that fresh challah wins if it adds to oneg Shabbos, with the Lechem Hapanim of Menachos 96b in the background.
hafrashas-challah/baking-challah-every-w.description: Bake fresh challah weekly without separating challah, or a big frozen batch with the mitzvah? Rav Elyashiv on oneg Shabbos, from Menachos 96b.

hafrashas-challah/separating-challah-fro.intro: David Olivestone's grandfather always put half a matzah in his bedikas chametz bag, and no one knew why. The answer: a baker who had not yet taken challah from baked matzos said to burn half a matzah with the chametz. The article on Menachos 57a also explains why challah from water-free egg matzah dough cannot become tamei, and what the Mishnah Berurah says to do with it.
hafrashas-challah/separating-challah-fro.description: How is challah taken from baked matzos, and why burn half a matzah with the chametz? A family custom and egg matzah challah, from Menachos 57a.

pidyon-shevuyim/paying-a-ransom-and-an-o.intro: Reuven was kidnapped, and his friend Shimon handed over a precious signet ring to set him free. When Reuven later asked Shimon to repay an old loan, Shimon felt the ring had more than covered it. In [Paying It Forward (And Back)](/daf/kesubos/91/paying-it-forward-and-back), the Ben Ish Chai uses Kesubos 91b to rule that money spent on a mitzvah has no bearing on the loan.
pidyon-shevuyim/paying-a-ransom-and-an-o.description: Does ransom money paid to free a captive offset a loan the rescuer owes him? The Ben Ish Chai rules from the orphans and the creditor in Kesubos 91b.

pidyon-shevuyim/paying-a-ransom-for-a-fr.intro: Shimon gave up a ring worth 1,000 dinarim to free his kidnapped friend Reuvein. A week later, Reuvein came to collect a 100-dinar loan Shimon owed him. In [A Ring of Truth](/daf/kesubos/91/a-ring-of-truth), the Ben Ish Chai turns to Kesubos 91 and rules that since Shimon never said the ring was payment, it was a mitzvah of pidyon shevuyim, and he still owes the loan.
pidyon-shevuyim/paying-a-ransom-for-a-fr.description: Can someone who paid to free a captive friend count it against a debt he owes him? The Ben Ish Chai answers from the orphans' case in Kesubos 91.

kashrus/air-up-water-bottle-kashrus.intro: The Air Up bottle makes plain water taste flavored through scent pods, and some have asked whether it needs a hechsher. Since Rava on Avodah Zarah 66b holds that aroma has no halachic substance, and the Chofetz Chaim permits smelling non-kosher items, the bottle may be used without certification. An OU Rabbinic Coordinator and Machon Madaei Technology l'Halacha agree, and the same applies to the Cigtrus device.
kashrus/air-up-water-bottle-kashrus.description: Does the scent-flavored Air Up water bottle need a hechsher? Why aroma alone is not eating, from Abaye and Rava on Avodah Zarah 66b and later poskim.

kashrus/anisakis-worms-in-fish.intro: The Gemara gives a blanket heter for worms found in the flesh of fish, which would seem to settle the question of the Anisakis worm in wild salmon and flounder. Yet some rabbanim argue that today's situation is markedly different. In [Cast Your Bread Upon The Waters](/daf/chullin/70/cast-your-bread-upon-the-waters), filed on Chullin 70, Rav Dovid Feinstein requires checking the fish while Rav Yisroel Belsky rules leniently.
kashrus/anisakis-worms-in-fish.description: Are the Anisakis worms in wild fish permitted like the worms the Gemara allows? Rav Dovid Feinstein and Rav Yisroel Belsky disagree, as seen in Chullin 70.

kashrus/are-leghorn-chickens-kosher.intro: In 2004, students saw White Leghorn hens perched with two toes on each side, a sign of a non-kosher dores in Chullin 59a. If so, their eggs would be forbidden too. But the question had already been studied: a relaxed Leghorn perches three and one, splitting two and two only when nervous or on a slippery perch.
kashrus/are-leghorn-chickens-kosher.description: Are White Leghorn chickens and their eggs kosher? Students saw them perch like a non-kosher bird, but research settled it. See the details in Chullin 59a.

kashrus/are-marshmallows-kosher.intro: Hot cocoa bombs need mini marshmallows, and non-kosher marshmallows are made with gelatin from animal bones. The article on Pesachim 23a notes that while eating them is forbidden in practice, some opinions consider them technically kosher, depending on how the gelatin is made or whether the ingredients are nullified by Torah law. That doubt raises the question of whether they may be sold to gentiles.
kashrus/are-marshmallows-kosher.description: Are marshmallows made with animal gelatin truly non-kosher? Why some call them technically kosher, and what it means for selling them. Pesachim 23a.

kashrus/avian-reovirus-and-kosher-chicke.intro: Around 2011, kosher plants found hundreds of chickens with torn or dissolved leg tendons, each one a treifah. The cause was Avian Reovirus, which had turned resistant to vaccines. Israel cut such treifos by over 90 percent by exposing breeder hens to the live virus, a method banned in America, as the article on Chullin 57a explains.
kashrus/avian-reovirus-and-kosher-chicke.description: How did a virus make so many chickens treif? Avian Reovirus damages leg tendons, and Israel and America responded differently. Tied to Chullin 57a.

kashrus/bad-tasting-insects-and-bitul.intro: A flea jumped into the stew at a meal of the Chavvos Yair, who would not eat it. The Panim Meiros first permitted it, citing the Rema that a creature with a bad taste can be nullified, but retracted since the Rema's source in the Rashba speaks of a bug that fell apart. Rabbi Shlomo Eiger offers another reading, building on Chullin 100.
kashrus/bad-tasting-insects-and-bitul.description: Can a bad-tasting insect be nullified in food? The Panim Meiros, the Rema and Rabbi Shlomo Eiger on a flea that fell into a stew. Building on Chullin 100.

kashrus/black-ivory-elephant-coffee.intro: Black Ivory coffee beans pass through the digestive tracts of elephants in Thailand. Beyond the questions about civet coffee, the beans stay inside longer, which raises kavush k'mevushal: an item soaking 24 hours in a non-kosher liquid can become non-kosher. Some suggest this is not a concern, in an article on Bechoros 7a.
kashrus/black-ivory-elephant-coffee.description: Is coffee fermented inside an elephant kosher? Black Ivory beans raise the issue of soaking for 24 hours, in an article built on Bechoros 7a.

kashrus/buying-eggs-from-a-non-jewish-fa.intro: May you buy eggs at a gentile's roadside farm stand? Chullin 66b raises three concerns: a treifah hen, a dead bird, and a non-kosher species. Tosfos in Chullin 64a notes that people bought eggs from gentiles where most birds were kosher, but Rabbi Tzvi Rosen of the STAR-K points out that six of the top ten backyard breeds lack a mesorah.
kashrus/buying-eggs-from-a-non-jewish-fa.description: May you buy eggs from a non-Jewish farmer's stand? Treifah hens, dead birds and non-kosher breeds are the concerns, per Tosfos and Chullin 66b.

kashrus/chatzi-shiur.intro: Is eating less than the punishable amount of a forbidden food still a Torah violation? Rebbe Yochanan holds that chatzi shiur is forbidden by the Torah, while Reish Lakish disagrees. Rav Yisrael Salanter reads Yoma 82b this way: the mother of Rebbe Yochanan refused even a small bite on Yom Kippur, a sign of the strict ruling her son would one day give.
kashrus/chatzi-shiur.description: Is half the forbidden amount still a Torah ban? Rebbe Yochanan and Reish Lakish on chatzi shiur, and Rav Yisrael Salanter's reading of Yoma 82b.

kashrus/checking-eggs-for-blood-spots.intro: The daf teaches that a blood spot can make a whole egg forbidden, because it may show that an embryo began to form. Today's commercial eggs are unfertilized and candled, so blood spots are rare and do not make the egg treif. Building on Chullin 59a, checking at home remains a minhag, and unchecked eggs may be eaten after the fact.
kashrus/checking-eggs-for-blood-spots.description: Must eggs be checked for blood spots? Modern eggs are unfertilized and candled, so checking is a minhag and unchecked eggs may be eaten. From Chullin 59a.

kashrus/checking-lettuce-for-insects.intro: Pesachim 39a explains why lettuce is the preferred marror: its name chasa recalls Hashem's compassion, and it turns from soft to hard like the Egyptians. Yet the Chofetz Chaim warns that one should use lettuce only if he can be sure it is insect-free. Heaven forbid, he writes, that someone transgress the Torah prohibition of eating insects for the rabbinic mitzvah of marror, when horseradish can be used instead.
kashrus/checking-lettuce-for-insects.description: Why does the Chofetz Chaim say to skip lettuce for marror unless it is free of insects? The Torah ban on bugs outweighs the hiddur. Pesachim 39a.

kashrus/choosing-a-butcher-by-appearance.intro: Two butchers served one neighborhood, and the one with the beard and long peyos turned out to be selling treif. Rav Moshe Feinstein ruled that people who used both shops were blameless, since they relied on the halacha that one Jew is believed on kashrus. In [The Accidental Aveirah](/daf/kesubos/85/the-accidental-aveirah), tied to Kesubos 85a, those who chose him for looking frummer were relying on their own faulty logic.
kashrus/choosing-a-butcher-by-appearance.description: Is buying from the butcher who looks frummer a valid basis for kashrus? Rav Moshe Feinstein on chezkas kashrus and a treif butcher, tied to Kesubos 85a.

kashrus/copepods-in-new-york-city-water.intro: Unfiltered New York City water holds tiny crustaceans called copepods, which on their own are certainly not kosher. One argument to permit them compares the reservoirs to the water pits in the Gemara, where creatures born in the water may be allowed. But those pits do not flow, while this water travels from the Catskills, and the article on Chullin 70 notes that Rav Dovid Feinstein requires filtering.
kashrus/copepods-in-new-york-city-water.description: Are the copepods in unfiltered New York City tap water a kashrus problem? Comparing reservoirs to the Gemara's water pits, with rulings, on Chullin 70.

kashrus/double-seal-on-wine.intro: Chazal required a double seal on uncooked wine to prevent tampering, while mevushal wine needs only one. In practice any seal that cannot be tampered with counts as double, but some argue a plastic cap can be removed and replaced, so it is just one seal; the OU considers it a double seal. [Don’t Make a “Pour” Decision](/daf/avodah-zarah/30/dont-make-a-pour-decision) ties the question to the mevushal debate on Avodah Zarah 30a.
kashrus/double-seal-on-wine.description: Does a plastic cap count as one seal or two on uncooked wine? The double seal Chazal required, and how the mevushal debate on Avodah Zarah 30a affects it.

kashrus/eating-treif-by-mistake.intro: When a supposedly kosher restaurant or store turns out to be serving treif, do the customers need to do teshuvah? Rav Moshe Feinstein ruled that if someone had a halachic basis to trust the place, it counts as an aveirah b'oines, beyond his control. His son Rav Reuvein Feinstein pressed him on a seeming contradiction, and the answer draws on Rava's courtroom in Kesubos 85a.
kashrus/eating-treif-by-mistake.description: Did someone who ate treif from a supposedly kosher store sin? Rav Moshe Feinstein explains when it is oines, drawing on Rava's court in Kesubos 85a.

kashrus/ein-mevatlin-issur-lechatchila.intro: One may not purposely nullify a forbidden ingredient. Boruch argues that buying a product and relying on bittul breaks this rule, while Shimon notes that some Acharonim say it was nullified on the shelf already. Pouring it into coffee to create sixty-to-one is clearly forbidden, in a dialogue tied to the mixtures of Zevachim 74.
kashrus/ein-mevatlin-issur-lechatchila.description: Can you buy a product and rely on bittul for a small forbidden ingredient? Ein mevatlin issur lechatchila, in a dialogue on the mixtures of Zevachim 74.

kashrus/faverolles-chicken-controversy.intro: In 1934 a French chicken with five toes divided the rabbinic world. The Chasam Sofer allows any breed substantially like a chicken with a mesorah, but the Minchas Elazar said the Faverolles differed in toes, head and even its cluck, so it needed its own tradition. The Sheires Yisrael answered that Syrian Sephardim ate it, citing Tosfos in Chullin 47.
kashrus/faverolles-chicken-controversy.description: Was the five-toed Faverolles chicken kosher? The Minchas Elazar forbade it, and the Sheires Yisrael cited Syrian Jews who ate it. A debate from Chullin 47.

kashrus/gid-hanasheh-in-a-ben-pekua.intro: A ben pekua, a calf found alive inside its slaughtered mother, does not carry the ordinary prohibitions of gid hanasheh or cheilev. Rebbi Meir disagrees, since he treats it as a regular animal in every way, but the halacha does not follow him. In [A Wedding Menu to Remember](/daf/chullin/75/a-wedding-menu-to-remember), a mashgiach uses Abaye's idea in Chullin 75b to explain why an unusual occasion keeps the rabbinic concern away.
kashrus/gid-hanasheh-in-a-ben-pekua.description: Why are the sciatic nerve and forbidden fats of a ben pekua not forbidden by Torah law? Rebbi Meir's view and Abaye's teaching in Chullin 75b explain it.

kashrus/is-bison-kosher.intro: Bison and buffalo are two different animals, and while the Rema discusses the buffalo, the bison is a separate species. The OU certifies bison following the Pri Megadim, while Rav Dovid Feinstein reportedly held one should be strict, a question tied to Chullin 45a and explored in [From Savanna to Supper?](/daf/chullin/45/from-savanna-to-supper)
kashrus/is-bison-kosher.description: Is bison kosher? It differs from the buffalo, the OU certifies it per the Pri Megadim, and Rav Dovid Feinstein was strict. A question tied to Chullin 45a.

kashrus/is-civet-coffee-kosher.intro: Kopi luwak is made from coffee beans eaten and passed by civets. Bechoros 7a discusses whether products of non-kosher animals are kosher, and the Ramban and Rosh are strict where the Rambam is lenient. In [Is Civet Coffee Kosher?](/daf/bechoros/7/is-civet-coffee-kosher), Rav Dovid Feinstein rules that the beans stay whole, like a kosher fish found inside a non-kosher one, so all would agree.
kashrus/is-civet-coffee-kosher.description: Are coffee beans eaten and passed by civets kosher? Rav Dovid Feinstein says the whole bean is unchanged, based on the rules taught in Bechoros 7a.

kashrus/is-giraffe-kosher.intro: Many say we don't eat giraffe because no one knows where on its long neck to shecht. But Chullin 45a teaches that the entire neck is fit for shechitah. The real question is mesorah, since some early commentators identify the zemer of Devarim as the giraffe, but that identification is itself disputed.
kashrus/is-giraffe-kosher.description: Is the giraffe kosher? Chullin 45a disproves the myth about where to shecht, so the real issue is whether a mesorah exists. Learn the details from the daf.

kashrus/is-the-braekel-chicken-kosher.intro: The Braekel is a heirloom chicken from a part of Belgium with no Jews, so it has no local mesorah. Rav Shternbuch ruled it too different from the standard chicken, while the followers of Rav Vosner say it is a purer breed and preferable. The debate draws on the same sources as the Faverolles case and Chullin 47, as traced in [It Clucks Like a Chicken, But Is It Kosher?](/daf/chullin/47/it-clucks-like-a-chicken-but-is-it-kosher)
kashrus/is-the-braekel-chicken-kosher.description: Is the Belgian Braekel chicken kosher? Rav Shternbuch says it needs its own mesorah, while Rav Vosner's followers prefer it. A debate tied to Chullin 47.

kashrus/kosher-chicken-breeds.intro: We have a mesorah that chickens are kosher, but there are hundreds of breeds. The Chasam Sofer ruled that a breed is kosher if it is substantially similar to a chicken with a mesorah. [Egg-cellent Advice](/daf/chullin/66/egg-cellent-advice) brings the STAR-K's finding that Silkie, Easter Egger, Australorp, Brahma, Cochin and Ameraucana lack an accepted mesorah under the Rema, building on Chullin 66b.
kashrus/kosher-chicken-breeds.description: Which chicken breeds are kosher? The Chasam Sofer's test of similarity, and six popular backyard breeds that lack a mesorah. Learn more from Chullin 66b.

kashrus/kosher-substitutes-for-forbidden.intro: Yalta told Rav Nachman that for every forbidden thing Hashem made a permitted match, like liver for blood and the brain of the shibbuta fish for pork, as told in Chullin 109b. Rav Nachman had roasted udders served to her in place of meat and milk. The article follows modern attempts, from the shibbuta fish to Spanish goose liver that tasted like pork.
kashrus/kosher-substitutes-for-forbidden.description: Did Hashem give a kosher match for every forbidden food? Yalta says so in Chullin 109b, and modern hunts for kosher food that tastes like pork follow.

kashrus/milk-from-treif-cows.intro: Most cattle found treif have lung lesions, and the rate rises with age. Rav Hershel Schachter is reputed to have said that in mature milking cows it could well be over 90 percent. Since milk from a treif animal is not kosher either, he is concerned about the milk from those older cows, as the article on Chullin 46 explains.
kashrus/milk-from-treif-cows.description: If most older dairy cows are treif, what about their milk? Rav Hershel Schachter's concern over the kashrus of milk from mature cows. From Chullin 46.

kashrus/nat-bar-nat.intro: Nathan cooked hot dogs in his mother's urn, which she uses for coffee with milk. [In Hot Water](/daf/pesachim/30/in-hot-water) uses Tosfos on Pesachim 30a to explain nat bar nat, a flavor that passes from meat to a clean utensil and then to pareve food. The Shulchan Aruch treats such food as pareve, the Rema prefers not to eat it with cheese initially, and the Vilna Gaon and Chochmas Adam add leniencies once the utensil has not been used for 24 hours.
kashrus/nat-bar-nat.description: Can pareve food cooked in a clean meat pot be eaten with dairy? Nat bar nat in Tosfos on Pesachim 30a, the Shulchan Aruch, Rema and the 24-hour rule.

kashrus/onion-cut-with-a-fleishig-knife.intro: Cold food touching a cold utensil usually picks up no taste, and a simple rinse is enough. Sharp foods are the exception: an onion cut with a cold fleishig knife becomes fleishig. The Rishonim in the discussion on Chullin 8b use this ruling as proof that ordinary, non-sharp foods cut with a knife need only a surface rinse.
kashrus/onion-cut-with-a-fleishig-knife.description: Why does an onion cut with a cold fleishig knife become fleishig when other cold foods do not? The rule of sharp foods, used by Rishonim on Chullin 8b.

kashrus/prohibition-of-raising-pigs.intro: During the Hasmonean civil war between Hyrcanus and Aristobulus, a pig was sent up the wall of Yerushalayim in place of a sheep for the daily offering, and the Sages cursed anyone who raises pigs. [How Far Would You Go for Cocoa Bombs?](/daf/pesachim/23/how-far-would-you-go-for-cocoa-bombs) compares this to Pesachim 23a, which seems to forbid trading in any non-kosher animal, and brings Tosfos' three answers, such as a special curse reserved for pigs.
kashrus/prohibition-of-raising-pigs.description: Why did the Sages curse anyone who raises pigs? The Hasmonean civil war story, and how it fits with the ban on trading non-kosher animals. Pesachim 23a.

kashrus/removing-cheilev-from-meat.intro: Butchers who kasher their own meat must cut away the forbidden fats with special non-kosher knives. The Rivam ruled that the meat must then be peeled wherever that knife touched it, but the butchers of Tosfos's day did not peel. In [Trimming The Fat](/daf/chullin/8/trimming-the-fat), Tosfos, the Rashba and the Rosh defend them on Chullin 8b: cold fat removed with a cold knife transfers no real taste.
kashrus/removing-cheilev-from-meat.description: Must kosher beef be peeled where the cheilev knife touched it? The Rivam says yes, but Tosfos, the Rashba and the Rosh defend the butchers, on Chullin 8b.

kashrus/signs-of-a-kosher-bird.intro: How can you tell a kosher bird from a forbidden one? Chullin 59a lists several signs, the most crucial being that a dores, a bird with predatory traits, is not kosher. A dores perches with two toes on each side, while a kosher bird puts three on one side and one on the other, as [Some Hard-Boiled Shailos](/daf/chullin/59/some-hard-boiled-shailos) explains.
kashrus/signs-of-a-kosher-bird.description: What signs mark a kosher bird? Chullin 59a teaches that a dores is forbidden and perches two toes on each side, unlike a kosher bird's three and one.

kashrus/signs-of-a-kosher-egg.intro: Chullin 66b gives two tests for a kosher egg: it is rounded at one end and pointed at the other, and the yolk sits inside the white. But the eggs of some predatory birds can mimic that shape. So where non-kosher birds are common, the signs are not enough, and the Gemara allows a merchant's word to confirm the species.
kashrus/signs-of-a-kosher-egg.description: How can you tell a kosher egg? Chullin 66b gives the shape test and the yolk test, but warns that predatory birds' eggs can mimic the kosher shape.

kashrus/smelling-non-kosher-food.intro: Is enjoying the aroma of forbidden food like eating it? Abaye and Rava argue on Avodah Zarah 66b whether aroma has significance, and we rule like Rava that it does not. But Tosafos on Avodah Zarah 12b forbids smelling roses used for idolatry, Rabbeinu Tam distinguishes items made for their scent, and the Pri Chadash, Chochmas Adam and Chofetz Chaim permit smelling non-kosher food.
kashrus/smelling-non-kosher-food.description: May one enjoy the smell of non-kosher food? Abaye and Rava on aroma in Avodah Zarah 66b, Rabbeinu Tam's distinction, and the poskim who rule leniently.

kashrus/treif-knife-on-kosher-meat.intro: What happens when an animal is slaughtered with a treif knife? In Chullin 8b, Rav requires the touched area to be thinly peeled, while Rabbah Bar Bar Chanah says washing is enough. The Gemara explains that the pressure of a knife can push taste into the meat, and Rashi says the halacha follows Rav since a Torah prohibition is at stake.
kashrus/treif-knife-on-kosher-meat.description: Does meat touched by a treif knife need peeling or just rinsing? Rav and Rabbah Bar Bar Chanah disagree in Chullin 8b over knife pressure and heat.

kashrus/whole-insects-not-nullified.intro: A forbidden ingredient can usually be nullified when it is less than one sixtieth of a mixture, but a whole bug is a beryah and is never nullified. In [Bugging Out](/daf/chullin/100/bugging-out), a guest argues that only significant creatures like the ant count. The Chavvos Yair answers that anything alive, and able to cause pain, is significant, building on Chullin 100.
kashrus/whole-insects-not-nullified.description: Why can't a whole insect be nullified in food, even in sixty times its size? The Chavvos Yair explains the rule of beryah, building on Chullin 100.

kashrus/why-bee-honey-is-kosher.intro: Bees are not kosher, yet their honey is. Bechoros 7a asks why: is there a special pasuk, or does the bee just carry kosher nectar without making it a true secretion? The Rambam allows honey from any insect, while the Ramban and Rosh allow only bee honey, and the Aruch HaShulchan ties this to the debate over horse urine.
kashrus/why-bee-honey-is-kosher.description: Why is bee honey kosher when bees are not, and is wasp honey kosher too? The Rambam, Ramban and Rosh differ, based on the Gemara in Bechoros 7a.

kashrus/zebu-beef-kashrus.intro: In 2004 it came out that much South American beef imported into Israel came from zebu cattle, with their fatty hump and drooping ears. The zebu has both kosher signs, but the Shach writes that we do not eat animals without a mesorah. Following the Chazon Ish, many Israeli hechsherim refuse zebu, while many American ones allow it, building on Chullin 45a.
kashrus/zebu-beef-kashrus.description: Is zebu beef kosher? It has both kosher signs, but many Israeli hechsherim follow the Chazon Ish and refuse it without a mesorah. Building on Chullin 45a.

basar-bechalav/dairy-or-meat-bread.intro: Pesachim 30a teaches that bread may not be baked in an oven smeared with fat, since someone might eat the meat bread with dairy. The rabbis therefore required that bread be pareve, which is why a kosher dairy hot dog bun is a contradiction. Dairy bread is allowed only if it looks distinctive, so the OU permits pizza crusts, calzones and garlic knots made with milk, since their pizza-shop look prompts people to ask.
basar-bechalav/dairy-or-meat-bread.description: Why must bread normally be pareve, and when may it be dairy? The rabbinic rule in Pesachim 30a and why pizza dough made with milk is permitted.

basar-bechalav/hot-water-urn-used-for-me.intro: Nathan cooked hot dogs in his mother's water urn, and now she fears her morning coffee with milk is ruined. Chullin 111b allows hot fish placed on a meat plate to be eaten with milk, an example of two flavor transfers. Since an urn is a special utensil, the Chochmas Adam allows water from it with milk once it is cleaned and unused for 24 hours.
basar-bechalav/hot-water-urn-used-for-me.description: Hot dogs were cooked in the water urn. May its water go in coffee with milk? Two flavor transfers and a 24-hour wait, per the Chochmas Adam. Chullin 111b.

basar-bechalav/non-dairy-creamer-after-m.intro: Non-dairy creamer may contain sodium caseinate, a milk derivative. After a deli sandwich, may it go into coffee? The OU explains Rav Yisrael Belsky's view: for someone who does not keep cholov Yisrael the creamer is fully kosher, so this is only a question of milk after meat, and the small amount of milk may be nullified, in a discussion of Zevachim 74.
basar-bechalav/non-dairy-creamer-after-m.description: May non-dairy creamer with a milk derivative go in coffee after meat? Rav Yisrael Belsky's ruling as the OU explains it, in a dialogue tied to Zevachim 74.

basar-bechalav/using-a-meat-pot-after-24.intro: Bread baked in a clean meat pan is parve, but may it be eaten with cheese? Chullin 111b discusses hot fish on a meat plate, and the Rema prefers not to rely on it at first. In [The Hot Dog That Got Nathan in Hot Water](/daf/chullin/111/the-hot-dog-that-got-nathan-in-hot-water), the Vilna Gaon permits it when the pan was unused for 24 hours.
basar-bechalav/using-a-meat-pot-after-24.description: May parve food cooked in a meat pot unused for 24 hours be eaten with dairy? The Rema, the Vilna Gaon and the Chochmas Adam weigh in. From Chullin 111b.

basar-bechalav/waiting-between-meat-and-.intro: How long should one wait after meat before eating dairy? In Chullin 105a, Mar Ukva says his father waited a full 24 hours, while he himself waited only from one meal to the next, roughly six hours. He called himself vinegar compared to wine, yet did not adopt his father's practice, and the article explores why.
basar-bechalav/waiting-between-meat-and-.description: How long do you wait between meat and milk? Mar Ukva's father waited 24 hours, while he waited from one meal to the next, about six hours. Chullin 105a.

shechitah/ben-pekua-meat-without-shechit.intro: A calf found alive inside a properly slaughtered mother may be raised and eaten without its own shechitah, according to the Tanna Kamma and Rebbi Shimon Shezuri. Rebbi Meir requires shechitah, and the Tanna Kamma still requires it rabbinically once the animal walks on the ground. Abaye in Chullin 75b says that when something unusual reminds everyone it is a ben pekua, that decree falls away.
shechitah/ben-pekua-meat-without-shechit.description: May a calf found alive inside its slaughtered mother be eaten without shechitah? Rebbi Meir, the Tanna Kamma and Abaye on the ben pekua, Chullin 75b.

shechitah/covering-blood-with-a-gold-coi.intro: After shechting a bird, its blood must be covered, and Chullin 88b says that with no dirt around, one may grind up a gold coin and use the dust.
