The Rema permits this only when the bird is worth more than the coin. The Pri Chadash disagrees, pointing to the glass broken under the chuppah: any positive purpose is enough.
shechitah/covering-blood-with-a-gold-coi.description: May one grind a gold coin to cover a bird's blood? The Rema allows it only if the bird is worth more, and the Pri Chadash argues, from Chullin 88b.

shechitah/eggs-from-a-treifah-chicken.intro: An egg laid by a hen with a fatal defect is forbidden like the hen, yet Chullin 66b relies on rov, since most birds are not treifos. Even with tendon disease common, a live hen cannot be checked, so the majority may be relied on. Still, a backyard hen attacked by a raccoon or with a splinted leg was ruled a treifah.
shechitah/eggs-from-a-treifah-chicken.description: Are eggs from a treifah hen forbidden? The Gemara relies on the healthy majority, but a raccoon attack or broken leg can make a hen treif. See Chullin 66b.

shechitah/lung-lesions-in-cattle.intro: We usually rely on the rule that most animals are not treif, but lungs are different, since lesions there are so common. One meat processor reports that 60 percent of his cattle are found treif. Building on Chullin 46, the Aruch HaShulchan explains that many lesions are not truly treif, but since we can no longer tell them apart, all are treated as treif.
shechitah/lung-lesions-in-cattle.description: Why must the lungs of every cow be checked? Lesions are so common that many cattle are found treif, and the Aruch HaShulchan explains why. From Chullin 46.

shechitah/tzomes-hagidim-in-chickens.intro: Inside a chicken's lower leg lies the tzomes hagidim, the junction of the tendons, and a single torn tendon there makes the bird a treifah. In Chullin 57a, a basket of birds with broken legs came before Rava. He checked each one at the tzomes hagidim, found the tendons intact, and declared them kosher.
shechitah/tzomes-hagidim-in-chickens.description: What is the tzomes hagidim, and why does one torn tendon make a chicken treif? Rava checks birds with broken legs in Chullin 57a. See how it is inspected.

shechitah/what-glatt-kosher-means.intro: Glatt means smooth, and glatt kosher first meant meat from an animal whose lungs had no lesions. The Rema allows lesions that come off easily, while the Shulchan Aruch requires completely smooth lungs, the standard called Beit Yosef glatt. Today the word even appears on fish, which have no lungs, a point made on Chullin 46 in [Glatt Or Not?](/daf/chullin/46/glatt-or-not)
shechitah/what-glatt-kosher-means.description: What does glatt kosher really mean? Smooth lungs, the Rema versus the Shulchan Aruch, and how the term came to mean a high standard. From Chullin 46.

bishul-akum-and-pas-akum/bishul-akum-and.intro: Does food cooked by a non-Jew become forbidden even when it could never be made in a home kitchen? Asked about Wise potato chips, Rav Dovid Feinstein answered that they can only be made in a factory, so bishul akum does not apply, a leniency first suggested by Rav Moshe. The same laws stand behind [Pasta Imposter](/daf/avodah-zarah/74/pasta-imposter) on Avodah Zarah 74b, about oven-ready lasagna noodles.
bishul-akum-and-pas-akum/bishul-akum-and.description: Are potato chips made only in factories subject to bishul akum? Rav Dovid Feinstein's answer, and the oven-ready lasagna case from Avodah Zarah 74b.

bishul-akum-and-pas-akum/jew-lighting-th.intro: Avodah Zarah 35b lists cooked food and bread among the things that must be made by Jews. Everyone agrees that a Jew turning on the oven makes the bread pas Yisrael, and the Rema says the same works for cooked dishes. The Shulchan Aruch disagrees about cooking, so Sephardim want the Jew to place the food on the fire or take a more active role, though he accepts lighting the fire for bread.
bishul-akum-and-pas-akum/jew-lighting-th.description: Does a Jew lighting the fire make a non-Jew's cooking bishul Yisrael? The Rema and the Shulchan Aruch differ for food and bread, from Avodah Zarah 35b.

bishul-akum-and-pas-akum/mevushal-wine.intro: On Avodah Zarah 30a, the gentile scholar Avleit avoided touching Shmuel's wine, and Shmuel told him it did not matter because the wine was cooked. Rav Moshe Feinstein held that pasteurized wine counts as mevushal, but Rav Elyashiv, Rav Shlomo Zalman Auerbach and Rav Ben Tzion Abba Shaul each rejected this for a different reason. [Mevushal or Lo Mevushal: That Is The Question](/daf/avodah-zarah/30/mevushal-or-lo-mevushal-that-is-the-question) shows how one bottle could be labeled both ways.
bishul-akum-and-pas-akum/mevushal-wine.description: What makes wine mevushal, and does pasteurization count? Shmuel and Avleit on Avodah Zarah 30a, Rav Moshe Feinstein, and the poskim who disagree.

bishul-akum-and-pas-akum/oven-ready-lasa.intro: Why does regular Ronzoni lasagna carry an OU while the oven-ready kind does not? Oven-ready noodles are precooked, and Avodah Zarah 74b deals with the bishul akum ban on food that is not eaten raw and is fit for a king's table. Rav Moshe Feinstein permitted food made with specialized factory equipment, but the OU uses that heter only with another leniency, while another agency relies on it alone.
bishul-akum-and-pas-akum/oven-ready-lasa.description: Why does oven-ready lasagna lack an OU? Precooked noodles, the bishul akum ban, and Rav Moshe Feinstein's factory leniency, from Avodah Zarah 74b.

bishul-akum-and-pas-akum/pas-palter.intro: Kosher bread baked by an individual gentile is forbidden, but bread from a non-Jewish bakery, pas palter, is the subject of dispute on Avodah Zarah 35b. Tosfos reports a lenient custom, while the Shulchan Aruch allows it only when no pas Yisrael is available or, as the Rashba says, when the pas palter is superior. The Rema permits it even when pas Yisrael is available, and the Shach advises following the Shulchan Aruch.
bishul-akum-and-pas-akum/pas-palter.description: May one eat kosher bread from a non-Jewish bakery? Pas palter on Avodah Zarah 35b, with Tosfos, the Shulchan Aruch, the Rema, and the Sephardic custom.

bishul-akum-and-pas-akum/pas-yisrael-dur.intro: Many people eat only pas Yisrael during the Aseres Yemei Teshuvah, so bread, bagels, cakes and muffins should all come from Jewish bakeries. Doughnuts are deep-fried, and many poskim say they are not in the bread family. The article on Bava Kamma 91b then asks what to do with pas palter already in the house.
bishul-akum-and-pas-akum/pas-yisrael-dur.description: Which baked goods need to be pas Yisrael during the Ten Days of Repentance, and what about doughnuts? A custom explored in an article on Bava Kamma 91b.

bishul-akum-and-pas-akum/wine-touched-by.intro: Chazal forbade drinking a gentile's wine, and even kosher wine poured or touched by one. Two reasons are given: the wine may have served in a ceremony honoring an idol, and drinking together may lead to inappropriate relationships. Avodah Zarah 30a teaches the exemption for cooked wine, so those who do not count pasteurized wine as cooked would not leave an open bottle of grape juice alone with non-Jewish help.
bishul-akum-and-pas-akum/wine-touched-by.description: Why does kosher wine become forbidden when a non-Jew pours or touches it? The two reasons behind the ban, and the mevushal exemption from Avodah Zarah 30a.

bishul-akum-and-pas-akum/wine-touched-by.intro: Does uncooked wine become forbidden when a Jew who does not keep Shabbos pours it? Rav Binyomin Forst writes in The Kosher Kitchen that the prohibition applies only to wine he actually touches, and that one raised without a religious background may not forbid it at all. A gentile pouring from the bottle, by contrast, forbids the whole bottle, following the sugya of wine and touch on Avodah Zarah 30a.
bishul-akum-and-pas-akum/wine-touched-by.description: Does wine poured by a Jew who does not keep Shabbos become forbidden? Rav Binyomin Forst's ruling, compared with a non-Jew's touch on Avodah Zarah 30a.

tevilas-keilim/borrowing-utensils-to-avo.intro: A utensil bought from a gentile must be toiveled, but one borrowed from a gentile may be used without tevilah. That is why some caterers borrow glassware, and why a person in need may give a utensil to a gentile and borrow it back. The Mishnah Berurah warns this works only for thirty days, the same limit Menachos 44a sets for borrowed tzitzis.
tevilas-keilim/borrowing-utensils-to-avo.description: May one use a utensil borrowed from a non-Jew without tevilah, and for how long? The Mishnah Berurah's thirty-day limit, tied to Menachos 44a.

tevilas-keilim/far-rockaway-keilim-mikva.intro: The daf in Chagigah 21 touches on the halachos of tevilas keilim, and that raises a question about the keilim mikvah in Far Rockaway. In a short video, [R’ Avrohom Sebrow Explains Setup of Far Rockaway Keilim Mikvah, In Light of todays Daf Yomi](/beyond-the-daf/r-avrohom-sebrow-explains-setup-of-far-rockaway-keilim-mikvah-in-light-of-todays-daf-yomi) walks through how that mikvah is arranged, prompted by R' Eli Stefansky's videos on the daf.
tevilas-keilim/far-rockaway-keilim-mikva.description: How is the Far Rockaway keilim mikvah set up? A short video explanation, given in light of the tevilas keilim halachos on the daf in Chagigah 21.

tevilas-keilim/food-cooked-in-an-untovel.intro: If food was cooked in a pot that was never toiveled, is it treif? Tevilah and kashrus are different laws, so a brand-new metal utensil needs tevilah even though it is certainly kosher, and food inadvertently made in it may still be eaten. [Tevilas Keilim: Clearing The Confusion](/daf/avodah-zarah/75/tevilas-keilim-clearing-the-confusion) on Avodah Zarah 75 also notes that kashering can be done piecemeal, while tevilah must cover the whole utensil at once.
tevilas-keilim/food-cooked-in-an-untovel.description: Is food cooked in a pot that was never toiveled still kosher? Why tevilas keilim and kashering are different laws, as taught at the end of Avodah Zarah 75.

tevilas-keilim/how-a-keilim-mikvah-works.intro: New dishes and utensils are immersed in a special mikvah, and its design must follow the halachos of tevilas keilim. Chagigah 21 and the next daf touch on these laws, which many learners met through R' Eli Stefansky's videos. A rebbe at Yeshiva Ateres Shimon explains in a video why a keilim mikvah is built the way it is, using the Far Rockaway mikvah as the example.
tevilas-keilim/how-a-keilim-mikvah-works.description: What makes a keilim mikvah work for immersing new dishes? A video on its setup and design, tied to the tevilas keilim halachos found in Chagigah 21.

tevilas-keilim/tevilah-for-a-keurig-mach.intro: Many Keurig machines would break if immersed in a mikveh. HaRav Moshe Heinemann ruled that such items may be used without tevilah, though that ruling is highly controversial. Some transfer ownership to a non-Jew and borrow the machine back, so any obligation is only rabbinic, building on the thirty-day borrowing idea of Menachos 44a.
tevilas-keilim/tevilah-for-a-keurig-mach.description: What about tevilah for a Keurig that would break in a mikveh? Rav Heinemann's ruling and selling it to a non-Jew, building on the idea in Menachos 44a.

tevilas-keilim/tevilah-for-silver-judaic.intro: Do silver Kiddush cups and Seder plates need tevilah? Very often yes: even pieces stamped by famous Israeli makers like Hazorfim or Hadad are frequently made in Italy, Hungary or Turkey. The mitzvah of tevilas keilim comes at the end of Avodah Zarah 75, and items bought in a Jewish store also need tevilah if the maker or distributor is gentile-owned.
tevilas-keilim/tevilah-for-silver-judaic.description: Do silver Kiddush cups and Seder plates need tevilah? Many Israeli-branded pieces are made abroad, so the mitzvah taught in Avodah Zarah 75 often applies.

tevilas-keilim/toveling-dishes-on-shabbo.intro: The Shulchan Aruch records a dispute over toveling a new dish on Shabbos, since it may look like fixing the utensil. The solution he offers is to give it to a non-Jew as a gift and borrow it back, since a utensil a non-Jew owns needs no tevilah. The Mishnah Berurah says to tovel it after Shabbos without a beracha, in an article on Beitzah 36a.
tevilas-keilim/toveling-dishes-on-shabbo.description: May new dishes be toveled on Shabbos? The Shulchan Aruch suggests giving them to a non-Jew and borrowing them back, in an article on Beitzah 36a.

tevilas-keilim/toveling-in-a-lake.intro: On a camping trip, can any lake serve to toivel a new grill? Not every lake or river is a kosher mikveh. A man-made lake filled and replenished by rainwater cannot be used for tevilas keilim; it must be formed by a natural spring, one of the common myths cleared up as the daf reaches the end of Avodah Zarah 75.
tevilas-keilim/toveling-in-a-lake.description: Can any lake be used to toivel a new grill on a camping trip? Why rain-fed lakes may not count as a mikveh for tevilas keilim, from Avodah Zarah 75.

tevilas-keilim/toveling-mishloach-manos-.intro: One family gave out candy in glass salt and pepper shakers for mishloach manos, raising the question of tevilah. In a piece tied to Megillah 7b, Rav Binyomin Forst ruled that if the people will keep them, tevilah is required. All 100 were toveled, which is hard with narrow shapes, since no air bubble may separate the walls from the water, and the shakers later turned up in friends' homes.
tevilas-keilim/toveling-mishloach-manos-.description: Do glass containers given as mishloach manos need tevilah? Rav Binyomin Forst says yes if recipients keep them, in an article tied to Megillah 7b.

tevilas-keilim/trusting-a-child-about-te.intro: Anyone, even a minor, may immerse a utensil, but a child is not normally believed that it was done. Rosh Hashanah 22 teaches that people do not lie about what will soon come out, and Rav Shlomo Zalman applied this to a boy saying he is bar mitzvah. By the same logic, a child sent to ask a gift giver whether a tray was toiveled may be trusted.
tevilas-keilim/trusting-a-child-about-te.description: May a child immerse a utensil, and is he believed it was toiveled? How Rosh Hashanah 22 and Rav Shlomo Zalman's ruling apply to a gift tray question.

tevilas-keilim/using-a-utensil-before-te.intro: May a new pot be used just once before it is toiveled? A utensil that needs tevilah may not be used even one time first; the myth comes from disposable aluminum pans, which may be used without tevilah, and perhaps the cheapest charcoal grills count as disposable too, but the grate of a regular grill does not. Avodah Zarah 75, where the mesechta ends, teaches the mitzvah.
tevilas-keilim/using-a-utensil-before-te.description: May a new utensil be used once before tevilah? Why not, and the exception for disposable aluminum pans and cheap grills, from the end of Avodah Zarah 75.

chadash-and-yashan/eating-chadash-on-the.intro: Once the Korban Omer could no longer be brought, new grain became permitted on the morning of the 16th of Nissan. The Mishnah on Rosh Hashanah 30a records that Rebbe Yochanan ben Zakai forbade it for the entire day, so that when the Beis HaMikdash is rebuilt people will not eat it before the Omer out of habit. The Imrei Emes sees in this takanah a message of hope.
chadash-and-yashan/eating-chadash-on-the.description: Why is new grain forbidden all day on the 16th of Nissan? Rosh Hashanah 30a: Rebbe Yochanan ben Zakai's takanah in case the Beis HaMikdash is soon rebuilt.

chadash-and-yashan/when-new-grain-become.intro: Without the Omer offering, the new grain becomes permitted by the day itself, the sixteenth of Nissan. Rav and Shmuel say it is allowed that morning, while Rebbe Yehudah says only after the whole day passes. [Everything Old Is New Again](/daf/menachos/68/everything-old-is-new-again) explains the dispute through ad v'lo ad bichlal, as discussed in Menachos 68.
chadash-and-yashan/when-new-grain-become.description: Does new grain become permitted on the morning of the 16th of Nissan or after the whole day? Rav and Shmuel versus Rebbe Yehudah in Menachos 68.

chadash-and-yashan/yashan-outside-eretz-.intro: Yashan, keeping away from new grain until after the Omer, has grown more popular in America, yet many in the Diaspora have long been lenient. Rabbeinu Baruch holds the mitzvah does not apply to lands far from Israel. The Rema adds that doubt over whether grain is new or old can form a s'fek s'feika, as the article on Menachos 68 explains.
chadash-and-yashan/yashan-outside-eretz-.description: Does the ban on new grain apply outside Eretz Yisrael? Rabbeinu Baruch and the Rema's double doubt explain why many are lenient, from Menachos 68.

chadash-and-yashan/yom-hanef-and-new-gra.intro: The Mishnah on Rosh Hashanah 30a records that new grain may not be eaten until the night after the 16th of Nissan. Rebbe Yochanan ben Zakai worried that once the Beis HaMikdash is rebuilt, people used to eating on the morning of the 16th would eat before the Korban Omer. [Takana Considerations](/daf/rosh-hashanah/30/takana-considerations) brings Rebbe Moshe Betzalel's insight, which moved the Brisker Rav, that this takanah gave the nation hope.
chadash-and-yashan/yom-hanef-and-new-gra.description: New grain stays forbidden until the night after the 16th of Nissan. Rosh Hashanah 30a explains the takanah and the hope it gave of a rebuilt Mikdash soon.

cholov-yisrael/non-dairy-creamer-and-cho.intro: A creamer can be labeled non-dairy and still say "Contains milk" on the back. For one who is strict about cholov Yisrael, even that small amount is a forbidden ingredient, so buying it means relying on bittul on purpose. That is why Rav Yisrael Belsky told such a person not to use it, in a dialogue tied to Zevachim 74.
cholov-yisrael/non-dairy-creamer-and-cho.description: Why may non-dairy creamer be a problem for those who keep cholov Yisrael? Rav Yisrael Belsky on milk derivatives, in a dialogue tied to Zevachim 74.

marriage/being-too-picky-in-shidduchim.intro: Sotah 2a teaches that forty days before a child is formed, a Heavenly voice calls out whose daughter he will marry. The Steipler explains this is not a fixed decree but a sign of a fitting match, and free will can lose it. In [Mazal Tov So-and-So!](/daf/sotah/2/mazal-tov-so-and-so), he warns that a boy who wants a girl with every quality, or who comes to a first meeting unprepared, may miss his bas Ploni.
marriage/being-too-picky-in-shidduchim.description: Can being too picky cost you your bashert? The Steipler on the Heavenly voice in Sotah 2a, arrogance in shidduchim and preparing for a first meeting.

marriage/chizkiyahu-refusing-to-marry.intro: King Chizkiya foresaw through Ruach HaKodesh that he would have wicked children, so he chose not to marry. In Berachos 10a, Yeshaya HaNavi tells him that his illness is a punishment, since he must keep the halacha and leave the future to Hashem. Chizkiya prayed, married Yeshaya's daughter, and still fathered the wicked Menashe, as [Leave the Rest to Hashem](/daf/yevamos/49/leave-the-rest-to-hashem) recounts.
marriage/chizkiyahu-refusing-to-marry.description: Why did King Chizkiya refuse to marry, and what did Yeshaya HaNavi tell him? Keep the mitzvah and trust Hashem, from Berachos 10a and Yevamos 49b.

marriage/choosing-a-wedding-date.intro: Wednesdays, the first half of the month, Sefirah, the Aseres Yemei Teshuvah and fast days leave very few dates for a wedding. The Sefer Chazon Yeshayah counts fewer than fifteen days a year if all customs are kept. In [Wednesday is the Day to Wed](/daf/kesubos/2/wednesday-is-the-day-to-wed), filed on Kesubos 2a, the Steipler and Rav Shach advise simply marrying on the earliest possible day.
marriage/choosing-a-wedding-date.description: How should a couple pick a wedding date? Sefirah, fast days and old customs, and why the Steipler and Rav Shach urged the earliest date, from Kesubos 2a.

marriage/delaying-a-wedding-over-a-dowry.intro: The bride's parents promised a large dowry but cannot pay it, so may the groom put off the wedding until they do? The Raavad, quoted by the Rema, warns that fighting over the wife's money will not bring success. In [Marrying for Money](/daf/kiddushin/70/marrying-for-money), the Chelkas Mechokeik and Aruch HaShulchan agree that delaying would count as marrying for money, the case condemned in Kiddushin 70a.
marriage/delaying-a-wedding-over-a-dowry.description: May a groom put off his wedding when the bride's parents cannot pay the promised dowry? The Raavad and Chelkas Mechokeik say no, from Kiddushin 70a.

marriage/disqualified-witness-at-a-chupp.intro: At a wedding, a man accused one of the kiddushin witnesses of being a thief, and the witness wound up to punch him. A guest argued that the couple was not married, since Sanhedrin 58b calls anyone who raises his hand against another a rasha. [Hitting A Nerve](/daf/sanhedrin/58/hitting-a-nerve) follows the plan to permit the cherem and quietly redo the kiddushin, until Rav Zilberstein ruled the witness valid.
marriage/disqualified-witness-at-a-chupp.description: A kiddushin witness nearly punched a heckler under the chuppah. Was the marriage valid? Rav Zilberstein's answer, built on Sanhedrin 58b and the poskim.

marriage/getting-married-on-wednesday.intro: The first Mishnah of Kesubos 2a sets Wednesday as the day for a first marriage, since the courts met on Thursday. Bar Kapara adds that the fifth day carries the blessing to be fruitful and multiply. Tosfos says his reason is good advice, not binding, yet the P'nei Yehoshua urges those who want to fulfill the words of the Sages to marry on Wednesday.
marriage/getting-married-on-wednesday.description: Why were weddings held on Wednesday, and does it still matter? Court days, Bar Kapara's fifth-day blessing and the P'nei Yehoshua, from Kesubos 2a.

marriage/how-much-to-pay-a-shadchan.intro: Shadchanim are halachically entitled to be paid, but how much? The Tiferes Yisrael, the Chasam Sofer, Rav Shlomo Kluger and Rabbi Sholom Mordechai Schwadron all record a share of the dowry, with a bonus when the families live in distant cities. In [The Out-Of-Town Bonus](/daf/bechoros/55/the-out-of-town-bonus), Rabbi Schwadron learns from Bechoros 55 when a river makes cities distant.
marriage/how-much-to-pay-a-shadchan.description: How much should a shadchan be paid, and when is there a distance bonus? Old rates from the Chasam Sofer and others, and a river rule from Bechoros 55.

marriage/is-your-bashert-predestined.intro: Sotah 2a says that forty days before a baby is formed, a Heavenly voice announces whose daughter he will marry. Why does it say the daughter of so-and-so, rather than naming her? One reading is that she has not been conceived yet, but Tosfos says the announcement comes whether or not she was already born, and the Iyun Yaakov points to a father's role in his daughter's marriage.
marriage/is-your-bashert-predestined.description: What does the Heavenly voice announcing a future match mean, and why the daughter of so-and-so? Tosfos and the Iyun Yaakov explain Sotah 2a.

marriage/kiddushin-performed-by-a-minor.intro: The Teshuvos Shmuel ruled that a minor's attempt at kiddushin calls for a get, but the Vilna Gaon said the halacha is not concerned with a minor's act. Scholars showed him a Yerushalmi that seemed to validate it, and the Gaon noted it also appears in the Tosefta of Parah. [A Minor Point](/daf/sanhedrin/2/a-minor-point), on Sanhedrin 2, explains why that settled it: the kiddushin there meant sanctifying the parah adumah water.
marriage/kiddushin-performed-by-a-minor.description: Does a minor's kiddushin need a get? The Teshuvos Shmuel said yes; the Vilna Gaon disagreed and explained a Yerushalmi with the Tosefta, on Sanhedrin 2.

marriage/kiddushin-through-an-agent.intro: A groom may appoint an agent to give the ring for him, though the chuppah and yichud must be his own. Still, the Gemara teaches that a mitzvah done oneself is greater than one done through a messenger. Tied to Makkos 14a, the Ohr Zarua lists marrying and preparing for Shabbos as the two mitzvos to do personally, while the Magen Avraham applies it to every mitzvah.
marriage/kiddushin-through-an-agent.description: May a groom send a messenger to betroth his bride? Why doing it oneself is preferred, with the Ohr Zarua and Magen Avraham, in a piece on Makkos 14a.

marriage/kiddushin-with-loan-forgiveness.intro: Dovid HaMelech tried to betroth Meirav by forgiving the riches Shaul owed him for defeating Golias. On Sanhedrin 19b, Rebbe Yehoshua ben Korcha agrees with Shaul that a loan alone cannot effect kiddushin. With Michal, Dovid added physical proof of his victory, and the halacha follows him: loan forgiveness together with an item of value works.
marriage/kiddushin-with-loan-forgiveness.description: Can forgiving a loan effect kiddushin? Dovid HaMelech, Meirav and Michal on Sanhedrin 19b, and why adding an item of value changes the halacha.

marriage/kiddushin-without-naming-the-br.intro: Tosfos in Kiddushin 52a tell of Rav Oshaya HaLevi's son, who handed a wealthy man a ring and said, "Your daughter is betrothed to me," without saying which daughter. A respected sage ruled that every daughter needed a get and he could marry none of them. Rabbeinu Tam first argued that the father surely meant his oldest, citing Lavan, but he later retracted.
marriage/kiddushin-without-naming-the-br.description: A groom betrothed one of several daughters through their father without naming her. Which one is married? Tosfos and Rabbeinu Tam in Kiddushin 52a.

marriage/marrying-a-father-in-laws-widow.intro: Tosfos on Yevamos 21a reveal a fact found nowhere in Tanach or the Bavli: Dovid HaMelech married Ritzpah bas Aya, the widow of his father-in-law Shaul. That shows such a marriage is permitted, but the Yerushalmi forbids it rabbinically, since onlookers may think a man is marrying his mother-in-law. Many Rishonim do not follow the Yerushalmi here, while Rabbeinu Tam stopped such a wedding in Provence even after the meal was prepared.
marriage/marrying-a-father-in-laws-widow.description: May a man marry his father-in-law's widow? Dovid HaMelech and Ritzpah, the Yerushalmi's maaris ayin concern, and Rabbeinu Tam's ruling, Yevamos 21a.

marriage/marrying-a-late-wifes-sister.intro: How could Dovid HaMelech have married two sisters, Meirav and Michal? Rebbe Yosi's students asked exactly this, as Sanhedrin 19b records. Even after a divorce one may not marry a former wife's sister, so Rebbe Yosi answers that Meirav had passed away before Dovid married Michal.
marriage/marrying-a-late-wifes-sister.description: Did Dovid HaMelech marry two sisters? Rebbe Yosi on Sanhedrin 19b says Meirav had died, since one may marry a wife's sister only after her passing.

marriage/marrying-a-step-sibling.intro: A step-sister is no relative at all, but step-siblings who grew up together might look like siblings to an onlooker. The Yerushalmi forbids such a marriage unless they move where no one knows them, yet Tosfos on Yevamos 21a note that the Bavli rules there is no concern. [Keeping It In the Family](/daf/yevamos/21/keeping-it-in-the-family) tells how the Chofetz Chaim himself married his step-sister for the sake of shalom bayis.
marriage/marrying-a-step-sibling.description: May step-siblings who grew up together marry? The Yerushalmi, Tosfos, the Shulchan Aruch, and the Chofetz Chaim's own marriage, from Yevamos 21a.

marriage/marrying-an-older-woman.intro: May a man marry a woman older than himself? In [An Age-Old Question](/daf/bava-metzia/84/an-age-old-question), an eleven-year-old Michoel Ber Weissmandl answers before Rav Dushinsky by joining three Gemaras. Reish Lakish married Rebbe Yochanan's sister, as told on Bava Metzia 84a, and since Rebbe Yochanan was orphaned at birth his sister was older, while Reish Lakish was younger than Rebbe Yochanan.
marriage/marrying-an-older-woman.description: Is it fine for a man to marry a woman older than him? A young Michoel Ber Weissmandl proved it from Reish Lakish's marriage, told in Bava Metzia 84a.

marriage/marrying-for-money.intro: Rav teaches in Kiddushin 70a that one who marries a woman only for her money will have children who act wrongly, and the money will quickly be lost. The Rivash, quoted by the Rema, limits this to a woman of tainted lineage whom he would never otherwise consider. The Vilna Gaon disagrees and reads the Raavad as condemning anyone who walks away from a shidduch over money.
marriage/marrying-for-money.description: Is it wrong to choose a spouse for wealth? Rav's warning in Kiddushin 70a, and how the Rivash, Raavad and Vilna Gaon define marrying for money.

marriage/panim-chadashos-at-sheva-bracho.intro: On a weekday, Sheva Brachos are said only if a new guest is present to add to the joy of the chosson and kallah. In [Sheva Brachos Shailos](/daf/kesubos/8/sheva-brachos-shailos), tied to Kesubos 8, Rav Moshe Feinstein rules that a stranger counts if a parent knows him, and a Torah scholar always counts. The Shulchan Aruch and Rema disagree about whether he must eat, and Rav Elyashiv wanted him to eat bread.
marriage/panim-chadashos-at-sheva-bracho.description: Who counts as panim chadashos at a weekday Sheva Brachos, and must the new guest eat? Rav Moshe Feinstein and Rav Elyashiv rule, tied to Kesubos 8.

marriage/parental-support-in-shidduchim.intro: On a second date, a girl admits that her parents cannot give support: may the boy end the shidduch? The Vilna Gaon says he may not, though he could have chosen a girl with support before dating began, while the Chelkas Mechokeik seems to allow it if he has other suitable suggestions. Drawing on Kiddushin 70a, the Chasam Sofer says to follow the Vilna Gaon, since parnassah comes from Hashem.
marriage/parental-support-in-shidduchim.description: May one end a shidduch because the other family cannot provide support? The Vilna Gaon, Chelkas Mechokeik and Chasam Sofer, from Kiddushin 70a.

marriage/proposing-marriage-during-mourn.intro: At his wife's burial, Yosef HaKohen saw his young children left without a mother, so he asked his wife's sister to marry him and care for them, and she agreed at once. Moed Katan 23a says he acted properly, even as an onen. [A Forced Tumah](/daf/zevachim/100/a-forced-tumah) adds the Rishonim's view: it was done for the orphans, and the chuppah waited until mourning ended.
marriage/proposing-marriage-during-mourn.description: Yosef HaKohen proposed to his wife's sister on the day of her burial, for his orphans. Why Moed Katan 23a and Zevachim 100a say he acted with propriety.

marriage/sheva-brachos-in-a-restaurant.intro: A chosson and kallah eat in a hotel or restaurant where most diners are not part of the simcha. Can Sheva Brachos still be said? Tied to Kesubos 8, Rav Moshe Feinstein allows it if it is clear the meal honors the couple, for example with a head table, and the Sefer Sovaya Simchos suggests adding a special food in their honor.
marriage/sheva-brachos-in-a-restaurant.description: Can Sheva Brachos be said in a restaurant where most diners are not part of the simcha? Rav Moshe Feinstein's answer, in a discussion tied to Kesubos 8.

marriage/sheva-brachos-on-the-seventh-da.intro: The seven days of celebration begin when the blessings at the chuppah end, the Rema writes, but Rav Moshe Feinstein counts from the day of the meal if it began after sunset. How late on the seventh day may Sheva Brachos be said? Tied to Kesubos 8, Rav Elyashiv held not past sunset, while Rav Moshe allowed up to 40 minutes after sunset in New York.
marriage/sheva-brachos-on-the-seventh-da.description: How late on the seventh day may Sheva Brachos be said, and when do the days begin? Rav Elyashiv and Rav Moshe Feinstein differ, tied to Kesubos 8.

marriage/two-brothers-marrying-two-siste.intro: Rebbi Yehuda HaChassid wrote in his will that two brothers should not marry two sisters, one of several customs that still guide many families. But was the will meant only for his descendants, or for all of Klal Yisrael? [Cautionary Customs](/daf/menachos/29/cautionary-customs) explores that debate, which the Noda BeYehuda and others take up, alongside a story in Menachos 29b.
marriage/two-brothers-marrying-two-siste.description: Should two brothers avoid marrying two sisters? Rebbi Yehuda HaChassid's will and the debate over whom it binds, with a story from Menachos 29b.

marriage/using-an-egg-for-kiddushin.intro: A chassan forgets the ring and offers his kallah an egg under the chuppah: is she married? Only something worth a perutah works for kiddushin, and Tosfos say an egg once was worth that much. Tied to Kiddushin 60, the Rosh says that an item worth a perutah somewhere else in the world creates at least a rabbinic marriage.
marriage/using-an-egg-for-kiddushin.description: Could a groom who forgot the ring marry his bride with an egg? It depends on whether it is worth a perutah, says an article filed on Kiddushin 60.

marriage/value-of-a-perutah-today.intro: Kiddushin needs an item worth at least a perutah, the smallest ancient coin. Rabbi Yosef Sebrow estimated that its buying power today is around thirty cents, which would make a single egg too cheap. In [Egg-sploring the Halacha](/daf/kiddushin/60/egg-sploring-the-halacha), filed on Kiddushin 60, measuring by the price of silver puts a perutah at only a penny or two.
marriage/value-of-a-perutah-today.description: What is a single perutah worth today for kiddushin? Estimates based on buying power or the price of silver, from an article filed on Kiddushin 60.

marriage/weddings-on-motzei-shabbos-and-.intro: The Gemara in Kesubos 5 worries that someone preparing a wedding feast on Motzei Shabbos might forget it is Shabbos and start cooking. One answer limits the worry to a meal right after Shabbos, the other to a meal for many guests, and the Hafla'ah accepts both. Many Rishonim say the Gemara finally permits Motzei Shabbos and Sunday, and the Chasam Sofer himself married on a Sunday.
marriage/weddings-on-motzei-shabbos-and-.description: Is it a problem to marry on Motzei Shabbos or Sunday? The Gemara in Kesubos 5 fears Shabbos violation, yet many Rishonim and the custom permit it.

marriage/wife-keeping-her-own-minhagim.intro: A kallah's mother lit seven Shabbos lights plus one per child, while her chasan's family started with two, so whose minhag should she keep? Most customs follow the husband, but Shabbos lights are usually the wife's own mitzvah, and the Shevet HaLevi warns against strife. In this discussion on Shabbos 23, Rabbi Doniel Neustadt points to Rebbe Moshe Feinstein on hair coverings and to Rebbe Yaakov Emden's wife.
marriage/wife-keeping-her-own-minhagim.description: Does a wife follow her husband's minhag or her mother's for mitzvos she does herself, like Shabbos candles? Poskim weigh in, in an article on Shabbos 23.

marriage/yerushalayim-shel-zahav-crown.intro: In their first year of marriage, Rebbe Akiva and Rachel were so poor that they rested their heads on straw. According to the Maharsha, cited in the discussion of Nedarim 50a, she would pick the straw out of his hair, and in thanks he promised her a crown bearing the Yerushalayim skyline once he could afford it. The Ran says he kept that promise many years later.
marriage/yerushalayim-shel-zahav-crown.description: Rebbe Akiva promised his wife a golden crown with the Yerushalayim skyline in their years of poverty on straw. The story behind it in Nedarim 50a.

marriage/younger-sibling-marrying-first.intro: Must a younger sibling wait for an older one to marry first? Lavan told Yaakov that giving the younger before the elder was not done in his place, but Rav Moshe Feinstein points to Kiddushin 51b and concludes that this is a custom, not a halacha. In [Kiddushin Conundrum](/daf/kiddushin/52/kiddushin-conundrum), Rav Shmuel Auerbach tells a younger brother not to delay dating.
marriage/younger-sibling-marrying-first.description: Should a younger son or daughter wait for an older sibling to marry? Rav Moshe Feinstein reads Kiddushin 51b and calls it a custom, not halacha.

kesubah/father-in-law-guaranteeing-the-k.intro: When Rav Huna married, his wealthy father Moshe ben Itzri guaranteed the kesubah, yet he later let his son live in poverty. Bava Basra 174b tells how Abaye thought Rav Huna could divorce his wife so she could collect from her father-in-law, then remarry her. The plan fell apart when Abaye learned Rav Huna was a kohen, who may not remarry a divorced wife.
kesubah/father-in-law-guaranteeing-the-k.description: A father guaranteed his son's kesubah. Could the son divorce and remarry so his wife collects from him? Abaye's plan for Rav Huna, in Bava Basra 174b.

kesubah/replacing-a-lost-kesubah.intro: Rebbi Meir teaches in Kesubos 54b that a couple may not live together when the kesubah is reduced below the minimum, so the wife can feel secure. The same applies if the kesubah is lost, and the halacha follows him. A new kesubah with a special text must be written, and until then the husband can give collateral, as [Kesubah Conundrums](/daf/kesubos/54/kesubah-conundrums-kesubos-54) explains.
kesubah/replacing-a-lost-kesubah.description: What must a couple do if their kesubah is lost? Rebbi Meir in Kesubos 54b, the special replacement text and collateral until a new one is written.

kesubah/value-of-a-kesubah-in-dollars.intro: The basic 200 zuz of a kesubah equals 960 grams of silver, which the article on Kesubos 54b values at about $519. Rav Moshe Feinstein explains that Ashkenazim add 200 zekukim of silver to make it a real deterrent to divorce. The Vilna Gaon values that addition at about $31,000, while the Derisha puts it at only $2,077.
kesubah/value-of-a-kesubah-in-dollars.description: How much is a kesubah worth in dollars? The basic 200 zuz, the extra 200 zekukim and the views of the Vilna Gaon and the Derisha, from Kesubos 54b.

kesubah/what-makes-a-kesubah-invalid.intro: An invalid kesubah counts as no kesubah at all, following Rebbi Meir in Kesubos 54b. Two common problems are blank spaces, which should be lined through like a check, and cross-outs or words added between lines. Such changes should be noted at the end before the witnesses sign, and otherwise a rav should be asked.
kesubah/what-makes-a-kesubah-invalid.description: What can make a kesubah invalid? Blank spaces, cross-outs and words between lines, and how to note changes before the witnesses sign, from Kesubos 54b.

divorce/coerced-get.intro: A get given by a husband whom beis din compelled is valid, and a person can be forced to bring a korban he promised. Bava Basra 48 places these next to Rav Huna's ruling that a forced sale stands because the seller got paid. Tosfos asks what the husband received, and answers that fulfilling a mitzvah counts as his payment.
divorce/coerced-get.description: How can a get be valid if beis din forced the husband to give it? Tosfos explains, in Bava Basra 48, that fulfilling a mitzvah counts as his payment.

divorce/using-a-found-get.intro: A man finds a get in a pile of refuse with his name, his wife's name and their town on it. In Gittin 3b, Rebbi Meir says it is kosher if he has witnesses sign and gives it to her, since the writing need not be for this couple. Tosfos notes the past tense suggests this works only after the fact, while Rabbeinu Tam allows it from the start.
divorce/using-a-found-get.description: May a man use a get he found that was written for another couple with the same names? Rebbi Meir, Tosfos and Rabbeinu Tam debate lishmah in Gittin 3b.

divorce/who-may-write-a-get.intro: The Mishnah in Gittin 22b says anyone may write a get, even a cheiresh, shoteh or kattan. Tosfos asks how such a person can be the husband's agent, and concludes that the writer need not be his agent at all. The Chasam Sofer explains that when the Torah does not require the husband to act himself, he may ask anyone, though in practice a monkey still cannot write a get.
divorce/who-may-write-a-get.description: May anyone write a get, even someone not legally competent? The Mishnah in Gittin 22b, Tosfos and the Chasam Sofer on whether the writer is an agent.

yibbum-and-chalitzah/chalitzah-with-a-le.intro: Yevamos 104 is clear that at chalitzah, the yevama removes the shoe from the yavam's right foot. If the yavam is left-footed, there are four opinions: the left foot, the right foot, neither foot, or, as the Rashba suggests, both feet. The Rema says removing both shoes is the accepted custom, and some require them to come off at the same time.
yibbum-and-chalitzah/chalitzah-with-a-le.description: Which shoe comes off at chalitzah when the yavam is left-footed? The Tur, the Ramban, the Rashba and the Rema's custom of both feet, Yevamos 104.

chinuch/age-of-chinuch.intro: From what age must a parent train a child in mitzvos? The Ritva explains a case on Yevamos 114a as a child too young for chinuch, and the Mishnah Berurah writes that it depends on the child's understanding, so a child who knows about Shabbos should hear Kiddush and Havdalah. Rav Neuwirth adds that the earliest stage, with no understanding at all, lasts until about two or three.
chinuch/age-of-chinuch.description: At what age does chinuch begin? The Ritva on Yevamos 114a, the Mishnah Berurah on a child's understanding, and Rav Neuwirth's age of two or three.

chinuch/bar-mitzvah-boy-and-torah-mitzvo.intro: Everyone today relies on a chazakah that a boy who turns 13 has the physical signs of adulthood. The article on Nedarim 23 explains that the Mishnah Berurah limits this to rabbinic mitzvos: the boy may lein and lead davening, but should not blow shofar for the congregation or write tefillin parashiyos. Once his beard is full, or by 18 according to the Chayei Adam, he counts as an adult even for biblical mitzvos.
chinuch/bar-mitzvah-boy-and-torah-mitzvo.description: May a boy who just turned 13 blow shofar, make Kiddush for adults or write tefillin? The Mishnah Berurah on relying on his age, from Nedarim 23.

chinuch/bar-mitzvah-in-a-leap-year.intro: A boy born on the 8th of Adar in a regular year turns thirteen in a leap year with two Adars. The Rema rules that he becomes bar mitzvah in Adar Sheini, though Rav Elyashiv held he should be strict from Adar Rishon, starting tefillin then but not counting for a minyan until Adar Sheini. The article on Shekalim 2 also covers the Magen Avraham's surprising view for a boy born in Adar Rishon.
chinuch/bar-mitzvah-in-a-leap-year.description: When is a boy born in Adar bar mitzvah in a year with two Adars? The Rema, Rav Elyashiv and the Magen Avraham weigh in, in an article on Shekalim 2.

chinuch/bar-mitzvah-speech-in-shul.intro: Could a bar mitzvah boy dodge his pshetl by saying he must not turn his back on the Aron Kodesh? Building on Yoma 52b and the Shaarei Efraim's warning about speakers with the wrong motives, the Chelkas Yaakov thinks the argument has some merit. Still, he rules that the speech may be given, because the experience can stay with the boy and guide him for life.
chinuch/bar-mitzvah-speech-in-shul.description: May a bar mitzvah boy give his pshetl with his back to the Aron Kodesh? The Chelkas Yaakov weighs the Shaarei Efraim's warning, discussed with Yoma 52b.

chinuch/birchas-ilanos-before-bar-mitzva.intro: Should children be trained to say Birchas Ilanos, and should a boy turning thirteen in Nissan wait for his bar mitzvah? Rav Chaim Kanievsky said to train them and that the boy need not wait. He contrasted it with Kiddush Levana, an obligatory blessing, while nobody is required to go out and see a blossoming tree; whoever does see one says the beracha right then.
chinuch/birchas-ilanos-before-bar-mitzva.description: Should a boy turning thirteen in Nissan wait to say Birchas Ilanos? Rav Chaim Kanievsky explains why, unlike Kiddush Levana, he says it right away.

chinuch/born-on-the-thirtieth-of-adar-ri.intro: A boy born on the 30th of Adar Rishon faces a puzzle, because in a regular year Adar has only 29 days. The Steipler ruled that he becomes bar mitzvah on the first of Nissan, so his twin born minutes later on the first of Adar Sheini would be bar mitzvah a month earlier. In this discussion on Shekalim 2, the Shevus Yaakov rules that the one born first is still the older brother.
chinuch/born-on-the-thirtieth-of-adar-ri.description: When does a boy born on the 30th of Adar Rishon become bar mitzvah? The Steipler says the first of Nissan, in an article on Shekalim 2, with a twin twist.

chinuch/children-fasting-before-bar-mitz.intro: Chinuch trains children in mitzvos, but not through physical pain. Children may eat before davening and kiddush, and Rav Shlomo Zalman writes that there is no custom for children to fast before bar mitzvah, though holding back candy is fine and Yom Kippur brings a few hours of fasting. The point arises in an article on Bava Metzia 5a about late Havdalah.
chinuch/children-fasting-before-bar-mitz.description: Should children fast or lose sleep for mitzvos before bar mitzvah? Rav Shlomo Zalman says chinuch is not physical pain, in an article on Bava Metzia 5a.

chinuch/competition-among-torah-teachers.intro: Ezra decreed that one teacher may set up right next to another, even though they would compete for the same students. Why not fear that the stress would make them teach worse? The Gemara on Bava Basra 21 answers that rivalry among teachers increases wisdom, since each tries harder to attract students, and the students end up learning more.
chinuch/competition-among-torah-teachers.description: Why did Ezra let Torah teachers compete side by side? The Gemara in Bava Basra 21 teaches that rivalry among teachers increases wisdom for the students.

chinuch/encouraging-students-to-think.intro: Rebbe Akiva once said the halacha follows a student's flawed version of a teaching, and the Gemara explains he did so to sharpen his students' minds. The Gaon Yaakov says it praised the student's sharp reasoning, or tested whether the others would catch the mistake. In [Teaching Lessons From The Tanna’im](/daf/eruvin/13/teaching-lessons-from-the-tannaim), on Eruvin 13, Rebbe Meir argued tamei was tahor to stir his students.
chinuch/encouraging-students-to-think.description: How did Rebbe Akiva and Rebbe Meir push their students to think? Praising sharp reasoning and arguing the other side, as discussed on Eruvin 13.

chinuch/enthusiasm-for-mitzvos-in-chinuc.intro: The pasuk in Vayikra repeats the word tell when speaking to the kohanim, and the Gemara learns that adults must see that children keep the mitzvos. Rav Moshe Feinstein explains the double telling: one teaches what the mitzvah is, and the other shows how much the parent enjoys it. [The Key to Success in Chinuch](/daf/yevamos/114/the-key-to-success-in-chinuch) on Yevamos 114a makes the point that a parent's enthusiasm is contagious, while complaining discourages.
chinuch/enthusiasm-for-mitzvos-in-chinuc.description: How do parents pass on a love of mitzvos? Rav Moshe Feinstein on the double telling in Vayikra and why enthusiasm works, tied to Yevamos 114a.

chinuch/extravagant-bar-mitzvah-celebrat.intro: [Only In Omerica](/daf/sanhedrin/68/only-in-omerica) opens with bar and bat mitzvah parties costing up to a million dollars, from a ballroom turned purple to a band flown in from Israel. Rav Moshe Feinstein writes that he never saw good come from a fancy bar mitzvah and urged keeping them simple. The article, on Sanhedrin 68, adds that an extravagant affair may even make one forget to count the Omer.
chinuch/extravagant-bar-mitzvah-celebrat.description: Have bar mitzvah parties gone too far? Rav Moshe Feinstein urged simple celebrations, and an article on Sanhedrin 68 weighs the cost of extravagance.

chinuch/origin-of-jewish-elementary-scho.intro: Yehoshua ben Gamla, whose story runs through Yoma 18a, is remembered for good: Rav Yehuda says in the name of Rav that without him the Torah would have been forgotten. He set up teachers of young children in every province and town, bringing them in at six or seven. Rav Henoch Leibowitz reasoned that since this is a rabbinic institution, every place must be fit for a day school.
chinuch/origin-of-jewish-elementary-scho.description: Who founded Jewish elementary schools? Yehoshua ben Gamla's enactment of teachers in every town, which saved the Torah, in a look tied to Yoma 18a.

chinuch/picture-books-for-teaching-torah.intro: When Yonason ben Uziel translated Nevi'im, the Tosfos Rid writes, Heaven was displeased because people would no longer work hard to understand the verses. Tied to Megillah 3, Rav Moshe Feinstein used this to advise against funding a picture book that illustrated the Torah. Rav Henoch Leibowitz compared teaching to setting a treat just far enough away that an infant learns to walk.
chinuch/picture-books-for-teaching-torah.description: Do picture books help or hinder children's Torah learning? Rav Moshe Feinstein cites the Tosfos Rid on making students think, in a piece on Megillah 3.

chinuch/sensitivity-to-students-feelings.intro: Rav Alter Henoch Leibowitz often said American bachurim are as fragile as tissue paper, easily hurt if a rebbe does not smile at them. So he rarely rebuked anyone directly, giving a shmuess to the whole yeshiva instead, and once handed a bachur his own yarmulke in place of an unfitting one. [Our Rosh Yeshiva](/beyond-the-daf/our-rosh-yeshiva) gathers these moments, including his warning not to brush off someone who interrupts learning to talk.
chinuch/sensitivity-to-students-feelings.description: Why Rav Alter Henoch Leibowitz avoided direct rebuke, gave his yarmulke to a bachur, and taught rebbeim to guard the feelings of fragile students.

chinuch/standing-up-to-peer-pressure.intro: Kalev had a ruach acheres, and Sotah 34b tells how he went alone to Chevron to pray to be saved from the spies' plot. HaRav Avrohom Kanarek saw his own father in this: in Leipzig, neighbors mocked him for sending his boys to yeshiva instead of the family business. [The Power to Withstand the Pressure](/daf/sotah/34/the-power-to-withstand-the-pressure) shows how that courage saved their lives.
chinuch/standing-up-to-peer-pressure.description: Kalev stood apart from the spies, and a father in Leipzig chose yeshiva despite scorn. Sotah 34b on the courage to resist peer pressure for Torah.

chinuch/stopping-a-child-from-doing-an-a.intro: Rav Yitzchak bar Bisna lost the beis midrash keys in a public area on Shabbos, and Rebbe Pedas told him to let children play nearby, knowing one would carry them back. Yevamos 114a uses this to ask whether minors must be stopped from forbidden acts. The Rambam says an unrelated adult need not, but a father must, because of his mitzvah of chinuch.
chinuch/stopping-a-child-from-doing-an-a.description: Must an adult stop a young child from carrying on Shabbos? Rav Yitzchak bar Bisna's lost keys, the Rambam and the Ritva, all from Yevamos 114a.

chinuch/teaching-children-berachos.intro: The Shulchan Aruch permits teaching children brachos in their full form, even though the children say them in vain, and the Mishnah Berurah allows the rebbi to say Hashem's name too. The article on Nedarim 7b adds the Eishel Avraham's advice: if the child already knows the name, say only the first syllable and let him finish. Rav Moshe Feinstein likewise permitted it when teaching an adult ba'al teshuvah.
chinuch/teaching-children-berachos.description: May a parent or rebbi say Hashem's name while teaching a child a bracha? The Shulchan Aruch, Eishel Avraham and Rav Moshe Feinstein, on Nedarim 7b.

chinuch/teaching-children-to-teach-each-.intro: Rebbe Chiya would go to a town, teach five children one Chumash each and six more one order of Mishna each. On Bava Metzia 85b, he then told them to teach each other their portions until he returned. That way every child became both a student and a teacher, and Rebbe exclaimed how great Rebbe Chiya's deeds were.
chinuch/teaching-children-to-teach-each-.description: Rebbe Chiya taught each child one part of Torah and had them teach each other, so every student became a teacher, as told in Bava Metzia 85b.

chinuch/teaching-weaker-students.intro: Hillel had 80 students, and the one counted as the least of them, Rabban Yochanan ben Zakai, became the leader of Klal Yisrael and the link through whom our Torah comes down. Bava Basra 134a leads Rav Moshe Chait to ask what would have happened had Hillel taught only his brightest students. A camp archery coach who wins by training his weakest archers makes the same point.
chinuch/teaching-weaker-students.description: Why should a rebbe invest in every student, not just the brightest? Hillel's weakest student, Rabban Yochanan ben Zakai, led Klal Yisrael. Bava Basra 134a.

chinuch/value-of-raising-children.intro: Mothers might feel left out when men go out to conquer Eretz Yisrael while they stay home with the children. The Yalkut Yehudah notes that the ban on women bearing weapons sits next to shiluach ha'kan, where we may not take a bird caring for her young. Raising children is so precious to Hashem that mothers are not drafted, as the article on Nazir 59a teaches.
chinuch/value-of-raising-children.description: Why are mothers not drafted even to conquer Eretz Yisrael? The Yalkut Yehudah links raising children to shiluach ha'kan, from an article on Nazir 59a.

jewish-names/does-a-name-affect-destiny.intro: Does a person's name shape his life? A 1999 study found that men with positive initials lived longer, and the Gemara in Megillah says Haman was Memuchan, a name meaning prepared for punishment. Discussing Sanhedrin 10b, the Acharonim explain that Divine intervention led the advisers' mothers to give odd names that later recalled Klal Yisrael's merit.
jewish-names/does-a-name-affect-destiny.description: Does a name shape destiny? Haman as Memuchan, a study on initials and lifespan, and the hidden potential of odd names, in a discussion of Sanhedrin 10b.

jewish-names/marrying-someone-with-a-par.intro: Rebbi Yehuda HaChassid's will warns against marrying someone with the same name as one's parent. The Noda BeYehuda encouraged such a shidduch, and the D'var Moshe points to Rami bar Tamra in Menachos 29b, though the Shita Mekubetzes reads the text differently. The Minchas Elazar permits it when the names are not exactly the same, and the Yabea Omer quotes poskim who call it irrelevant for those over twenty.
jewish-names/marrying-someone-with-a-par.description: May one marry someone who shares a parent's name? The Noda BeYehuda, Minchas Elazar and Yabea Omer on a custom from a will, with Menachos 29b.

jewish-names/name-of-avraham-avinus-moth.intro: What was the name of Avraham Avinu's mother? Bava Basra 91a gives it as Amasla'i, the daughter of Karnevo, along with the names of Dovid HaMelech's mother and Shimshon's mother and sister. The Gemara says these names matter as a reply to the heretics, and the Shevet Mussar adds that Avraham's mother is remembered for hiding him from Nimrod.
jewish-names/name-of-avraham-avinus-moth.description: What were the names of the mothers of Avraham, Dovid and Shimshon? Bava Basra 91a records them, and the Shevet Mussar explains why one was preserved.

jewish-names/naming-a-child-after-a-rash.intro: The Gemara in Yoma says a child should not be given the name of a rasha, and the Toras Chaim suggests this applies only to real names, not to nicknames. [What’s In A Name?](/daf/eruvin/53/whats-in-a-name) connects this to the dispute in Eruvin 53 over whether Amrafel or Nimrod was the real name, and asks about modern people named Dathan, Nimrod and Omri.
jewish-names/naming-a-child-after-a-rash.description: May parents name a child after a rasha from Tanach, and does that include nicknames? The Toras Chaim and the Amrafel and Nimrod debate in Eruvin 53.

taharas-hamishpacha/filling-a-mikvah-wit.intro: The Shulchan Aruch rules that a mikvah filled with drawn water becomes kosher if it freezes and melts, because melted ice is like rain. When Omaha's only mikvah was drained by mistake during a drought, the community tried exactly that, hauling in more than a ton of ice. [The Iceman Cometh](/daf/pesachim/17/the-iceman-cometh) tells the story alongside Pesachim 17b, including the storm that made all the effort unnecessary.
taharas-hamishpacha/filling-a-mikvah-wit.description: Can melted ice fill a mikvah instead of rain? The Shulchan Aruch says yes, and Omaha tried it with a ton of ice during a drought. Pesachim 17b.

taharas-hamishpacha/minimum-size-of-a-mi.intro: On Pesachim 17b, Rav Papa says any gathering of water in the ground with about 3 ounces counts as a mikvah, yet Rashi notes that a mikvah needs 40 seah. Rashi explains that biblically 40 seah is needed for people, while a utensil only needs enough water to cover it at once. To avoid confusion, the rabbis required 40 seah for every mikvah, about 2 feet by 2 feet by 6 feet according to the Chazon Ish.
taharas-hamishpacha/minimum-size-of-a-mi.description: How much water must a mikvah hold? Forty seah for people, far less for utensils by Torah law, and why the rabbis set one size. Rashi on Pesachim 17b.

taharas-hamishpacha/rainwater-for-a-mikv.intro: Water drawn in a vessel, mayim sheuvim, cannot be used for a mikvah, at least for the first 40 seah, though Tosfos on Pesachim 17b says this rule is only rabbinic. The most common solution is to collect rainwater from the mikvah's roof and carry it to a holding pool through half-pipes. In Omaha, a storm of 1.37 inches refilled the pool, and the article even calculates how the roof captured enough rain.
taharas-hamishpacha/rainwater-for-a-mikv.description: Why do mikvaos collect rain from the roof instead of filling from a tap? Drawn water is invalid, a rule Tosfos on Pesachim 17b calls rabbinic.

adoption/adopted-son-called-to-the-torah.intro: May an adopted boy be called to the Torah by his adoptive father's name? [Marrying Meirav and Michal](/daf/sanhedrin/19/marrying-meirav-and-michal) shows how the answer grows from Sanhedrin 19b, where Meirav's sons are called Michal's because she raised them. Rav Moshe Feinstein, building on the Rema and the Vilna Gaon, permits it, but Rav Shlomo Zalman reportedly disagreed.
adoption/adopted-son-called-to-the-torah.description: May an adopted son be called up by his adoptive father's name? Rav Moshe Feinstein permits it from Sanhedrin 19b; Rav Shlomo Zalman reportedly disagreed.

adoption/raising-an-orphan-as-ones-own.intro: Why does the Navi call Meirav's five sons the children of Michal? Rebbe Yehoshua ben Korcha explains on Sanhedrin 19b that Michal raised them after Meirav died, and one who raises an orphan is regarded as having given birth to him. The Rema rules that a document may call a stepson a son, and the Vilna Gaon traces this to the Gemara.
adoption/raising-an-orphan-as-ones-own.description: One who raises an orphan is as if he gave birth to him. Michal and Meirav's sons on Sanhedrin 19b, and how the Rema applies it to legal documents.

ribbis/borrowing-groceries-from-a-neighb.intro: Chazal forbade lending consumable items, since prices can rise and the lender may profit, as Tosfos explains on Bava Metzia 75a. Hillel said a woman should not lend her friend a loaf of bread, but the halacha permits neighbors, who do not mind small price changes. In [Neither a Lender Nor a Borrower Be?](/daf/bava-metzia/75/neither-a-lender-nor-a-borrower-be), the Nesivos Shalom permits eggs, ketchup and sugar, items with a stable price.
ribbis/borrowing-groceries-from-a-neighb.description: May neighbors lend each other eggs, bread or sugar despite the ribbis rules? Tosfos, Hillel and the Nesivos Shalom weigh in, from Bava Metzia 75a.

ribbis/lending-with-interest-and-resurre.intro: Rabbi Akiva Eiger is said to have defended a steep burial fee for a man who lent with interest, since such a man would never rise at techiyas hameisim. A possible source is a Targum Yerushalmi that Tosfos quote on Bava Metzia 70b: one man of Ephraim missed Yechezkel's resurrection because he lent with interest. Tosfos explain that he lost a bonus, not that he was punished.
ribbis/lending-with-interest-and-resurre.description: Do those who lend with interest lose techiyas hameisim? A Rabbi Akiva Eiger story and a Targum quoted by Tosfos on Bava Metzia 70b explore it.

ribbis/repaying-a-loan-with-a-larger-ite.intro: If you borrow a loaf of bread, may you return one that is a little bigger? The Shulchan Aruch says no, but the Rema, who holds that neighbors are not exacting with each other, allows a slightly larger loaf or onion. The Mishnas Ribbis warns that a clear difference, like returning twelve eggs for eleven, is still ribbis, in a discussion of Bava Metzia 75a.
ribbis/repaying-a-loan-with-a-larger-ite.description: May you repay a borrowed loaf with a bigger one, or return a dozen eggs for eleven? The Rema and the Mishnas Ribbis draw the line, from Bava Metzia 75a.

ribbis/ribbis-devarim-verbal-interest.intro: A borrower may not even greet a lender he did not greet before the loan, and he surely may not bless him, because of ribbis devarim, verbal interest. Rav Shlomo Zalman Auerbach permits a simple thank you but not tizkeh l'mitzvos, a real blessing. [The Many Faces of “Shkoyach”: From a divine blessing at Har Sinai to a casual “thanks”— how a common colloquialism carries surprising weight in Jewish law](/daf/menachos/99/the-many-faces-of-shkoyach-from-a-divine-blessing-at-har-sinai-to-a-casual-thanks-how-a-common-colloquialism-carries-surprising-weight-in-jewish-law) asks about shkoyach, from Menachos 99b.
ribbis/ribbis-devarim-verbal-interest.description: May a borrower thank, greet or bless his lender? Ribbis devarim, Rav Shlomo Zalman on tizkeh l'mitzvos, and shkoyach, from an article on Menachos 99b.

ribbis/thanking-a-lender.intro: A borrower may not even greet his lender if he did not do so before the loan, so may he say thank you? Rav Shlomo Zalman Auerbach permits a plain thank you but forbids tizkeh l'mitzvos, which is a real blessing. [Shkoyach, Reb Noach](/daf/yevamos/62/shkoyach-reb-noach-yevamos-62) traces shkoyach to Hashem's words to Moshe on Yevamos 62a, and the Nesivos Shalom permits it when said without thinking of its meaning.
ribbis/thanking-a-lender.description: May a borrower thank his lender or say shkoyach? Verbal ribbis, Rav Shlomo Zalman Auerbach and the Nesivos Shalom, with Yevamos 62a on yeeshar kochachu.

loans/borrower-claiming-he-returned-an-i.intro: If something was lent without witnesses, the borrower is believed when he says he returned it. Rabba teaches this on Bava Basra 45a, but if witnesses saw the loan, he is not believed. [Purim Torah Rings True](/daf/bava-basra/45/purim-torah-rings-true) playfully applies this to Haman's claim that he returned the king's ring, and to Esther's answer that a known liar is not believed.
loans/borrower-claiming-he-returned-an-i.description: Is a borrower believed when he says he returned what he borrowed? Rabba's rule in Bava Basra 45a, and how witnesses to the loan change the answer.

loans/lenders-ownership-of-collateral.intro: Rebbi Yitzchak teaches that a creditor acquires the collateral he holds, and Rashi takes this to mean he is liable even for losses beyond his control. His proof is the pasuk that a borrower will bless the lender who returns his garment at night. Since a borrower may not bless his lender, that blessing must be like rent for the lender's own property, as the discussion around Yevamos 62a explains.
loans/lenders-ownership-of-collateral.description: Does a lender own the collateral he holds? Rebbi Yitzchak's proof from the borrower's blessing, Rashi on liability, and ribbis, tied to Yevamos 62a.

loans/repaying-loans-used-to-save-lives.intro: During the Holocaust, the Bobover Rebbe, Rav Shlomo Halberstam, borrowed to buy visas and papers, and after the war a lender demanded full repayment. Rav Moshe Feinstein ruled that loans used to save lives must be repaid. In [Stealing to Save a Life?](/daf/kesubos/19/stealing-to-save-a-life), on Kesubos 19a, he agreed the inflated value signed under duress might not be owed.
loans/repaying-loans-used-to-save-lives.description: Must money borrowed to save lives be fully repaid? The Bobover Rebbe's Holocaust-era loans and Rav Moshe Feinstein's ruling, discussed from Kesubos 19a.

loans/seizing-assets-for-a-creditor.intro: When a debtor cannot pay all his creditors, may an outsider grab assets for one of them? Rav Nachman allows it, but the halacha follows Rebbe Yochanan, who forbids it since the others lose out. Building on Gittin 11b, the article weighs Rashi's exception for an appointed agent, the Shach's view on a paid employee, and Tosfos's idea that one creditor may seize for another.
loans/seizing-assets-for-a-creditor.description: May someone seize a debtor's assets for one creditor when there isn't enough for all? Rav Nachman and Rebbe Yochanan, with Rashi and Tosfos, on Gittin 11b.

loans/unspecified-payment-toward-a-debt.intro: What happens when money is handed over without saying what it is for? When orphans in Kesubos 91b paid a creditor 50 zuz hoping to buy back their father's land, Abaye ruled that since they did not specify, the creditor could treat it as payment of the rest of the debt. The Ben Ish Chai applied the same rule to a ring given as ransom by a friend.
loans/unspecified-payment-toward-a-debt.description: If money is given without stating its purpose, may the receiver apply it to a debt? Abaye's ruling in Kesubos 91b and the Ben Ish Chai's ransom case.

loans/what-a-creditor-must-leave-a-debto.intro: When a debt is collected, some things must stay with the borrower. A beraisa on Bava Metzia 113b says he keeps two beds, one for eating and one for sleeping. Shmuel warns that sleeping right after a meal without walking a few steps is harmful, so Chazal treated the second bed as a necessity that nudges him to walk.
loans/what-a-creditor-must-leave-a-debto.description: What must a creditor leave a debtor? A beraisa says two beds, one for eating and one for sleeping, because of Shmuel's health advice, in Bava Metzia 113b.

damages/breaking-an-object-already-falli.intro: If someone throws a vase off a roof and another person smashes it in mid-air, Rabbah on Bava Kamma 17b says the second person is exempt, since the vase was already considered broken. But Tosfos says a window is not broken until the rock thrown at it actually hits. [Breaking Point](/daf/bava-kamma/17/breaking-point) explains the difference through the Bach and others.
damages/breaking-an-object-already-falli.description: Who pays if someone smashes a vase already falling from a roof? Rabbah in Bava Kamma 17b says it was already broken, but a target is a different case.

damages/damage-that-saved-a-life.intro: A pet snake bit a man, and the antivenom cured a deadly illness he did not know he had. Rav Zilberstein exempts the snake's owner and compares it to the fisherman of Menachos 64a, whose act saved a life. In [Dinim on Damages](/daf/bava-kamma/21/dinim-on-damages), the Mekor Chaim and Kinyan Torah argue over smashed liquor bottles that spared their owner a future arrest.
damages/damage-that-saved-a-life.description: Must you pay for damage that ended up saving the victim's life? Rav Zilberstein, the Mekor Chaim and Kinyan Torah, with a proof from Menachos 64a.

damages/damaging-a-rare-collectible.intro: Boruch owned the only two copies of a misprinted stamp, and Shimon accidentally tore one, making the other twice as valuable. The Shiltei Giborim learns from Bava Kamma 78b that Shimon need not pay, since we look at the whole picture of the loss, but the Shaar HaMishpat disagrees. [A Stamping Ground](/daf/bava-kamma/2/a-stamping-ground) reports that even Rav Zilberstein was unsure.
damages/damaging-a-rare-collectible.description: If you ruin one of two rare stamps and the other doubles in value, must you pay? The Shiltei Giborim and Shaar HaMishpat on Bava Kamma 78b disagree.

damages/destroying-property-in-wartime.intro: While fighting the Philistines, Dovid HaMelech wanted to destroy a private field where the enemy was hiding, but he was unsure whether that was allowed. Bava Kamma 61b tells how three warriors risked their lives to bring the question to the Sanhedrin. The Raavad prefers this reading, and Dovid also asked about paying for tools hidden in a burned haystack.
damages/destroying-property-in-wartime.description: May an army destroy a private field to save soldiers' lives? Dovid HaMelech's question about the Philistines and the field, in Bava Kamma 61b.

damages/digging-a-pit-in-a-public-area.intro: If someone digs a pit in a public street and an ox falls in and dies, he must pay. Bava Kamma 7 brings a dispute: Rav says the digger pays only for harm from the pit's noxious air, while Shmuel adds damage from the impact. In [Of Cats, Cattle, and Craters](/daf/bava-kamma/7/of-cats-cattle-and-craters), Rabbeinu Peretz explains why even broken bones are blamed on the fumes.
damages/digging-a-pit-in-a-public-area.description: Is a pit digger liable for damage from fumes or from impact too? Rav and Shmuel argue, and Rabbeinu Peretz explains Rashi's question, in Bava Kamma 7.

damages/diverting-floodwater-to-a-neighb.intro: May someone build barriers to keep floodwater off his land if the water will then flood his neighbor? Rav Elchanan Wasserman says yes, since he is only protecting what is his, but once his property is already flooded, the Yerushalmi says he may not pour the water out toward the neighbor. Rav Elchanan uses this to explain a deathbed gift on Bava Basra 145.
damages/diverting-floodwater-to-a-neighb.description: May you block floodwater from your land if it then floods a neighbor, or pump it out once it arrives? Rav Elchanan Wasserman's view, from Bava Basra 145.

damages/goring-ox-liability.intro: An ox that gores pays half damages the first three times, and full damages from the fourth. Rebbe Yehuda says the three gorings must be on three different days, while Rebbe Meir says three in one day count even more. The halacha follows Rebbe Yehuda, yet Rebbe Meir's logic, discussed with Bava Kamma 15b, is applied elsewhere in halacha.
damages/goring-ox-liability.description: When is an ox a habitual gorer, owing full damages? Rebbe Yehuda requires three separate days; Rebbe Meir disagrees. Discussed with Bava Kamma 15b.

damages/indirect-damage-liability.intro: Must someone who causes harm only indirectly pay for it? Bava Kamma 47a shows that a man who throws toxic walnuts to a neighbor's dog cannot be forced to pay when it dies, since the animal ate them on its own, unlike someone who shoots the dog directly. Beis din would still tell him that paying is the right thing to do, though it cannot enforce it.
damages/indirect-damage-liability.description: Do you owe for harm you caused only indirectly? Beis din tells you to pay but cannot force it, as Bava Kamma 47a shows with a neighbor's poisoned dog.

damages/learning-nezikin-for-protection.intro: The Chasam Sofer teaches that studying Seder Nezikin, the laws of damages, can protect a person from real physical or financial harm. A harsh decree can be fulfilled through the learning instead of actual damage. [Understanding The Gravity Of The Situation](/daf/bava-kamma/17/understanding-the-gravity-of-the-situation) opens with this thought while learning Bava Kamma 17b.
damages/learning-nezikin-for-protection.description: Can learning the laws of damages protect you from harm? The Chasam Sofer says studying Seder Nezikin can take the place of real loss. From Bava Kamma 17b.

damages/liability-for-accidental-damage.intro: The very first Mishna in Bava Kamma 2 lists man among the four main categories of damagers. From this comes the phrase "Adam muad l'olam": a person is always responsible for damage he causes, even completely by accident. When Shimon tore a friend's rare stamp while admiring it, saying it was an accident did not free him from paying.
damages/liability-for-accidental-damage.description: Are you liable for damage you cause completely by accident? Adam muad l'olam: a person always pays, as the first Mishna in Bava Kamma 2 teaches.

damages/liability-for-escaped-wild-anima.intro: When a circus lion escaped in Italy, its keeper said it was tame, while the mayor told people to stay home. Bava Kamma 15b records a dispute about whether a predator can be domesticated. Tosfos holds the owner would not pay if the lion ate a pet, but the Vilna Gaon notes that the Rambam and Shulchan Aruch rule the owner is liable.
damages/liability-for-escaped-wild-anima.description: Must the owner pay if his escaped lion causes damage? Tosfos says no, but the Rambam and Shulchan Aruch say yes. The discussion starts from Bava Kamma 15b.

damages/liability-for-fire-damage.intro: Is a fire like property its owner failed to guard, or like an arrow he shot? Reish Lakish and Rebbe Yochanan disagree on Bava Kamma 60b, and Rebbe Yochanan says "Isho mishum chitzo": a person who lights a destructive fire is liable as if he shot an arrow, even for damage far away. The Nemukei Yosef adds that all the burning is counted at the moment the fire is lit.
damages/liability-for-fire-damage.description: Is someone who lights a fire liable like one who shoots an arrow? Rebbe Yochanan and Reish Lakish disagree about fire damage in Bava Kamma 60b.

damages/ox-that-gores-only-on-shabbos.intro: The Mishna on Bava Kamma 37a speaks of an ox that gores only on Shabbos. Rashi says a Jewish-owned ox has the day off and is more restless. Tosfos quotes a Yerushalmi that everyone looks like a stranger in Shabbos clothing, and [It Looks Like Shabbos](/daf/bava-kamma/37/it-looks-like-shabbos) tells how Rebbe Meir Simcha used this to explain why a baby refused to nurse on Shabbos.
damages/ox-that-gores-only-on-shabbos.description: Why would an ox gore only on Shabbos? Rashi says it rests that day; a Yerushalmi says people in Shabbos clothes look like strangers. From Bava Kamma 37a.

damages/paying-for-sentimental-value.intro: When someone damages an item, does he pay what it means to the owner, or what it would sell for? A posek ruled that a damaged used metal candlestick called for only a small payment, despite its sentimental value. A rare stamp is different, since collectors would pay for it, as the stamp case discussed with Bava Kamma 2 shows.
damages/paying-for-sentimental-value.description: Do damages cover sentimental value or only market value? A used family candlestick versus a collectible stamp, in a case discussed with Bava Kamma 2.

damages/poisoning-a-neighbors-animal.intro: One may not deliberately poison a neighbor's animal, and beis din would stop someone who tried. But if the animal dies from eating what he threw, beis din cannot force him to pay, because the harm was indirect. [Poison Pills](/daf/bava-kamma/56/poison-pills), filed on Bava Kamma 56, tells of a dog in Italy fed toxic walnuts by a neighbor.
damages/poisoning-a-neighbors-animal.description: What if someone feeds a neighbor's dog poison? Beis din would stop him, but cannot force payment for indirect harm. A case filed on Bava Kamma 56.

damages/shepherd-liability-for-predator-.intro: A shepherd steps away and a wolf eats a sheep, so is he liable? Bava Metzia 106 asks whether he could have fought off the wolf had he been there. Rav Sheishes asks why we do not consider a miracle like Dovid HaMelech's, and the Gemara answers that a deserving owner would get a miracle even without the shepherd, as Rebbe Chanina ben Dosa did.
damages/shepherd-liability-for-predator-.description: Must a shepherd who left his flock pay for a sheep a wolf ate? Bava Metzia 106 asks if he could have fought it off and whether a miracle counts.

damages/splitting-a-ransom-paid-to-bandi.intro: When bandits attack a caravan and the travelers pay them off, who pays how much? Bava Kamma 116b says the cost is divided by how much money each traveler has, but if the bandits came to kill, the payment is split evenly, since every person's life is worth the same. [Gold Overboard](/daf/bava-kamma/116/gold-overboard) uses this to argue about a sinking ship.
damages/splitting-a-ransom-paid-to-bandi.description: How do travelers split the cost of paying off bandits? By wealth if robbers want money, evenly if lives are at risk, as Bava Kamma 116b explains.

damages/throwing-cargo-overboard-to-save.intro: When a storm forces passengers to lighten the ship, does each one lose an equal value, or an equal weight? Rashi on Bava Kamma 116b says everyone throws off the same weight, so 100 pounds of gold goes along with 100 pounds of copper. The Rema and Aruch HaShulchan then argue whether one passenger can force another to throw more.
damages/throwing-cargo-overboard-to-save.description: When cargo must be thrown off a sinking ship, is the loss shared by weight or by value? Rashi on Bava Kamma 116b says by weight, even gold beside copper.

theft-and-robbery/asking-forgiveness-aft.intro: Once a thief has paid back what he took, must he still ask forgiveness? The Rambam says someone who damages property need not ask after paying, but a thief must. In [A Superbowl Stumper](/daf/bava-kamma/96/a-superbowl-stumper), a man who hid a friend's ticket, based on Bava Kamma 96, argues he never meant to gain from it, which makes him a damager rather than a thief.
theft-and-robbery/asking-forgiveness-aft.description: Must a thief who already paid still ask forgiveness? The Rambam treats theft and damage differently, and a hidden ticket tests it, Bava Kamma 96.

theft-and-robbery/borrowers-who-never-re.intro: A guest walks out with an item, the homeowner shouts that he stole it, and the guest says he bought it, and we believe the guest, since outright theft is unlikely. But if the homeowner says he only lent it, we believe the homeowner. In [Impulse Purchases](/daf/shevuos/45/impulse-purchases), the Nesivos explains with the Gemara on Shevuos 46 that people find it easy to keep borrowed things.
theft-and-robbery/borrowers-who-never-re.description: Why is a homeowner believed when he says an item was lent, not stolen? The Nesivos on people who never return what they borrow, from Shevuos 46.

theft-and-robbery/eating-stolen-food-unk.intro: A father of the bride grabbed the wrong food from the caterer, served it at the wedding, and then asked each guest to pay. Rav Chisda says the owner can collect from the thief or from whoever ate the food. [Stolen Wedding Food](/daf/bava-kamma/111/stolen-wedding-food), filed on Bava Kamma 111, adds the Baal HaMaor, Tosfos, the Shita Mekubetzes and the Machne Efraim on whether a guest who didn't know must pay.
theft-and-robbery/eating-stolen-food-unk.description: Must a guest pay for stolen food he ate without knowing? Rav Chisda, the Baal HaMaor and the Shita Mekubetzes weigh in, in a case filed on Bava Kamma 111.

theft-and-robbery/paying-for-benefit-rec.intro: Even if a guest is not liable for eating stolen food, must he still pay for the benefit he got? Halacha says one pays for benefit gained at someone else's expense. But the benefit is measured by what he actually saved, not the food's price, and Rabbi Zilberstein says on Bava Kamma 111 that an invited guest may have saved nothing at all.
theft-and-robbery/paying-for-benefit-rec.description: Must you pay for benefiting from someone else's property, and how much? Measuring the benefit, not the price, in a wedding case filed on Bava Kamma 111.

theft-and-robbery/returning-a-stolen-ite.intro: Can a thief hand back the exact ticket he took after the game is over, the way the Mishnah lets him return chometz that became forbidden over Pesach? With coins that are no longer legal tender, Rav Yehuda says he may not, since anyone can see they are worthless, and Rav Huna disagrees. The Shulchan Aruch follows Rav Yehuda and the Rema follows Rav Huna, in Bava Kamma 96.
