minhagim/following-the-customs-of-our-fa.description: Why should we keep the customs of past generations? Yitzchak kept his father's names for the wells, and Rabbeinu Bachye's lesson, from Nedarim 12.

minhagim/haircut-on-rosh-chodesh.intro: Many avoid taking a haircut or shaving on Rosh Chodesh, a custom that comes from the will of Rebbi Yehuda HaChassid. The Mishna Berura writes that some places have this custom because he commanded them so. The article on Menachos 29b reads that wording as a sign that someone without a family custom has no obligation to keep it.
minhagim/haircut-on-rosh-chodesh.description: Why do some avoid haircuts on Rosh Chodesh, and must everyone? The Mishna Berura on Rebbi Yehuda HaChassid's will, from an article on Menachos 29b.

minhagim/keeping-customs-without-a-clear.intro: When the Nachalas Shiva ruled against a custom in Ashkenaz, Rav Chanoch Segal of Vienna wrote a fiery defense of minhagim. He described elders who would give their lives for a custom even without a clear basis, since customs are many people's strongest link to Yiddishkeit. The article filed on Gittin 33 opens with the Chasam Sofer's play on the words Minhag Yisrael, Torah hee.
minhagim/keeping-customs-without-a-clear.description: Why do communities guard old customs even when their source is unclear? Rav Chanoch Segal of Vienna defends minhagim in Ashkenaz, in a piece on Gittin 33.

minhagim/no-mirrors-in-chassidic-wedding.intro: Many chassidishe wedding halls have no mirrors in the men's restrooms, and the source goes back to Avodah Zarah 29a. Tosfos and the Shulchan Aruch forbid a man to look in a mirror except for a haircut or a medical need, while the Rema permits it where men are used to doing so. Chassidim may follow the stricter view to copy the Torah scholars the Ran describes, and Rav Yonason Eibshitz warns against mirrors for kabbalistic reasons.
minhagim/no-mirrors-in-chassidic-wedding.description: Why do many chassidic wedding halls have no mirrors in the men's rooms? The stricter view of Tosfos and the Shulchan Aruch from Avodah Zarah 29a explains.

minhagim/origin-of-the-kitniyos-custom.intro: Rebbe Yochanan ben Nuri treats rice like grain in Pesachim 35a, but Rav Huna ate cooked rice on Pesach. Rabbeinu Yerucham called avoiding kitniyos a foolish custom, while Rabbeinu Peretz said an ancient minhag should not be dismissed lightly. The Shulchan Aruch permits kitniyos, and the Rema, whom Ashkenazim follow, forbids it.
minhagim/origin-of-the-kitniyos-custom.description: Where does the kitniyos custom come from? Pesachim 35a, Rabbeinu Yerucham and Rabbeinu Peretz, and the split between the Shulchan Aruch and the Rema.

minhagim/tikkun-after-shacharis.intro: After Shacharis, some put out liquor, herring and cake, called tikkun, in memory of a loved one, though Megillah 28a forbids eating and drinking in shul. Rav Moshe Feinstein writes that the leniency of the Rashba and Ramban for a need would not cover tikkun, since it is not a mitzvah. He concludes that shuls allowing it must rely on Rashi and the Ohr Zarua.
minhagim/tikkun-after-shacharis.description: May tikkun of liquor and cake be served in the shul after Shacharis? Rav Moshe Feinstein weighs the Rashba, Ramban and Rashi, from Megillah 28a.

minhagim/weddings-in-the-first-half-of-t.intro: The Rema records a custom to marry only in the first half of the month, while the moon is growing, rather than when it wanes. The article on Kesubos 2a cites the Zohar that Divine mercy is stronger in the first half of the month and judgment in the second. The Sefer Chazon Yeshayah suggests this custom is why the poskim did not insist on Wednesday weddings, since too few dates would remain.
minhagim/weddings-in-the-first-half-of-t.description: Why do some marry only in the first half of the Jewish month? The Rema's custom, the Zohar on mercy and judgment, and its effect on dates, from Kesubos 2a.

minhagim/writing-birthdates-in-seforim.intro: Many families in Europe had the custom of writing a child's name and birthdate inside the father's seforim. In a playful dialogue tied to Kiddushin 63b, a boy whose gabbai doubts his bar mitzvah finds this note in his father's Mikraos Gedolos. The Taz ruled that writing in a father's seforim can be relied on to show which son is the firstborn, even for inheritance.
minhagim/writing-birthdates-in-seforim.description: Can a birthdate written in a father's sefer prove a boy's bar mitzvah? The Taz relied on such writing for a firstborn, in a dialogue on Kiddushin 63b.

mesorah/decline-of-the-generations.intro: A question troubled Rabbah and Rav Yosef for 22 years, and Tosfos asks why they did not simply drop a postulate that clashed with a Mishnah. The answer is that Rabbah received it from his teachers, who surely knew the Mishnah too. Since earlier generations understood Torah more deeply, he chose to live with the question, as the article on Nedarim 12 explains.
mesorah/decline-of-the-generations.description: Why did Rabbah live with an unanswered question for 22 years rather than reject his teachers? Tosfos on the decline of the generations, from Nedarim 12.

mesorah/innovation-versus-tradition-in-j.intro: The Chovos HaLevavos warns not to stray from the path of earlier generations, since their plans were already weighed. Yet in Chullin 6b, Chizkiyahu destroyed the copper snake that his righteous ancestors had left standing. [Serpentine Path to Prominence](/daf/chullin/6/serpentine-path-to-prominence) concludes that a talmid chacham who finds new ideas truly needed may proceed, as with the Mussar and Chassidic movements.
mesorah/innovation-versus-tradition-in-j.description: When may one depart from the path of earlier generations? The Chovos HaLevavos warns against change, yet Chizkiyahu acted alone. From Chullin 6b.

mesorah/mesorah-for-kosher-animals.intro: Does a mammal with split hooves that chews its cud still need a tradition? The Shach says we eat no animal without a mesorah, while the Pri Megadim says mammal signs are simple, so a new species is treated as a doubtful chaya. The Chochmas Adam and Chazon Ish forbid it outright, and Rav Shlomo Miller explains why, building on Chullin 45a.
mesorah/mesorah-for-kosher-animals.description: Does an animal with both kosher signs still need a mesorah? The Shach, the Pri Megadim, the Chazon Ish and Rav Shlomo Miller, building on Chullin 45a.

mesorah/mesorah-for-kosher-birds.intro: The Torah lists only 24 forbidden birds, so every other bird should be kosher. But since we can no longer identify those 24 species, the Rema rules that we eat only birds with an accepted tradition. In [Birds of a Feather: The Great Chicken Controversies](/daf/chullin/47/birds-of-a-feather-the-great-chicken-controversies), this reverses the rule that held at Sinai, in a discussion tied to Chullin 47.
mesorah/mesorah-for-kosher-birds.description: Why do we eat only birds with a mesorah, though most species are not on the forbidden list? The Rema's safeguard and the Chasam Sofer, from Chullin 47.

semichah/semichah-under-roman-decree.intro: After the Bar Kochva revolt, Rome decreed death for anyone who gave or received semichah, and ruin for the town that hosted it. In [No Ordinary Ordination](/daf/sanhedrin/92/no-ordinary-ordination), the Gemara in Sanhedrin 14a tells how Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava ordained five great students between Usha and Shafram. When soldiers came, he stayed behind to block them so the chain of semichah would go on.
semichah/semichah-under-roman-decree.description: How did semichah survive Hadrian's ban? Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava ordained the next generation's leaders and gave his life to save them, in Sanhedrin 14a.

machlokes/anonymous-mishnah-with-two-opi.intro: On Bava Metzia 41a, one unsigned Mishnah seems to follow Rebbe Yishmael in one law and Rebbe Akiva in the very next. Rebbe Yochanan accepts this and says he would carry the clothing of anyone who could explain it all as one view. The Sefer Chemda Genuza tells how Rebbe Heschel claimed he could, and paid a price for his boast.
machlokes/anonymous-mishnah-with-two-opi.description: Can one anonymous Mishnah follow two opposing Tannaim? Rebbe Yochanan says yes and dares anyone to explain it otherwise, in Bava Metzia 41a.

machlokes/letting-someone-win-an-argumen.intro: Sometimes you can prove the other side wrong and should still let it go. In [Happy Accidents](/daf/bava-kamma/88/happy-accidents), Rav Chisda asks Rabbah not to tell the students about his mistake, on Bava Kamma 88b. Rav Henoch Leibowitz once found his view backed by a great Acharon, yet never told the other gedolim, so he would not seem to gloat.
machlokes/letting-someone-win-an-argumen.description: When is it better to stop arguing and let another keep his view? Rav Chisda asks Rabbah to keep his error quiet, in Bava Kamma 88b, and others follow.

machlokes/oven-of-achnai.intro: Rebbe Eliezer called on a carob tree, a canal and the beis midrash walls to prove his view about an oven, and each one moved, yet the Sages rejected the miracles. In [A Halachic Argument](/daf/bava-metzia/59/a-halachic-argument), the Maharsha on Bava Metzia 59b reads each sign as a real argument, with the slow-growing carob and the canal flowing uphill. Rav Gestetner explains why he said this carob tree.
machlokes/oven-of-achnai.description: A carob tree, a canal and leaning walls tried to prove Rebbe Eliezer right. The Maharsha explains each sign in the famous oven dispute of Bava Metzia 59b.

chumros/chumros-at-others-expense.intro: Rav Dovid Feinstein did not rely on mechiras chametz for real chametz, and he even avoided buying chametz after Pesach from stores that used the sale. Yet one year he bought fresh challos at a Jewish bakery that had been closed for nine days, asking how he could deny them parnassah. A personal chumrah should not come at the cost of a local business; the sale itself is discussed in [Chametz for Sale](/daf/avodah-zarah/63/chametz-for-sale) on Avodah Zarah 63b.
chumros/chumros-at-others-expense.description: Should a personal chumrah hurt a small local store? Rav Dovid Feinstein's approach to chametz after Pesach, with mechiras chametz from Avodah Zarah 63b.

chumros/mocking-others-stringencies.intro: Choosing not to take on a chumrah is one thing, and ridiculing someone else's is another. Rav Mattisyahu Solomon cited Rabbeinu Yonah that mocking another person's care in mitzvos, even without insulting the person, can lead toward heresy. In [Skipping Steps or Grabbing Dessert?](/daf/chullin/105/skipping-steps-or-grabbing-dessert), this caution closes a discussion of Chullin 105a.
chumros/mocking-others-stringencies.description: Is it harmful to mock someone else's chumros? Rav Mattisyahu Solomon cites Rabbeinu Yonah on scorning stringencies. A warning tied to Chullin 105a.

chumros/pesach-chumros-versus-halacha.intro: By the letter of the law, some hidden chametz may stay where it is over Pesach. Yet the Piskei Teshuvos notes that the nashim tzidkaniyos of Klal Yisrael would never use a mixer with visible chametz, and the Shulchan Aruch even records scraping walls. The article on Bava Metzia 42a stresses telling halacha from minhag, since chumros sometimes must yield to pressing needs.
chumros/pesach-chumros-versus-halacha.description: Which Pesach cleaning is required and which is a cherished chumra? The Piskei Teshuvos separates halacha from custom, in an article on Bava Metzia 42a.

chumros/taking-on-stringencies.intro: Mar Ukva in Chullin 105a said he was like vinegar compared to his father, who waited a full day after meat. Why not just wait longer? Rav Yisrael Salanter compared growth to a meal served in order, and [Beyond The Letter Of The Law](/daf/chullin/105/beyond-the-letter-of-the-law) brings Rav Henoch Leibowitz's warning that a chumrah above one's level can breed falsehood and arrogance.
chumros/taking-on-stringencies.description: Should you take on chumros beyond your spiritual level? Rav Yisrael Salanter and Rav Henoch Leibowitz on growing step by step, from Chullin 105a.

chumros/when-extra-piety-leads-astray.intro: The Rashbam always kept his eyes lowered out of humility, and so he almost stepped into a wagon with a forbidden mixed team. His brother Rabbeinu Tam stopped him and warned, "Don't be a big tzaddik!" [Of Mules and Mussar](/daf/bava-basra/133/of-mules-and-mussar) explains, through Rav Nosson Gestetner and Bava Basra 133b, why the Rashbam felt he could rely on Heavenly protection and why his brother disagreed.
chumros/when-extra-piety-leads-astray.description: Can a pious habit make someone miss a real halachic problem? Rabbeinu Tam warns the Rashbam not to be a big tzaddik, a story tied to Bava Basra 133b.

beis-hamikdash/airspace-of-the-beis-hami.intro: Zevachim 87b asks whether the air above the Mizbeach shares its holiness, and leaves it unresolved. The Lechem Mishneh says the Rambam resolves it from other Gemaras, while the Divrei Chaim says the real question is whether limbs held above count as placed down. [Something In The Air](/daf/zevachim/87/something-in-the-air-2018) adds the Beis Shlomo: a barrier in between stops the holiness.
beis-hamikdash/airspace-of-the-beis-hami.description: Does the air above the Mizbeach share its holiness? Zevachim 87b leaves it open, and the Divrei Chaim, Rambam and Beis Shlomo each read it differently.

beis-hamikdash/aliyah-leregel.intro: The first Mishnah in Chagigah 2 says everyone must go up to the Beis HaMikdash on the festivals, except those listed. Tosfos notes that the Gemara exempts some workers, such as a tanner, whom the Mishnah never lists. So every rule has unlisted exceptions, and owning land in Eretz Yisrael might be one more requirement.
beis-hamikdash/aliyah-leregel.description: Who must make the pilgrimage to the Beis HaMikdash on the festivals? Tosfos on exemptions the Mishnah never lists, like the tanner. From Chagigah 2.

beis-hamikdash/bamah-altars.intro: Before the Beis HaMikdash there were private altars and public altars, and a Mishnah says even a Yisrael could serve on a private one. The Minchas Avraham, based on the Meshech Chochmah, says the need for a bechor applied only to a public altar. Avraham and Noach still needed it, the discussion of Zevachim 112 explains, because they offered on the future site of the Beis HaMikdash.
beis-hamikdash/bamah-altars.description: Who could serve on the private and public altars before the Beis HaMikdash? The Minchas Avraham on why the Temple site mattered, from Zevachim 112.

beis-hamikdash/bird-deterrent-on-the-bei.intro: The kalya orev was a device that kept ravens and other birds off the roof of the Beis Hamikdash. In [The Mystery of the Kalya Orev: Avian Architecture in the Beis Hamikdash](/daf/menachos/107/the-mystery-of-the-kalya-orev-avian-architecture-in-the-beis-hamikdash), Menachos 107a sets off a debate: the Aruch says it was a plate with a frightening image, Rashi says iron spikes, and Rabbeinu Gershom says the roof was sloped with a small flat peak.
beis-hamikdash/bird-deterrent-on-the-bei.description: What was the kalya orev on the roof of the Beis Hamikdash? Rashi, the Aruch and Rabbeinu Gershom debate spikes, plates and a sloped roof in Menachos 107a.

beis-hamikdash/collection-boxes-in-the-b.intro: The Beis HaMikdash had collection boxes called shofros, narrow on top and wide at the bottom, so giving was easy and stealing was hard. Chizkiya says in Shekalim 6 that six of them all paid for extra communal olos when the Mizbeach was idle. [Six Collection Boxes and Sunny Days](/daf/shekalim/18/six-collection-boxes-and-sunny-days) explains why one box for each weekday kept the kohanim from feeling cheated.
beis-hamikdash/collection-boxes-in-the-b.description: Why did the Beis HaMikdash have six shofar-shaped boxes for extra communal offerings? Chizkiya's answer in Shekalim 6 and the kohanim's weekday shifts.

beis-hamikdash/finding-the-site-of-the-b.intro: Zevachim 54b tells how Dovid HaMelech, with Shmuel HaNavi, found the place destined for the Beis HaMikdash, and how Doeg was jealous. In [Sleeping Duty](/daf/zevachim/54/sleeping-duty), Rabbi Henoch Moshe Levin explains that Doeg had long searched for this secret himself. Dovid succeeded through his vow not to rest until he found it.
beis-hamikdash/finding-the-site-of-the-b.description: How did Dovid HaMelech find the site of the Beis HaMikdash, and why was Doeg so jealous? His vow not to rest until he found it, as told in Zevachim 54b.

beis-hamikdash/fruit-tree-wood-on-the-mi.intro: The Mishna in Tamid says the kohanim liked to use branches of fig and nut trees for the wood on the mizbeach, which seems to clash with the ban on cutting fruit trees. The Mishneh L'melech says cutting branches was never forbidden, while the Be'er Sheva says a mitzvah counts as a constructive purpose. The question is raised alongside the discussion in Bava Kamma 91b.
beis-hamikdash/fruit-tree-wood-on-the-mi.description: Why did kohanim burn fig and nut wood on the mizbeach? The Mishneh L'melech and Be'er Sheva weigh the ban on cutting fruit trees, with Bava Kamma 91b.

beis-hamikdash/going-up-on-har-habayis.intro: Some people immerse in a mikveh and then go up on Har HaBayis, since a tamei meis may enter the outer area. [Still Sacred](/daf/zevachim/107/still-sacred) lists the problems: no one knows exactly where the Beis HaMikdash stood, and onlookers may copy them without knowing the rules. The Steipler, Rav Shach and Dayan Weiss forbade it, and Rav Herschel Schachter adds that the Rabbanut must be heeded, in a discussion of Zevachim 107.
beis-hamikdash/going-up-on-har-habayis.description: May Jews go up on Har HaBayis today after immersing? Why the Steipler, Rav Shach and Rav Schachter say no, in a discussion growing out of Zevachim 107.

beis-hamikdash/holiness-of-the-temple-si.intro: Zevachim 107 records a dispute: Rebbe Yochanan says offering a korban outside the Beis HaMikdash still brings kareis even after the churban, while Reish Lakish says it does not. The Gemara ties this to whether the site kept its holiness. The Rambam rules like Rebbe Yochanan, and the Mishnah Berurah writes that the sanctity was for its time and for the future.
beis-hamikdash/holiness-of-the-temple-si.description: Did the site of the Beis HaMikdash keep its holiness after the churban? Rebbe Yochanan and Reish Lakish argue in Zevachim 107, and the Rambam rules.

beis-hamikdash/kedushah-of-the-kosel-tod.intro: Rashi on Avodah Zarah 52b says the vessels of the Beis HaMikdash lost their kedushah when idolaters broke in. Does that apply to the Kosel? The Rogatchover says the lesser sanctity of the Second Beis HaMikdash could not be profaned that way, and Rav Moshe Feinstein adds that the Kosel was never overrun and the Shechinah never left it.
beis-hamikdash/kedushah-of-the-kosel-tod.description: Did the Kosel lose its holiness when the Beis HaMikdash fell? The Rogatchover and Rav Moshe say Rashi's rule in Avodah Zarah 52b does not apply to it.

beis-hamikdash/keeping-a-stone-from-the-.intro: A man was allowed to take a small stone fragment from a dig near the Kosel, but may he keep it? [When Less Is Too Much](/daf/bechoros/15/when-less-is-too-much) brings Rav Moshe Feinstein, who rejects using Rashi on Avodah Zarah 52b to permit it and says displaying it is forbidden benefit. A well-known posek told the man to throw it into the ocean.
beis-hamikdash/keeping-a-stone-from-the-.description: May you keep a stone fragment from the Kosel as a keepsake? Rav Moshe forbids it, and a posek advised throwing it in the sea, Avodah Zarah 52b.

beis-hamikdash/kiyor-made-from-copper-mi.intro: The kiyor in the Mishkan was made from the copper mirrors of the righteous women in Mitzrayim. If ordinary used items are unfit for holy use, as the used wood of Menachos 22b suggests, how could mirrors become part of the Mishkan? The Magen Avraham says affixing or reshaping them was enough of a change, while the Chasam Sofer says they were melted down and recast.
beis-hamikdash/kiyor-made-from-copper-mi.description: How could mirrors used by the women in Mitzrayim become the kiyor? The Magen Avraham and Chasam Sofer explain, in light of the used wood of Menachos 22b.

beis-hamikdash/kohen-circling-the-mizbea.intro: UPS saves fuel by avoiding left turns, but on the Mizbeach the kohen turned right even when left was shorter. Zevachim 62 teaches that every turn should be to the right, with a few exceptions. [Doing the Right Thing](/daf/zevachim/62/doing-the-right-thing-2025) carries this to the bimah, where the Shulchan Aruch, the Mishnah Berurah and the Vilna Gaon weigh speed against turning right.
beis-hamikdash/kohen-circling-the-mizbea.description: Why did kohanim circle the Mizbeach to the right even when left was shorter? Zevachim 62, and how the rule carries over to walking up to the bimah.

beis-hamikdash/lechem-hapanim-miracle.intro: On the festivals, the kohanim showed the Lechem Hapanim to the people, saying how beloved they were before Hashem, since the week-old bread was as fresh and warm as when it was placed on the Shulchan. The Rashba says steam could be seen rising from it. Menachos 96b leads Tosafos to ask whether it was baked on Friday or on Shabbos, and how the miracle worked in each case.
beis-hamikdash/lechem-hapanim-miracle.description: How did the Lechem Hapanim stay fresh and warm all week, and was it baked on Friday or Shabbos? The Rashba and Tosafos on the miracle in Menachos 96b.

beis-hamikdash/lottery-for-removing-the-.intro: Kohanim once raced for the right to clear the ashes from the mizbeach, and when one pushed another and broke his leg, the Sages set up a lottery. Why had there been no lottery before? Yoma 21a explains that the Sages assumed few kohanim would want to wake up early, since rising early is harder than staying up late, but the kohanim proved them wrong.
beis-hamikdash/lottery-for-removing-the-.description: Why did kohanim draw lots for clearing the altar ashes? Yoma 21a tells of the race that broke a leg, and why the Sages thought few would rise early.

beis-hamikdash/making-a-seven-branched-m.intro: Rosh Hashanah 24a forbids making a candelabra like the Menorah, but permits five, six or eight branches. The Shulchan Aruch bans a seven-branch menorah of any metal, and the Ohel Moshe even uses this to bolster why Chanukah is eight days. Rav Dovid Feinstein and the Birchei Yosef hold one should not even own a seven-branch leichter.
beis-hamikdash/making-a-seven-branched-m.description: May one make or own a seven-branch menorah? Rosh Hashanah 24a, the Shulchan Aruch and the Birchei Yosef, plus a Chanukah answer for why we light eight.

beis-hamikdash/mishkan-in-shiloh.intro: Zevachim 119b reads the words menuchah and nachalah as hints to the Mishkan in Shiloh. Why call Shiloh a resting place if the land was not yet fully conquered? Rashi explains that once the Mishkan stood there, the rest of Eretz Yisrael was easy to conquer, a calm compared with the years before.
beis-hamikdash/mishkan-in-shiloh.description: Why is the Mishkan in Shiloh called a resting place when the land was not yet conquered? Rashi explains, from the verse discussed in Zevachim 119b.

beis-hamikdash/ner-maaravi-miracle.intro: Each lamp of the Menorah got half a log of oil and burned out by morning, but the Ritva writes that the Ner Maaravi stayed lit until the next evening. This daily miracle answers the Beis Yosef's famous question of why Chanukah has eight days and not seven. [The Candles Burning Bright](/daf/zevachim/11/the-candles-burning-bright) shows the link to Zevachim 11b, where even the first day held a miracle.
beis-hamikdash/ner-maaravi-miracle.description: The Ner Maaravi of the Menorah burned until the next evening every day. How this miracle answers the Beis Yosef's Chanukah question, from Zevachim 11b.

beis-hamikdash/oil-and-wicks-for-the-tem.intro: Zevachim 11b says the kohen had to put in enough oil to last from evening until morning. Rashi says this half log was the same all year, so in summer the flames burned into the day. The Shitah Mekubetzes, based on the Yerushalmi, adds that thicker wicks were used in summer, which leads to a creative answer about a miracle on the first night of Chanukah.
beis-hamikdash/oil-and-wicks-for-the-tem.description: How much oil went into the Menorah, and why were summer wicks thicker? Rashi and the Shitah Mekubetzes on Zevachim 11b, with a twist on Chanukah.

beis-hamikdash/replicating-temple-vessel.intro: The Gemara on Rosh Hashanah 24a forbids copying the Temple courtyard, the Shulchan or the Menorah, which alarmed the Chasam Sofer, since matzos were made on metal tables. The Lehoros Nassan, based on Tosfos in Yoma 54b, says only a table in the Shulchan's exact design is forbidden. [Rules For Temple Tools](/daf/rosh-hashanah/24/rules-for-temple-tools) also tells how Machon HaMikdash justified its golden menorah.
beis-hamikdash/replicating-temple-vessel.description: Is a metal table forbidden as a copy of the Shulchan? Rosh Hashanah 24a bans replicating Temple vessels, and the Lehoros Nassan explains what it covers.

beis-hamikdash/shape-of-the-lechem-hapan.intro: According to Rebbe Chanina in Menachos 94b, the lechem ha'panim were shaped like an upside-down ches. Yet the kohanim cut them and ate them on Shabbos. The Mishnas Yehuda uses this to explain Rav Yaakov Emden's ruling that a cake shaped like a letter or picture, such as a dreidel, may be cut on Shabbos, which even the Chazon Ish accepts.
beis-hamikdash/shape-of-the-lechem-hapan.description: What shape was the lechem ha'panim, and what does it teach about cutting letter-shaped cakes on Shabbos? Rebbe Chanina and Rav Yaakov Emden, Menachos 94b.

beis-hamikdash/shape-of-the-luchos.intro: Were the Luchos square or rounded on top? Bava Basra 14a gives their size as six tefachim by six and says nothing about curved space in the Aron, which implies they were square, and the Tosafos Rosh agrees. Rounded Luchos are a later image, but a 700-year-old German Machzor already shows them that way, so it need not be a non-Jewish idea.
beis-hamikdash/shape-of-the-luchos.description: Were the Luchos square or rounded on top? The Gemara's measurements in Bava Basra 14a imply square tablets; where did the familiar rounded image come from?

beis-hamikdash/shelter-for-the-metzora-a.intro: A metzora was sent outside Yerushalayim, left to face the harsh sun and the pouring rain. Pesachim 85b teaches that the area under the city's gates was deliberately left unsanctified, so he could find shelter there. [Sensitive Situations](/daf/pesachim/85/sensitive-situations) sees a lesson in this: even someone who brought his punishment on himself deserves our concern.
beis-hamikdash/shelter-for-the-metzora-a.description: Why were the gateways of Yerushalayim left unsanctified? Pesachim 85b explains it let the metzora, barred from the city, find shelter from sun and rain.

beis-hamikdash/turning-right-for-mitzvos.intro: Yoma 17b teaches that all turns should be to the right, toward the east. A kohen at the top of the mizbeach ramp would take the long way around rather than turn left, even if it meant five right turns. [Doing The Right Thing](/daf/yoma/17/doing-the-right-thing) notes the Mishneh Halachos, who points out that the rule applies only to Temple service, so a driver may turn whichever way he likes.
beis-hamikdash/turning-right-for-mitzvos.description: Why did kohanim always turn right on the mizbeach? Yoma 17b's rule of right turns, the bimah, and why the rule applies only to Temple service.

beis-hamikdash/yom-kippur-at-the-first-t.intro: When the first Beis HaMikdash was finished, the nation celebrated for seven days, one of which was Yom Kippur, and on the sages' counsel they ate and drank. Moed Katan 9a says they feared punishment until a Heavenly voice said they would all merit the World to Come, and each had a baby boy that year. The Maharsha says all of you includes even those who ate for pleasure.
beis-hamikdash/yom-kippur-at-the-first-t.description: Why did the nation eat and drink on Yom Kippur at the first Beis HaMikdash dedication, and what reward came? Moed Katan 9a and the Maharsha explain.

beis-hamikdash/zecher-lemikdash.intro: Tosfos asks why the Mishnah on Rosh Hashanah 30a lists the lulav takanah and the new grain takanah together. The Chasam Sofer notes that no remembrance was made after the First Beis HaMikdash fell, and suggests this is part of why the Second did not last longer. Properly remembering the Beis HaMikdash, he says, is how we merit its rebuilding, which is why the two takanos go together.
beis-hamikdash/zecher-lemikdash.description: Why remember the Beis HaMikdash? The Chasam Sofer on Rosh Hashanah 30a: remembering it, as with the lulav on Sukkos, is how we merit its rebuilding.

korbanos/eating-the-korban-pesach-in-yer.intro: The Korban Pesach could be eaten anywhere in Yerushalayim, but Rav says on Pesachim 85b that only ground floors had the city's sanctity, not upper stories or roofs. After the meal people climbed to the roof for Hallel, which the Baal HaMaor explains as an escape from crowding. The Chasam Sofer counters that the city was crowded, but no one ever complained.
korbanos/eating-the-korban-pesach-in-yer.description: Why couldn't the Korban Pesach be eaten on a Yerushalayim roof, and why did people go up there for Hallel? Rav, the Baal HaMaor and Pesachim 85b explain.

korbanos/eizehu-mekoman.intro: Why was Eizeh Mekoman, which begins Zevachim 47a, chosen for the daily morning tefillah? One reason is that the chapter has no disputes. The Tiferes Yisrael adds that it speaks of curtains, though the Beis HaMikdash had walls, because Hashem taught this text to Moshe in the days of the Mishkan, and no one dared change it.
korbanos/eizehu-mekoman.description: Why is Eizeh Mekoman said every morning? It has no disputes, and the Tiferes Yisrael explains its mention of curtains, at the start of Zevachim 47a.

korbanos/honey-in-korbanos.intro: Menachos 58a discusses the prohibition of mixing honey into korbanos in the Beis HaMikdash. The Radvaz notes that honey in the Torah usually means date honey, yet he concludes the prohibition covers any kind. Rashi on Chumash limits it to sweetener from a fruit, which seems to leave out bee honey, and the debate echoes in the laws of Kiddush wine.
korbanos/honey-in-korbanos.description: Which sweeteners does the ban on honey in korbanos cover? The Radvaz says any honey, Rashi only fruit, with echoes for Kiddush wine, from Menachos 58a.

korbanos/korban-chagigah-on-erev-pesach.intro: The Korban Pesach had to be eaten when mostly full, out of respect, or, says the Yerushalmi, so a hungry person would not break its bones. That is why a Korban Chagigah was offered alongside it and eaten first. The Mishnah in Pesachim 69b teaches that when erev Pesach fell on Shabbos, the Chagigah was not brought, because it does not override Shabbos, so other food had to fill people up.
korbanos/korban-chagigah-on-erev-pesach.description: Why was a Korban Chagigah eaten before the Korban Pesach, and why was it skipped when erev Pesach fell on Shabbos? The Mishnah in Pesachim 69b.

korbanos/korban-pesach-deadline-at-midni.intro: Rabbi Akiva says the Korban Pesach may be eaten all night, and Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah says only until midnight. Abaye and the Gra say even Rabbi Akiva set a rabbinic limit, but the Rashba disagrees. An anonymous Mishnah in Zevachim 56b follows the midnight view, and Tosfos rules that way, while the Ran and others follow Rabbi Akiva.
korbanos/korban-pesach-deadline-at-midni.description: May the Korban Pesach be eaten all night, or only until midnight? Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah, and the Mishnah in Zevachim 56b that decides.

korbanos/korban-pesach-in-the-midbar.intro: The Sifrei says Bnei Yisrael brought the Korban Pesach only once in 40 years in the desert, and counts it against them. Tosfos explain that they did bring it, but only once was it optimal, since many had sons without a bris, and those sons later could not eat it at all. [Clouds in the Forecast](/daf/yevamos/71/clouds-in-the-forecast) on Yevamos 71b explores why they were faulted for something that seemed beyond their control.
korbanos/korban-pesach-in-the-midbar.description: Did Bnei Yisrael bring the Korban Pesach in the desert? The Sifrei says only once; Tosfos explain why it fell short of the ideal, from Yevamos 71b.

korbanos/lechem-hapanim.intro: The twelve loaves of lechem hapanim were baked on Friday, set on the Shulchan on Shabbos and eaten the next Shabbos, making them at least nine days old. Menachos 100b says they were sometimes eleven days old, when Rosh Hashanah fell on Thursday and Friday. Rashi asks how they were eaten when the next Shabbos was Yom Kippur, and answers that they were eaten that night.
korbanos/lechem-hapanim.description: How long did the twelve showbread loaves stay on the Shulchan, and when could the kohanim eat them? The nine- and eleven-day cases in Menachos 100b.

korbanos/maaser-beheimah.intro: In the times of the Beis HaMikdash, every tenth animal born in a flock was brought as ma'aser beheimah. Two flocks about ten miles apart do not combine to reach ten. Bechoros 55 adds that Rabbi Meir treats flocks across the Jordan as separate, and Rebbe Ami reasons that a bridge would make them one.
korbanos/maaser-beheimah.description: What is ma'aser beheimah, and when do two flocks combine to make ten? Distance, the Jordan River and a bridge are weighed in the Gemara on Bechoros 55.

korbanos/non-jew-eating-the-korban-pesac.intro: A non-Jew went up to Yerushalayim every year disguised as a Jew and ate the korban Pesach. Rabbi Yehudah ben Besaira told him to ask for the fatty tail, which is burned on the Mizbeiach, and he was found out. Building on Chagigah 2, Tosfos then asks why the rabbi did not go to Yerushalayim himself, and suggests he was too old or owned no land in Israel.
korbanos/non-jew-eating-the-korban-pesac.description: How was the non-Jew who ate the korban Pesach found out? Rabbi Yehudah ben Besaira's clever trick with the fatty tail, and Tosfos's question. Chagigah 2.

korbanos/pomegranate-wood-spit-for-korba.intro: The Mishnah on Pesachim 74 says the Korban Pesach was roasted on a spit of pomegranate wood, since little moisture escapes from it. But is it not forbidden to cut down fruit trees? The Panim Yafos says a great mitzvah makes the cutting constructive, while others say trimming branches is not the forbidden act, and the Talmud's frequent comparison of mitzvos to a pomegranate makes the wood especially fitting.
korbanos/pomegranate-wood-spit-for-korba.description: Why was the Korban Pesach roasted on pomegranate wood, and how could a fruit tree be cut for it? The Mishnah on Pesachim 74 and the Panim Yafos.

korbanos/salt-on-korbanos.intro: The Torah commands, on all your offerings you shall offer salt. Menachos 20a explains that salting every korban and mincha is a mitzvah, and the Rambam rules that a korban brought without salt is invalid. Since Chazal compare our table to the mizbe'ach, the Rema rules that salt should be on the table before Hamotzi, carrying the korban into every Jewish home.
korbanos/salt-on-korbanos.description: Must every korban and mincha be salted? Menachos 20a calls it a mitzvah, the Rambam rules an unsalted korban invalid, and the Rema carries it to our table.

korbanos/selling-the-bechorah.intro: Yaakov was not born a bechor, so how could he do the avodah? Most commentators say Esav sold him that right, and the Midrash Rabbah says so outright. Some ask how one can sell a right that did not yet exist, a question the Rivash, Tur and Ketzos HaChoshen address, but in a discussion of Zevachim 112 the avodah was already relevant right away.
korbanos/selling-the-bechorah.description: How could Esav sell his bechorah and its right to the avodah to Yaakov? The Midrash and the problem of selling a future right, from Zevachim 112.

korbanos/semichah-on-korbanos.intro: An owner leans his hands on his shelamim, and Rashi assumes a berachah is usually said first, like for shofar or matzah. But when two animals are mixed up, one maaser beheimah and one shelamim, Rashi says he leans on both without a berachah. As explained in the article on Eruvin 49, leaning on the wrong animal first would be an interruption before the mitzvah even began.
korbanos/semichah-on-korbanos.description: Is a berachah said before semichah on a korban? Rashi's ruling for two mixed-up animals, a maaser beheimah and a shelamim, is explained here on Eruvin 49.

korbanos/shtei-halechem-from-eretz-yisra.intro: The Shtei HaLechem brought on Shavuos must come from the new wheat and from moshvoseichem, your settlements, meaning Eretz Yisrael. Must the wheat have grown there, or is arriving there enough? Menachos 69b asks this about wheat that fell from the clouds, and the Chasam Sofer and the Yad David each suggest what the requirement demands.
korbanos/shtei-halechem-from-eretz-yisra.description: Must the Shavuos Shtei HaLechem come from wheat grown in Eretz Yisrael? Menachos 69b asks about moshvoseichem with wheat that fell from the sky.

korbanos/who-paid-for-the-ketores.intro: When Hashem told Moshe kach lecha, take for yourself, did that mean Moshe paid for the ketores? Rebbe Yoshiya says yes, and the Rashash explains that the ketores for the Mishkan's inauguration came from Moshe's own funds. Rebbe Yonason says on Yoma 3b that it came from communal funds, and the words mean that Hashem, kivyachol, preferred Moshe's money to theirs.
korbanos/who-paid-for-the-ketores.description: Was the ketores at the Mishkan's inauguration bought with Moshe's own money? Rebbe Yoshiya and Rebbe Yonason debate kach lecha, from Yoma 3b.

kohanim/answering-amen-to-birkas-kohanim.intro: Normally one may not answer amein in the middle of Shemoneh Esrei, so Rabbi Shragga Kallus asked when it might be allowed. One answer is Birkas Kohanim, after the bracha of Modim, which Rav Shlomo Zalman permits though Rav Elyashiv and Rav Chaim Kanievsky do not. In [Saying Amein to Birkas Kohanim](/daf/sotah/38/saying-amein-to-birkas-kohanim), Rav Moshe says someone in Shema answers amein, based on Sotah 38.
kohanim/answering-amen-to-birkas-kohanim.description: Must those being blessed answer amein to Birkas Kohanim, even in Shema or Shemoneh Esrei? Rav Moshe, Rav Shlomo Zalman and others, in light of Sotah 38.

kohanim/birkas-kohanim-while-sitting.intro: Avodah done sitting is invalid, as Zevachim 23b teaches, and Birkas Kohanim is compared to the avodah. Rabbeinu Yitzchak in Tosfos says a kohen who blesses while sitting has done nothing. The Panim Meiros suggests he may even break a mitzvas asei, and the Mishnah Berurah rules that a kohen who cannot stand without leaning should not duchen at all.
kohanim/birkas-kohanim-while-sitting.description: Must kohanim stand to bless the people? Zevachim 23b, Rabbeinu Yitzchak and the Mishnah Berurah on a kohen who cannot stand without leaning on something.

kohanim/buying-the-position-of-kohen-gad.intro: The elders asked the Kohen Gadol to review the Yom Kippur passages, in case he had never learned them, and Yoma 18a asks how such a man could be appointed. In the Second Beis HaMikdash it happened: Marta bas Baitos paid King Yannai to appoint Yehoshua ben Gamla. Yet he is praised elsewhere, including for the golden lottery box of Yoma 37a, and the Maharsha, Tosfos and the Ritva each resolve the contradiction.
kohanim/buying-the-position-of-kohen-gad.description: Could the office of Kohen Gadol be bought? Marta bas Baitos and Yehoshua ben Gamla in Yoma 18a, and how the Maharsha, Tosfos and the Ritva explain it.

kohanim/giving-beef-tongue-to-a-kohen.intro: Every time a non-sacred animal is slaughtered, the Torah commands giving the foreleg, the jaw with the tongue, and the stomach to a Kohen. The Mishnah in Chullin 130a applies this everywhere and in every age. [Bite Your Tongue](/daf/chullin/130/bite-your-tongue) asks whether the tongue in stores is a problem, and notes that a Bas Kohen may receive it too.
kohanim/giving-beef-tongue-to-a-kohen.description: Must the beef tongue go to a Kohen? The mitzvah of the foreleg, jaw and stomach, the buyer's burden, and why a Bas Kohen may take it. From Chullin 130a.

kohanim/king-uziyahu-and-the-ketores.intro: King Uziyahu was a tzaddik and a wise man, yet he entered the Heichal to offer Ketores, reasoning that the ban on a non-kohen did not apply to a king. He was struck with tzara'as and lived his last 25 years in seclusion. Had he looked at Dovid and Shlomo, who never offered it, he would have been saved, as the article on Nedarim 12 explains.
kohanim/king-uziyahu-and-the-ketores.description: Why was the righteous King Uziyahu struck with tzara'as after offering Ketores? He ignored the kings before him, as an article on Nedarim 12 explains.

kohanim/kohanim-removing-shoes-before-du.intro: Sotah 39b gives two reasons why kohanim remove their shoes before Birkas Kohanim. Muddy shoes on a raised platform would be disrespectful to the tzibbur, and a kohen whose laces came loose might step down, and people would think he was not a real kohen. [A Kohen and His Colorful Socks](/daf/sotah/39/a-kohen-and-his-colorful-socks) adds that shoes should be hidden, and Rav Moshe Feinstein saw no issue with bright socks.
kohanim/kohanim-removing-shoes-before-du.description: Why do kohanim take off their shoes before Birkas Kohanim, and are bright socks a problem? The two reasons in Sotah 39b and Rav Moshe Feinstein's view.

kohanim/kohen-at-a-tzaddiks-grave.intro: Rabbeinu Chaim HaKohen said that had he been alive when Rabbeinu Tam died, he would have become tamei to attend the funeral. Tosfos in Kesubos 103b records this, based on the day Rebbe Yehuda HaNasi died. In [Can a Kohen Go to a Tzaddik’s Funeral?](/daf/kesubos/103/can-a-kohen-go-to-a-tzaddiks-funeral), Rebbe Shlomo Kluger rejects the idea that tzaddikim impart no tumah, and the Kitzur Shulchan Aruch warns kohanim away from their graves.
kohanim/kohen-at-a-tzaddiks-grave.description: May a kohen become tamei to attend a tzaddik's funeral or visit his grave? Rabbeinu Chaim HaKohen, Tosfos and the Ran on Rebbe's funeral, in Kesubos 103b.

kohanim/kohen-at-his-wifes-funeral.intro: Must a kohen become tamei for his wife's burial? Yosef HaKohen's friends said a wife is like a meis mitzvah, and when he refused, they forced him under the ohel. The story in Zevachim 100a rests on Rabbi Akiva's teaching that it is a mitzvah for a kohen to become tamei for a close relative, and Tosafos says he may even be compelled.
kohanim/kohen-at-his-wifes-funeral.description: May a kohen be forced to become tamei for his wife's burial? Rabbi Akiva's teaching and Tosafos, in the story of Yosef HaKohen from Zevachim 100a.

kohanim/kohen-flying-over-a-cemetery.intro: The tumah of a cemetery rises skyward with no upper limit, so may a kohen fly over one? The Gemara in Nazir 55 brings Rebbe Yossi ben Rebbe Yehudah's large box that blocks tumah, and the plane might seem similar. But the Gemara says a moving box does not work, Rabbeinu Chananel requires support from the ground, and the Rambam rejects the box altogether.
kohanim/kohen-flying-over-a-cemetery.description: May a kohen fly on a plane that passes over a cemetery? Whether a plane is like the box that blocks tumah, with Rabbeinu Chananel and the Rambam, Nazir 55.

kohanim/kohen-giving-up-the-first-aliyah.intro: The Minchas Elazar writes that his father always called a kohen first, even when many people had yahrzeits, since asking a kohen to waive his honor slights it. Yet when it was known that no Levi was present, a kohen could choose to give up his two aliyos to avoid extra berachos. The article on Kesubos 25b notes that others disagree, and says whatever the kohen does for the sake of Heaven is fine.
kohanim/kohen-giving-up-the-first-aliyah.description: May a kohen give up the first aliyah, for a yahrzeit or to save extra berachos? The Minchas Elazar's view and the Munkacser custom, from Kesubos 25b.

kohanim/kohen-in-a-non-jewish-cemetery.intro: A kohen searching for a bungalow colony spotted a non-Jewish cemetery with a tree over a grave and a thick cable running for miles. [A Grave Problem](/daf/sukkah/5/a-grave-problem) begins on Sukkah 5a and turns to Bava Metzia 114b, where Eliyahu HaNavi stood in a gentile cemetery. His rabbi followed the Shulchan Aruch and the Rema: a kohen should be stringent and treat such graves like Jewish ones.
kohanim/kohen-in-a-non-jewish-cemetery.description: May a kohen walk under the ohel of a non-Jewish grave? Eliyahu HaNavi in Bava Metzia 114b, Tosfos, and the Shulchan Aruch's strict ruling for kohanim.

kohanim/kohen-ruling-on-tzaraas.intro: A poor kohen planning a trip abroad taught his wife the laws of tzaraas so she could take his place, says the Midrash Tanchuma. Must a kohen wear bigdei kehunah when ruling on tzaraas? The Chazon Ish assumes not, the Tiferes Yaakov disagrees based on Yoma 43a, and the Kol Torah and the Pardes Yosef debate whether the wife herself ruled or only advised a male kohen.
kohanim/kohen-ruling-on-tzaraas.description: Must a kohen wear bigdei kehunah to rule on tzaraas, and could his wife rule? The Chazon Ish, the Tiferes Yaakov, Yoma 43a and the Pardes Yosef.

kohanim/lottery-for-kohanim-in-the-beis-.intro: Lotteries assigned the daily avodah among kohanim in the Beis HaMikdash. But was there a lottery on Yom Kippur, when Yoma 32 makes clear that the Kohen Gadol performed all the avodah himself? The Kesef Mishneh, citing the liturgy of the Geonim, explains that daily tasks like removing the ashes still had to be done, and regular kohanim drew lots for them.
kohanim/lottery-for-kohanim-in-the-beis-.description: Were lots drawn for the avodah on Yom Kippur, when the Kohen Gadol did it all? The Shvus Yaakov's question and the Kesef Mishneh's answer, Yoma 32.

kohanim/matanos-kehunah-outside-eretz-yi.intro: The Mishnah in Chullin 130a states that the gifts of foreleg, jaw and stomach apply even outside Eretz Yisrael. Yet Rebbe Illai holds otherwise, and Rashi extends the Diaspora practice to these gifts as well, though the Vilna Gaon was strict everywhere. In Eretz Yisrael the leniency does not apply, but the Chazon Ish notes that Kohanim of proven lineage are no longer found.
kohanim/matanos-kehunah-outside-eretz-yi.description: Do matanos kehunah apply outside Eretz Yisrael? The Mishnah, Rebbe Illai, Rashi, the Vilna Gaon and the Chazon Ish weigh in. Learn it from Chullin 130a.

kohanim/matanos-kehunah-to-a-kohens-daug.intro: The foreleg, jaws and stomach of a slaughtered animal are gifts for the kohen. Ulla gave them to a kohen's daughter instead, and Rashi explains that she may receive them even if she married a Yisrael, since unlike terumah they have no holiness and anyone may eat them. In [A Kohen By Any Other Name](/daf/kiddushin/8/a-kohen-by-any-other-name), tied to Kiddushin 8a, Rav Kahane accepted them for his wife.
kohanim/matanos-kehunah-to-a-kohens-daug.description: May the priestly gifts of meat go to a kohen's daughter married to a Yisrael, and may her husband share them? Rashi and Tosfos on Kiddushin 8a.

kohanim/obligation-to-hear-birkas-kohani.intro: Sotah 38 says the kohen has a mitzvah to bless Klal Yisrael, but does the one being blessed have a mitzvah too? The Sefer Chareidim says yes, and the Haflaah adds that turning one's back violates it, while the Mahari Assad sees only a chance to help the kohanim. Rav Moshe Feinstein writes that in America, where Birkas Kohanim is only on yom tov, everyone who is not sick must come to hear it.
kohanim/obligation-to-hear-birkas-kohani.description: Is a non-kohen obligated to hear Birkas Kohanim, or is it only a lost chance? The Sefer Chareidim, Haflaah and Rav Moshe weigh in, based on Sotah 38.

kohanim/reciting-pesukim-during-birkas-k.intro: Sotah 39b lists verses a Yisrael may say during Birkas Kohanim, but Rebbe Chanina bar Pappa objects that a servant whose king is blessing him should listen. The Mishna Berura rules that the verses may not be said while the kohanim are actually blessing. Rav Shlomo Zalman Auerbach adds that one should not even pause for Kaddish or Kedushah then, since Hashem is blessing us.
kohanim/reciting-pesukim-during-birkas-k.description: May you say pesukim or answer Kaddish while the kohanim bless you? Rebbe Chanina bar Pappa in Sotah 39b, the Mishna Berura and Rav Shlomo Zalman.

kohanim/rotation-of-the-kohanims-shifts.intro: The kohanim were split into 24 mishmaros, each serving one week, and every mishmar was split again into six family groups, one for each weekday, with all of them sharing Shabbos. Menachos 107 shows how this rotation caused jealousy over the hides from extra communal korbanos, and why Chizkiyah says six separate collection boxes were set up to keep the peace.
kohanim/rotation-of-the-kohanims-shifts.description: How were the kohanim divided into 24 weekly mishmaros and daily family shifts, and why did hides cause jealousy? Chizkiyah explains in Menachos 107.

kohanim/seeing-a-kohen-doctor.intro: If using a kohen for personal needs is forbidden, may a patient see a doctor who is a kohen? The Zera Chaim proves from Yoma 49a that it must be allowed, since Rebbe Chanina was a medical expert and also took money for pidyon ha'ben. Later authorities explain why: the doctor is paid, and healing is itself a mitzvah.
kohanim/seeing-a-kohen-doctor.description: May a patient be treated by a doctor who is a kohen? The Zera Chaim proves it is allowed from Rebbe Chanina, a medical expert and a kohen, in Yoma 49a.

kohanim/standing-for-birkas-kohanim.intro: The Torah compares Birkas Kohanim to the avodah, and avodah done sitting is invalid, as Zevachim 23b teaches. [Fasten Your Seatbelts And Prepare For Minchah](/daf/zevachim/23/fasten-your-seatbelts-and-prepare-for-minchah) shows how far Rabbeinu Yitzchak takes this: a seated blessing is not just less ideal, it does not work at all.
kohanim/standing-for-birkas-kohanim.description: Why must kohanim stand while blessing the people? Birkas Kohanim is compared to the avodah, which is invalid when done sitting, as Zevachim 23b teaches.

kohanim/using-a-kohen-to-serve-you.intro: Rabbeinu Tam once let a kohen pour water over his hands, and a student asked how that could be allowed. In [Good Help Is Hard To Find](/daf/yoma/49/good-help-is-hard-to-find), the answers range from the kohen lacking priestly garments to Rabbeinu Peter's view that a kohen may waive his honor. The Rema rules that way, while the Mishnah Berurah prefers to be strict unless the kohen benefits, a point the article ties to Yoma 49a.
kohanim/using-a-kohen-to-serve-you.description: May you let a kohen serve you, and can he waive the honor due to him? Rabbeinu Tam, Rabbeinu Peter and the Rema weigh in, discussed alongside Yoma 49a.

tumah-and-taharah/average-height-of-a-pe.intro: The Gemara treats the average person as three amos tall, a figure that matters for the minimum size of a mikveh. Tosfos in Chagigah 11b says the head is not included. This explains why a privacy fence must be four amos, and Tosfos finds support in the Targum Sheni on the hanging of Haman's sons.
tumah-and-taharah/average-height-of-a-pe.description: How tall is an average person in halacha? Tosfos says three amos without the head, which affects mikveh size and privacy walls. Learn it from Chagigah 11b.

tumah-and-taharah/do-non-jewish-graves-t.intro: Does a gentile's grave give off tumah to whatever is above it? In the Gemara in Bava Metzia, Eliyahu HaNavi tells Rabbah bar Avuhah that Rebbe Shimon bar Yochai holds it does not. The Rambam rules like Eliyahu, but Tosfos quote Rabbeinu Yitzchak that such graves carry tumah like any other, a machlokes Rishonim explored on Sukkah 5a.
tumah-and-taharah/do-non-jewish-graves-t.description: Do non-Jewish graves convey tumah through an ohel? Eliyahu HaNavi cites Rebbe Shimon bar Yochai, while the Rambam and Tosfos differ. From Sukkah 5a.

tumah-and-taharah/everyone-is-tamei-meis.intro: Today we are all presumed tamei meis, so the Rambam says that walking where the Beis HaMikdash stood brings kareis. Yet a tamei meis may enter the rest of Har HaBayis, which only other kinds of tumah bar. The discussion of Zevachim 107 explains why some immerse first, and why the gedolim still warn against going up.
tumah-and-taharah/everyone-is-tamei-meis.description: Why are all people today presumed tamei meis, and which holy areas does that bar them from? The Rambam and Mishnah Berurah, discussed with Zevachim 107.

tumah-and-taharah/how-the-chanukah-oil-b.intro: Rav teaches in Pesachim 16a that liquids in the Beis HaMikdash cannot become tamei, so how did the Yevanim defile the oil for the Menorah? The Shoel U'Meishiv says the breach of the walls lessened the Beis HaMikdash's sanctity, and the Pri Chadash says oil used for idolatry becomes tamei anywhere. The Teshuvah Mi'Ahavah suggests the oil had congealed, making it a food that could become tamei.
tumah-and-taharah/how-the-chanukah-oil-b.description: If liquids in the Beis HaMikdash cannot become tamei, how did the Greeks defile the Menorah oil? Three answers to Rav's teaching in Pesachim 16a.

tumah-and-taharah/kohanim-walking-under-.intro: A person becomes tamei when he is under the same roof as a meis, and Sukkah 13b shows that even a tree can count as that roof. That is why kohanim are careful not to walk under trees whose branches spread over graves in a cemetery. Rashi and the Meiri go on to argue whether a large leafy vegetable that will soon wilt can also be such a roof.
tumah-and-taharah/kohanim-walking-under-.description: Why do kohanim avoid walking under trees in a cemetery? Branches over a grave can act as a roof that carries tumah, as the Gemara in Sukkah 13b teaches.

tumah-and-taharah/meis-mitzvah.intro: A meis mitzvah, someone with no one to bury him, must be buried even by a kohen. The Ran says this is how Eliyahu HaNavi buried Rebbe Akiva, since people feared Rome. He suggests every attendee at a tzaddik's funeral fills a unique role, so for each kohen it is like a meis mitzvah, though Tosfos disagrees, in the discussion on Kesubos 103b.
tumah-and-taharah/meis-mitzvah.description: Why may even a kohen bury a meis mitzvah, and is a tzaddik's funeral like one? The Ran explains Eliyahu burying Rebbe Akiva, in Kesubos 103b.

tumah-and-taharah/produce-made-susceptib.intro: Produce cannot become tamei while attached to the ground, but once harvested, contact with one of seven liquids, olive oil among them, makes it able to receive tumah. Rebbe Yochanan HaChorani saw that olives sent by Rebbe Tzadok were moist with oil and refused them. [Olive What He’s Having](/daf/yevamos/15/olive-what-hes-having) on Yevamos 15 explains, with Tosfos, why he worried and what made him finally accept.
tumah-and-taharah/produce-made-susceptib.description: When does harvested produce become able to receive tumah? The seven liquids, and the moist olives Rebbe Yochanan HaChorani refused, from Yevamos 15.

tumah-and-taharah/trees-and-cables-sprea.intro: A tree branch over a grave can form an ohel and pass tumah to whatever lies beneath it, even a cable that runs for miles. In the story told with Sukkah 5a, a kohen three miles from a cemetery worried about walking under such a cable. The cable measured 3.3 inches, and since only an ohel of at least a tefach carries tumah, his rabbi said he need not be stringent.
tumah-and-taharah/trees-and-cables-sprea.description: Can a tree over a grave pass tumah to a cable miles long? A kohen's real case, the tefach rule for an ohel, and the cut branches, from Sukkah 5a.

tumah-and-taharah/tumah-from-the-grave-o.intro: The Rashba holds that the graves of idolaters do not pass on tumah through an ohel. So he was asked about a Jew who abandoned his faith and adopted pagan beliefs. Citing Rebbe Meir in Kiddushin 36a, who says Jews are called Hashem's children even when they worship idols, the Rashba ruled that such a person's grave still passes on tumah like any Jewish grave.
tumah-and-taharah/tumah-from-the-grave-o.description: Does the grave of a Jew who left his faith pass on tumah through an ohel? The Rashba rules from Rebbe Meir's teaching in Kiddushin 36a about sinners.

tumah-and-taharah/tumah-of-lands-outside.intro: Chazal decreed that one who leaves Eretz Yisrael for chutz la'aretz becomes tamei. Tosfos gives two reasons: people who died in the Flood are buried all over chutz la'aretz, and the Sages wanted to keep people from leaving Eretz Yisrael. In Nazir 55, Rebbe Yossi ben Rebbe Yehudah says a large box blocks this tumah, though the Gemara questions a moving one.
tumah-and-taharah/tumah-of-lands-outside.description: Why did Chazal decree that lands outside Eretz Yisrael impart tumah, and can a box block it? Tosfos and Rebbe Yossi ben Rebbe Yehudah, from Nazir 55.

tumah-and-taharah/tumah-waived-for-the-c.intro: When most of Klal Yisrael was tamei from idols, Chizkiyahu added a month so they could purify themselves before Pesach. [A Rosh Chodesh Addition – Sometimes](/daf/sanhedrin/12/a-rosh-chodesh-addition-sometimes) notes the principle that tumah is waived for the tzibbur, so they could have brought the Korban Pesach anyway. On Sanhedrin 12b he asks forgiveness, perhaps for not relying on that rule.
tumah-and-taharah/tumah-waived-for-the-c.description: A communal korban may be brought even if most people are tamei. Why then did Chizkiyahu add a month before Pesach and seek forgiveness? Sanhedrin 12b.

tumah-and-taharah/who-slaughters-the-par.intro: Rav says on Yoma 42a that a kohen must slaughter the Parah Adumah, even though shechitah of korbanos usually needs no kohen. Like ruling on tzaraas, it is a scriptural decree rather than true avodah, so the Chazon Ish concludes the kohen need not wear his priestly garments. [Tzaraas Rulings](/daf/yoma/42/tzaraas-rulings) notes that the Rambam rules any Jew, man or woman, may perform it.
tumah-and-taharah/who-slaughters-the-par.description: Who may slaughter the Parah Adumah? Rav on Yoma 42a requires a kohen, the Chazon Ish says no priestly garments, and the Rambam allows any Jew.

churban/kamtza-and-bar-kamtza-story.intro: A wealthy man's servant brought his party invitation to Bar Kamtza, the host's enemy, instead of his friend Kamtza. Humiliated in front of the rabbis, Bar Kamtza went to Caesar and sent a blemished offering to the Beis HaMikdash. In Gittin 55b, Rabbi Yochanan says the Temple was destroyed because of the anavah of Rabbi Zecharia ben Avkolos.
churban/kamtza-and-bar-kamtza-story.description: How did a party invitation sent to the wrong man lead to the churban? The story of Kamtza and Bar Kamtza in Gittin 55b, and Rabbi Zecharia ben Avkolos.

churban/takanos-after-the-churban.intro: After the Churban, Rebbe Yochanan ben Zakai made the lulav a seven-day mitzvah everywhere, as a remembrance of the Beis HaMikdash. People took it as a sign the Mikdash would not soon return, and the Imrei Emes explains that his second takanah on Rosh Hashanah 30a, about new grain, answered that despair. Together they taught people to remember the past while expecting the rebuilding any year.
churban/takanos-after-the-churban.description: Rebbe Yochanan ben Zakai's takanos after the Churban, on lulav and new grain, and what they told a despairing nation, from the Mishnah, Rosh Hashanah 30a.

churban/yerushalayim-destroyed-for-stric.intro: Rebbe Yochanan says Yerushalayim was destroyed because people stuck to the strict law and would not go beyond it, though other sins are named too. The Chofetz Chaim answers that one who never forgives an iota is judged the same way in Heaven, so their strictness sealed their fate. The Aruch HaShulchan on Bava Metzia 99b urges us to forgive negligent workers.
churban/yerushalayim-destroyed-for-stric.description: Was Yerushalayim destroyed for insisting on the letter of the law? The Chofetz Chaim explains, and the Aruch HaShulchan applies it, in Bava Metzia 99b.

hekdesh/meilah-for-sound-sight-and-smell.intro: Pesachim 26a teaches that there is no me'ilah for sounds, sights and smells, and Rashi gives the example of listening to the music of the Leviyim's instruments. Rava infers that a lesser prohibition still applies, so one may not sit and enjoy that music. From here, Rabbeinu Yerucham concludes that wherever benefit from an item is forbidden, one may not enjoy its smell, sound or appearance either.
hekdesh/meilah-for-sound-sight-and-smell.description: Is enjoying the sound, sight or smell of hekdesh forbidden benefit? Me'ilah and the music of the Leviyim, with Rava and Rashi on Pesachim 26a.

hekdesh/meilah-from-temple-stones.intro: Could a Kosel fragment on a shelf be harmless, since no one is really using it? Rav Moshe Feinstein rules that displaying it like a trophy gives personal pleasure and pride, which is the very definition of benefit from holy property. Even if someone thought the stones had lost their kedushah, using them for oneself would be wrong, in an article on Bechoros 15b.
hekdesh/meilah-from-temple-stones.description: Is displaying a holy stone forbidden benefit from hekdesh? Rav Moshe says a Kosel fragment on a shelf is me'ilah, in an article on Bechoros 15b.

hekdesh/offspring-of-a-redeemed-blemishe.intro: A blemished korban is redeemed and becomes permitted. But on Bechoros 15b, if it conceived while still holy and gave birth after redemption, the newborn keeps a trace of kedushah. That trace is too slight to redeem, so the animal can never be offered or eaten, much like a bank that demanded a $0 payment no one could make.
hekdesh/offspring-of-a-redeemed-blemishe.description: Why is the newborn of a redeemed blemished korban forbidden forever? Its holiness is too slight to be redeemed, as the Gemara in Bechoros 15b explains.

teshuvah/are-sinners-still-hashems-child.intro: Rebbe Yehuda says the Jewish people are called Hashem's children only when they follow the right path, while Rebbe Meir says they keep that name even when they sin. In [We are Hashem’s Children](/daf/kiddushin/36/we-are-hashems-children), Rashi reads Rebbe Meir's last verse in Kiddushin 36a as a promise of teshuvah. The Maharit and the Rashba say we are beloved children even before we return.
teshuvah/are-sinners-still-hashems-child.description: Are Jews still called Hashem's children when they sin? Rebbe Meir and Rebbe Yehuda, with Rashi, the Maharit and the Rashba, in Kiddushin 36a.

teshuvah/atonement-after-death.intro: When a nazir's term is cut short, Nazir 31 compares his chattas to that of a person who died, which may not be offered, since there is no atonement after death. The Rema cautions that this is true only of korbanos. Through tzedaka and Yizkor on Yom HaKippurim, the departed can still gain atonement, which the Mishna Berura says is why the day's name is plural.
teshuvah/atonement-after-death.description: Can a person who has passed away still gain atonement? There is no atonement after death for korbanos, but the Rema says Yizkor helps, from Nazir 31.

teshuvah/atonement-for-indirectly-causin.intro: Dovid HaMelech only asked for bread while running for his life, yet Sanhedrin 95a says he was held accountable for the slaughter of Nov's kohanim. [Agents Of Destruction](/daf/sanhedrin/95/agents-of-destruction) follows the Be'er Sheva, who learns that even an unforeseen death needs kapparah. The Tzemach Tzedek argues that Dovid should have seen the danger, and the Chidah adds his view on Avner.
teshuvah/atonement-for-indirectly-causin.description: Does someone who indirectly and unknowingly caused a death need atonement? The Be'er Sheva learns it from Dovid HaMelech and Nov in Sanhedrin 95a.

teshuvah/baal-teshuvah-shaving-his-head.intro: The Terumas HaDeshen records a custom that a heretic who returns shaves all his hair and goes to the mikveh, echoing the Levi'im who shaved after the Golden Calf. The Rema permits this on chol ha'moed, though the Shvus Yaakov says to use scissors, not a razor. The Mishnah Berurah explains that he is not counted for a minyan until he shaves, as the article on Nazir 38 shows.
teshuvah/baal-teshuvah-shaving-his-head.description: Why does a returning penitent shave his head and immerse, and may he do it on Chol HaMoed? The Terumas HaDeshen and the Rema, in an article on Nazir 38.

teshuvah/children-not-bound-by-a-parents.intro: Korach knew from a prophecy that Shmuel HaNavi would descend from him, so he felt sure he would survive his rebellion. His mistake was assuming his sons would share his fate, though his sons had joined the rebellion, yet at the last minute they did teshuvah and were saved. [The Gift of Teshuvah](/daf/bava-basra/74/the-gift-of-teshuvah), filed on Bava Basra 74a, draws the lesson that children can always choose a different path.
teshuvah/children-not-bound-by-a-parents.description: Korach's sons joined his rebellion, yet repented in time. A lesson from Bava Basra 74a: children are never locked into a parent's wrongdoing.

teshuvah/do-mitzvos-cancel-out-aveiros.intro: Shekalim 14a teaches that Hashem does not overlook aveiros, so a person can do many mitzvos and still not erase his sins. The Netziv explains with a picture: mitzvos are like healing herbs and aveiros are like poison, and each works only on the one who takes it. The antidote Hashem gave for that poison is teshuvah, which, like mitzvos, helps only the person who does it.
teshuvah/do-mitzvos-cancel-out-aveiros.description: Do good deeds erase sins? Shekalim 14a says Hashem does not overlook aveiros, and the Netziv explains why only teshuvah is the cure for wrongdoing.

teshuvah/is-anyone-beyond-teshuvah.intro: When the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed, Avraham Avinu pleaded for his children, and Hashem answered every defense until Avraham cried out, is there no teshuvah for them? Hashem said Klal Yisrael is like a leafy olive tree, slow to bear fruit but sure to return. The Gemara in Menachos 53 teaches that teshuvah is always an option.
teshuvah/is-anyone-beyond-teshuvah.description: Can a person or a whole nation stray too far to do teshuvah? Avraham pleads for his children and Hashem answers with the slow olive tree in Menachos 53.

teshuvah/overcoming-despair-in-teshuvah.intro: Discouragement can block teshuvah as much as sin itself. [Don’t Despair](/daf/rosh-hashanah/30/dont-despair) starts from the takanos of Rosh Hashanah 30a and brings the father of Rav Henoch Leibowitz: thoughts that impede avodas Hashem are a tool of the yetzer hara. Rabbeinu Yonah in Yesod HaTeshuvah advises a penitent to imagine himself newly born, returning to regret later.
teshuvah/overcoming-despair-in-teshuvah.description: Why can despair block teshuvah? Rosh Hashanah 30a, Rav Henoch Leibowitz's father and Rabbeinu Yonah on starting fresh before dwelling on past sins.

teshuvah/publicly-confessing-a-sin.intro: Sotah 7b says Yehudah's public admission moved Reuven to confess his own sin in public. But Rav Sheshes says it is brazen to spell out one's sins, and Rashi explains this in two ways: it shows a lack of shame, or it adds to the chillul Hashem. So why could Reuven confess, when only Yehudah had a life to save?
teshuvah/publicly-confessing-a-sin.description: Should a person tell others about his sins? Rav Sheshes calls it brazen, yet Reuven confessed in public. The Gemara in Sotah 7b and Rashi's two views.

teshuvah/shame-that-remains-after-atonem.intro: Rebbe Akiva wept over the woman whose vow was annulled without her knowing, who still needs atonement. Rav Sholom Schwadron compares two thieves let off by a judge, one overjoyed and one ashamed he ever stole. Rebbe Akiva saw, as Nazir 23a shows, that the disgrace of sin can survive atonement, and [The Shame Of Sinning](/daf/nazir/23/the-shame-of-sinning) asks why we are not moved.
teshuvah/shame-that-remains-after-atonem.description: Can the shame of sin remain after forgiveness? Rebbe Akiva wept and Rav Sholom Schwadron explains with two thieves, from the Gemara in Nazir 23a.

teshuvah/teshuvah-at-the-last-moment.intro: Why did Moshe ask that Korach's followers be swallowed alive? On Bava Basra 74a, Rabbah bar Bar Channa hears them cry, "Moshe and his Torah are true, and we are liars." The Rashbam says they could say this only because they went down alive, and the Belzer Rebbe explains that Moshe wanted to leave them a chance for teshuvah.
teshuvah/teshuvah-at-the-last-moment.description: Why were Korach's followers swallowed alive? To leave them a chance for teshuvah, explains the Belzer Rebbe, from a story told in Bava Basra 74a.

teshuvah/teshuvah-of-king-menashe.intro: Menashe's crimes were as heinous as they come, yet on Sanhedrin 102b he claims he does not belong with Achav and Yeravam, since he repented. The Maharsha explains why he tested Rav Ashi on bread: it is a sign that Hashem accepts repentance, as with Adam. Rebbe Yochanan teaches that Menashe's teshuvah shows there is always room to return.
teshuvah/teshuvah-of-king-menashe.description: King Menashe sinned terribly yet repented. Sanhedrin 102b, the Maharsha on bread as a sign of teshuvah, and Rebbe Yochanan's lesson for ba'alei teshuvah.

teshuvah/teshuvah-of-ninveh.intro: Yonah refused to warn Ninveh, fearing their teshuvah would reflect badly on Klal Yisrael. The Iyun Yaakov explains on Yevamos 98a that Yonah misjudged: Ninveh's teshuvah was only temporary, and within thirty days they returned to their old ways. That actually showed Klal Yisrael in a good light, since they are capable of lasting change.
teshuvah/teshuvah-of-ninveh.description: Did the teshuvah of Ninveh last? The Iyun Yaakov says it faded in thirty days, showing Klal Yisrael's power of lasting change, from Yevamos 98a.

teshuvah/value-of-small-spiritual-improv.intro: As the Yamim Noraim approach, the yetzer hara whispers that one small change cannot matter. [Every Bit Counts](/daf/chagigah/9/every-bit-counts) answers from Chagigah 9b, where skipping the 101st review earns a harsh title. Rav Avrohom Kalmanowitz explains that whoever sees any part of avodas Hashem as insignificant is missing something, while even the smallest gain is precious.
teshuvah/value-of-small-spiritual-improv.description: Does a small spiritual change really matter? Rav Avrohom Kalmanowitz on the 101st review shows that every gain in serving Hashem counts. See Chagigah 9b.

humility/a-rebbe-learning-from-his-stude.intro: Avimi was a demanding rebbe who gave Rav Chisda figurative blows for forgetting his learning. Later Avimi forgot Maseches Menachos and went to his own talmid to relearn it. Menachos 7 says he thought it would be more successful this way, and Rav Chaim Shmulevitz explains that the humbling route made him a fitting vessel for Torah.
humility/a-rebbe-learning-from-his-stude.description: Why did Avimi travel to his own student Rav Chisda to relearn a masechta? Rav Chaim Shmulevitz on humility as the key to Torah, from Menachos 7.

humility/arrogance-as-self-deception.intro: The Mesilas Yesharim teaches that arrogance is a kind of falsehood: a person looks only at his strengths and denies his weaknesses. R' Yisrael Salanter adds that he may admit his faults but treats them as small, while making much of his friend's faults. [Humblebrags](/daf/sukkah/20/humblebrags), filed on Sukkah 20a, explains that real humility comes from the truth, like a chauffeur who is not proud of the limousine he drives.
humility/arrogance-as-self-deception.description: Arrogance comes from ignoring your own weaknesses, and humility from an honest look at yourself. The Mesilas Yesharim's view, in an article on Sukkah 20a.

humility/arrogance-in-torah-learning.intro: In [A Humbling Metaphor](/daf/zevachim/113/a-humbling-metaphor), the Vilna Gaon reads the huge newborn Re'em of Zevachim 113b as a student who skips the basics and jumps into deep analysis. Puffed up and lacking foundations, he cannot win by truth, so he turns to insults that dam the flow of Torah. Real growth, the Gaon warns, takes years of humble, orderly learning.
humility/arrogance-in-torah-learning.description: The Vilna Gaon reads the giant newborn Re'em in Zevachim 113b as an arrogant student who skips the basics, and warns why humble learning is needed.

humility/asking-advice-from-those-less-g.intro: The verse "Let us make man" sounds plural. Sanhedrin 38b explains that Hashem first consulted the ministering angels, and Rashi says this teaches humility: seek advice even from those of lesser stature. If Hashem, who needs no advice, consulted the angels, surely we should ask others even when we feel no need.
humility/asking-advice-from-those-less-g.description: Why did Hashem say Let Us Make Man? Sanhedrin 38b and Rashi teach humility: seek counsel even from those of lesser stature, even when you think you know.

humility/concealing-ones-piety.intro: When Yonasan ben Uziel learned Torah, birds flying overhead were scorched, yet nothing like that is said about his teacher Hillel. The Kotzker Rebbe explains on Bava Basra 134a that Hillel was even greater and knew how to hide the power of his Torah. [Hitting the Target With All Talmidim](/daf/bava-basra/134/hitting-the-target-with-all-talmidim) adds the Chofetz Chaim, who said Kinnos like everyone else in shul and wept only at home.
humility/concealing-ones-piety.description: Why did great tzaddikim hide their spiritual intensity? The Kotzker Rebbe on Hillel and the Chofetz Chaim on Tishah B'Av, with Bava Basra 134a as a source.

humility/giving-up-honor-for-another.intro: When the Rosh HaYeshiva passed away, the rabbis chose Rav Yosef, but he turned the position down and Rabba was appointed. For twenty-two years Rav Yosef refused any display of honor so the reigning Rosh HaYeshiva would get his full respect. [Do Not Despair](/daf/bava-kamma/67/do-not-despair) brings the Chofetz Chaim's view of how Hashem rewarded him, based on Bava Kamma 67b.
humility/giving-up-honor-for-another.description: Rav Yosef turned down leadership and avoided honor for 22 years so Rabba would be respected. The Chofetz Chaim explains his reward, from Bava Kamma 67b.

humility/humility-and-torah-greatness.intro: The emperor's daughter told Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya that his magnificent Torah was stored in an ugly vessel. In Nedarim 50b he answered that just as wine spoils in silver and gold, Torah keeps best in a humble container. [Focusing on the Positive](/daf/nedarim/50/focusing-on-the-positive) explains that his plain appearance kept him humble in spirit, which let him reach loftier levels of Torah.
humility/humility-and-torah-greatness.description: Why is Torah stored best in a plain vessel? Rabbi Yehoshua ben Chananya's answer to the emperor's daughter in Nedarim 50b on humility and Torah.

humility/knowing-you-are-humble.intro: Can a humble person know that he is humble? Rav Yosi said, I have true humility, to question the Mishnah that humility ended with Rebbe. The article on Sukkah 20a explains that humility is honest self-awareness, so knowing it does not undo it, and Rav Meir Chodosh adds that Rav Yosi spoke to defend Rebbe's honor.
humility/knowing-you-are-humble.description: Can you know you are humble without losing it? Rav Yosi's claim of true humility, and why humility is honest self-awareness, in an article on Sukkah 20a.

humility/lying-for-the-sake-of-humility.intro: When Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai asked Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi whether a rainbow appeared in his lifetime, he said yes, though none had. The Chida finds a precedent in Bava Metzia 23b, where a talmid chacham may deny knowing a masechta, but why stay humble in Gan Eden, where everything is revealed? The Chochmas Hamitzpun says humility had become so much a part of him that he kept it even there.
humility/lying-for-the-sake-of-humility.description: May a talmid chacham play down his knowledge to stay humble? The Chida links Bava Metzia 23b to a rainbow story in Kesubos 77b about Gan Eden.

humility/misplaced-humility.intro: Why does the Gemara in Gittin 55b blame the churban on the humility of Rabbi Zecharia ben Avkolos? The Pardas Shaul says he felt unworthy to give the bold lenient ruling the moment needed. In [Misplaced Modesty](/daf/gittin/55/misplaced-modesty), the Ben Yehoyada adds that sending the question to the Sanhedrin delayed things, and Caesar's men took it as a refusal.
humility/misplaced-humility.description: How can humility be a fault? The Pardas Shaul and the Ben Yehoyada explain why Rabbi Zecharia ben Avkolos's anavah led to the churban, in Gittin 55b.

humility/moshe-admitting-he-forgot-a-hal.intro: When Aharon explained why the Rosh Chodesh korban was burned, Moshe admitted he had heard the halacha from Hashem but forgotten it. Zevachim 101a praises him for this, and the Chochmas HaMitzpun asks why plain honesty deserves praise. His answer in [Excuses, Excuses](/daf/zevachim/101/excuses-excuses): Moshe had a strong reason to hide it, since Korach and others could claim he forgot other things too.
humility/moshe-admitting-he-forgot-a-hal.description: Moshe admitted to Aharon that he heard a halacha but forgot it. Why does Zevachim 101a praise this? The Chochmas HaMitzpun shows what Moshe risked.

humility/rejoicing-over-anothers-mistake.intro: Could great sages feel even a little pleased when a colleague gets something wrong? Rashi seems to think so: on Bava Kamma 88b, Rav Chisda asks Rabbah not to reveal his error, because students would be happy that his view was disproven. Rashi says Rav Chisda was protecting them from the punishment such joy would bring.
humility/rejoicing-over-anothers-mistake.description: Why did Rav Chisda hide his error from his students? Rashi says they would rejoice and be punished for it, a danger even for sages, in Bava Kamma 88b.

humility/small-aleph-in-vayikra.intro: Sefer Vayikra opens with a small aleph, and the Rosh explains it with a Midrash. Moshe Rabbeinu was uneasy that the word vayikra showed Hashem called to him directly, and asked that future generations know he preferred vayikar. In this article filed on Sukkah 20a, wanting to teach that lesson is not pride, since true humility rests on seeing oneself truthfully.
humility/small-aleph-in-vayikra.description: Why is the aleph of Vayikra written small? The Rosh ties it to Moshe Rabbeinu's humility, and an article on Sukkah 20a explains why it isn't pride.

hakaras-hatov/appreciating-what-you-have.intro: When a poor man asked Rebbe Akiva and his wife for straw so his wife could lie down after giving birth, Rebbe Akiva remarked that some people have even less. The Gemara in Nedarim 50a says the man was Eliyahu HaNavi. [Cultivating Gratitude](/daf/nedarim/50/cultivating-gratitude) shares Rabbi Moshe Elefant's explanation that Eliyahu gave them something worth more than gold: the habit of appreciating what they had.
hakaras-hatov/appreciating-what-you-have.description: Why did Eliyahu HaNavi ask the poor Rebbe Akiva for straw? Nedarim 50a teaches gratitude by looking at those who have less, not those who have more.

hakaras-hatov/birthday-as-a-day-of-thank.intro: A rebbi carrying a birthday cake into yeshiva was asked why, since only Pharaoh is recorded in the Torah celebrating a birthday. He answered that Chazal encourage a seudas hoda'ah on the anniversary of a miracle, and childbirth is a great miracle. Tosafos in Bava Basra say the shalom zachar celebrates that same survival of mother and baby, and [Happy Birthday](/daf/avodah-zarah/5/happy-birthday) sets this beside Avodah Zarah 5a.
hakaras-hatov/birthday-as-a-day-of-thank.description: Can a birthday be a day of thanks for the miracle of birth, like a seudas hoda'ah or a shalom zachar? A rebbi's answer, with the sugya on Avodah Zarah 5a.
