angels-and-sheidim/angels-in-the-purim-s.description: Which angels were sent in the Purim story to sway Achashverosh and bring down Haman? The hidden miracles of Esther's plan, as told in Megillah 15b.

angels-and-sheidim/angels-not-singing-at.intro: On Sanhedrin 39b, the angels wanted to sing as the Egyptians drowned, but Hashem stopped them, saying His creations were drowning. Yet the Jewish people sang Az Yashir that very day. The article explains that Jews may rejoice at the fall of non-Jewish enemies, while the angels had no such permission, so half Hallel recalls their silence.
angels-and-sheidim/angels-not-singing-at.description: Why did Hashem stop the angels from singing at Krias Yam Suf while Israel sang Az Yashir? Sanhedrin 39b and what it means for half Hallel on Pesach.

angels-and-sheidim/let-us-make-man-meani.intro: The Gemara on Sanhedrin 38b discusses "Let us make man" as a verse that could lead to heretical readings. Rav Yehuda in the name of Rav says Hashem first created angels and asked their opinion, yet the next verse says He alone created man. The Alter of Slabodka says the moral lesson was worth the risk of misreading.
angels-and-sheidim/let-us-make-man-meani.description: Why does the Torah say Let Us Make Man in plural? Sanhedrin 38b on Hashem consulting the angels, and why the lesson was worth the risk of misreading.

nevuah/death-of-yeshayahu-hanavi.intro: A scroll found in Yerushalayim, cited in Yevamos 49, reveals how Yeshaya HaNavi died: at the hands of his own grandson, King Menashe. Menashe accused him of false prophecy, pointing to the 15 years Yeshaya said were added to Chizkiya's life, beyond his set years. The question was a real one, but Menashe only wanted an excuse, since the penalty for false prophecy is death.
nevuah/death-of-yeshayahu-hanavi.description: How did Yeshaya HaNavi die? A scroll in Yevamos 49b tells of his grandson Menashe, who branded him a false prophet over Chizkiya's 15 added years.

nevuah/elisha-and-the-bears.intro: Youths who lost their water business mocked Elisha HaNavi as he left Yericho, and bears came out of a forest and attacked them. In Sotah 46b, Rav and Shmuel argue whether the forest was there before or was created by a miracle too. The Gemara says the bears would not attack unless their home was nearby, and the Maharsha asks why Hashem didn't simply create bolder bears.
nevuah/elisha-and-the-bears.description: When youths mocked Elisha, bears attacked them. Rav and Shmuel argue in Sotah 46b whether the forest was also created by a miracle, and why it mattered.

nevuah/how-many-times-hashem-spoke-to-yo.intro: Rebbe Akiva taught that Hashem spoke to Yonah only twice, as Yevamos 98a reports. Yet the pesukim show Hashem speaking to him again after Ninveh, and the Midrash says Yonah brought a prophecy to Yehu. [Yonah & His Prophesies](/daf/yevamos/98/yonah-his-prophesies) weighs the answers of Tosfos, the Maharsha, the Yashresh Yaakov and the Chemdas Shlomo.
nevuah/how-many-times-hashem-spoke-to-yo.description: Did Hashem speak to Yonah only twice? Rebbe Akiva's teaching, the prophecy to Yehu, and Tosfos and the Maharsha's answers, from Yevamos 98a.

nevuah/moshes-forty-days-without-food-or.intro: A medrash says that during his forty days in the heavens, Moshe not only went without food but never slept at all. Since Nedarim 15a teaches that no one can stay awake for three days, why does the Torah mention only the fasting? The Dubno Magid answered that Moshe followed the angels' custom of not eating, and he could only know they never ate if he never slept.
nevuah/moshes-forty-days-without-food-or.description: Why does the Torah mention Moshe's forty-day fast but not that he never slept? The Dubno Magid's clever answer, built on Nedarim 15a and a medrash.

nevuah/yonahs-refusal-to-go-to-ninveh.intro: Why did Yonah flee instead of warning Ninveh? The Radak explains that Yonah worried their teshuvah would reflect badly on Klal Yisrael, who had not repented, and he was punished in that Hashem spoke to him only twice. The Iyun Yaakov asks why concern for Klal Yisrael would be punished, and answers on Yevamos 98a that Yonah simply misjudged the situation.
nevuah/yonahs-refusal-to-go-to-ninveh.description: Why did Yonah refuse to go to Ninveh? The Radak on his concern for Klal Yisrael and the Iyun Yaakov on why he was still punished, from Yevamos 98a.

avodah-zarah/aharon-and-the-golden-calf.intro: Why did Aharon help make the Golden Calf? On Sanhedrin 6a, Rabbi Elazar explains that after seeing Chur killed, Aharon feared the people would kill him too and never be forgiven. The Meiri and Rashi fault him for compromising instead of standing firm, while Tosfos understands that Aharon was praised.
avodah-zarah/aharon-and-the-golden-calf.description: Why did Aharon help make the Golden Calf? Sanhedrin 6a says he feared a worse sin after Chur's death. The Imrei Tzvi, the Meiri, Rashi and Tosfos weigh in.

avodah-zarah/bowing-to-an-official-weari.intro: Sanhedrin 61b permits bowing to a person out of respect, so why did Mordechai refuse to bow to Haman, who declared himself a god, as Megillah 19 says, and wore idols around his neck? [Should Mordechai Have Bowed to Haman?](/daf/sanhedrin/61/should-mordechai-have-bowed-to-haman) contrasts Rav Oppenheim, who permits bowing to such an official, with the Terumas HaDeshen, who cites Mordechai to forbid it.
avodah-zarah/bowing-to-an-official-weari.description: May a Jew bow to an official wearing idols? Why Mordechai refused Haman, Rav Oppenheim and the Terumas HaDeshen, with Sanhedrin 61b and Megillah 19.

avodah-zarah/church-bells-and-church-clo.intro: Rabbeinu Yerucham, building on Pesachim 26a, rules that one may not listen to music used for avodah zarah. The Minchas Elazar permitted glancing at a church steeple clock by the letter of the law, since it is a public service, though he advised against it, and church bells that call people to prayer seem more problematic. The Chofetz Chaim still lets one walk past such music without intending to enjoy it.
avodah-zarah/church-bells-and-church-clo.description: May you enjoy church bells or set your watch by a church clock? Rabbeinu Yerucham, the Minchas Elazar and the Chofetz Chaim, based on Pesachim 26a.

avodah-zarah/coins-with-a-human-face.intro: The beraisa in Rosh Hashanah 24b forbids fashioning images of humans, but the Shulchan Aruch limits this to a raised image, such as a face on a coin. When a coin was minted with the likeness of a rav, Rav Yaakov Emden ruled that it was no honor at all but a biblical violation. A flat drawing or painting of a person, as ['Draw' Your Own Conclusion](/daf/avodah-zarah/43/draw-your-own-conclusion) explains on Avodah Zarah 43, is permitted.
avodah-zarah/coins-with-a-human-face.description: Is it forbidden to mint a coin or medal with a person's face? Rav Yaakov Emden's ruling on raised images, from Avodah Zarah 43 and Rosh Hashanah 24b.

avodah-zarah/destruction-of-the-copper-s.intro: Whoever looked at the copper snake Moshe made was healed, and it lasted over 700 years. Chullin 6b asks why the righteous kings Assa and Yehoshafat left it, if Chizkiyahu later destroyed it once people worshipped it. They felt it recalled the miracle, and the Gemara says his ancestors left Chizkiyahu room to achieve prominence.
avodah-zarah/destruction-of-the-copper-s.description: Why was Moshe's copper snake kept for 700 years, then destroyed by Chizkiyahu? Assa and Yehoshafat left it to recall the miracle. Learn it from Chullin 6b.

avodah-zarah/drawing-the-sun-and-moon.intro: Most rishonim say that because the sun and moon look flat in the sky, even a flat drawing of them is forbidden. The Sfas Emes adds that a sliver of the moon is also forbidden, since that is how it appears, while a partial sun is allowed. Rav Moshe Feinstein permitted young children's drawings that look nothing like the sun, and [Over the Moon](/daf/avodah-zarah/43/over-the-moon) traces it all from Avodah Zarah 43.
avodah-zarah/drawing-the-sun-and-moon.description: May one draw the sun or moon, or a sliver of either? The Sfas Emes and Rav Moshe Feinstein on children's art, from Avodah Zarah 43 and Rosh Hashanah 24b.

avodah-zarah/making-sculptures-of-people.intro: Carving or molding a statue of a person is certainly forbidden, based on the beraisa in Rosh Hashanah 24b that lists humans among the images one may not fashion. The Shulchan Aruch limits the ban on human images to raised forms, so a painting or drawing of a person is permitted. The sun and moon are different, explain most rishonim on Avodah Zarah 43, because people appear full-bodied while those bodies appear flat.
avodah-zarah/making-sculptures-of-people.description: Why is a statue of a person forbidden while a flat painting is allowed? The Shulchan Aruch's rule, from Rosh Hashanah 24b and Avodah Zarah 43.

avodah-zarah/pictures-of-the-moon-in-tex.intro: Avodah Zarah 43 implies that one may not own pictures of the moon at home, and the Shulchan Aruch rules this way. But the reason is suspicion that the owner worships them, and the Vilna Gaon already wrote that some of these suspicions no longer apply. Rav Dovid Feinstein said no one suspects a science magazine reader, and that covering moon pictures in children's textbooks is not even worth the chumrah.
avodah-zarah/pictures-of-the-moon-in-tex.description: Must textbooks with pictures of the moon be thrown out? Why the suspicion behind the rule on Avodah Zarah 43 no longer applies, per Rav Dovid Feinstein.

avodah-zarah/roman-emperors-birthdays-as.intro: The Gemara on Avodah Zarah 5a lists the birthdays of powerful Roman leaders among the idolaters' official festivals. Because of this, doing business with idol worshippers around those dates was forbidden, to avoid supporting their celebrations. The Gemara says nothing about birthdays of Torah-observant Jews, a silence that left room for generations of debate and reflection.
avodah-zarah/roman-emperors-birthdays-as.description: Why the Gemara counts Roman rulers' birthdays among idolatrous festivals, and the ban on doing business around those days, as taught on Avodah Zarah 5a.

avodah-zarah/sin-of-the-golden-calf.intro: Chur stood up against those who wanted to replace Moshe, and Sanhedrin 7a reveals that the people killed him for it. Aharon was ready to die al Kiddush Hashem, but he knew that killing him too would be a sin Klal Yisrael could never recover from, unlike the Golden Calf. [Lessons Learned from Chur](/daf/sanhedrin/7/lessons-learned-from-chur) explores how he could take part in one sin to prevent a worse one.
avodah-zarah/sin-of-the-golden-calf.description: Why did Aharon help make the Golden Calf after Chur was killed? Sanhedrin 7a on preventing a worse sin, and how Tosfos and the poskim explain his choice.

avodah-zarah/worshipped-water-sources.intro: Rebbe Yochanan teaches on Avodah Zarah 59a that public water cannot become forbidden, even if an idolater worships it, despite the usual ban on benefiting from a worshipped item. Private water, the Gemara infers, would become forbidden. Tosfos asks how such a case exists, since Yehoshua made all water sources public, and answers with a man-made well or land with no neighbors around.
avodah-zarah/worshipped-water-sources.description: Why does worshipped public water stay permitted to drink while a private source may become forbidden? Rebbe Yochanan and Tosfos on Avodah Zarah 59a.

avodah-zarah/worshipping-idols-out-of-fe.intro: Is idol worship done out of fear or respect for a person still idolatry? On Sanhedrin 61b, Abaye says it is, while Rava says it counts only if the person truly accepts the idol as a god. Rava also says in Avodah Zarah 54a that one must give up his life only for public idol worship, though the halacha requires dying rather than worshipping even in private.
avodah-zarah/worshipping-idols-out-of-fe.description: Is idol worship done out of fear still avodah zarah? Abaye and Rava on Sanhedrin 61b, Avodah Zarah 54a, and when one must give up one's life instead.

medicine-and-health/choosing-the-lesser-.intro: When a medical problem is not life-threatening, Hatzalah members are taught to pick the lesser violation of Shabbos. HaRav Dovid Weinberger calls this ha-kal ha-kal techilah, but warns it is never for real emergencies, where delay might cost a life. [LOL: Lots Of Learning](/daf/shabbos/104/lol-lots-of-learning) shows why it matters which acts are more severe, using the laws of writing in Shabbos 104b.
medicine-and-health/choosing-the-lesser-.description: In a non-life-threatening case on Shabbos, one should choose the lesser melacha. How Hatzalah applies this rule, with the writing laws of Shabbos 104b.

medicine-and-health/doctors-charging-for.intro: The Rambam writes that healing a person is part of the mitzvah of returning a lost object. That raises a hard question: a finder may not charge for returning a lost item, so how can a doctor charge for healing? The discussion, tied to Yoma 49a, notes that a finder who leaves paid work may charge for his time, and Rabbi Bleich applies that same idea to doctors.
medicine-and-health/doctors-charging-for.description: If healing is part of returning a lost object, may a doctor charge for it? The Rambam's view and the finder who leaves paid work, discussed with Yoma 49a.

medicine-and-health/donating-blood-for-a.intro: In 1993 a sick man in Yerushalayim needed more blood credit, and ten bachurim went to donate in his name. Two were turned away, and one sat sadly. The other asked strangers at the center to credit their donations to the patient, and he got all he needed, a story told with Zevachim 24 about saving part of a mitzvah.
medicine-and-health/donating-blood-for-a.description: A bachur turned away from giving blood asked strangers to credit their donations to a sick man. A story of saving part of a mitzvah, told with Zevachim 24.

medicine-and-health/easing-a-patients-mi.intro: Bava Basra 156b allows a critically ill person to make a kinyan on Shabbos so that worry does not harm him. Rav Nissin Karelitz and the Shevet HaLevi explain that this is not true pikuach nefesh, only concern for the patient's well-being. Even so, the poskim allow some rabbinic Shabbos laws to be set aside to put his mind at ease.
medicine-and-health/easing-a-patients-mi.description: Can a sick person's peace of mind permit rabbinic acts on Shabbos? Bava Basra 156b allows a kinyan to calm him, even without true pikuach nefesh.

medicine-and-health/exceptions-to-pikuac.intro: Pikuach nefesh usually overrides every aveira except idolatry, forbidden relationships, and murder. Yet there are exceptions: the Yam Shel Shlomo forbids falsifying Torah, Tosfos counts public shaming, and Rashi may even read Bava Kamma 60b to say stealing is not allowed in danger. Rav Yaakov Kamenetzky ruled that even pikuach nefesh does not permit a chillul Hashem.
medicine-and-health/exceptions-to-pikuac.description: Does saving a life override every sin except the big three? Falsifying Torah, public shaming and chillul Hashem may be exceptions. From Bava Kamma 60b.

medicine-and-health/how-long-can-a-perso.intro: The Gemara in Nedarim 15a calls an oath not to sleep for three days a vain oath, since no one can stay awake that long. So how did three contestants watch television for over 86 hours to set a Guinness record? [Sleeping Duty](/daf/nedarim/15/sleeping-duty-2022) points to microsleep, brief episodes of real sleep that a person may not even notice, sometimes with his eyes wide open.
medicine-and-health/how-long-can-a-perso.description: Nedarim 15a says no one can stay awake for three days. How did TV marathon contestants last 86 hours? Microsleep explains the apparent record.

medicine-and-health/medicines-from-non-k.intro: In the Gemara's time, people drank donkey urine as medicine, and Rav Sheshes ruled it not kosher on Bechoros 7a. One version of his ruling permits horse and camel urine, which is processed less in the body. That matters for Premarin, a hormone drug made from the urine of pregnant mares, and the Rambam permits such urine while most Rishonim forbid it.
medicine-and-health/medicines-from-non-k.description: Is a drug from horse urine, like Premarin, kosher? Rav Sheshes rules on donkey urine, and the Rambam and other Rishonim differ, in Bechoros 7a.

medicine-and-health/overeating-and-healt.intro: Gittin 70a quotes a beraisa that whoever fills his belly will become sick, and Rav Papa adds that this is true even of healthy food. Eliyahu HaNavi advised stopping when two-thirds full, and the Rambam writes that most sickness comes from overeating. The Raavad adds that holding back for the sake of Heaven can be greater than a fast.
medicine-and-health/overeating-and-healt.description: Why does the Gemara warn against filling your belly, even with healthy food? Gittin 70a, the Rambam and the Raavad on overeating, health and self-control.

medicine-and-health/remote-danger-and-pi.intro: In Kesubos 39a, the Sages tell someone not to use a forbidden step to prevent a life-threatening condition, relying instead on Hashem protects the simple. How can this be? The Binyan Tzion says remote risks count only when danger is present now, while the Achiezer says the Gemara's risk was simply too farfetched to override halacha.
medicine-and-health/remote-danger-and-pi.description: How remote can a danger be and still override Shabbos? The Binyan Tzion and the Achiezer on present versus future danger, explaining Kesubos 39a.

medicine-and-health/saving-a-mother-in-d.intro: When a baby endangers its mother during birth, the Gemara in Sanhedrin 72 rules that once it is partly born it may not be harmed, since we do not choose one life over another. The Rambam explains that the baby is not a rodeif, because being born is a natural process and it takes no action of its own. The Tiferes Yisroel adds that the baby made no bad decision.
medicine-and-health/saving-a-mother-in-d.description: When a baby endangers its mother in birth, why can't it be harmed once partly born? The Rambam and the Tiferes Yisroel on Sanhedrin 72 and the rodeif.

medicine-and-health/surgical-skin-markin.intro: Before surgery, doctors often write on a patient's skin to make sure the right limb is operated on. Does that run into the prohibition of tattooing? The Nishmas Avraham quotes Rav Shlomo Zalman as permitting it, in the article on Gittin 20b that weighs how far the rabbinic extension of the tattoo ban reaches.
medicine-and-health/surgical-skin-markin.description: May doctors mark a patient's skin before surgery despite the tattoo prohibition? Rav Shlomo Zalman permits it, in an article on skin writing on Gittin 20b.

medicine-and-health/thermometer-strips-o.intro: Shemiras Shabbos Kehilchasa allows a forehead thermometer strip whose numbers always show but change color, yet Rav Shlomo Zalman limited this to a miktzas choleh. He explains that placing the strip is an intentional act that starts the change, unlike glasses darkened passively by the sun. The Orchos Shabbos questions the passive reasoning from Sanhedrin 77a, where tying someone in the sun makes one liable.
medicine-and-health/thermometer-strips-o.description: May a color-changing forehead thermometer strip be used on Shabbos? Shemiras Shabbos Kehilchasa and Rav Shlomo Zalman's limit, read with Sanhedrin 77a.

medicine-and-health/two-travelers-with-o.intro: Two travelers have water enough for only one, and Rebbe Akiva teaches from the word imach that your own life comes first. Yet the same word, said about an eved Ivri in Kiddushin 20a, means a master must give his only pillow to his slave. Rabbi Shmuel Niman's answer to this contradiction, raised by the Maharam Schiff, rests on logic: the travelers are equal, so water handed over would only have to be handed back.
medicine-and-health/two-travelers-with-o.description: Two travelers, one canteen: why your own life comes first, yet a master must give his only pillow to his eved Ivri, as the Gemara teaches in Kiddushin 20a.

medicine-and-health/vaccines-on-shabbos.intro: May Shabbos be broken to get a vaccine? Rav Shlomo Zalman ruled one may not do so for the smallpox vaccine, since the chance that a one- or two-day delay matters is farfetched. He suggested it might be different if missing Shabbos meant waiting years, as the article on Kesubos 39a explains in weighing remote risks.
medicine-and-health/vaccines-on-shabbos.description: May Shabbos be broken to receive a vaccine? Rav Shlomo Zalman on the smallpox vaccine and remote risk from a short delay, in an article on Kesubos 39a.

medicine-and-health/walking-after-eating.intro: Shmuel warns that going to sleep right after eating, without walking even a few steps, is harmful. On Bava Metzia 113b, that is why a debtor keeps two beds, set four amos apart. Telling someone to walk rarely works after a good meal, so Rashi says the setup will condition him to get up and walk.
medicine-and-health/walking-after-eating.description: Shmuel says walking a few steps after eating before sleep protects health. That is why a debtor keeps two beds, as taught in Bava Metzia 113b.

aveilus/burial-of-jews-with-tattoos.intro: Many people believe that a Jew with a tattoo cannot be buried in a Jewish cemetery, and the idea has spread through Jewish and secular media. As the article on Gittin 20b notes, Rabbi Dr. Ari Zivotofsky showed that this belief has no basis in Jewish law. A person who transgressed this prohibition may be buried there like anyone who violated other Torah laws.
aveilus/burial-of-jews-with-tattoos.description: Can a Jew with a tattoo be buried in a Jewish cemetery? A common myth with no basis in Jewish law, noted in an article on tattoos and skin, Gittin 20b.

aveilus/saying-hamakom-yenachem.intro: Men rushing out of a shivah house after davening often just say HaMakom yenachem and leave. Rav Moshe Feinstein rules that this is a blessing that Hashem should comfort the mourner, not nichum aveilim itself, so it does not fulfill the mitzvah. Rav Elyashiv, in his comments on Moed Katan 28b, seems to disagree and holds that saying it does count.
aveilus/saying-hamakom-yenachem.description: Does saying HaMakom yenachem alone fulfill comforting mourners? Rav Moshe says it is only a blessing, while Rav Elyashiv may disagree, on Moed Katan 28b.

aveilus/shemuah-rechokah.intro: When Rav arrived from Bavel, his answers told Rabbi Chiya that his brother and sister had died, and Rabbi Chiya removed his shoes but still planned to go to the bathhouse. Moed Katan 20a learns from this that someone who hears of a death more than thirty days later mourns for only one day, and even then only for part of it.
aveilus/shemuah-rechokah.description: How does one mourn on hearing of a relative's death more than thirty days later? Rabbi Chiya's brief mourning teaches the rule in Moed Katan 20a.

aveilus/telling-someone-a-relative-died.intro: Must one tell a person that a close relative has died? The Mordechai learns from Rav and Rabbi Chiya in Moed Katan 20a that there is no obligation, that bad news should be hinted rather than stated, and that one may not lie when asked. [Spreading The News](/daf/moed-katan/20/spreading-the-news) adds the Rema's custom to tell a son so he can say Kaddish.
aveilus/telling-someone-a-relative-died.description: Must one tell someone a close relative died, and how should bad news be shared? The Mordechai and Shulchan Aruch learn from a story in Moed Katan 20a.

aveilus/waiting-for-the-mourner-to-speak.intro: Rebbe Yochanon says in Moed Katan 28b that visitors should not speak to a mourner until he speaks first. So how can people say HaMakom yenachem at the funeral lines, in shul on Friday night, or when rushing out of a shivah house? Rav Moshe Feinstein and the Divrei Sofrim explain that it is a separate blessing, not a conversation, so it may come first.
aveilus/waiting-for-the-mourner-to-speak.description: Must visitors wait for the mourner to speak first, and how does HaMakom yenachem fit? Rebbe Yochanon and Rav Moshe Feinstein, from Moed Katan 28b.

aveilus/withholding-news-of-a-death.intro: The Alter of Slabodka hid the news of young Rav Yaakov Yitzchak Ruderman's father's death so he could finish Shas, saying that growth in Torah outweighs the Kaddish he would miss. Years later, Rav Yechezkel Sarna held back the news of Rav Meir Chodosh's father until thirty days had passed. The article on Moed Katan 20a ties both stories to the halacha that one need not tell.
aveilus/withholding-news-of-a-death.description: When was news of a death held back to protect Torah study? The Alter of Slabodka and Rav Yechezkel Sarna, tied to the halacha in Moed Katan 20a.

aveilus/yahrzeit-in-a-leap-year.intro: If a parent died in Adar of a regular year, when is the yahrzeit fast in a leap year? The Rema says Adar Rishon, which seems to clash with his ruling that a bar mitzvah falls in Adar Sheini. [The Great Leap Forward](/daf/shekalim/2/the-great-leap-forward), on Shekalim 2, explains with the Mahari Mintz that the yahrzeit marks twelve months, and the Mishnah Berurah suggests fasting in both.
aveilus/yahrzeit-in-a-leap-year.description: When is a yahrzeit kept in a leap year if the parent died in Adar? The Rema, Mahari Mintz and Mishnah Berurah answer, in an article on Shekalim 2.

gedolim/misinterpreting-the-actions-of-g.intro: People saw Rav Moshe Feinstein put down one milk carton and pick up another, and word spread that he preferred its hechsher. In truth, the first carton was empty. Tied to Kiddushin 8a, [A Kohen By Any Other Name](/daf/kiddushin/8/a-kohen-by-any-other-name) adds a rav whose shower ruling for men was misapplied, and a clever quip of the Chasam Sofer that was wrongly spread as halacha.
gedolim/misinterpreting-the-actions-of-g.description: How do the casual acts or quips of great rabbis get spread as rulings? Rav Moshe Feinstein's milk carton and the Chasam Sofer, tied to Kiddushin 8a.

technology-and-halacha/opening-the-freez.intro: A Lakewood bachur joked that he does not open a freezer on Shabbos, but the question is real: opening the door makes the compressor turn on sooner. Rav Shlomo Zalman permitted it as gerama for a rabbinic issue, and the Taz's rule covers the chance it starts at once. The article on Kesubos 6 notes some still open it only while the compressor runs.
technology-and-halacha/opening-the-freez.description: May you open a fridge or freezer on Shabbos if it makes the compressor run sooner? Rav Shlomo Zalman, the Taz and the Mishnah Berurah, from Kesubos 6.

technology-and-halacha/self-driving-cars.intro: One well-known talmid chacham advised a doctor to buy a self-driving car for Shabbos emergencies, based on Rav Chaim Kanievsky's view that speaking is not a bodily act of melacha. Even so, rabbinic concerns like uvda d'chol and v'daber davar may remain. The article traces this back to Moshe's writing of the Torah in Menachos 30a.
technology-and-halacha/self-driving-cars.description: Could a doctor use a self-driving car in a Shabbos emergency? Rav Chaim Kanievsky's view of speech as non-melacha, traced back to Menachos 30a.

technology-and-halacha/texting-on-shabbo.intro: Is typing a text on Shabbos the full melacha of writing? HaRav Shlomo Zalman says typing on a computer is only rabbinic, while the Shevet HaLevi says it can be the most severe form. Building on Shabbos 104b, the article asks whether screen savers change things, since writing must last, like the difference between fruit juice, which is rabbinic, and writing on skin that fades.
technology-and-halacha/texting-on-shabbo.description: Is texting on Shabbos the melacha of writing? HaRav Shlomo Zalman, the Shevet HaLevi and the role of screen savers, with Shabbos 104b in the background.

technology-and-halacha/voice-activated-d.intro: When a person speaks to a phone or computer and it performs a melacha, has he done the melacha himself? The Steipler says using a computer is the normal way and not a shinui, so it is forbidden, while Rav Chaim Kanievsky holds that speech is not a melacha of the body, so it may be permitted on a Torah level. The question grows out of Menachos 30a.
technology-and-halacha/voice-activated-d.description: Is speaking to a smart device that does melacha on Shabbos like doing it yourself? The Steipler and Rav Chaim Kanievsky differ, starting from Menachos 30a.

jewish-history/1848-cholera-yom-kippur-i.intro: During the 1848 cholera epidemic, Rav Yisrael Salanter went up to the bimah in Vilna on Yom Kippur and made Kiddush so everyone would eat. The Chofetz Chaim was a young boy in that shul, and Rav Yaakov Kamenetzky heard it was really tea and cake. [Required Eating on Yom Kippur?](/daf/shevuos/28/required-eating-on-yom-kippur), filed on Shevuos 28, weighs what really happened.
jewish-history/1848-cholera-yom-kippur-i.description: In 1848 cholera, Rav Yisrael Salanter told Vilna to eat on Yom Kippur. What happened, and was it Kiddush or tea and cake? An article on Shevuos 28.

jewish-history/burial-of-the-beitar-vict.intro: Rav Masneh says on Taanis 30b that Tu B'Av marks the day the Romans finally allowed the victims of Beitar to be buried. Hadrian had refused, and only the next emperor, after receiving payment, gave permission. The bodies had not decomposed despite years in the open, a clear sign that Hashem still loved His people even in exile.
jewish-history/burial-of-the-beitar-vict.description: Why do we remember Beitar on Tu B'Av? Rav Masneh on the late burial of the victims and the miracle that their bodies stayed whole, from Taanis 30b.

jewish-history/derech-haofel-road-histor.intro: Pope Paul VI refused to land at Lod Airport in 1964, so a new road was paved from East Jerusalem around the Old City's southeastern walls. Today that road, Derech HaOfel, carries thousands of Torah learners to the Kosel, the Jewish Quarter and yeshivos like Yeshivat HaKotel and Aish HaTorah. [Road to Redemption](/daf/avodah-zarah/2/road-to-redemption) connects it to Avodah Zarah 2, where Rome's works end up serving Torah.
jewish-history/derech-haofel-road-histor.description: Derech HaOfel was paved for a 1964 papal visit and now carries Torah learners to the Old City. Its history, read through Rome's claim on Avodah Zarah 2.

jewish-history/granada-massacre-of-1066.intro: The Raavad tells of Rabbi Shmuel HaLevi, a Jewish prince in Spain who bought costly manuscripts of the Mishnah and Talmud for students far and wide. His son Rabbi Yosef lacked only his father's humility, and the jealous Berber princes had him and the Jews of Granada killed on Shabbos, the ninth of Teves. In an article filed on Shevuos 15b, this first known massacre of Jews by Muslims in Spain is offered as one reason for that day's fast.
jewish-history/granada-massacre-of-1066.description: On the ninth of Teves, the Jews of Granada were massacred, the first such killing in Muslim Spain. The Raavad's account, in an article on Shevuos 15b.

jewish-history/jewish-military-chaplains.intro: In 1960, Rabbi Benjamin Samson became a Jewish chaplain at Sheppard Air Force Base in Texas, running services, teaching classes and building a sukkah. When a young airman planned to be baptized, the chaplain persuaded him to learn about Judaism first. The story opens a halachic discussion in the article on Gittin 41a about whether his mother could call on Shabbos.
jewish-history/jewish-military-chaplains.description: A Jewish Air Force chaplain in Texas ran services, built a sukkah and kept an airman from baptism, a story that opens a halachic question on Gittin 41a.

jewish-history/mir-yeshiva-escape-during.intro: HaRav Avrohom Kanarek grew up in Leipzig, where his father sent his boys to yeshiva in spite of the neighbors' scorn. Because they were in yeshiva, the boys escaped the Holocaust by fleeing with the Mirrer Yeshiva to China and Japan, while the Jews who stayed in Leipzig were deported. On his father's yahrzeit, Rav Kanarek tied this to Kalev's courage in Sotah 34b.
jewish-history/mir-yeshiva-escape-during.description: How did yeshiva boys from Leipzig survive the Holocaust? They fled with the Mirrer Yeshiva through Japan and China, as told in an article on Sotah 34b.

jewish-history/napoleon-cloak-story.intro: In 1812, as the French army fled Moscow, Reb Yosef Luria of Mogilev guided a weary rider to safety, and the rider, claiming to be Napoleon, handed him his royal cloak. Decades later it was made into a paroches in Yerushalayim, and [The Emperor’s Used Clothes – For the Aron Kodesh?](/daf/menachos/22/the-emperor-s-used-clothes-for-the-aron-kodesh--menachos-22) asks if that is allowed, starting from Menachos 22b.
jewish-history/napoleon-cloak-story.description: A Jew in Mogilev helped Napoleon flee in 1812 and got his cloak, later sewn into a paroches. Was that allowed? The halacha begins in Menachos 22b.

jewish-history/popes-1964-visit-to-israe.intro: In 1964 Pope Paul VI became the first pope to visit Israel, an 11-hour trip in which he never called Israel by name and avoided Yad Vashem. Rabbi Berel Wein points out that the United States paid to pave a road into East Jerusalem for the trip, and three years later Israeli forces used it to reunite Yerushalayim. The article reads this through Avodah Zarah 2, where Rome's building turns out to serve Torah.
jewish-history/popes-1964-visit-to-israe.description: Pope Paul VI's 1964 visit to Israel and the road paved for it, which later helped reunite Yerushalayim, read in light of Rome's claims on Avodah Zarah 2.

jewish-history/slavuta-shas-and-vilna-sh.intro: When the Romm brothers printed the Vilna Shas, the Slavuta printers claimed Rebbe Akiva Eiger was too old to have ruled against them, and he wrote a fierce reply. Later a Slavuta bookbinder was found dead, and the Russian authorities falsely accused the Shapira brothers of murder and closed the presses. The story explains the Daf Yomi order, in an article on Beitzah 37.
jewish-history/slavuta-shas-and-vilna-sh.description: How did a printing rivalry between Slavuta and Vilna lead to a false murder charge? The story behind the Daf Yomi order, in an article on Beitzah 37.

jewish-history/spies-generation-dying-in.intro: After the sin of the meraglim, the men of that generation would dig graves each erev Tishah B'Av and sleep in them, and thousands died every year. In the 40th year they woke up, and by the full moon of the 15th they knew the decree was over, as Taanis 30b recounts. The Midrash's figure of 15,000 deaths a year sparks a puzzle that Rabbeinu Tam, the Rashbam and the Chavos Yair each try to solve.
jewish-history/spies-generation-dying-in.description: How did the generation of the spies die in the desert, and why did it end on Tu B'Av? The graves of Tishah B'Av and the yearly count, from Taanis 30b.

jewish-history/tosfos-written-before-mar.intro: Bava Kamma 77a has only two lines of Gemara, and the rest of the page is filled by two long Tosfos. The Minchas Elazar had a tradition from the Bnei Yissaschar that the Baalei Tosfos wrote them on their last night, after choosing death over conversion. A closing phrase about not lengthening further may hint that their time had run out.
jewish-history/tosfos-written-before-mar.description: Two long Tosfos fill Bava Kamma 77a. A tradition says the Baalei Tosfos wrote them the night before they were killed for refusing to convert.

jewish-history/translation-of-the-torah-.intro: King Ptolemy put 72 elders in separate rooms and told each to translate the Torah. Every one of them made the same changes, a clear miracle, yet the eighth of Teves is remembered as a sad day. In [Ta’anis In Teves](/daf/megillah/9/taanis-in-teves), filed on Megillah 9, the reason is that the Torah makes the Jewish nation special, and now any nation could claim it.
jewish-history/translation-of-the-torah-.description: Why is the miraculous Greek translation of the Torah for King Ptolemy a sad day? The fast of the eighth of Teves, from an article filed on Megillah 9.

eretz-yisrael/dividing-eretz-yisrael-by-.intro: Shiloh is called a nachalah because Yehoshua divided the land there by lottery. But the Gemara said the division took seven years while the Mishkan was in Gilgal. [Lots Of Land: Daf 119b in Zevachim](/daf/zevachim/119/lots-of-land-daf-119b-in-zevachim) explains, based on Zevachim 119b and Rashi, that only the seven remaining tribes took part in the lottery at Shiloh.
eretz-yisrael/dividing-eretz-yisrael-by-.description: How was Eretz Yisrael divided by lot, first at Gilgal and then at Shiloh? Rashi explains which seven tribes were left, in a discussion of Zevachim 119b.

eretz-yisrael/learning-torah-in-eretz-yi.intro: Someone who learns better with a chavrusa may hesitate to move to Eretz Yisrael, where he would have no suitable partner. Rav Yaakov Emden says this is no reason to stay away, since the air of Eretz Yisrael makes one wise and its kedusha makes up for the missing chavrusa. The point appears in a discussion of Taanis 7a, which praises learning together like iron sharpening iron.
eretz-yisrael/learning-torah-in-eretz-yi.description: Should one learn in Eretz Yisrael without a good chavrusa? Rav Yaakov Emden says the Land's kedusha makes up for it, in a look at Taanis 7a on learning.

eretz-yisrael/making-aliyah-on-yom-tov-s.intro: Visitors from chutz la'aretz keep two days of Yom Tov in Eretz Yisrael. On Pesachim 52, the article brings Rav Shlomo Zalman's ruling about an American who decided in the middle of Yom Tov sheni to settle in Eretz Yisrael for good: it instantly stops being Yom Tov for him, and he may even need to put on tefillin. Rav Shlomo Zalman uses this to explain why a visitor might ask an Israeli to do melacha.
eretz-yisrael/making-aliyah-on-yom-tov-s.description: What if a visitor decides on Yom Tov sheni to settle in Eretz Yisrael for good? Rav Shlomo Zalman says Yom Tov ends for him at once. Pesachim 52.

eretz-yisrael/meaning-of-mearas-hamachpe.intro: Why is the burial cave of the Avos called Me'aras HaMachpelah, the doubled cave? In Eruvin 53, Rav and Shmuel disagree: one says the cave had a second floor, and the other says it was doubled because four couples were buried there. The Toras Chayim notes a practical difference for someone who sells a Me'aras HaMachpelah for burial.
eretz-yisrael/meaning-of-mearas-hamachpe.description: Why is the cave of the Avos called the doubled cave? Rav and Shmuel give two reasons in Eruvin 53, and the Toras Chayim finds a difference for contracts.

eretz-yisrael/owning-land-in-eretz-yisra.intro: Is owning land in Eretz Yisrael a requirement for aliyah leregel, as debated in Pesachim 8b? Tosfos in Bava Basra says every family owns its ancestral land, yet Tosfos also suggests Rabbi Yehudah ben Besaira owned none. The Vilna Gaon explains that he descended from the people of Ephraim who left Egypt too early and never received a share.
eretz-yisrael/owning-land-in-eretz-yisra.description: Does every Jewish family own a share of Eretz Yisrael? Tosfos and the Vilna Gaon on land, aliyah leregel and Rabbi Yehudah ben Besaira. From Pesachim 8b.

eretz-yisrael/reunification-of-jerusalem.intro: Avodah Zarah 2 teaches that what Rome built for itself will one day be shown to have served Torah. A road paved in 1964 with American funds carried Pope Paul VI toward the Old City, and in the Six-Day War three years later Israeli troops used it to flank Jordanian positions. In this way the road helped reunite Yerushalayim and paved the way for the Torah learned in the Old City today.
eretz-yisrael/reunification-of-jerusalem.description: How a road built in 1964 for a papal visit let Israeli troops flank the Jordanians and reunite Yerushalayim in 1967, read through Avodah Zarah 2.

non-jews/answering-christian-virgin-birt.intro: Why does Bava Basra 91a name Shimshon's sister, who appears nowhere in Tanach? Rav Yaakov Kamenetsky explains that someone would one day point to Shimshon's birth as proof that a baby can be born without a father. Knowing that Shimshon had a sister shows his parents were not barren, and the article adds a question about lineage from Dovid.
non-jews/answering-christian-virgin-birt.description: Why does the Gemara name Shimshon's sister? Rav Yaakov Kamenetsky says it answers later claims of a birth without a father. From Bava Basra 91a.

non-jews/convert-is-like-a-newborn.intro: Yevamos 22a teaches that a ger who converts is like a newborn child, with real halachic results. The Nachlas Yaakov uses this to explain the souls that Avraham and Sarah made in Charan, since those they brought to convert became new people. [Department Of Redundancy Department](/daf/yevamos/22/department-of-redundancy-department) also brings the Shita Mekubetzes and the Medabeir Kadumos on the Gemara's odd phrase, a convert who converted.
non-jews/convert-is-like-a-newborn.description: What does it mean that a convert is like a newborn? Yevamos 22a, Avraham's souls made in Charan, and Tosfos in Kesubos 11a on a conversion paradox.

non-jews/converts-from-amalek.intro: Sanhedrin 96b says that some of Haman's descendants taught Torah in Bnei Brak, but how could they convert if the Mechilta says converts from Amalek are not accepted? The Emek Bracha, Sridei Aish, Yad Dovid and Megillas Sefer each offer an answer. The Mechilta also says Rebbe Yehoshua of Bnei Brak did not accept that rule, which may be why they settled there.
non-jews/converts-from-amalek.description: May a descendant of Amalek convert? Sanhedrin 96b says Haman's descendants taught Torah in Bnei Brak, and the poskim explain how it could happen.

non-jews/converts-in-positions-of-leader.intro: Gittin 57b identifies Sancheriv's descendants as Shmaya and Avtalyon, who became the nasi and the head of beis din. If the Rambam is right that they were converts, how could they hold positions of authority? The Maharal says they had one Jewish parent, while the Magen Avos says the rule applies only when equally qualified candidates exist, and none matched them.
non-jews/converts-in-positions-of-leader.description: May a convert hold a position of authority? Shmaya and Avtalyon led Klal Yisrael, and the Maharal and the Magen Avos explain how, based on Gittin 57b.

non-jews/descendants-of-haman-learning-t.intro: The Gemara in Gittin 57b says Haman's descendants learned Torah in Bnei Brak, though converts from Amalek are not accepted. In [Converting Bad Into Good](/daf/gittin/57/converting-bad-into-good), the Megillas Sefer suggests a child adopted without anyone knowing his lineage. The Kli Chemda says Haman became Mordechai's slave, which erased his lineage from Amalek.
non-jews/descendants-of-haman-learning-t.description: How could Haman's descendants learn Torah if converts from Amalek are not accepted? The Megillas Sefer, Kli Chemda and Chasam Sofer, on Gittin 57b.

non-jews/ger-toshav-before-conversion.intro: A ger toshav is a non-Jew who accepts the seven Noahide laws. Some suggest this status can work as a first step: an Amaleki first becomes a ger toshav, and only then fully converts. The idea comes up while explaining how Haman's descendants came to teach Torah in Bnei Brak, as Sanhedrin 96b reports.
non-jews/ger-toshav-before-conversion.description: A ger toshav accepts the seven Noahide laws. Could that be a path to full conversion, even for a descendant of Amalek? A look at Sanhedrin 96b.

non-jews/moabite-converts-and-dovids-lin.intro: When Doeg questioned whether Dovid, a descendant of Rus, could even join the Jewish congregation, the issue went to the Beis Medrash. Amasa ben Yeter planted a sword and declared that a Moabite woman is permitted while a Moabite man is forbidden, a tradition from Shmuel HaNavi. The article on Sanhedrin 82 explains how this settled Dovid's lineage.
non-jews/moabite-converts-and-dovids-lin.description: Is a Moabite woman permitted to marry into Israel? Amasa ben Yeter's sword, the tradition from Shmuel HaNavi and Dovid HaMelech's lineage, Sanhedrin 82.

animals/feeding-stray-dogs-on-shabbos.intro: Normally one may not go to the effort of feeding animals that are not one's own on Shabbos. Shabbos 155 makes one exception for wild dogs, whose food is scarce, so feeding them is an act of compassion, and the Magen Avraham even calls it a mitzvah. Still, it should be only a small amount and not on a regular basis, since Hashem gave dogs a slow digestion.
animals/feeding-stray-dogs-on-shabbos.description: Why may you feed stray dogs on Shabbos when other animals that aren't yours are off limits? The Gemara's exception in Shabbos 155 and the Magen Avraham.

animals/muzzling-animals-to-prevent-thef.intro: Rashi notes that Avraham Avinu's camels were muzzled so they would not graze in other people's fields. But if R' Pinchas ben Yair's donkey in Chullin 7a refused untithed grain, why did Avraham's camels need muzzles? The Ramban, Maharzu, Rabbi Eliyahu Mizrachi and Yeriyos Shlomo each answer, and the Be'er BaSadeh says that donkey was the exception.
animals/muzzling-animals-to-prevent-thef.description: Why were Avraham's camels muzzled if a tzaddik's animals avoid sin? The Ramban, the Maharzu and others answer, with the donkey of Chullin 7a.

animals/understanding-the-speech-of-tree.intro: The Gemara says that Rebbe Yochanan ben Zakkai understood the speech of trees, and Rashi says he does not know what this means. The Rashbam explains it as tree care, Rabbeinu Gershom as incantations, and the Rashba and Ritva take it literally. The article on Nazir 10a uses this to show that the Gemara still has a point: cows don't talk.
animals/understanding-the-speech-of-tree.description: What does it mean that Rebbe Yochanan ben Zakkai understood the speech of trees? Rashi, the Rashbam, Rashba and Ritva explain, in an article on Nazir 10a.

animals/vegetarianism-in-judaism.intro: Rabbi Mordechai Becher taught that in the Torah's view animals have no rights, yet we must treat them properly because concern for their pain is from the Torah. He answered a vegetarian who said animals shouldn't eat other animals by pointing to the food chain. In this discussion filed on Shabbos 109, the idea that a compassionate person should avoid meat has some place, but only for one who has reached perfection.
animals/vegetarianism-in-judaism.description: Does compassion for animals mean a Jew should not eat meat? Rabbi Mordechai Becher on animal rights and vegetarianism, in a discussion on Shabbos 109.

travel/adding-personal-requests-to-tefil.intro: Tosfos on Pesachim 104b explains that Tefillas HaDerech is really a prayer dressed as a bracha, and that has practical results. In [Wandering Jews](/daf/pesachim/104/wandering-jews-2013), Rav Shlomo Zalman permits adding specific requests, such as protection from traffic accidents or terrorists. Rav Chaim Kanievsky adds that it is better to say it oneself than to hear it from someone else, since requests for mercy should come from one's own mouth.
travel/adding-personal-requests-to-tefil.description: May you add your own requests to Tefillas HaDerech, and should you say it yourself? Tosfos, Rav Shlomo Zalman and Rav Chaim Kanievsky. Pesachim 104b.

travel/crossing-the-date-line-during-sef.intro: What if a traveler crosses the halachic dateline during the Omer and loses a day? Rav Shlomo Zalman ruled he counts with everyone else but without a bracha for the rest of the Omer, since he missed a day. Even so, someone who knows this will happen should begin with a bracha, as the article on Sanhedrin 68 explains, just like a forgetful man.
travel/crossing-the-date-line-during-sef.description: Lost a day crossing the date line during Sefirah? Rav Shlomo Zalman on how to keep counting the Omer afterward without a bracha, along with Sanhedrin 68.

travel/davening-on-an-airplane.intro: Should you stand for Shemoneh Esrei on a plane? Rav Shlomo Zalman Auerbach ruled that one should sit, since standing is hard and davening in the aisle or by the bathrooms disturbs others. [Davening on a Plane](/daf/zevachim/23/davening-on-a-plane) traces the question back to Zevachim 23b, where avodah done sitting is invalid, and the Shulchan Aruch's rule for riders on a donkey.
travel/davening-on-an-airplane.description: Stand or sit for Shemoneh Esrei on a plane? Rav Shlomo Zalman says sit and keep the aisles clear. The question traced back to the avodah in Zevachim 23b.

travel/davening-while-driving.intro: Berachos 30a lets a person riding a donkey daven without dismounting, since otherwise he would rush. Rav Shlomo Zalman Auerbach ruled that one should not daven while driving a car, because distracted driving can be fatal. A donkey can avoid danger on its own, while a car needs the driver's full attention.
travel/davening-while-driving.description: May you daven while driving a car? The Gemara lets a rider daven on a donkey, but Rav Shlomo Zalman Auerbach says a car is different. See Berachos 30a.

travel/emergency-landing-for-a-sick-pass.intro: Rav Elyashiv held that Shabbos may be broken to rush a patient to the hospital even if the chance he gets worse is under five percent. But a plane should not make an emergency landing, inconveniencing hundreds, for a risk that small. In [To Save a Life](/daf/kesubos/39/to-save-a-life), on Kesubos 39a, a paramedic's flight to Israel nearly landed in Tehran.
travel/emergency-landing-for-a-sick-pass.description: When does a sick passenger justify diverting a flight? Rav Elyashiv's five percent rule versus Shabbos rescue, and a flight to Israel, from Kesubos 39a.

travel/saying-tefillas-haderech-after-an.intro: Why does Tefillas HaDerech end with Baruch atah but not begin with it? The Maharam MiRotenburg says it was meant to follow Ma'avir sheinah, so the Mishnah Berurah advises saying another long bracha, such as Asher Yatzar or Borei Nefashos, right before it. The article on Pesachim 104b tells of a boy who thought his family's custom was simply to eat before the prayer, and of Rabbi Nosson Adler, who smelled spices.
travel/saying-tefillas-haderech-after-an.description: Why say Asher Yatzar or a bracha achronah right before Tefillas HaDerech? The Maharam MiRotenburg, Mishnah Berurah and Rashba explain. Pesachim 104b.

travel/when-to-say-tefillas-haderech.intro: Tefillas HaDerech ends with Baruch atah but does not begin with it. The Maharam MiRotenburg says it was meant to follow another berachah, so the Mishnah Berurah advises saying Asher Yatzar or a berachah acharonah first. In [Wandering Jews](/daf/berachos/11/wandering-jews), Berachos 11 and the Rashba offer a reason why many people are not careful about this.
travel/when-to-say-tefillas-haderech.description: Why say another berachah before Tefillas HaDerech? The Maharam MiRotenburg, the Rashba and the Mishnah Berurah on the traveler's prayer. Berachos 11.

rodeif/is-an-unwitting-attacker-a-rodef.intro: If a misinformed pilot is about to fire on his own disguised soldiers, may he be shot down as a rodef? The Rambam says anyone may stop a pursuer, and Rashi on Sanhedrin 72b discusses Sheva ben Bichri, while the Tiferes Yisrael limits it to one who made a bad decision. Rav Elyashiv ruled that a pilot risking his life to save others is the opposite of a rodef.
rodeif/is-an-unwitting-attacker-a-rodef.description: Is someone who unknowingly endangers others a rodef? The Rambam, Rashi on Sheva ben Bichri, the Tiferes Yisrael and Rav Elyashiv's ruling, Sanhedrin 72b.

rodeif/sacrificing-one-life-to-save-many.intro: A pilot unknowingly carries a deadly drug to a Pesach retreat, and two generals ask whether to shoot him down to save many. [When Do You Kill a Rodeif?](/daf/sanhedrin/72/when-do-you-kill-a-rodeif) weighs Rashi on Sheva ben Bichri, who allows killing a lone person for many only if he would die anyway, against the Rambam's view of Sanhedrin 72, until Rav Elyashiv rules the heroic pilot is no rodeif.
rodeif/sacrificing-one-life-to-save-many.description: May one innocent life be taken to save many? Rashi on Sheva ben Bichri, the Rambam and Rav Elyashiv's ruling in a rescue dilemma, from Sanhedrin 72.
